Closes #2

> **Stacked on #28** (issue #26). CI cannot be green without that fix — `plugin/scripts/validate_plugin.py` exits 1 on any clean checkout today. Base is set to that branch so this PR shows only its own diff and gets a genuinely green run. **Retarget to `main` once #28 merges.**

## What changed and why
Adds `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: `pull_request` + pushes to `main`, py3.11/py3.12 on ubuntu-latest, each running `check_portable_paths.py` → `sync_plugin.py --check` → `validate_plugin.py` → the fast shard in `tests/ci_shard.txt`. The full ~1,700-test suite stays out of per-PR CI per `docs/inbox/SUITE-COORDINATION.md`.

- Learnings: [x] n/a

`tests/test_router.py` was in the issue’s starting list but is **not** green in a fresh clone and is excluded, with the reason recorded in `tests/ci_shard.txt`: `test_e2e_prompt_to_rfa` needs the git-ignored `extracted/racbasicsampleproject` corpus (owner machine), and the `spec -> ifc` cases need `ifcopenshell`, an optional dependency. author: feulf
body:
Found by verifying the first real notarized build instead of trusting it.

Notarizing only the `.dmg` gets the download past Gatekeeper, but the app dragged out to `/Applications` carries no ticket of its own — `stapler validate` on the copied app said *"does not have a ticket stapled to it"*. It passes `spctl` anyway **only because macOS can reach Apple's notary service**; a first launch without network is refused.

The app is now notarized and stapled before the disk image is built around it, and the image is still notarized and stapled in turn (Gatekeeper judges the download before it judges the app inside). `ditto` does the zipping so the bundle's symlinks and resource forks survive the round trip.

Verified end to end on a real build:
- both submissions `status: Accepted`, both staple+validate actions worked
- the app copied out of the dmg validates its own ticket
- `spctl` accepts it with a `com.apple.quarantine` attribute set, as a browser download would have
- the quarantined copy launches and its hook server answers

Also brings `package-lock.json`'s version field back in step — it had drifted at 0.1.0 through two releases.

author: asoroca1
body:
## The functional problem

Export always dumped **every member profile**, regardless of the stage, search, and filters on screen — and it couldn't reach prospects, invitees, or pending requests at all. Standing in "Prospects, filtered to 2019" and hitting Export gave you all members. Silently wrong output is worse than an error.

## What it does now

Two sources, chosen at the top of the dialog:

- **This list** — exactly the rows in view. Any stage, honouring stage + search + filters, or the current selection when people are ticked. Pipeline columns: stage, role, tags, invite dates, request message, camp years.
- **Member profiles** — the existing rich profile export, for people who have joined.

Both name the scope and the exact row count, above the columns *and* on the button ("Download 1,284 rows"), so what downloads is never a surprise.

New endpoints `GET /people/export.csv`, `/people/export/preview`, `/people/export/fields`. All share one `resolveFilteredPeople` helper with `GET /people`, so the list and its export can't drift apart.

## The visual problem

The dialog outgrew the viewport and was clipped top and bottom, and the preset row overflowed its right edge (both visible in the screenshot that prompted this). It's now 940px with a two-pane body — column picker left, live preview right — each scrolling internally so the dialog stays 480px tall instead of unbounded. The picker is searchable, selected columns show their order (#1, #2…), and All/Reset are one click. The dialog declares its own CSS tokens so it renders correctly wherever it's mounted.

## Verification

- API: 31 suites / 141 tests pass. Lint and build clean.
- Harness-checked: dialog fits the viewport (480/720px), no page overflow, switching sources swaps the column catalog and scope label, column toggling reorders and refetches the preview, console clean.

author: allxsmith
body:
Closes #493. Second of three stacked label-association PRs following #492 (merge order: this one → #494's PR → #495's PR).

## What

The convenience `label` prop on **Autocomplete** and **Taginput** rendered an unassociated Field label, and a user-supplied `id` landed on the wrapper `<div>` instead of the labellable inner `<input>`. Both now run through the `useAutoLabelId` hook from #492: the inner input gets your `id` (or a generated one), the label gets a matching `for`, and an explicit `labelProps.htmlFor` wins outright.

## Behavior changes to review

- **id relocation**: a user-supplied `id` now applies to the inner text input (the labellable control), not the wrapper div. Verified nothing in the repo, docs, stories, or skills relied on the old placement; anyone targeting the wrapper by `#id` in CSS/tests would need to adjust. Documented in the props tables.
- **Taginput naming**: the hardcoded `aria-label="Add tag"` becomes a fallback — suppressed when the wired visible label names the input (aria-label would otherwise shadow it), kept when unlabeled or nested in an outer `Field`.
- **Taginput at `maxTags`**: the text input isn't rendered, so the label deliberately renders without `for` instead of dangling.

## Tests

New `describe('label association (#493)')` blocks in both suites: association via `getByLabelText`, id relocation locked (input has it, wrapper doesn't), `labelProps.htmlFor` override, no-label/no-id, inside-Field no injection, both aria-label fallback directions, and the maxTags unwired case. All React 18/19-safe (no id text asserted). `pnpm all` green.

## Docs / skill

Accessibility sections updated on `autocomplete.md` and `taginput.md`; TSDoc shadow-redeclares drive the regenerated props tables; `skills/bestax-form` moves both components into the auto-wired list (remaining manual: `Field`-composed usage and the group inputs — #494 and #495 are next in the stack).

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

* **Accessibility Improvements**
  * Autocomplete and Taginput now automatically associate labels with their inputs.
  * Added support for custom input IDs and label properties, including explicit association overrides.
  * Improved accessible-name handling when labels are absent or inputs are hidden.

* **Documentation**
  * Updated component references and form guidance to explain label wiring, IDs, and edge cases.

author: yidada
body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds an opt-in personal Weixin channel for self-hosted Multica deployments. A workspace admin can bind a Multica Agent by scanning a Tencent iLink Bot QR code, then use that Agent from a one-to-one personal Weixin conversation without exposing a public callback endpoint.

Multica already supports Lark, Slack, DingTalk, and WeCom, but WeCom smart bots do not cover personal Weixin accounts. The missing channel meant a self-hoster could not use a private household or personal assistant from the Weixin client they already use. This change introduces a separate `weixin` adapter and leaves the existing WeCom integration unchanged.

The adapter deliberately limits its initial scope to private text messages from the exact Weixin account that confirms the QR login. Group traffic, media, and messages from other users are ignored. Tencent bot tokens are encrypted at rest with `MULTICA_WEIXIN_SECRET_KEY`.

## Related Issue

No linked issue; this PR proposes the personal Weixin channel as a new feature.

## Type of Change

- [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [x] New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement (no behavior change)
- [x] Documentation update
- [x] Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] CI / infrastructure

## Changes Made

- Added `server/internal/integrations/weixin`, covering iLink QR login, installation persistence, encrypted token storage, long-poll message ingestion, private-sender filtering, Agent dispatch, and context-token-aware replies.
- Added workspace APIs to list, begin, poll, and revoke personal Weixin installations.
- Added Agent and Settings UI for QR binding, status polling, connection state, and revocation.
- Added core API schemas, TypeScript types, query keys, realtime invalidation, and English, Simplified Chinese, Japanese, and Korean copy.
- Added `weixin_chat` issue origin migrations using separate check and validation steps.
- Added `MULTICA_WEIXIN_SECRET_KEY` to the self-host configuration and documented channel setup and the current single-replica requirement.
- Added a bounded 20-second QR status poll so Tencent's long poll cannot overrun the outer web request deadline.

## Thinking Path and Design Notes

The existing channel architecture already provides generic installation storage, issue creation, daemon execution context, event publication, and outbound reply hooks. The new adapter follows those boundaries so Weixin remains isolated from WeCom and the other channels.

Tencent's QR confirmation returns a bot token, bot ID, iLink user ID, and a regional base URL. The implementation validates all returned base URLs against Tencent's Weixin domain, encrypts the token before persistence, and starts a long-poll worker for each active installation. iLink context tokens are retained beside the live worker because they are needed for reliable replies.

This context-token state currently lives in process memory. Deployments enabling personal Weixin should therefore run one backend replica until cross-replica outbound routing is available. The server logs this constraint at startup and the self-host documentation calls it out explicitly.

## How to Test

1. Set `MULTICA_WEIXIN_SECRET_KEY` to a generated 32-byte secret and start the backend.
2. Open an Agent, then select **Capabilities → Integrations → Connect personal Weixin**.
3. Scan the QR code with a personal Weixin account and confirm the login.
4. Send a private text message from the scanning account and verify that the bound Agent replies.
5. Verify that a different sender, a group message, and non-text items are ignored.
6. Disconnect the installation and verify that its long-poll worker stops.

Automated and build checks run for this change:

- `GOCACHE=/tmp/multica-go-cache go test ./internal/integrations/weixin ./internal/daemon/execenv`
- `pnpm --filter @multica/views exec vitest run agents/components/agent-overview-pane.test.tsx agents/components/tabs/integrations-tab.test.tsx` — 23 tests passed
- Production Docker frontend build, including Next.js compilation and TypeScript checking
- Production Docker backend build and database migration startup
- Live QR creation and repeated QR-status polling against Tencent iLink
- `git show --check HEAD`

## Risks and Follow-ups

- The connector depends on Tencent iLink Bot API behavior and should remain deployment opt-in.
- The current implementation supports private text conversations only.
- Multiple backend replicas require shared context-token state or routed outbound delivery before this channel can be considered replica-safe.

## Checklist

- [x] I have included a thinking path that traces from project context to this change
- [x] I have run tests locally and they pass
- [x] I have added or updated tests where applicable
- [ ] If this change affects the UI, I have included before/after screenshots
- [x] I have updated relevant documentation to reflect my changes
- [x] If I added a new runtime / coding tool / UI tab, I synced the change to **landing copy** (`apps/web/features/landing/i18n/`) and **relevant docs** (`apps/docs/content/docs/`) — Not applicable to landing copy: this adds a channel section inside the existing Integrations tab; channel docs are updated.
- [x] If this PR touches Chinese product copy, I checked it against `apps/docs/content/docs/developers/conventions.zh.mdx` (terminology, mixed-rule for `task` / `issue` / `skill`)
- [x] I have considered and documented any risks above
- [x] I will address all reviewer comments before requesting merge

## AI Disclosure

**AI tool used:** OpenAI Codex

**Prompt / approach:** Implement personal Weixin support as a separate Agent channel, following Multica's existing chat-integration boundaries and a Tencent iLink QR-login reference flow. Codex inspected the repository conventions and existing Lark/Slack/DingTalk/WeCom adapters, implemented the backend and UI, added migrations and documentation, deployed the branch locally, and exercised the QR flow before opening this PR.

## Screenshots (optional)

The feature was visually verified in the local Agent integrations page; screenshots can be added during review if requested.

author: sanity
body:
## Problem

`NodeInfo::uptime_seconds` in the node-diagnostics response is always `0`. It
was a hardcoded literal in the `QueryNodeDiagnostics` handler:

```rust
uptime_seconds: 0, // TODO: implement actual uptime tracking
```

The `TODO` had been there for the field's whole lifetime, so every
`freenet service report` upload has claimed the node had zero uptime.

This is the field a human reaches for when diagnosing a restart loop or a
wedged node, so a silently-dead value is actively misleading rather than
merely absent — someone debugging a node that keeps restarting would read
`uptime_seconds = 0` as confirmation of their hypothesis. Same failure class
as #3987, where a `HashMap` with non-string keys made the whole
`network_status` field upload empty for about ten months unnoticed.

### Evidence

Three independent user diagnostic reports, all reading `uptime_seconds = 0`
while every sibling field in the same response carries real data:

| Report | Connected peers | Hosting contracts | `uptime_seconds` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `R7JSRK` | 18 | 933 | `0` |
| `WEWYWY` | 169 | 1813 | `0` |
| `R7W5NC` | 83 | 706 | `0` |

`R7JSRK` came from a node that had been running roughly seven hours at report
time. In all three, `location`, `listening_address`, `is_gateway`,
`active_connections` and `system_metrics` are populated correctly — the zero
is specific to this one field, not a symptom of a broken response.

## Solution

`P2pConnManager` records the instant it was built and computes elapsed seconds
when a diagnostics query arrives.

Two details worth a reviewer's attention:

- **The clock is the node's injectable time source**, taken from
  `NodeConfig::hosting_time_source_override` and falling back to
  `InstantTimeSrc`. This mirrors how `OpManager` sources the interest
  manager's clock (`op_state_manager.rs`), honours the DST rule against bare
  `Instant::now()` in `crates/core/`, and lets a simulation advance uptime
  deterministically.
- **The start instant is carried across the destructure/rebuild** at
  event-loop entry rather than re-read from the clock. Re-reading there would
  restart the measurement at event-loop entry and silently under-report uptime
  for the life of the process. There is an inline comment at that site saying
  so, because it is the obvious thing for a future edit to get wrong.

The helper saturates rather than panicking if the clock reports an instant
before the start. That is unreachable with the production monotonic clock, but
a diagnostics query must never be able to take the node down.

### Scope

Only `uptime_seconds` was dead. Every other field in `NodeDiagnosticsResponse`
was checked against the three reports above and carries real values.

One adjacent oddity, noted but deliberately **not** changed here to keep this
to one logical change: the handler computes
`let _network_subs = op_manager.get_network_subscriptions();` and discards it,
so `response.subscriptions` contains application subscriptions only. That is a
question about intended semantics rather than a dead field, and is filed
separately if it turns out to be wrong.

No wire-format or stdlib change: `uptime_seconds` already exists on
`freenet_stdlib::client_api::NodeInfo`.

## Testing

Two tests reproduce the bug. Both were verified by re-applying the exact
`uptime_seconds: 0` literal and re-running:

- `test_node_diagnostics_reports_nonzero_increasing_uptime`
  (`crates/core/tests/node_diagnostics_uptime.rs`) boots a gateway and queries
  diagnostics over the real WebSocket client path twice, asserting uptime is
  non-zero **and strictly increasing**. Under the mutation it fails, with the
  node's own log showing the wire response carrying `uptime_seconds: 0`. The
  increasing assertion is what stops a future hardcoded constant from passing
  a bare `> 0` check.
- `node_diagnostics_computes_uptime_rather_than_hardcoding_it` is a
  source pin bounded to the `NodeInfo { .. }` literal in the handler, so
  re-inlining a value at the call site fails CI. It fails under the mutation
  with the offending literal printed.

Two further unit tests cover the helper's boundaries on a mock clock:
sub-second truncation, the 1-second boundary, the seven-hour `R7JSRK` case,
and a clock behind the start instant. **These pass under the mutation by
design** — they exercise the helper directly, so they are coverage for the
computation, not reproductions of the call-site bug.

Also verified end to end: the e2e test asserts against a real node's real
diagnostics reply rather than a unit-level stub, which is what makes it catch
the handler dropping the helper call.

Closes #5223

author: sonichi
body:
Found by **Sutando-Pro** while chasing something unrelated; they explicitly did not claim it. Verified from the artifacts before acting, and the class is larger than either of us first said.

## The class, AST-enumerated at module scope

`src/slack-bridge.py` binds **nine** paths from the resolved workspace **at import**:

```
:97  TASKS_DIR             :103 OWNER_ACTIVITY_FILE
:98  RESULTS_DIR           :115 ACCESS_BACKUP_FILE
:99  STATE_DIR             :494 PENDING_REPLIES_FILE
:100 INBOX_DIR
:101 ARCHIVE_TASKS_DIR
:102 ARCHIVE_RESULTS_DIR
```

**#2615 rebound two of them.** Its fixture comment states the mechanism exactly right — a constant derived from `STATE_DIR` at import does not re-derive when `STATE_DIR` is rebound later — and then enumerates *one member* of the class instead of the class. `PENDING_REPLIES_FILE` (:494) is bound identically to `OWNER_ACTIVITY_FILE` (:103) and stayed aimed at the operator's real workspace.

That fixture also sets `SUTANDO_WORKSPACE` for isolation. `resolve_workspace()` **ignores** it (removed v0.8/#1440), so that line does nothing and the manual rebinding was carrying the entire burden alone.

## The fix discovers by relationship, not by name

Naming nine constants just moves the deadline to the tenth. `rebind_workspace()` walks the module's attributes and re-points every `Path` that lies **under the module's own resolved root**, preserving its relative position. A constant added later is covered the day it is added.

## Evidence

```
live state/slack-pending-replies.json    4 entries, channels C1 / D_TEST
pre-fix fixture style (2 names only)     PENDING_REPLIES_FILE under real root: True
with rebind_workspace()                  nothing left under the real root
tofu fixture after conversion            7/7 pass, live file mtime unchanged
83 slack/hermetic/bridge suites          pass
```

The coverage test leads with a **control**: discovery must find ≥8 paths and specifically `STATE_DIR`, `OWNER_ACTIVITY_FILE`, `PENDING_REPLIES_FILE` — a vacuous discovery would make every other assertion in the file pass for free.

## Scope, stated rather than implied

- Fixes **slack's** fixture. `discord-bridge.py` binds **12** such paths and `telegram-bridge.py` **9** by the same pattern. The helper covers them, but their fixtures are not converted here and I have not audited which of their tests leak.
- **Not touched:** the 4 polluted live entries. Deleting rows from the operator's `state/` is his call, not a test fix.
- Pro noted the `outbox.log` rows carry no `status`/`sent`/`dry_run` field, so **whether anything was delivered is not determinable** from that file. I am not asserting a send, and neither did they.

## Two of my own errors, since they affect how to read this

I removed `self._orig_state` while leaving two references to it — 7/7 failed until fixed. And Pro's line numbers (`:97`, `:485`) and entry count (25) differ from what I measured here (`:96`, `:494`, 4 entries); the mechanism is identical, so I take those as a different head rather than a disagreement.

Related: #2622 (mine, open) lints the CCD-vs-workspace axis for *resolver stub arity* — a different shape, so this is not a duplicate of it.

@sonichi flagging you for the 4 live entries — that part is a decision, not a fix.

author: joshting11fh
body:
## Summary
- `search_web` was previously scoped to general context only — any question about the app's own clinics/regions had to come from Supabase alone. Relaxes this narrowly: for a "tell me about X" style question naming a specific clinic/region, the model can now supplement the DB facts with idiosyncratic web color (what the clinic's own site emphasizes, notable local mentions), similar to how a Gemini-style answer blends a knowledge panel with live search.
- Structured/numeric facts (ownership, GP count, composite/supply/demand scores, ratings, billing type) are explicitly still Supabase-only — the existing "app data always wins on conflict" and web-attribution rules are unchanged.
- **Latency mitigation** (this was flagged as a real cost before building it):
  - New prompt rule: for "tell me about X" questions, call the matching DB lookup tool (`query_clinics`/`query_sa3_regions`/`resolve_gazetteer_region`) and `search_web` in the *same* turn — they don't depend on each other once the name is known, so they execute concurrently instead of adding a sequential round-trip.
  - Told to say plainly when a search comes back thin (common for small independent clinics with little web footprint) instead of padding the answer with generic filler.
  - Trimmed the `search_web` tool's own footprint: `maxResults` 5→3, added `maxTokensPerPage: 512` / `maxTokens: 4000` caps — faster search call, less for the model to read before answering.

## Test plan
- [x] `node --check api/assistant.js`
- [x] Confirmed `gateway.tools.perplexitySearch({...})` constructs correctly with the new trimmed params (`node -e` runtime check of `.args`)
- [ ] Real behavior (does it actually enrich clinic answers, does latency stay acceptable) needs a live deploy with `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY` — same limitation as every other change to this endpoint; cannot be exercised against a real model locally

body:
Promotion de `staging` vers `main`. Fusion sans conflit, `main` ne portait aucun travail propre.

## Ce qui passe en production

| Domaine | Contenu |
|---|---|
| Paiement | Fapshi en paiement direct — NotchPay supprimé |
| Billetterie | QR code du billet, envoi par email, renvoi à la demande |
| Contrôle d'accès | Trois régimes par événement : `AUCUN`, `QR_FIXE`, `QR_TOURNANT` |
| Annuaire | Ouverture aux partenaires accrédités |
| Comptes | Changement d'adresse email avec confirmation |
| Sécurité | Empreintes de mot de passe retirées des réponses, correctif nanoid |
| Documentation | Contrat OpenAPI complet — 51 chemins, 54 schémas |

## À poser avant la mise en service du paiement

L'environnement `production` attend les identifiants du service **live** :

- `FAPSHI_API_USER`, `FAPSHI_API_KEY`, `FAPSHI_WEBHOOK_SECRET` — secrets
- `FAPSHI_BASE_URL` = `https://live.fapshi.com` — variable

Tant qu'ils sont absents, **l'application refuse de démarrer en production** : encaisser avec la passerelle factice reviendrait à livrer des billets sans débiter personne, et ce garde-fou est délibéré.

L'URL de webhook à déclarer sur le service live est `https://<domaine>/api/v1/webhooks/fapshi`.

## Migrations à jouer avant le basculement

`migrationsRun` est désactivé en production. La commande de release doit passer avant :

pnpm run migration:run:prod

author: scala-steward
shotwellj
body:
The `/ingest` endpoint shipped in #76 and #78 with **no operator documentation**. The only description of the wire contract, the client requirements, and the failure semantics lived in a chat log. A design partner could not integrate without being walked through it by hand.

## `docs/guides/ingest-integration.md`

- **Why an application shouldn't own the chain** — single-writer design, and a forked chain *verifies clean*, so nothing looks broken until a regulator runs the verifier
- **Server setup**, including the single-machine constraint and why the file lock can't reach across two
- **The wire contract** — full payload, field semantics, every status code
- **What a client owes**: durable outbox, stable `event_id` written once, ordered batches with in-order partial acks, self-capped batch size, decisions-not-queries
- **The retry classification** — only a malformed payload spends the give-up budget. `503` is the *first* response a correct client ever sees (the endpoint is inert until its token is set), so treating it as fatal would strand the opening batch of evidence
- **The tenant trap** — `export_evidence` exports the *chat session's* tenant, not the ingesting one. Asking Claude to export returns an empty bundle and looks like "nothing was recorded." `/ingest/export` is the right call
- **Covenant semantics on ingest** — a loaded covenant is a retrospective second opinion, never enforcement. `no_rule` instead of a fabricated block, because recording a completed foreign action as "blocked" would invent an enforcement event inside a chain whose purpose is not lying

Linked from `deploy/mcp/README.md`.

**Every factual claim in the guide is asserted against the source before commit** — status codes, the 100-event cap, endpoint paths, the `no_rule` verdict. A doc that drifts from the code is worse than no doc.

## Also: fuzz job timeout

`timeout-minutes: 15`. Last night a runner was reaped mid-queue after 45 minutes and reported as a red ❌ with no steps and no logs — indistinguishable from a real test failure. A cap makes infrastructure failure legible as infrastructure failure.

author: snow6060
body:
Phase 3 — Safety & Limits Hardening

Strengthens SQL validation and adds resource safeguards, after confirming
DuckDB's true read-only connection mode is incompatible with in-memory
databases, and that DuckDB has no reliable built-in query cancellation.

- engine.py:
  - Keyword-blocklist matching upgraded from substring to whole-word
    matching (regex word boundaries), preventing false positives on
    column/identifier names that merely contain a forbidden word as a
    substring (e.g. "updated_at")
  - String literal contents are now stripped before keyword scanning,
    preventing false positives on legitimate search terms inside quotes
    (e.g. a query searching for '%update%' in data no longer gets
    blocked as if "UPDATE" were a SQL command)
  - New validate_query() method: checks SELECT-only, forbidden keywords,
    and now also validates syntax via EXPLAIN before execution, catching
    malformed SQL early
  - Query results are now capped at 1000 rows via fetchmany(), with the
    response indicating whether truncation occurred, rather than
    silently returning a partial picture
  - DuckDB connection now sets memory_limit='2GB' as a safeguard against
    a runaway query exhausting available RAM
- main.py:
  - /query now runs queries in a background thread with a best-effort
    15-second timeout — if exceeded, the client gets a clear error
    rather than hanging indefinitely. Documented clearly as best-effort:
    DuckDB does not guarantee the underlying query actually stops
    running, only that the gateway stops waiting on it
  - Table name collisions during startup are now caught and reported
    with a clean, readable error message and a deliberate exit, instead
    of crashing with a raw traceback (resolves a known issue documented
    since Phase 1.5)

Verified before implementation (see commit history for the research):
- DuckDB's access_mode='READ_ONLY' is fundamentally incompatible with
  :memory: databases, confirmed via DuckDB's own documentation and an
  open feature request — this ruled out true read-only mode as an
  option and shaped the keyword-hardening approach instead
- DuckDB has no reliable way to cancel an in-progress query from Python,
  confirmed via multiple open DuckDB GitHub issues — this shaped the
  "best-effort, not guaranteed" framing of the response timeout

Tested manually:
- Normal queries return the new {rows, truncated, row_limit} shape
- A query with no LIMIT against the full 560K-row dataset correctly
  truncates to exactly 1000 rows with truncated: true
- A legitimate search query containing the word "update" inside a
  string literal (WHERE Name LIKE '%update%') now succeeds, where it
  would have previously false-positived as a forbidden keyword
- A genuine DROP TABLE attempt is still correctly blocked
- Duplicate table names on startup now produce a clean error message

Known limitations (intentional, documented in docs/notes.md):
- String literal stripping does not handle SQL's doubled-quote escape
  convention ('it''s') — a rare edge case, accepted for now
- The query timeout is best-effort only; a genuinely stuck query may
  continue consuming resources in the background even after the client
  receives a timeout error

author: josue-commits
body:
The "Made with Dapta Forms" badge on every public form opened **app.dapta.ai** — a login screen. It should open the product's landing page.

## Why it lives here and not in the deploy pipeline

The destination came from `NEXT_PUBLIC_SIGNUP_URL`, which the release pipeline passes as an explicit `--build-arg`, so no default in this repo could win. But the pipeline passes exactly six build args, and **any `ARG` it does not pass keeps its Dockerfile default** — so a separate variable puts this back in the repo that owns the button, shipping through the normal release flow.

## The two questions were one variable

That is why the destination could not move without the deployment moving with it. They are now separate:

| | decides | unset |
|---|---|---|
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_SIGNUP_URL` | **whether** the badge/CTA render (open-core opt-in) | nothing renders — unchanged |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_LANDING_URL` | **where** they point | falls back to the signup URL |

A landing URL alone turns nothing on, which is the case that guards the open-core contract and has its own test: a bare fork still carries no upstream branding and no dead link, and a self-hoster who configured only a signup URL sees no change whatsoever.

Unlike the other brand vars this one ships a real Dockerfile default (`https://www.daptaforms.ai`), because it is a fact about the **product** rather than about a deployment: the badge names Dapta Forms, so the page it opens is Dapta Forms' own. `publish-gate` passes — the landing is a different domain from the `*.dapta.ai` hosts the scan blocks.

## The `www.` is load-bearing

The apex 301s to www **and drops the query string**. Measured:

```
https://daptaforms.ai/?utm_source=dapta-forms&…   → https://www.daptaforms.ai/           (all tags gone)
https://www.daptaforms.ai?utm_source=dapta-forms&… → …/?utm_source=…&utm_content=mkxus7  (0 redirects, intact)
```

The loop appends `utm_source=dapta-forms`, `utm_medium=badge|confirmation`, `utm_campaign=made-with-dapta` and `utm_content=<accountCode>`. The landing reads those on load and forwards them to its signup CTA, but falls back to `utm_source=landing` when it sees none — so with the apex, every badge-driven signup would have credited the landing for its own traffic, silently.

## Verification

- `growthTarget` is pure and tested in `@quill/shared` — 8 tests covering preference, fallback, the fork gate, and non-http values on either side
- The three deployments that actually exist, asserted end to end: Dapta's image → `www.daptaforms.ai?utm_…`; bare fork → `null`; signup-only self-hoster → byte-identical to today
- `pnpm typecheck` 16/16 · `pnpm test` 16/16 · `pnpm lint` 16/16 · publish-gate PASSED
- Changeset included (`@quill/shared` minor)

Both stages of the Dockerfile declare it — `build` for the client-bundle inlining, `run` because server components read `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` from the runtime env.

author: vitali87
body:
Fixes #30.

The issue's discipline held: two theories were already refuted, so this starts from what the failing assert actually CLAIMS. `assert!(!is_alive(&socket))` after dropping the listener is a proxy — it asserts that no process anywhere holds a listening fd for the path, which is a much stronger property than "ensure_relay and relay_serve did not steal the socket".

## The mechanism the proxy is vulnerable to

On macOS, `bind` cannot set `CLOEXEC` atomically (no `SOCK_CLOEXEC`); Rust's std sets it with a separate `ioctl` after `socket()`. A concurrent test thread's fork/spawn in that window — the parallel suite spawns shells, servers and PTYs constantly — inherits a duplicate of the listening fd. Dropping the test's listener then closes only one of two handles: the socket stays connectable, `is_alive` returns true, and the test fails with no steal having occurred. This fits every observation: connect succeeding on a "closed" socket, load dependence, isolation-cleanliness, and both sightings being on the Mac (Linux's atomic `SOCK_CLOEXEC` has no window — this box cannot reproduce it). Stated as the consistent explanation, not a proven capture; the fix below is immune either way, so the next occurrence — if any — would fail loudly with the routing message instead of the ambiguous liveness one.

## Fix

- **The test now asserts the invariant directly** (v0.1.699): after both calls short-circuit, it drains the probe connections they queued, makes one fresh connect, and requires `accept()` on the ORIGINAL listener to yield it — proof the path still routes here. An inherited fd duplicate shares this listener's queue (immune); a thief that rebound the path swallows the fresh connect and the accept comes up dry. Verified red with a simulated thief (staging + rename, `bind_socket_0600`'s exact shape): "the fresh connect never reached this listener". The `!is_alive`-after-drop proxy assert is gone.
- **The issue's hardening candidate ships too**: `session::is_alive` now distinguishes "nothing is listening" from "the probe could not run" — `EMFILE`/`ENFILE`/`EAGAIN`/`ENOMEM` report alive (the conservative side: worst case a caller attaches and gets a clean connect error) instead of sending `ensure_relay`/`attach_or_create` down the spawn path against a live server.

Full suite green (3056 + 6, 0 failed); the reworked test 5/5 solo; clippy zero warnings; fmt clean. Release notes replaced for 0.1.699.

author: funnan-dev
body:
The radar already refused to detect anything behind the duel arena's pillars, but the cone was still drawn straight through them. It now carves shadows the way a point light would, so the drawn volume matches what the sensor can actually see.

## How

A new `awen.shapes` primitive, `ShapeSectorOccluded`, sweeps rays across the wedge and stops each one at the first occluding disc — `min(reach, s - sqrt(r² - h²))`, the polar restatement of the closest-point rule `Geo.lineOfSight` already shares between the sensor, seeker and trigger gates. The boundary feeds one persistent `PathPolyline` from a readonly binding, matching how every other primitive in the module computes its geometry.

Exact tangent bearings (`β ± asin(r/d)`, doubled a twentieth of a degree apart) and each disc's centre bearing are inserted alongside the uniform rays, so shadow edges stay radial and bites bottom out exactly on the near face without paying for a dense sweep. Occluders arrive as plain `{x, y, r}` rows in source units with a `positionScale`, keeping the framework module free of briarthorn's `Obstacle` type.

`ViewSituation` draws it in world bearings under the same rotation `ViewObstacles` carries, so every bite lands on its own drawn disc, and dims the pre-existing cone to a faint underlay — the scope now separates where the antenna points from what it can see.

## Notes

- The cone fill is ~10% alpha with the range rings showing through it, so shadows have to be real holes in the geometry; painting over them in the background colour would erase the rings.
- The shadow set is held to the pillars the terrain layer actually draws. The cull predicate lives once in `ViewObstacles.draws()` and is called by both, because the minimap's whole-fit cull hides pillars that are substantially inside the picture — casting from those produced a large bite with no visible cause.
- The polyline binding early-returns while the item is hidden. Bindings evaluate on invisible items, and three `ViewSituation` instances are alive at once.

## Verification

- 121/121 tests pass; `clang-format-check` and `qmllint-check` are clean.
- The ten new tests were mutation-tested: dropping the apex offset, flipping the pixel conversion, removing the wrap-around window, deleting either tangent pad, and collapsing the ray pitch are each caught. The first draft of the suite passed against all six of those.
- Checked in the running duel on both the attack scope and the minimap.

author: jasperfrontend
body:
Two commits. The first replaces three bespoke tag substituters with the pipeline the live overlay already uses; the second puts control values into the bag it receives. ## 1. Previews render through the shared pipeline Three preview surfaces each carried a copy of the same twelve lines: loop the sample data, build a literal regex per key by string interpolation, replace. ```js const pattern = new RegExp(`\[\[\[${tag}]]]`, 'g'); ``` `resources/dsl/dsl.json` forbids hand-rolled tag regexes in its opening comment, and this is why: that pattern only matches a bare `[[[tag]]]`, so `[[[followers_total|number]]]` never matched its own sample value even though the value was in the same object. What happened next depended on which preview you opened. The Builder canvas and the composed-overlay preview followed up with a catch-all `replace(/\[\[\[[^\]]*]]]/g, '')` that deleted the tag; the overlay create page did not, so the same tag stayed on screen raw. One bug, two symptoms. The comment claiming they used the "same preview approach" was close enough to stop anyone checking. That catch-all also ate the block syntax, which is what made control-heavy blocks look broken rather than merely empty: - `[[[if:...]]]BIG[[[else]]]small[[[endif]]]` rendered `BIGsmall` - a `foreach` rendered its body exactly once with the loop markers gone All three now call `renderTemplateSource()`, which runs `processTemplate` then `replaceTagsWithFormatting` - the same two passes in the same order as `OverlayRenderer.parseSource()`. Removing the strip is not a regression: `replaceTagsWithFormatting` already resolves an absent value to `''`, so unmatched tags still vanish. They now pass through `?? default` on the way. Locale reaches previews for the first time, from `auth.user.locale`, so `currency` / `date` / `number` format rather than not formatting at all. ## 2. Control tags resolve `getSampleTemplateData()` returns 53 keys and every one is a static Twitch tag. Not one `c:` key, ever, so no control had ever resolved in any preview on any surface. `[[[followers_total]]]` worked and `[[[c:myname]]]` did not. The values were already client-side - the edit route ships `userScopedControls` and the template's own controls for the controls manager, and the Builder holds `BuilderControlDef`s for blocks placed this session. None of it reached the preview. No new endpoint or query; `controlsToPreviewData()` turns either shape into the `c:` half of the bag. Key derivation mirrors `OverlayTemplateController`'s render query, because a preview resolving a *different* key set than the overlay is worse than one resolving none: source-managed controls use the namespaced broadcast key, everything else `c:` + key, each with its `_at` companion in Unix seconds. Membership matches too. Smaller calls: - **Timers are computed, not read** - their stored `value` is not the number on screen. That logic moved out of `ExpressionBuilder.vue` rather than being copied. - **Random-mode numbers return their stored value** instead of rerolling, so the canvas does not change on every keystroke. - **Builder definitions have no timestamps**, so their `_at` stays absent rather than being faked to `now()`. - **`useHelpReference.ts` keeps its own tag regex on purpose** - it wraps literal tags in clickable `` for the help pages. ## Verification No JS test runner exists in this repo and none was added. The real modules were bundled with esbuild and run in node. Pipeline behaviour: ``` pipe formatter | "1,234" bare unmatched tag | "" ?? default on absent | "nothing yet" conditional true branch | "BIG" conditional false branch | "small" currency pipe | "€12.50" foreach over array | "
  • ana
  • bo
    • " html encoding | "<script>alert(1)</script>" css encode:false | ".a > .b { width: 40px }" ``` Against real local data (template 232), before and after control injection: ``` BEFORE "Hello Jasper" present : false first : AFTER "Hello Jasper" present : true first : ``` ## Not covered `head` is still unparsed in all three previews, exactly as before. Tags in `head` render literally. Pre-existing, and outside "replace the stripper". Iterables (`[[[foreach:subscribers as sub]]]`) still render empty - nothing supplies a `subscribers` array. That needs invented data rather than real data, which is a separate piece of work. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: sarajo
body:
Implements Phase 1 of the Circe spec: the wizard runs end to end, a tile spawns and streams a real conversation over ACP, and the permission gate works. 24 commits.

Per §1.3 and §12.3 this is the human review gate. **Phase 2 does not start until this is reviewed.**

## What's here

- **Hermes integration** — binary location with a minimum-version check, profile enumeration and the §5.4 realness rule, non-interactive profile creation, and the device-code provider login.
- **Transport** — one `hermes -p <profile> acp` subprocess per tile, ACP JSON-RPC over stdio.
- **Permission gate** — three states, cycling, per-profile persistence, and mid-response liveness.
- **Wizard** — Screens 1–7, including the zero-tile guard.
- **Tile** — window, transcript, composer, gate button, per-profile theming.
- **State** — atomic persistence of bounds, tabs, transcripts, gate mode.
- **Docs** — twelve ADRs, eight compat notes, README, MIT license.

## Verification

Run on this branch:

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `npm run typecheck` | clean |
| `npm test` | 180/180 |
| `npm run build` | ok |
| `npm run test:e2e` | 8/8 in 14.1s |
| §10.1 wizard happy path | 1.4s (budget 90s) |
| §10.3 render lag | 1001 chunks, p95 1.3ms (budget 300ms) |

## Notable fix in this branch

The E2E suite previously took 4.2 minutes and failed one test, with an intermittent `SIGSEGV` on quit. Root cause: `before-quit` started asynchronous teardown and let Electron proceed, so the state file's write continuations were scheduled to resume on a V8 isolate already being disposed. `installQuitHandler` now holds the quit open until teardown is durable. See `docs/adr/0012-async-teardown-on-quit.md`.

## Still outstanding — for the reviewer

- **Task 19 Step 1** — the clean-tree run (`rm -rf node_modules out && npm ci && …`) has not been done. Results above are from an incremental tree.
- **Task 19 Step 3** — the manual runbook against a real Hermes install with a real provider needs a human. CI only exercises the mock.
- **ADR count is twelve, not the eleven the plan lists.** All eleven planned entries are present; 0012 was added for the teardown fix.
- **`npm audit` reports 7 vulnerabilities** in the resolved dependency tree, pre-existing from the initial install and never triaged.
- **Real-Hermes `stderr` shape is unverified** for the non-zero exits of `hermes profile create`; `create.ts` forwards it verbatim into user-facing copy. Deliberately not probed — see compat notes §5.
- **The §5.5 coding-profile inference has no true positive** on real data. All eight profiles on the dev machine infer false, so true-positive behaviour rests on fixtures alone.

author: jimmy058910
body:
A developer trap found while working #718 chunk D, routed to `.claude/rules/` per the repo's own convention (a trap that only bites developers goes in the matching rules file, so it auto-loads when Claude touches those paths).

## The trap

`sha256sum -c` resolves the path written **inside** the checksums line and opens it from the working directory. It does not verify whatever you piped in. So renaming a download breaks verification permanently:

```
# WRONG - the checksums line names the original asset
curl -fsSL "$URL/actionlint_1.7.12_linux_amd64.tar.gz" -o actionlint.tar.gz
grep " actionlint_1.7.12_linux_amd64.tar.gz$" checksums.txt | sha256sum -c -
  -> sha256sum: actionlint_1.7.12_linux_amd64.tar.gz: No such file or directory
     FAILED open or read
```

The error reads like a corrupt download rather than a naming mistake, which is what makes it worth writing down.

## Why it belongs next to the existing convention

The Download Hardening Convention already covers `-f`, `--retry*`, and the `gzip -t` / `xz -t` / `unzip -t` integrity checks. Checksum verification is the same step one layer up, and this is the way it silently never runs.

## Provenance

I wrote this exact bug into the #749 actionlint recipe, and **executing it** is what caught it — reading it looked fine. It fails loudly rather than silently, but it fails on *every* invocation, which means any recipe carrying it has provably never been run. That is the generalisable half, and the entry says so: run any download recipe you write.

Measured after the fix: 2353908 bytes downloaded, checksum `OK`, `gzip -t` OK, extracted binary a valid 64-bit x86-64 ELF.

## Checks

Docs-only, single file, no runtime behaviour — CI is sufficient. `pre-commit` passes (`markdownlint-cli2`, `doc-links`, `mixed line ending`).

author: ms-bc
body:
## Regression guard: Person intake must never mint MJ Users

5.33.0 removed the auto-provisioning that made every job applicant an authenticated user with the `UI` role (#36, fixed in #39, shipped 2026-08-07). **Nothing currently stops it coming back.**

The fix deleted the `Save()`/`Delete()` lifecycle hooks outright rather than adding an opt-out, so there is no behavior left to unit-test — the protection *is* the absence. This PR makes that absence load-bearing.

### The guard

One file, `packages/CoreEntitiesServer/src/__tests__/PersonEntityServer.guard.test.ts`, two deliberate layers:

- **Prototype check** — `Save`/`Delete` are not own-properties of `PersonEntityServer.prototype`. Catches the exact shape the defect had. Own-property descriptors, not `in`/truthiness: both methods must keep working via the inherited `BaseEntity` chain; what must never return is *this class* overriding them.
- **Source scan** — no `MJ: Users`, `MJ: User Roles`, `MJUserEntity`, `MJUserRoleEntity`, `'UI'`, or `LinkedUserID` in executable code. Catches provisioning reintroduced inside a *helper*, which an override-shaped check alone would miss.

Comments are stripped before scanning: the class doc-comment quotes the removed behavior verbatim ("created (or linked) an active `MJ: Users` record") and that history is worth keeping, but it would otherwise trip every pattern.

Two tests guard the guard — that `Save`/`Delete` genuinely still exist to be overridden, and that the scanned file is really there — so a rename or a moved file can't make this pass vacuously.

### Verified in both directions

Green against current `next` proves little on its own. I restored the pre-fix 283-line `PersonEntityServer` from `main@4cb37d8` and confirmed the guard **fails 8 of 10** — both prototype assertions and all six source patterns — then restored the fixed version and confirmed 10/10 green. A guard only ever exercised against fixed code is decoration.

### Packaging

This package declares its own `vitest` devDependency and `"test": "vitest run"`, so the guard runs standalone via `npm test -w @mj-biz-apps/common-core-entities-server` — it does not depend on the repo-wide test wiring PR, so neither blocks the other.

Also excluded `src/**/__tests__/**` from the tsconfig: `include: ["src/**/*"]` plus `files: ["/dist"]` would have compiled the test into `dist/` and **published it to npm**. Verified `dist` is clean.

No changeset: no runtime or published-API change.

### What this does NOT close

Worth stating plainly, because 5.33.0 shipping can read as "handled":

**Hosts that ran Person intake on 5.32.0 or earlier still hold minted applicant accounts.** Those are live MJ Users, `IsActive = 1`, carrying the `UI` read role. The release stopped new minting; it neither audits nor revokes what already exists, and nothing in this repo does either. Any affected host should audit `__mj.User` for `UI`-holding accounts corresponding to people who should never sign in. That remediation is unowned and is not addressed by this PR.

author: rc4l
body:
## An offline catalogue of experiences

Hosting made you assemble a server by hand. This ships a catalogue of ready-made **experiences** in the
release, picked from the HOST tab and started in one press.

An experience is a folder: `addon.json` says what it is and which files it needs, `server.cfg` says how
to run it. Two ship to start with, Duel 40 and Skulltag. The split matters because the same mappack can
sit under different rules, and a preset per combination does not scale.

- A restricted JSON reader, so a catalogue entry cannot reach anything a config file should not
- IWAD substitution with the outcome stated: host on what the entry wants, or name what stood in for it
- A compatibility check for what may be loaded together, ahead of anything loading
- The HOST tab redrawn as a list of experiences and a detail column, settings behind a button

## The reachability check discarded the registry's reply

The INTERNET option stayed white however well a port was forwarded.

The request went out to `cl_fua_serverregistry_list`. The registry answered. `cl_main` then decided
"is this from the registry?" against `fua_serverregistry_host`, which is the **server's** announce
target and a different setting. Any local-registry test leaves the two disagreeing, and from then on
every reply from the real registry was dropped: no cookie, so the check timed out reporting that the
registry never answered, and the option went white, because a registry that says nothing is not
evidence about anyone's router.

Replies now come from any registry the browser actually queries, which is the whole resolved list
rather than one address, since that is where the queries go.

Two smaller pieces alongside it:

- `Failed` expires after five seconds instead of the full ten minute TTL. It is the absence of an
  answer, not an answer, and caching it meant one swallowed packet painted the option white for the
  rest of the sitting.
- `fua_portstatus` prints which leg the check reached. A white option covered four different failures
  and none of them said so.

## Verified

Against the live registry, with `fua_serverregistry_host` deliberately left on `127.0.0.1` so the
misconfiguration was still present: the probe reports `port 10666: reachable`, the registry echoes the
public address back, and INTERNET draws green.

In-engine hosting starts a server, auto-joins it with rcon, and reaches the registry's server list.
1568 tests pass.

author: jmchilton
body:
> **Posted by Claude (AI assistant) on behalf of @jmchilton — they did not write this text personally.**

Two follow-ups from reviewing #23275, offered as a PR against your branch rather than pushed to it. Both are annotations and comments — no behavior change, and the tests pass at the same counts as before.

The design holds up. I went hunting for cross-contamination in `metadata_out` and there isn't any — `_get_runtime_context` builds a fresh context per call, `data_fetch` allocates the dict per item, no mutable defaults anywhere. Hanging it on the runtime context rather than `FilesSourceOptions` is right, and not just conveniently so: `FilesSourceOptions` is a `StrictModel`, pydantic copies on construct, and it's semantically an input model. The byte-based cap is correctly framed, and `sanitize_drs_name()` survived ~50 hostile inputs beyond the ones in your tests — no separator leaks, no `.`/`..` leaks, no invalid UTF-8 from a mid-character byte cut. The red commit is a real red commit: 7 failed at `a63e101d71`, 29 passed at `568f058ad4`.

### 1. Type the metadata channel

`metadata_out: Optional[dict]` leaves both `metadata_out["name"]` and `source_metadata.get("name")` as `Any`, so a typo in the key type-checks fine on either side and silently degrades to the URI basename — the bug this PR exists to fix, reintroduced as a silent one. `lib/galaxy/files/sources/` already reaches for `TypedDict` for loose JSON-ish payloads (`invenio.py`, `dataverse.py`, `elabftw.py`), so `RealizedSourceMetadata` follows that rather than starting a second convention.

Worth being precise about how much this actually buys, since I checked with mypy rather than assuming. The write side gets a direct `TypedDict "RealizedSourceMetadata" has no key "nmae"`. The read side does **not** — `.get()` with a non-key returns `object`, and it only errors downstream when that `object` reaches `_has_src_to_path`'s `tuple[str, str, bool]` return annotation. Caught either way, but by a different mechanism than you'd expect.

Also carries the `FilesSourceRuntimeContext` class docstring (it's an output channel now, and the class-level line is what people skim) and two lines on `sanitize_drs_name()` saying why it isn't `galaxy.util.sanitize_for_filename` — that's the function the next reviewer will ask about, and the answer is worth writing down once: it maps everything outside `[A-Za-z0-9_.]` to `_`, so `ünïcödé.txt` becomes `________.txt`; it has no length bound; and on rejection it substitutes a random id where you need `None` to fall back to the URI basename.

### 2. `_has_src_to_name`'s comment

"Logic should broadly match logic of `_has_src_to_path`" stopped being true for `drs://`. The divergence is correct — resolving a DRS name needs the very fetch deferral exists to avoid — but the comment as written sends the next reader hunting a bug that isn't there.

### Not patched — flagging instead

- **The deferred divergence never heals.** `model/deferred.py:265` calls `stream_url_to_file()` with no `metadata_out`, so a deferred `drs://` keeps the UUID *permanently*, not just until materialization. I agree it's out of scope here, but `deferred.py:265` is where it'd be cheap later — probably worth an issue against `dev` rather than silence.
- **The `handle_upload` bound is correct by accident of dead code.** `os.path.splitext(name)[1]` appears twice in `upload_util.py`; you mention the unsniffable-binary one. The other feeds `uploaded_file_ext`, which is harmless only because `handle_uploaded_dataset_file_internal()` accepts it and never reads it. Worth a sentence so whoever eventually wires it up doesn't silently widen a remote server's say over datatype selection. `is_extension_unsniffable_binary()` does hold up otherwise — it requires a `Binary` subclass *without* a sniffer, so `bam` isn't in the reachable set, and the parity argument with plain `https://` uploads is real.
- **Pre-existing, adjacent, not yours:** `_get_runtime_context()` — the function this PR extends — does `self.template_config = self.template_config.model_copy(update=extra_props)` from a per-call path, mutating the shared long-lived file source instance, so `opts.extra_props` from one fetch persists into every later fetch through that source. `metadata_out` deliberately avoids exactly this bug class, which is why I found no contamination. Deserves its own issue against `dev`.
- `url.split("/")[-1]` is now three copies in `data_fetch.py` (`:526`, `:557`, `:589`). A `_name_from_url()` helper would cover all three, but I didn't want to widen the diff on a release branch.

### Testing

`test/unit/files/test_drs.py` and `test/unit/app/tools/test_data_fetch.py`: 64 passed, identical to before these commits. black / ruff / flake8 clean via pre-commit; isort run separately, since it isn't a pre-commit hook here.

The two commits are kept separate so you can drop either one.

body:
## Summary

- Collections created from scratch are now stored as one `jolt.yaml` holding every request and folder, instead of a real directory tree of per-request `.yaml` files — so organizing them can never collide with the filesystem the way real folders/files could.
- Collections that already exist in today's folder-per-directory format are read, edited, and saved exactly as before — no conversion, no migration path (deliberate, see spec's Change log / D-019).
- Renaming a request or a folder is possible for the first time, but **only on the new single-file format** — an old-format collection shows a clear "not available" error on `ctrl+r` instead of silently doing nothing or attempting a risky real file/directory rename.
- The move-request prompt (`ctrl+g`) now suggests existing folder names as you type, via `bubbles/textinput` (tab to accept) — applies to a move on either collection format.
- Environments are untouched: still separate files, still `*.local.yaml` for secrets.

Full spec: `specs/0014-single-file-collections.md`. Spec `0013` (an earlier, narrower draft — rename + move autocomplete only, assuming real on-disk folders) is archived in the same PR, superseded by this one.

author: akshaykumarjangra
body:
💡 What: Replaced an N+1 query vulnerability in `GET /threads` (fetching latest messages in a loop using `Promise.all(threads.map())`) with a single batched query using Drizzle's `inArray` and `.selectDistinctOn()`. Added explanatory comments in the code.

🎯 Why: The original implementation caused one extra database query for every chat thread fetched. As the number of threads grows, this could lead to significant latency and database load.

📊 Impact: Reduces database queries for the `GET /threads` endpoint from N+1 to exactly 2 queries, significantly improving endpoint response times and lowering database overhead, regardless of the number of threads fetched.

🔬 Measurement: Verify the fix by running the native node test suite `npx tsx --test $(find . -name "*.spec.ts")` to ensure there are no syntax or type errors in the modified route. Review `server/chat-routes.ts` visually to confirm the `Promise.all` loop is replaced and explanatory comments are present.

author: condensed69
body:
## Bug
Clicking "Franchise offer" threw `Uncaught ReferenceError: g is not defined` at `game.js` render, and kept throwing on every subsequent render (the tick loop re-renders continuously) — so the app appeared to freeze/do nothing.

Root cause: the prestige modal template referenced the raw game-state `g` directly (`g.regulars`, `g.night`) instead of the view-model `v` that `render()` actually has in scope. Confirmed live via browser console (screenshot from user) and traced with `git log -S` to the original prestige-system commit — **predates the perk tree PR**, unrelated to #28.

Because the Perks tab only renders once `g.prestiges > 0`, this bug has silently blocked anyone who's never prestiged from ever seeing the Managers/Special Shifts/Perk Tree content that's already shipped on `main`.

## Fix
`renderVals()` now computes `prestigeRegulars`/`prestigeNight` (where `g` is actually in scope) and the modal template reads them off `v`, same pattern as every other field.

- `node --check game.js` — pass
- `node economy.test.mjs` — 149/149 pass

Reported from a real run (`20260807-164651`): the page said **"Failed."** and offered **"Save the results"** for a run that had completed fine and whose results were already published. Both were this page believing the runner's shorthand rather than reading what it meant. Pairs with [campfire-stress#7](https://github.com/deepwa7er/campfire-stress/pull/7).

## "Failed" → "finished · thresholds crossed"

k6 ends a run non-zero when its thresholds were crossed. The run completed, every number on the page above is good, and at 500 VUs against `stock` it is the finding being looked for. The page now says so and explains it:

> The run completed and every number above is good. k6 ended it reporting that thresholds were crossed, which means the server was slower than the limits the harness asks for — a finding about the server, not a fault in the run.

A run that genuinely broke still says so in red, and says its results are likely partial.

## The stale button

Worse, because it contradicted something true. The frame stops polling once a run is no longer `running` — but publishing starts a few seconds later, since the final chart payload is computed from k6's whole output first. The frame froze on the moment before and offered to save results already on their way.

It now keeps watching through the runner's new `pending` state and settles on **Open the full report**. Verified against the live runner:

```
16:56:15  poll=true   running
16:57:28  poll=true   succeeded · Saving the results…     ← used to freeze here
16:57:59  poll=false  succeeded · Open the full report
```

"Save the results" is kept for the case it was written for: a run nothing will publish on its own, which is a stopped one.

Five new tests covering each state. Full suite green (84 runs, 281 assertions), rubocop clean.

author: val-grasley
body:
Closes the pin debt from the 2026-08-07/08 typechecker-arc session. **Two self-draining must-fail pins, three explicit not-pinnable declarations.** `test/` only — no compiler source.

`sh test/must_fail_census.sh --all` listed all five as candidates; none appear after this.

## Pinned

**`1397-xmod-samename-type-impl-symbol-collapse/`** — #1397, **S0 silent wrongness**. Two modules each declaring their own `Thing` with their own `impl Label Thing` collapse into ONE emitted symbol. Verb `run`, `exit: 0`, `stdout: aamod|aamod` — where **`aamod|zzmod` is correct**, hand-derived from source before anything was run. The IR mechanism was re-confirmed on the pinning binary: `grep -c 'define .*@mdk_impl_Thing_label'` returns **1** where it must be 2. Control (`zzmod_distinct.mdk`, type renamed `Zeeb`) isolates the same-name collision as the single variable and prints the correct `aamod|zzmod`.

**`1396-priv-ctor-outranks-public-import-eval/`** — #1396, **S1**. A module's private, unexported constructor out-ranks a publicly imported one of the same spelling.

⚠️ **This pin is cut against the CURRENT shape, not the issue body's.** #1396 was filed against `main` before PR #1393 merged, when *both* engines were wrong and agreed. #1393 gated the mangler's ctor-export table on `dataVis = VisPublic`, which **fixes the native half**. Measured now: `check` 0 (`w : TQ` typechecks) · `run` **exit 1** `E-NONEXHAUSTIVE-MATCH` · built binary prints the correct **`7`**. So the surviving defect is eval-only, and the pin says so. The issue carries a comment recording that shift; pinning the body's shape would have pinned a state that no longer exists.

Verb `run`, `exit: 1`, **no `stdout:` claim** — deliberately. Stdout is empty on the broken path and the diagnostic goes to stderr, which this harness's `run` verb captures but never reads. Documented in `why-stdout`, modelled on `1343-priv-helper-name-collision-dict-panic`. Control (`mp_safe.mdk`, private colliding ctor dropped) prints `7`.

The `w : TQ` annotation is the discriminator throughout: it type-checks, proving typecheck resolved `Zz` to the public arity-1 constructor and that `7` is the correct answer.

## Declared not-pinnable

Appended to `test/MUST-FAIL-NOT-PINNABLE.txt` with reasons. All three are tooling/doc defects with **no program observable** a must-fail row can grade:

- **#1391** — `diff_compiler_dict_semantics.sh` reds for an unwired fixture but never for an *unfixtured spec clause*. No `main.mdk` expresses "this gate's coverage claim is inflated."
- **#1392** — `SHADOW-SEMANTICS.md` row 9c prose-records a fixed bug (#410) as an open KNOWN-BAD segfault. Pure doc staleness; the gate already grades that cell `ALL_EXACT`.
- **#1394** — 🚨 **self-referential.** `diff_compiler_must_fail.sh`'s own `build-run` classifier never reads the distinctive `126` it returns on build failure, so such a pin misgrades as `DRAINED` with an *"APPEARS FIXED — go close it"* banner. **The harness cannot pin a bug in itself** — a fixture would need the gate to grade its own verdict, which no verb supports. The entry also warns that any `DRAINED` `build-run` verdict elsewhere in this corpus should be hand-verified until #1394 is fixed.

## Gates

- `diff_compiler_must_fail.sh` — **71 fixtures, 71 reproduce, 0 DRAINED, 0 control-broke, 0 malformed.** Both new rows report `REPRO`.
- `must_fail_census.sh --all` — none of #1391/#1392/#1394/#1396/#1397 remain as candidates.
- `diff_compiler_snapshot_frontend.sh` — 198/198, confirming no collateral golden movement.
- Consumers of `must_fail_fixtures/` + `MUST-FAIL-NOT-PINNABLE.txt` enumerated word-bounded: the only programmatic executors are `diff_compiler_must_fail.sh` and `must_fail_census.sh`, both run above. Every other hit is a comment-only cross-reference.

## Note on capture discipline

Both pins record a **wrong** observable on purpose — that is what a must-fail row is. In both cases the correct answer was hand-derived from the source *first*, and the pin asserts the bug still reproduces so the gate flips red and names the issue the moment it is fixed. Neither is a captured golden.

Refs #1396, #1397, #1391, #1392, #1394 — none drained by this PR.

body:
Closes #4. Closes #5.

`Threefold.chi_eq` and `Fourfold.chi_eq`, the `n = 3` and `n = 4` specialisations of
`NumericalVariety.chi_eq_sum`, plus `CalabiYauThreefold.IsCalabiYau`.

## What this adds

| Declaration | Statement |
|---|---|
| `Threefold.chi_eq` | `χ(E) = r·∫td₃ + ∫c₁·td₂ + ∫ch₂·td₁ + ∫ch₃` |
| `CalabiYauThreefold.IsCalabiYau` | class: `td₁ = 0`, `∫td₃ = 0` |
| `CalabiYauThreefold.chi_eq` | `χ(E) = ∫c₁·td₂ + ∫ch₃` |
| `CalabiYauThreefold.chi_eq_of_chComp_eq` | on a CY3, `χ` does not see the rank |
| `Fourfold.chi_eq` | `χ(E) = r·∫td₄ + ∫c₁·td₃ + ∫ch₂·td₂ + ∫ch₃·td₁ + ∫ch₄` |

Both proofs are `Surface.chi_eq` verbatim with `Finset.sum_range_succ` fired one and two more
times. No lemma in `Numerical/RiemannRoch.lean` changed — that is the evidence
`degree_ch_mul_todd` is genuinely dimension-general rather than a surface theorem stated with
a variable in it.

## One correction to issue #4

The issue sketches the Calabi-Yau collapse as three terms, keeping `∫ch₂(E)·td₁`. It is two:
the class asserts `td₁ = 0`, which kills that term along with the rank term. The file states
two and says why in the module docstring.

## Not done, written up rather than stubbed

No threefold or fourfold **model**, so both `chi_eq` statements are conditional on the
instance existing — the state A6a was in before `Examples/K3Model`. Recorded in each module
docstring and in `ROADMAP.md`. The rank-one analogues are `ℚ[t]/(t⁴)` and `ℚ[t]/(t⁵)`,
reachable from `NumericalRing.ofGradedBasis`.

## Verification

Full build from scratch green, no warnings. `scripts/Audit.lean` covers the four new public
theorems; the audit prints only `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]` across all 43
declarations and never `sorryAx`. No `sorry` anywhere.

Independent of #6 / the `agent/a8-euler-pairing` branch; both are cut from `main` and can
merge in either order.

author: bobzhang
body:
## Summary

Milestone 7: the first backend. `PageModel` → deterministic, self-contained SVG.

- Per-code-unit `x` lists built from each run's own advances — the layout is baked into the coordinates, so a viewer with different fonts cannot shift it. Surrogate pairs share their lead's position.
- XML escaping, `font-weight`/`font-style`, solid fills, base64 data-URL images, explicit page background. Link regions skipped (non-visual; PDF backend's job).
- 3-decimal coordinate rounding keeps goldens byte-stable.

## On goldens — a correction to the design record, and a dropped dependency

The plan was to guard goldens with `Milky2018/svgdiff`, asserting `analysis_status == "complete"` so that "zero differences" would mean "equal". **Probing showed that is not achievable, and that svgdiff cannot guard this backend's output at all** (svgdiff 0.5.13):

- Any document with a `viewBox` or a `<text>` element reports `partial` (`renderer_viewport_raster_unproven`, `analysis_coverage_unproven`).
- Changing a `<text>` fill from `#000000` to `#ff0000` yields **zero** differences — font-dependent text semantics are outside its supported subset. It *does* detect shape changes (the page background rect).

Text is nearly everything this backend emits. Against that, svgdiff costs **five third-party packages** (svgdiff, mizchi/svg, mizchi/pixelmatch, Milky2018/xml, svgdiff-raster-codec) inside the dependency closure that office's fresh-agent release gate reviews and locks — which is what surfaced this: CI's "installed Office release smoke" job failed with *resolved dependency inventory does not match the tracked build lock*. Expanding a reviewed supply-chain closure is not a mechanical lock bump.

So the goldens are **exact reviewed snapshots**. The emitter is deterministic (fixed bundled metrics, fixed rounding), so they catch everything svgdiff would have, plus the text changes it cannot see. `goldens.mbt` records the measurement and the reasoning, so the trade can be revisited if svgdiff gains text coverage.

## Tests

8/8 (6 emitter + 2 goldens): deterministic render, XML escaping, bold/italic, rect/image data URIs, per-code-unit x count, multi-page; plus two reviewed goldens — a mixed Latin/CJK line (family mapping, per-char fallback, run splitting, CJK line-height raise) and a justified article page (heading keep-next, first-line indent, justification landing exactly on the 270pt measure).

body:
Slater called it before I could prove it. The teal band across the bottom of every screen was the `.bay` layer's own radial glow, centred at `50% 110%` so its brightest part sits exactly at the bottom edge.

**Worth recording why this took so long to see.** In a desktop browser the layer is invisible: `.bay` is fixed at `z-index: -2`, `body` carries an opaque background, and a body background box paints *after* negative z-index children, so the whole thing is covered. In WKWebView it renders. Every screenshot I took locally showed flat black while his phone showed the glow, which is why sampling my own render kept agreeing with me and disagreeing with reality.

Gone entirely: the three-gradient background, the drifting shimmer, the floating motes, both keyframes, the element, and the reduced-motion rule that referenced it. The app now paints one flat `--ink` from the header to the last pixel, verified by sampling the render down the centre column.

That also retires the last of this morning's insurance: the gap is handled by measuring the viewport, the slab that mismatched it is gone, and now the gradient that made a seam visible in the first place is gone too.

author: tugrulcan
body:
Closes #138

## What changed

**`src/hooks/useSrsProgress.ts`** (srs-engine scope, unchanged by this update): the SRS save effect already caught `localStorage.setItem` failures but only `console.error`'d, leaving the UI silently diverged from storage on QuotaExceededError / private-mode / full-storage. Added a visible destructive toast ("Progress not saved") on that catch path, alongside the existing console.error and keep-in-memory-state fallback. No storage shape change, no new version needed.

**`src/hooks/useSettings.ts`** (frontend-expert scope, this update): fixes the one code defect review flagged on this branch. `updateSettings` ran `console.error` + `toast()` *and* the `localStorage.setItem` write itself inside the `setSettings((prev) => ...)` updater. `useState` updaters must be pure — React re-invokes them during render (reproduced via `Home.tsx`'s eager-reducer render path as "Cannot update a component (`Toaster`) while rendering a different component", with duplicate-toast risk under StrictMode double-invoke).

Fix: moved the write and the toast into a `useEffect` keyed on `[settings, isLoading]` — the shape already used in `useSrsProgress.ts` — with `updateSettings` reduced to a pure `setSettings((prev) => ({ ...prev, ...newSettings }))`.

**First-load guard (avoiding #167's bug):** a persist effect keyed on `[settings, isLoading]` alone fires once on *every* mount, because the load effect's own `setSettings`/`setIsLoading` transition satisfies that dependency change — not just on a real `updateSettings` call. #167 (an earlier attempt at this same ticket) was closed for exactly that: it wrote `DEFAULT_SETTINGS` to storage for users who had never opened Settings, and showed a false "not saved" destructive toast on every app open (and every route change, since `useSettings` mounts in five places) in a permanently storage-less browser. This PR adds a `skipNextPersistRef` ref, initialized `true` and cleared on the first post-load effect run, so that one mount-triggered pass is skipped and only genuine `updateSettings` calls can persist or toast-fail.

**Copy mismatch fixed:** the toast's title read "Progress not saved" while its own description talked about "settings changes" being lost — title and description disagreed within the same toast. Retitled to "Settings not saved" so they agree, and stays distinct from `useSrsProgress.ts`'s "Progress not saved" toast for its own store.

**Known limitation (not fixed here, srs-engine's file):** `useSrsProgress.ts`'s persist effect has no dedupe on repeated write failures — every `srsStates` change while storage stays broken queues another destructive toast. In practice this is currently masked only by `TOAST_LIMIT=1` in `use-toast.ts` collapsing the visible stack to one, not by any actual dedupe logic; a sustained storage failure during an active practice session (recording an answer changes `srsStates` on every card) would otherwise re-toast on every card. Flagged for srs-engine as a follow-up, out of scope for this PR.

## Verification (commit `d5d04ba06fe09dcb193a8f6843c4a561c56d1069`, after merging `origin/main`)

`npm run lint` — 0 errors, 1 pre-existing warning in `AppErrorBoundary.tsx` (`react-refresh/only-export-components`), a file not touched by this PR.

`npm run typecheck` — clean, no output.

`npm run build` — succeeds, `dist/` emitted (route-level lazy chunks per main's #117 work).

`npm test` (vitest) — **281 passed, 0 failed**, 19 test files, including qa's `useSettings.test.ts` "quota exceeded on write (issue #138)" repro (asserts no toast before the write, then exactly one destructive toast titled `/not saved/i` after a throwing `setItem`, with the in-memory value still updated) and `useSrsProgress.test.ts`'s equivalent.

Merged `origin/main` first (much had landed since this branch was cut: repo-wide format, PWA/manifest work, dark mode, lazy routes, the `getDueItems` O(V²) perf fix, import-validation hardening in `useSrsProgress.ts`, etc.). One conflict, in `src/hooks/useSrsProgress.ts`: kept main's newer version (`getAllConjugatedVerbs`, `parseImportedProgress`/`isSrsState`) and reapplied only this branch's own already-committed 9-line delta on top — the toast import and the `toast()` call in the save effect's catch path. No other file needed manual reconciliation.

## Resumen

Publica el embudo comercial de automatización de AgentesVA y completa el cierre del diagnóstico con resultados accionables, captura de leads y seguimiento medible.

## Qué cambia

- Añade resultados deterministas por encaje, presupuesto, plazo y riesgo, con prioridad, complejidad, oportunidades y siguiente paso.
- Añade `/gracias-diagnostico/` con reserva configurable, alternativas por perfil y tracking consentido del funnel.
- Protege la reserva con resultados HMAC firmados y caducables; los enlaces directos o manipulados caen a revisión manual.
- Conserva una clave de idempotencia durante reintentos y bloquea reinicios concurrentes para reducir leads duplicados.
- Corrige el foco y el offset de la cabecera fija en escritorio y móvil.
- Actualiza arquitectura, operación, analítica, pruebas y release notes para `v0.5.0.0`.

author: chris-dare-dev
body:
Closes #6.

The dual involution and the Euler pairing `χ(E,F) = ∫_X ch(E)^∨·ch(F)·td(X)` — the bilinear
form Bridgeland stability conditions are actually defined against.

## What this adds

`CohLean/Numerical/Dual.lean` — `NumericalRingWithDual`, the `(-1)ⁱ` involution, as a
**mixin** over `NumericalRing`. Not a field of it (that would break every instance in
`Numerical/Examples/`) and not an `extends` (that would give two paths to `NumericalRing n A`
whenever a `NumericalVariety` is also in scope, and instance search would see a diamond).

`CohLean/Numerical/EulerPairing.lean`:

| Declaration | Statement |
|---|---|
| `chi₂` | `χ(E,F) = ∫ ch(E)^∨·ch(F)·td(X)` |
| `chi₂_eq_sum` | the expansion in any `n`, one term per `(i,j)` with `i + j ≤ n` |
| `Surface.chi₂_eq` | the `n = 2` specialisation |
| `Surface.chi₂_eq_chi_of_isStructureSheafLike` | pairing against a rank-one class with vanishing higher `chᵢ` returns the existing `chi` |
| `K3.chi₂_eq_neg_mukaiPairing` | `χ(E,F) = −⟨v(E), v(F)⟩` — the check the issue named |

`chi₂` needs **no** dual instance. `chDual` is the explicit alternating sum, which the grading
alone supplies, so the pairing and all of its consequences are available on any
`NumericalVariety`. The involution is used in exactly one lemma, `chi₂_eq_degree_dual_ch`,
which is what earns `chDual` its name.

## The symmetry claim in the issue is false

Issue #6 asks for `chi₂ E F = chi₂ F E` in even dimension. It does not hold, and it is not a
convention problem. `Surface.chi₂_sub_chi₂_swap` measures the obstruction exactly:

`χ(E,F) − χ(F,E) = 2·(r_E·∫c₁(F)·td₁ − r_F·∫c₁(E)·td₁)`

`ℙ²` is already in this repo and has `td₁ = (3/2)H ≠ 0`, so the failure is exhibited rather
than hypothetical. Symmetry holds exactly when `td₁ = 0`, proved as
`Surface.chi₂_symm_of_toddComp_one_eq_zero`, hence on every K3 and Calabi-Yau. The general
`χ(E,F) = (-1)ⁿ χ(F,E)` is Serre duality — a B5 theorem about `Ext`, not an identity between
these integrals — so it is not asserted at Layer A.

## Not done, written up rather than stubbed

`NumericalRingWithDual` has no instance yet, so `chi₂_eq_degree_dual_ch` alone is conditional.
Nothing else depends on it, and the `(-1)ⁱ` sign convention is pinned independently by
`K3.chi₂_eq_neg_mukaiPairing`. The cheapest instance is `Examples/RankOneSurface`: `H ↦ −H`
extends to `ℚ[t]/(t³)` because `(−H)³ = 0`.

`chi₂` is also not packaged as a `BilinForm` and the radical is not constructed — that belongs
to the numerical-lattice issue, which has to fix a `ℤ`- or `ℚ`-structure on `N` first.

## Verification

Full build from scratch green, no warnings. `scripts/Audit.lean` covers the fourteen new
public declarations; the audit prints only `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]` across
all 53 declarations and never `sorryAx`. No `sorry` anywhere.

Independent of #4 / #5 and the `agent/a7-threefold-fourfold` branch; both are cut from `main`
and can merge in either order.
