Builds the participant and admin UI on top of the auction backend. > **Stacked on #14.** Base is `claude/auction-purse-backend-45wpdb`, so this diff shows only the frontend work. Merge #14 first, then retarget this to `main`. ## Two backend additions the UI needed - Contest responses now carry `effective_max_players_per_team` — the per-contest override with the global fallback already applied — so the client never has to combine the two sources and drift from the server's rule. - `GET /api/players?contest_id=…` narrows to auctioned players (`price > 0`, Active) when the contest is an auction, keeping unsold players out of the pool at the source rather than filtering client-side. ## Team builder `useTeamBuilder` resolves the contest before loading players and branches on format. Auction contests fetch one open pool instead of per-slot requests, size the squad from `contest.squad_size` rather than slot totals, and track spend, remaining purse and per-real-team counts. The rule check is a pure function of a given selection, so the state updater validates against its own `prev` — reading render state there would let two batched clicks slip a player past the budget. The UI gains: - a purse bar with spend progress and per-team counters - team and value/points filters over the pool - cards showing what each player sold for, greying out anyone unaffordable or from a team already at its cap Per-team counts are rendered outright rather than hidden behind a tooltip, which would not reach touch users on a UI this mobile-first. Player value is formatted per contest format — rupees for slot-based, points for auction — so auction figures do not read as rupees in the contests that still treat `price` as a price tag. ## Admin The contest form gains squad format, purse, squad size and per-team cap inputs, shown only for auction contests. ## Two bugs found along the way - **`compactShowPrice` was declared but never implemented.** The builder uses compact cards, so auction users would have picked without seeing a single price. body:
runner-guard's RGS-012 rule (secret exfiltration via outbound HTTP) flagged the compiler-generated "Install gVisor (runsc)" step across 59 workflow files. The step downloads a pinned gVisor release from `storage.googleapis.com` and verifies it via SHA-512 before install — no secrets ever leave the runner — so this is a false positive that will keep re-triggering on every new/changed workflow that enables the sandbox.

## Suppress at the source
- Added `# runner-guard:ignore RGS-012` comments above the curl download lines in `generateGVisorInstallStep` (`pkg/workflow/copilot_engine_installation.go`), documenting the pinned-version + SHA-512-verified rationale.
- Regenerated all workflows so the suppression propagates to every affected `.lock.yml`.

## Defense-in-depth in gh-aw's own runner-guard integration
- Added `filterGvisorInstallFindings` (`pkg/cli/runner_guard_gvisor_exfiltration.go`), following the same pattern as the existing RGS-004 activation-gate filter.
- Given a finding's file/line, it walks backward to the nearest step boundary and only drops the finding if that step is genuinely the gVisor install step — so real RGS-012 findings elsewhere in the same file are still reported.
- Wired into `parseAndDisplayRunnerGuardOutput`, applied whenever `gh-aw compile --runner-guard` runs (including the daily static-analysis-report workflow).

```go
// pkg/cli/runner_guard.go
output.Findings = filterRunnerGuardFindings(output.Findings, gitRoot)
output.Findings = filterGvisorInstallFindings(output.Findings, gitRoot)
```

author: ank-khoaho
body:
Closes backlog **A3**. Reading was covered by `SheetNames`/`ReadSheet`; this closes writing.

Built with a design doc, an implementation plan, and a fresh subagent per task with a spec-and-quality review gate after each, then a whole-branch review.

## What's new

```csharp
byte[] workbook = WorkbookEditor.Create(new[]
{
    XlsxSheet.Named("Sales",   new[] { new object?[] { "Region", "Total" },
                                       new object?[] { "EMEA", 1200 } }),
    XlsxSheet.Named("Summary", new[] { new object?[] { "Grand total",
                                       XlsxFormula.From("SUM(Sales!B2:B2)") } }),
});

workbook = WorkbookEditor.AppendRows(workbook, "Sales", newRows);
```

Six methods and two types: `Create(IEnumerable<XlsxSheet>)` and `AppendRows`, each with `Stream` and file-path forms, plus `XlsxSheet` — completing the `DocxBlock`/`PptxSlide` trio — and `XlsxFormula`.

**Formulas needed no method of their own.** `XlsxFormula` is a *cell value*, dispatched in the one shared `SetCellValue` helper, so `Create`, `AppendRows` and the existing `SetCell` all gain it from a single line and cannot disagree about it. A `SetFormula` trio was in the approved design and **cut on review** — three public members that would have done what `SetCell` already does. That matters here: this package stays below 1.0.0 permanently, so semver never starts protecting consumers, and every member is pinned in an approved-API file forever.

## The limit, stated plainly

A formula is written with **no cached value**. Excel recalculates on open and this library computes on read — but a third-party reader that only reads cached values (openpyxl with `data_only=True`) sees an empty cell until Excel has opened and saved the file. A formula that cannot be evaluated reads back as its Excel error string (`#DIV/0!`, `#NAME?`, `#REF!`) rather than throwing. All measured before the design was written.

## Behaviour change worth reviewing

An invalid sheet name now throws `ArgumentException` naming the parameter, where it previously reached ClosedXML and surfaced as a `DocumentConversionException` wrapping someone else's message. Excel's real rules (≤31 characters, none of `: \ / ? * [ ]`) now live in one helper used by every path that names a sheet. The reviewer independently verified no existing test, sample or caller passes a name the new rules reject.

## Defects caught by the process, not by the tests

Worth listing, because they're the reason the review layers exist:

- **A new `Stream` overload escaped an entire suite.** `StreamOverloadTests` keys on *strings*, so the existing `"WorkbookEditor.CreateAsync"` entry mapped only to the single-sheet overload — exactly the bypass `CLAUDE.md` warns about. Fixed, then proven by deliberately breaking the overload and watching the right tests fail.
- **A mutation check that proved nothing.** The plan's mutation for "appending doesn't destroy other sheets" made *every* test die on the same line, because an empty workbook has no worksheets at all. Re-run with a mutation that deletes only other sheets: exactly one test failed, 57 passed.
- **`ReadSheet`'s documentation was left false** — it still said nothing in this library evaluates formulas. Then the fix over-corrected it to "evaluated on read, not from a cache", which is *also* false. This repo's own `FormulaWorkbookWithStaleCachedValue` fixture settles it: ClosedXML honours a cache when the file has one, and evaluates only when it doesn't. Both branches are now documented, including that a cached value can be stale.
- **The package README** — the one nuget.org renders — was never updated, while the root README pointed at it as "Full surface".
- Adding overloads made eight existing `<see cref="Create"/>` references **ambiguous** (CS0419) across five files, a build error. Each was disambiguated and checked to point at the overload its prose actually means.

## Verification

- `dotnet build -c Release --no-incremental` — 0 warnings, 0 errors
- **561 tests × 2 TFMs = 1122 results**, all passing (up from 1042)
- `--locked-mode` restore clean; no `packages.lock.json` change — no dependency was added
- third-party notices `--check` clean
- mutation-verified: formula dispatch, sheet preservation, the deep-copy guarantee, and the `StreamOverloadTests` registration

## Follow-up, recorded now rather than rediscovered

`IWorkbookEditor` cannot mirror these until the core package publishes — the extensions project references `Ank.DocToolkit` as a *published* `PackageReference`. That gap has opened three times before, once for two full releases. It's in the backlog row as this ships.

body:
Appends one correcting entry to `AGENT_WORKLOG.md`. No other file changes; `21 0` on `git diff --numstat`, and the historical bytes are preserved.

## What it corrects

The entry written before PR #118 was pushed states that opening a pull request "does not publish the page, which stays `noindex, nofollow` and unreachable from `main` until a merge and a deployment that are separate author decisions".

The second half is false for this repository. While #118 was still an unmerged draft, `https://metawritingecology.org/artistic-research/public-slice/2026-08-07/` already returned 200 with content that existed only on that branch, and `/artistic-research/` already linked to it. A successful pull-request build deploys to the **production** environment — the Cloudflare check on #118 names it in its own URL, `.../metawritingecology-site/production/builds/...`.

The historical entry is left byte-unchanged, as `AGENTS.md` requires. The correction is a new entry.

## Why it matters beyond one page

"Push now and decide about publication later" is not an available state in this repository. The gate that matters is before the push, not before the merge. Any work stream targeting this repository that plans otherwise is planning a state that does not exist.

Reachable and linked, not indexable. That is the state the slice design intended after publication; what differed was when it happened.

author: m-shogo
body:
Add the pure historical feature adapter that feeds the frozen N2-040 scanner without touching runtime registration or databases.

The adapter accepts only `historical-readonly` program snapshots and maps exactly the canonical historical-safe program/motor fields into explicit first/second/third trifecta roles: class, national/local win rate, national/local top-2 rate, motor/boat top-2 rate, and venue motor/boat top-2 rate (27 values total). Course remains derived by the scanner from the canonical selection itself.

It reuses `classifyProgramFeatureSafety`; any non-null live-only current snapshot field (`courseAvgSt`, `courseTop3Rate`, `flyingCount`, `lateStartCount`, `exhibitionStResidual`, etc.) blocks the entire adaptation. Missing selected boats also block. Individual safe-value missingness remains null and is never imputed.

For the fields already classified as historical-safe by the repository contract, the adapter records a conservative pre-close availability upper bound equal to the decision cutoff and an explicit adapter ID. It never exposes racer identity fields, registration numbers, motor/boat IDs, ST, exhibition, or weather. Those timed families remain separately gated by the scanner until exact timed adapters are reviewed.

No database write, Current BUY, LINE, public publishing, automatic promotion, automated betting, or production authority is introduced. This is source-shaping only; canonical TASK-N2-040 remains dormant.

author: spcoding12
body:
💡 **What**: The optimization implemented
Replaced all `.select()` CSS queries with `soup.find(class_=[...])` in `src/detector.py`. Replaced `str(tag)` and `.string` calls on `<script>` iteration with `.text`. Adjusted specific return logic to prioritize parsing out fast fields like `meta generator` versions before generic body checks.

🎯 **Why**: The performance problem it solves
Executing multiple `.select()` arrays in BeautifulSoup is highly unoptimized compared to native attribute lookups. Furthermore, calling `str(tag)` on elements with many children completely forces serialization of the entire DOM branch back to a string, resulting in catastrophic lag on large Javascript bundles hidden inside `<script>` elements.

📊 **Impact**: Expected performance improvement
Dramatically reduces per-page framework detection time. Benchmarks showed improvements for detecting Vuepress dropping from ~6.2s to ~1.2s, MkDocs dropping from ~5.7s to ~0.7s, and GitBook from ~4.7s to ~1.0s.

🔬 **Measurement**: How to verify the improvement
Run the test suite `python -m pytest tests/` or manually trigger the crawler over large documents. Look at standard CPU usage during heavy multi-page loads.

author: mgd43b
body:
## Summary

Two independent retrieval defects, both provider-agnostic and both affecting the default setup.

**1. FTS5 matched surface forms only.** The index was created with `tokenize='unicode61'`, which does no stem folding. Every one of these scores zero hits today:

| query | chunk contains | `unicode61` | `porter unicode61` |
|---|---|:---:|:---:|
| `authenticate` | "authentication" | **0** | 1 |
| `rotate` | "rotates" | **0** | 1 |
| `debug` | "debugging" | **0** | 1 |
| `fail` | "failed" | **0** | 1 |

Because the lexical leg feeds one half of the hybrid RRF merge in `Retriever.retrieve`, these are not ranking misses — the candidate never enters the funnel, and no downstream reranking can recover it.

`porter unicode61` layers the Porter stemmer over the same character-class tokenizer, so tokenization is unchanged and only stem folding is added. An FTS5 table's tokenizer is fixed at creation, so the migration rebuilds the index from the existing rows. `chunks_fts` is a standalone table holding its own content, so **nothing is re-embedded and no reindex is required**.

**2. `model.embeddingProvider` was silently ignored.** It was consulted only when the main provider could not embed at all (`if (!mainPlugin.capabilities.embedding)`), so it was dropped for Ollama and OpenAI, which can. Embedding dimensions are resolved from that same field, so:

```typescript
model: { provider: 'ollama', embeddingProvider: 'openai' }
```

created a 1536-D LanceDB collection and then filled it with 1024-D Ollama vectors.

`IngestPipeline` had a matching problem: it resolved its embedder by scanning the registry for the first embedding-capable plugin. The main provider registers first, so honoring the override in `bootstrap.ts` alone would have indexed through one model while querying through another. The pipeline now accepts the embedder explicitly and falls back to the registry scan only when none is supplied, keeping existing callers working.

The two halves have to ship together — fixing only `bootstrap.ts` would make the mismatch worse rather than better.

## Type of Change
- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Breaking change
- [ ] Documentation update
- [ ] Refactoring

## Related Issue

None — found while investigating hybrid retrieval recall.

## Checklist
- [x] Tests added/updated for changes
- [x] Documentation updated (if adding features) — n/a, no new features or config surface
- [x] `npx changeset` run for user-facing changes
- [x] `npm run typecheck` passes
- [x] `npm run test` passes
- [x] No new `any` types introduced
- [x] Error messages are actionable (include what went wrong + how to fix)

## Breaking Changes

None. The migration runs in place on existing databases and preserves all rows. Behavior only changes where it was previously broken: `embeddingProvider` now takes effect where it was ignored, which was a configuration that produced a mismatched index.

## Test Plan

16 new tests across three files.

**`packages/core/tests/storage/fts-stemming.test.ts`** — five parameterized cases for terms that scored zero before; exact surface forms still match; unrelated terms still don't. Plus a migration test that builds a pre-migration `unicode61` index with rows, stamps migrations 001–008 as applied, runs the migration over it, and asserts the old rows both survive and become stemmable.

**`packages/core/tests/ingest/embedder-routing.test.ts`** — registers a tracking embedder in the registry first (mirroring bootstrap's order), passes a different one explicitly, and asserts the supplied one is used and the registered one is not. Also covers the registry fallback and the no-embedder-at-all error path.

**`packages/server/tests/embedding-provider-override.test.ts`** — the override decision itself: routes when different, no-ops when unset, empty, or naming the main provider, and still routes when the main provider cannot embed.

Full suite: build 26/26, tests 51/51, typecheck 50/50.

Happy to split this into two PRs if you'd prefer them reviewed separately.

author: nelsong6
body:
Three things, in the order they became necessary.

## Rocks drop when the board assembles

ADR-0045 gave the units a staggered drop and drew an explicit line around it — *"Neutral rocks
are scenery, not deploying units → no drop."* Rocks are not scenery here; blocking one path is
most of what makes one board different from another, so the board revealed with its whole
obstacle course already standing and the armies were then placed onto it.

Placed rocks now take part in that entrance, on the same `arrivalOffset` fall curve, ordered by
board depth so the position lays itself down from the far corner toward the player. The first
rock is released well before the first unit; the unit choreography is untouched and its live gate
still passes. `BoardDrawOp` gains an optional `structure` identity so every op of one prop takes
the same offset — that is what keeps a flat-contact prop's two clipped halves from shearing apart
mid-fall. See ADR-0518.

## Prop candidates get a review board

Generated prop artwork had nowhere to be judged. `/surface-lab` does this for terrain and
`WallCandidateReview` does it for walls; props had only `/prop-lab`, which tunes the seat of art
that is already installed. That gap was load-bearing: acceptance requires owner review evidence
carrying a live surface URL, so with no prop review surface there was no legal path from a
generated PNG to a board at all.

`PropCandidateLab` mounts every staged candidate on the real board renderer at canonical 1x over
selectable terrain, beside the art it would replace. Reached by click from the Props catalog.

## The prop domain opens for acceptance

Even with the instrument, every prop candidate was refused: *"prop candidates remain bridge-only
until their typed completeness validator and game-owned review instrument exist."* Every prop in
the game today arrived over the legacy bridge because of it. `propArtMediaIssue` is the validator
that refusal named.

## Verification

- `frontend`: `npm run check` — 326 files, 2717 tests, tsc and every guard script.
- `backend`: `npm run test:backend` — green including both DB-free smokes.
- `npm run verify:unit-arrival` still passes against the campaign entrance.
- New: `npm run shot:assembly` records a live entrance frame by frame, because the frames between
  two settled states are the only thing that can show a drop.

## Content installed

17 rock props (`rock-px-00..16`), each accepted with owner proof naming the candidate board.
Catalog revision 1744 → 1778, drawable 299 → 300, prop seats 4 → 5. Nothing existing was retired
or repointed; `props/rock` is untouched.

Still to come, tracked separately: demoting the old `rock` and `fieldstone` art to Placed Art, and
reskinning rocks already placed on existing levels.

author: rywils
body:
Fixes #12.

## Summary

- `_applyEdgeResize()` in tilingManager.js divides by a fork's computed width/height to get a new split ratio. For a thin, deeply nested tile that fork rect can legitimately come out to zero width or height (computeNodeRect doesn't subtract gaps the way computeLayout's traversal does), so the division produces NaN and that gets written straight into fork.splitRatio.
- That corrupted NaN doesn't blow up right away, it sits there until the tree gets laid out again (a workspace switch, for example), at which point the NaN rect gets passed into metaWindow.move_frame()/move_resize_frame() in animator.js with no validation. Those are native Mutter calls, and passing NaN into them segfaults the whole compositor, not just HyperGnome, since extensions run in-process.
- Fixed at the source: guard the division in _applyEdgeResize() so a zero-size fork just bails out instead of corrupting the ratio.
- Fixed at the boundary too, as defense in depth: animateWindow and snapWindow in animator.js now refuse to pass a non-finite rect to the native move calls.

## Test plan

- Reproduced the crash on GNOME Shell 50.1 by tiling down to a thin nested tile, resizing near its edge, then switching workspaces - confirmed via journalctl + apport crash report (signal 11) and the JS stack trace pointing at animator.js:196 <- tilingManager.js:1220, plus a "nan" Clutter warning right before the crash.
- Applied the fix, repeated the same repro steps several times, no crash and no NaN warnings in the logs.

author: centraldetransplante-cyber
body:
## Bug

Achado numa simulação real de QA: o rascunho RTF editável do ofício de
indeferimento (`GET /processos/{id}/oficio-rascunho`,
`OficioService.gerarRascunhoRtf`) tinha todos os textos fixos SEM
acentuação nenhuma ("Regulacao", "Divisao", "Oficio n", "apos analise"
etc.) — diferente do PDF antigo (`OficioService.gerar`), que o CLAUDE.md
já documenta como corrigido (acentuação correta, é documento oficial).

## Correção

- Todos os literais fixos de `gerarRascunhoRtf` foram acentuados
  ("Regulação", "Divisão", "Ofício nº", "após análise", "Permanecemos à
  disposição", "À equipe solicitante", fallback do motivo "(motivo não
  informado)").
- `OficioService.NUMERO_NAO_ATRIBUIDO` (fallback compartilhado entre PDF e
  RTF) também foi acentuado — de quebra corrige o mesmo placeholder no PDF.
- **Nenhuma mudança no mecanismo de escape**: `escaparRtf` já cobria
  corretamente acentuação (`\'hh` no code page `\ansicpg1252` declarado no
  cabeçalho do RTF); os literais só precisavam continuar entrando via
  `linha(...)`/`centralizado(...)`, que já chamam `escaparRtf`.

## Validação

- Gerei o RTF de verdade num teste, escrevi em disco e **li os bytes**
  para inspecionar os escapes gerados: confirmado `Regula\'e7\'e3o`
  (Regulação), `Of\'edcio n\'ba` (Ofício nº), `\'c0 equipe` (À equipe) etc.
  — estrutura RTF intacta (chaves balanceadas, sem corrupção).
- Novo teste `OficioServiceTest.rascunhoTemAcentuacaoCorretaNosTextosFixos`
  (decodifica `\'hh` de volta para o caractere original via helper de
  teste `desescapaRtf` e compara com os literais acentuados esperados).
- Teste de fallback existente atualizado para decodificar antes de
  comparar (a string RTF crua nunca contém "número"/"não" literalmente).
- Suíte completa: **889 testes, 0 falhas** (JDK 21).

## CLAUDE.md

Nova subseção "Bug corrigido: rascunho RTF sem acentuação (2026-08-08)"
dentro de "Ofício de indeferimento: sempre ANEXADO, nunca gerado".

author: deepak0x
body:
## Summary

`School::apiCreate` called `RateLimiter::assertWithinLimit` unconditionally, and `User::apiUpdateBasicInfo` invokes it internally when a user enters a new school name. Because `RateLimiter::assertWithinLimit` keys the bucket on the immediate caller (`School::apiCreate`), both the direct `/api/school/create` endpoint and the internal profile-update path share the same rate-limit bucket. A user who updates their profile with new school names ~6 times in the same window could hit `contentCreationRateLimitExceeded` without ever calling the school-create endpoint directly.

## Changes

`frontend/server/src/Controllers/School.php`:
- Added a `bool $internal = false` parameter to `apiCreate`. When `true`, the user-facing `RateLimiter::assertWithinLimit` is skipped, so internal controller-to-controller calls don't consume the external quota.

`frontend/server/src/Controllers/User.php`:
- `apiUpdateBasicInfo` now calls `School::apiCreate(..., internal: true)` for the internal school creation.

`frontend/tests/controllers/RateLimiterTest.php`:
- Added `testSchoolCreateViaProfileUpdateNotRateLimited`: 6 profile updates with distinct new school names must not throw, while direct `School::apiCreate` calls still hit their own limit on the 6th.

## Test plan

- `testSchoolCreateViaProfileUpdateNotRateLimited` covers the regression (internal path not rate-limited; direct path still limited).
- Existing `testSchoolCreateRateLimit` continues to verify the direct endpoint is limited.
- The fix is minimal and does not change the public `/api/school/create` behavior for external callers.

Fixes #10077

author: ilbzzz
body:
### CodeMender Security Fix

**Finding ID**: `d946f148-f8c7-5092-a06e-1d9fd3b10504`
**Title**: SQL Injection in Login
**Severity**: CRITICAL
**Vulnerability Type**: SQL Injection
**File Path**: `/app/juice-shop-local/routes/login.ts`
**Start Line**: 34

#### Analysis
The `login` function in `routes/login.ts` passes user-supplied input directly into a SQL query via string interpolation without any sanitization or parameterized queries. The `req.body.email` parameter is retrieved from the incoming HTTP request and is inserted into the `SELECT * FROM Users WHERE email = '...'` SQL string. 

Because of the lack of input validation and sanitization, an attacker can manipulate the query logic by passing an email value like `admin@juice-sh.op' OR 1=1--` to bypass the password check and log in as the first user (likely an administrator) without providing a valid password.

Conceptual Exploit Payload:
```json
{
  "email": "admin@juice-sh.op' OR 1=1--",
  "password": ""
}
```

author: mohapatras
body:
Prepares BV to talk to ai4i orchestrate over its **public** URL with API-key auth, per the reference curl:

```
curl 'https://demo.ai4inclusion.org/api/v1/chat/completions' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer dac2b90e...' \
  -d '{"model":"google/gemma-4-31B-it","messages":[...],"stream":true}'
```

## The problem

Only `_build_gemma_agrinet_model()` read `VLLM_API_KEY`. The agrinet and moderation models in the `LLM_PROVIDER=vllm` branch hardcoded `api_key="not-needed"`.

Flipping the URLs alone would therefore authenticate the gemma call and **not** moderation — and moderation runs first and blocks every token (`app/services/chat.py:208`). It would 401 before the generator's first `yield`, and the farmer would get a well-formed, empty 200 stream with nothing in the logs. That is the exact signature of the last two demo outages.

## The change

- `_resolve_gateway_api_key()` hoisted out of the gemma builder and used by all three model paths.
- `_normalize_openai_base_url()` moved above the provider branch and applied to the vllm URLs too, so a pasted `.../chat/completions` is trimmed to the API root in all three places rather than just one.
- `VLLM_MODERATION_MODEL_URL` falls back to the agrinet URL when **blank** as well as when unset. The deployed values file carries every key, so an empty string is the likelier misconfig.

**No behavior change until the config flips.** With `VLLM_API_KEY` blank, `_resolve_gateway_api_key()` returns `"not-needed"` — byte-identical to what the vllm branch sent before. Verified explicitly.

## Verified against the live gateway

Not inferred from code — measured.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Real `moderation_agent.run()` through the gateway | **OK in 1.8s** (this is the call that would 401 without this PR) |
| Streaming via `run_stream_events` | **62 incremental deltas, first at 0.47s** |
| SSE buffering | **None.** TTFB 0.49s vs 25.5s total for a 133 KB response |
| Streamed tool calls | Correct `delta.tool_calls` format |
| 107 KB body, 28 tool schemas | **200**, TTFB 0.42s — no body-size limit |
| `max_completion_tokens` | Honored identically to `max_tokens` |
| Wrong / missing key | `401 {"message":"missing X-User-ID"}` — fast and loud, not a hang |
| `X-API-Key` header | **401.** Only `Authorization: Bearer` works |
| Extra `serviceId` field | Ignored, 200 |
| Bogus model | 404 immediately |

Two consequences worth noting:

- **`AGRINET_STREAMING_ENABLED` can stay `true`** — SSE buffering through the gateway was an open question and the answer is no buffering.
- **`X-API-Key` is not accepted**, contradicting what was previously documented. Doesn't block anything (`VLLM_API_KEY` already feeds Bearer), but the assumption was wrong.

New: responses carry `x-ratelimit-limit: 3000`, `x-ratelimit-plan: P2`, `x-ratelimit-auth-type: apikey`. Rate limiting is **per API key**, and BV spends 3+ gateway calls per farmer turn. Not a factor while BV bypassed the gateway in-cluster.

## Tests

`tests/test_gateway_api_key.py` — five offline tests covering key propagation to all three paths, the blank-key no-regression case, URL normalization, the moderation-URL fallback, and that a missing agrinet URL still fails loudly. 12 passed with the existing body-compat suite.

## Deploy

Paired with `COSS-India/ai4i-services-env` — the URLs and the key live there. **Merge and deploy this first**, then flip config, otherwise you get the empty-stream failure described above. Frontend needs no change: the UI only ever calls the BV backend, and its `VITE_API_KEY` is BV's own auth, unrelated to orchestrate.

author: chaiyavongforgame121-create
body:
## What

Delivery, pickup and dine-in change the price, the fields the diner has to fill in and where the food ends up — but the storefront let them fill a whole cart before ever asking. A dine-in order could be placed with no table, so the food had nowhere to go.

A blocking modal now sits over the menu, cart and checkout until a channel is chosen, and both the checkout and the server enforce the per-channel required fields.

## Client

- **Blocking gate** on menu / cart / checkout — deliberately *not* the layout, which also wraps order tracking, receipts and account pages that must stay reachable without an order type.
- Not dismissible (no backdrop click, no Escape, no close button) and **traps focus**: the gate renders inside `<main>`, after the header in DOM order, so without a trap the first Tab landed on the brand link and a keyboard user could bypass it entirely. The trap is also what makes `aria-modal` real for a screen reader.
- Delivery only appears when the branch has the entitlement; `resolveChannel()` clears a stale delivery choice when the diner crosses to a branch that cannot deliver.
- The channel is persisted **with the branch it was chosen at** (cart store → version 2), so switching branches re-asks rather than carrying a pickup choice into a restaurant across town. Diners change it later from the `Segmented` control already in the menu header.
- Checkout blocks submit on a missing table number (dine-in) or drop-off preference (delivery).

## Server — `place-order` v9.4

The client is not the authority, so the same rules land in the edge function:

- `channel` is validated against the enum → `400 invalid_channel` instead of a `500` from a Postgres cast three steps later.
- New `source` (`web` | `counter` | `pos`) replaces the hardcoded `'web'`. Unknown values fall back to `web`, the strictest bucket, so a forged one cannot loosen a rule.
- Dine-in from `source: web` requires a table → `400 table_required`. Staff surfaces are exempt: the counter legitimately rings up walk-in dine-in with no table.
- A supplied `table_number` is resolved against the branch's active `tables` rows to populate `orders.table_id` — **a column no surface has ever written**.
  - Matched with `eq`, never `ilike`: PostgREST aliases `*` to `%`, so a diner typing `*` would have matched every table in the branch and `.limit(1)` (no `ORDER BY`) would hand them an arbitrary one. Reproduced live before fixing.
  - Scoped to `dine_in`/`qr_ordering`, because the staff views keep the typed table in state across a channel switch and would otherwise stamp a pickup order with a real table's FK. Counter and POS now also clear the table number on channel change — the other half of that fix.

## Verification

Edge function deployed and smoke-tested live, 7/7:

| case | result |
|---|---|
| `dine_in` + `source:web`, no table | `400 table_required` |
| `channel:"banquet"` | `400 invalid_channel` |
| `dine_in` + `table_number:"1"` | `201`, `table_id` resolved |
| `dine_in` + `table_number:"*"` | `201`, `table_id` **null** |
| `pickup` + `table_number:"1"` | `201`, `table_id` **null** |
| `dine_in` + `source:counter`, no table | `201`, `source=counter` |
| no `source` at all | `201`, falls back to `web` |

Test orders were cancelled afterwards, not deleted. `pnpm turbo run type-check` → 7/7. Cart-store unit tests cover the six channel cases. Checklist updated in `docs/TEST-CASES.md` (1.2.0, 1.7.10–1.7.12).

## Deploy ordering

The edge function is **already live in production** (version 12). The web app on Vercel is still on the old bundle, which sends no `table_number` — so dine-in via production web returns `400 table_required` until this merges and the web surface redeploys. Pickup and delivery are unaffected. Pre-launch, so no real orders are impacted.

body:
### Description

This PR resolves #64 by replacing the static list of FAQs with a modern, collapsible accordion layout.

Previously, all FAQ answers were fully expanded by default. This created an unnecessarily long page that was difficult to scan and discouraged the addition of detailed, in-depth answers.

### Changes Made

- Replaced the static FAQ list with a collapsible accordion layout, so answers are hidden by default and expand on click.
- Redesigned the styling to support the new interactive layout.
- Added UI polish: a chevron icon that rotates on expansion, a smooth fade-in animation, and dynamic border/shadow highlighting on hover and expansion.

### Result

Hiding answers by default significantly improves the scannability of the page, allowing users to quickly find the specific question they are looking for without endless scrolling. This approach also scales much better as the program grows and more FAQs are added.

Closes #64

author: l-carp55
body:
## What changed
- Keep standardized 90 ft running time (`T90`) as the redesigned base-speed target.
- Add `src/ratings/speed_production.mjs` with explicit priority: T90 Tier A-D > scouting > Tier-E proxy > clearly marked legacy fallback.
- Add `src/cards/t90_pipeline_adapter.mjs` so card generation records T90 evidence/status and uses T90 automatically once a frozen reference/model can produce a rating.
- Route `build_card.mjs`, `build_cards_batch.mjs`, and `appraise_season.mjs` through the T90 adapter.
- Legacy values are never silently relabeled as T90.
- Keep 30m/50m acceleration evidence separate from the production point estimate unless protocol/temporal gates are met.
- Add permanent scope-control / Definition-of-Done rules to `CLAUDE.md`.

## Post-wiring appraisal QA
- Freeze a 29-player PowerPro-blind v3 physical evaluation sample.
- Preserve owner feel bands as independent QA labels only; no coefficient or player correction is fitted to them.
- Curate the five largest profile disagreements (並木 / 小園 / 矢野 / 村林 / 細川) and block stale, protocol-unknown, or first-step-start 50m values from numeric T90 conversion.
- Audit T90→1-100 scale alternatives. The current v3 linear evaluation scale remains best of the tested mappings (11/18 owner-QA bands; mean distance 2.30 points); sample-centered alternatives degrade fit.

## Full MLB T90 calibration
- Fix Baseball Savant current Running Splits header handling (`seconds_since_hit_010/030/090`) and add `scripts/calibrate_t90_bridge_v2.mjs`.
- Fetch and join Baseball Savant Running Splits + Sprint Speed for **2017-2025**.
- Full sample: **4,381 player-seasons / 1,222 players**.
- Leave-one-year-out results:
  - Sprint Speed only: MAE **0.04463s**, RMSE **0.05540s**.
  - Sprint Speed + T10: MAE **0.03065s** (**31.3%** reduction).
  - Sprint Speed + T30: MAE **0.02111s** (**52.7%** reduction), held-year MAE ~0.0199-0.0246s.
- Adjacent-year repeatability is high (T90 r=0.930; Sprint Speed r=0.938).
- The three MLB models are therefore frozen as `CALIBRATED_FULL_MLB_2017_2025_LOYO` in `configs/speed_t90_models.json`.
- The transferable conclusion is structural: acceleration/split information materially improves 90-ft prediction beyond Sprint Speed alone.

## NPB+ transfer gate
- Canonicalize the NPB+ metric to its official name **Sprint Speed / スプリントスピード**; keep legacy DB `top_speed_kmh` as a compatibility storage name.
- Official public material confirms Hawk-Eye optical player tracking powers NPB+ speed data, but does not establish the MLB Statcast Sprint Speed formula (`fastest one-second window` plus qualified-run seasonal aggregation) as numerically identical.
- Re-audit NPB+ 2026 players directly against the full 2017-2025 Savant files using `bm_player.name_en`, not only `mlb_bridge`.
- True historical overlaps: **6** (モンテロ / 秋山翔吾 / カリステ / 筒香嘉智 / サンタナ / ポランコ).
- Within the project’s <=4-year temporal gate: only **2** (モンテロ: 2024→2026; 筒香: 2022→2026). This remains far too small to identify a defensible NPB+→T90 regression or error distribution.
- A targeted primary/official-source search found no public calibration set that pairs named NPB professionals’ Hawk-Eye Sprint Speed with clean same-setting 30m/90ft/T90 labels.
- Therefore the NPB+ bridge calibration gate is **closed for current scope**. Reopen only with more near-season same-player overlap, a published formula establishing metric equivalence, or direct NPB trajectory/T90 labels.
- The existing NPB v3 mapping remains evaluation-only/provisional; MLB coefficients are not unit-converted into the NPB+ production model.

## T90 uncertainty handling
- Update `configs/speed_t90_uncertainty.json` from the full MLB multi-year validation.
- MLB validated MAE floors:
  - Sprint + T30: **0.02111s**
  - Sprint + T10: **0.03065s**
  - Sprint only: **0.04463s**
- NPB+ has **no numeric MAE floor** until its cross-system/direct-NPB bridge is calibrated. The MLB error is reference-only and must not be displayed as an NPB confidence/error interval.
- `src/ratings/speed_t90_display.mjs` keeps point estimates and uncertainty metadata separate; clean short-distance evidence may produce candidate ranges without hand tuning.

## Validation
- GitHub Actions run `31292874269`: **SUCCESS** end-to-end.
  - `scripts/test_npb_plus_sprint_speed_alias.mjs`: PASS.
  - `scripts/test_speed_t90_uncertainty.mjs`: PASS.
  - 2017-2025 Savant acquisition: PASS.
  - full MLB calibration v2: PASS.
  - calibration artifact upload: PASS.
- Existing production-wiring regression tests / WBC / season appraisal checks remain in the branch history.

## Completion boundary
Speed v1 is complete as a **production architecture and MLB physical calibration path**. Remaining NPB numerical uncertainty is explicit rather than hidden. This does **not** claim that every NPB player already has a final `T90_PRIMARY` rating, that the NPB production reference CDF is frozen, or that an NPB+→T90 bridge has been calibrated.

Parking Lot / future trigger only: new near-season NPB+/MLB overlap, a published NPB+ Sprint Speed definition equivalent to MLB Statcast, or direct NPB T90/trajectory labels; then calibrate NPB+ and freeze the complete NPB T90 reference CDF. Prime-composite speed composition also remains separate.

author: robobun
body:
## Symptom

`require()` of an ESM entry silently skips evaluating one CommonJS module of the graph: no throw, exit 0, the module's top-level code just never runs. Deterministic (10/10) on 1.4.0 and on current main; Node evaluates the full graph. Found by fault-injection fuzzing at zero faults; independent of `NODE_COMPILE_CACHE`.

<details>
<summary>8-file repro</summary>

```
# main.cjs
require("./a.mjs");
# a.mjs
import "./b.mjs";
import "./d.mjs";
import "./e.mjs";
(globalThis.T ??= []).push("a");
console.log("N=" + globalThis.T.length + " " + globalThis.T.join(","));
# b.mjs
import "./c.cjs";
(globalThis.T ??= []).push("b");
# c.cjs
require("./e.mjs");
(globalThis.T ??= []).push("c");
# d.mjs
import "./f.cjs";
(globalThis.T ??= []).push("d");
# e.mjs
import "./f.cjs";
import "./h.mjs";
(globalThis.T ??= []).push("e");
# f.cjs
require("./h.mjs");
(globalThis.T ??= []).push("f");
console.log("f.cjs evaluated");
# h.mjs
(globalThis.T ??= []).push("h");
```

```
bun main.cjs  ->  N=6 h,e,c,b,d,a                      (f.cjs never evaluated)
node main.cjs ->  f.cjs evaluated / N=7 h,f,e,c,b,d,a
bun a.mjs     ->  f.cjs evaluated / N=7 h,f,e,c,b,d,a  (direct ESM entry is fine)
```

Worse: if `f.cjs` ends in `throw new Error("boom")` instead, `bun main.cjs` still prints `N=6` and exits 0. The user's error is swallowed entirely. Extension-independent (same with `.js` files).
</details>

## Cause

Three steps, traced with instrumentation on a debug build:

1. `require("./a.mjs")` drives the whole graph load on the loader's synchronous module queue. `f.cjs` (a CJS module imported by two ESM files) is mid-fetch when its body runs during makeModule, and that body does `require("./h.mjs")` while `h.mjs` is also mid-fetch. The reactions that would settle h's registry entry sit on the outer drain's queue, which the nested `loadModuleSync` cannot reach: `JSModuleLoader::loadModule` reuses the pending fetch promise, nothing drains, and `esmLoadSync` reports the pending load as `require() async module "h.mjs" is unsupported. use "await import()" instead.` even though `h.mjs` has no top-level await.

2. The spurious TypeError aborts f's body. The synthetic-source error path evicts f from the require cache (so a later `require()` can retry) and rethrows, but the rejection's reaction is itself stranded on the outer queue and is ultimately dropped.

3. A later nested load (c.cjs's `require("./e.mjs")`) replays makeModule for f. The synthetic module generator looks f up in the require cache, gets `undefined` from `JSMap::get`, and because `undefined` is a truthy `JSValue` the old `if (entry)` check passed and the missing-entry branch was unreachable. It fell through both branches and produced an **empty module record, with no error**. e and d then link against empty-f, everything "succeeds", and f's side effects (or its real error) vanish.

## Fix

Both halves are in the bindings; no WebKit change needed.

- `functionEsmLoadSync` (ZigGlobalObject.cpp): inline `loadModuleSync` and, when the target's registry entry is status Fetching with a pending fetch promise, re-issue the fetch synchronously and settle the entry's fetch promise while our queue is current, so the whole chain drains here. This mirrors the synchronous-replay path `hostLoadImportedModule` already has for dependency edges, and is the same tolerance pattern as the in-flight handling in #37185: the stranded async settle later lands on an already-settled promise and is dropped.

- `commonJSModuleSyntheticSourceCode` (JSCommonJSModule.cpp): test the missing require-cache entry explicitly (`isUndefinedOrNull`) and throw instead of fabricating an empty module. The eviction path now also records the evaluation error on the module's registry entry, so the replay rethrows the original error (e.g. the user's `boom`) rather than a generic one, matching what Node reports.

## Verification

- Repro above: `N=7 h,f,e,c,b,d,a` matching Node, 10/10, on release-style and debug+ASAN builds. Same with the `.js`-extension flavor, with `NODE_COMPILE_CACHE` (cold and warm), and with `BUN_FEATURE_FLAG_DISABLE_ASYNC_TRANSPILER=1`.
- The `throw new Error("boom")` variant now exits 1 printing `boom from f.cjs` with the correct stack (was: exit 0, no output beyond `N=6`).
- New tests in `test/js/bun/resolve/require-esm-nested-cjs-sibling.test.ts`; both fail on an unfixed build and pass with this change.
- No regressions: `test/js/bun/resolve` (require/esm/import-defer/dynamic-import suites), `test/js/node/module`, `test/js/bun/test/mock`, `test/bundler/bundler_splitting.test.ts` all pass.
- The concurrent-import race test from #33184 (issue #33180) also passes with this change.

## Relation to open PRs in this area

- #33184 fixes the same underlying gap (top-level sync loads cannot settle a mid-flight entry) from a different reproduction, the concurrent `import` race in #33180, with the same pre-settle technique in the same function. Verified here: #33184 alone fixes this PR's silent-skip repro, but not the swallowed-error variant (still `N=6`, exit 0). The two PRs conflict textually in `functionEsmLoadSync`; whichever lands second rebases that hunk. The require-cache half of this PR is independent of that choice.
- #37185 fixes the sibling door where the require target goes through `fetchCommonJSModule` (source already transpiled) instead of `esmLoadSync`; different file, no conflict.
- The `ASSERTION FAILED: module->loadedModules().size() <= loadedModulesCountBefore + 1` abort on debug builds for some of these graphs (e.g. this graph with `BUN_FEATURE_FLAG_DISABLE_ASYNC_TRANSPILER=1 bun a.mjs`) is pre-existing, unchanged by this PR, and addressed in oven-sh/WebKit#396.

<!-- robobun:evidence:begin -->

---

**[review]** gate passed · iteration 2 · 3 files touched

<details><summary>fails on main (without fix)</summary>

```console
ASAN without fix: 3 FAILED
$ BUN_DEBUG_QUIET_LOGS=1 bun scripts/build.ts --profile=debug --quiet test "--reporter=junit" "--reporter-outfile=/tmp/mechgate.xml" test/js/bun/resolve/require-esm-nested-cjs-sibling.test.ts

author: vraj-ai
body:
## Problem The OpenCode provider snapshot never populates `skills`, so the `$` picker is always empty for OpenCode models. Claude and Codex both list theirs — `ClaudeProvider` calls `discoverClaudeSkills`, `CodexProvider` parses `skills/list` — but `OpenCodeProvider` has no skill code at all, so `ServerProvider.skills` falls back to its `[]` default. Users with skills installed in OpenCode's own directories see them work through OpenCode's built-in `skill` tool, but they never appear in T3 Code's picker, which makes it look like the skills aren't loaded. ## Approach Filesystem discovery, mirroring the existing `ClaudeSkills` driver. I looked at reading the SDK instead (`client.skill.list()`), but the local install path builds its inventory from `opencode models` / `opencode agent list` and never starts a server — and there is no `opencode skill` CLI command. Using the SDK would mean spawning a server purely to probe, and would leave the common non-`serverUrl` install with no skills. Scanning the filesystem covers both install paths with no extra process. `OpenCodeSkills` scans OpenCode's skill roots: - user: `/skill` and `/skills` - project: `/.opencode/skill` and `/.opencode/skills` honouring `OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR` then `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` then `~/.config`, matching what OpenCode itself resolves, so the picker reflects the directories the spawned runtime actually reads. It matches OpenCode's `{skill,skills}/**/SKILL.md`, so nested skills are found via a depth-bounded walk, and `stat` follows symlinks because the common multi-agent layout symlinks each skill into the config dir. Discovery is best-effort in the same way as `ClaudeSkills`: unreadable roots and entries without parseable frontmatter are skipped, so a broken skill can never degrade the snapshot. Project scope wins name collisions, matching OpenCode's later-scan-wins resolution. ## Scope note Two lines of the diff widen `checkOpenCodeProviderStatus`'s context to `FileSystem | Path` and provide those services in `OpenCodeDriver`, exactly as `ClaudeDriver` already does for `checkClaudeProviderStatus`. Both were already in `OpenCodeDriver`'s declared requirements. This does not touch `skills.paths` or `skills.urls` from `opencode.json`. The server is spawned with `OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT={}`, so those never apply to skills in T3 Code today, and covering them would mean parsing a config that is deliberately discarded. ## Verification - `pnpm test src/provider` — 491 passed, 0 failures - `pnpm typecheck` — clean - `vp lint` / `vp format --check` — clean - 4 new tests: user + project discovery, singular `skill` dir and nested skills, project-wins collision, and skipping malformed/unnamed frontmatter and missing roots - Against a real install (37 skills in `~/.config/opencode/skills`), discovery returns all of them with correct paths and descriptions; before this change the snapshot reported none ## On CONTRIBUTING I read it, and I realise this is closer to "feature work" than a pure bug fix, so close it if it is not wanted. I kept it to ~19 lines of wiring plus one new driver and its tests, and modelled it as closely as I could on `ClaudeSkills` rather than introducing a new pattern. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- > [!NOTE] > **Low Risk** > Read-only filesystem probing during provider status checks; failures are ignored so a broken skill tree cannot break the snapshot. > > **Overview** > **OpenCode provider snapshots now include skills** so the `$` picker can list them like Claude and Codex, instead of always returning an empty `skills` array. > > Adds **`discoverOpenCodeSkills`**, which scans user config (`skill` / `skills` under the resolved OpenCode config dir) and project workspace (`.opencode/skill(s)`), finds nested `SKILL.md` files, parses YAML frontmatter for `name` / `description`, skips bad entries, and lets **project scope override user** on name clashes. **`checkOpenCodeProviderStatus`** calls that helper on successful probes and passes the result into **`buildServerProvider`**. **`OpenCodeDriver`** wires **`FileSystem`** and **`Path`** into the status-check effect (same pattern as Claude). New unit tests cover discovery, nesting, collisions, and malformed files. > > Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit fd5a0c388edcc6821a556407418e5ff5e7df8c5e. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot). > [!NOTE] > ### Report OpenCode skills in the provider snapshot by discovering skill files from the filesystem > - Adds [`discoverOpenCodeSkills`](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/pull/5683/files#diff-cc288deb72faf88498ea5a2aaaa726ac39c323a31ecaeab42c645c04df33d6ec) to walk user (`~/.config/opencode/{skill,skills}`) and project (`.opencode/{skill,skills}`) directories, parsing YAML frontmatter from `SKILL.md` files to extract name and description. > - Project-scoped skills override user-scoped ones on name collision; results require a valid `name` field and are sorted alphabetically. > - Updates [`checkOpenCodeProviderStatus`](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/pull/5683/files#diff-4477b51690b8bf5db4f32c13ac9bb4ed2be7798d366111f84b38be236cc034bd) to call `discoverOpenCodeSkills` and include the resulting skills array in the returned `ServerProviderDraft`. > - Provides `FileSystem` and `Path` services to the `checkOpenCodeProviderStatus` effect in [`OpenCodeDriver.create`](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/pull/5683/files#diff-5a06651977dc543feb1fa81fc993b93165158b17e4204e51ac4b4c97c362d2f6) to satisfy the updated effect environment. > > > >

author: jeremy
body:
## Problem

`TYPE_CONST_STRING` stores a pointer into a Ruby String:

```c
case TYPE_CONST_STRING:
    ...
    else { dst->pointer = rb_string_value_cstr(src); }
```

A String argument is safe. `argv` holds it and keeps it in place.

A `to_str` object is not. `rb_string_value_cstr` writes the coerced String back into `src`. `argv` still holds the original object, not the String. The next loop turn overwrites `src`. After that, only `converted_args` holds the String.

The pointer must stay valid until `ffi_call` returns. `ffi_call` runs under `rb_thread_call_without_gvl`, so another thread can compact the heap during the call. `converted_args` must keep the String **in place**, not only alive.

Master does this. `converted_args` sits in the `ALLOCV` buffer. The GC scans that buffer conservatively, and a conservative scan pins the object.

## Gap

No test covers this.

Before #205, `converted_args` was a Ruby Array. The GC may move an Array's elements, so the String moved while the pointer stayed, and the C function read the vacated slot. #205 replaced the Array with the buffer and fixed the fault as a side effect. Nothing records that the buffer is required.

## Change

1. `test_call_const_string_from_to_str_after_compaction` in `test/fiddle/test_function.rb`.
2. A comment at `converted_args` in `ext/fiddle/function.c` stating the requirement.

The test calls `strcspn` as `[TYPE_CONST_STRING, TYPE_VOIDP] -> TYPE_SIZE_T`. Arg 0 is a `to_str` object returning a fresh 100-byte String. Arg 1 is a `to_ptr` object, which makes Fiddle call `Pointer.[]`; that allocation lets the GC run after the pointer is stored.

The subject holds no `"Z"`; the reject set is `"Z"`. A correct call returns 100. A stale pointer returns 0, because a vacated slot holds zero bytes.

Three details are load-bearing. Remove any one and the test passes on a faulty build; each has a comment:

- Churn is the subject's byte size, half of it dropped. The compactor only evacuates non-full pages.
- `to_ptr` returns a **new** `Pointer` each time. An existing `Pointer` gives Fiddle nothing to allocate.
- The intact-case call runs **after** the loop. A call before it prepares the CIF, and that preparation is part of what opens the window.

## Result

| tree | arm64-darwin, ruby 3.4.10 | aarch64-linux, ruby 3.4.7 |
|---|---|---|
| `d389bbf` (before #205) | fail | fail |
| master | pass | pass |

Three runs per tree on darwin, same result each time. Full suite on master with this change: 242 tests, 668 assertions, 0 failures, 1 error, 3 omissions. The error is `test_nogvl_poll` needing `envutil`; it fails the same way without this change.

Environment: ruby 3.4.10 [arm64-darwin23]; ruby 3.4.7 [aarch64-linux], glibc 2.36, libffi 3.4.4.

## Note

Released versions still have the fault. I measured 1.1.6 and 1.1.8 on both platforms: a two-argument call of this shape returns the wrong result on every iteration under `GC.stress` with `GC.auto_compact`. Master is correct. You may want a release.

I report this as latent. The trigger is the declared argument type plus a `to_str` object in place of a String. In one application that loads fiddle at boot, all 227 bundled gems put every `Fiddle::Function.new` behind a Windows-only branch.

body:
## What changed

author: syhongart
body:
검수관 판정: 조건부 (재확인: 118c754)

감독 지시: *"캐릭터 꾸미기 누르면 캐릭터 디자인으로 바로 이동해야지."*

그전에는 미술관 로비까지만 보내고 사용자가 거기서 편집기를 **다시 찾아 눌러야** 했다. 버튼 이름이 약속한 것과 실제로 일어나는 일이 달랐다.

## 무엇을 바꿨나

- `mypage/app.ts` — `buildAvatarDeepLink('./index.html', 'mypage')`
- `ui-hud.ts` — `initUI` 끝에서 파라미터를 읽어 편집기를 연다. **파라미터는 소비한다**(`replaceState`)
- `ui-avatar-editor.ts` — `close()` 에 **1회성** 복귀 콜백
- `avatar-deeplink.ts` — 프로토콜 SSOT (신규)

**돌아올 길**을 함께 넣었다. 없으면 편집기를 닫는 순간 미술관 로비에 남고, 사용자는 자기가 왜 거기 있는지 모른다.

## 검수 이력 — 반려 → 조건부 → 재확인 3회

**첫 판본은 반려됐다.** 블로커 3건의 뿌리가 하나였다 — **1회 명령을 세션 상태로 남긴 것.**

| | 증상 | 처방 |
|---|---|---|
| B1 | 미술관에서 `C`키로 편집기 열고 저장 → **튕겨 나감** | 파라미터 소비 + 훅 1회성 |
| B2 | ESC·배경클릭으로 닫으면 **복귀 안 됨**(주석은 된다고 적음) | `close()` 단일 지점으로 |
| B3 | 사진 공유 링크에 딥링크가 실려 **제3자가 편집기 화면을 봄** | 파라미터 소비 |

**편집기 코드가 이미 답을 적어 두었다** — *"`close()`는 ✓·×·ESC가 모두 지나는 단일 지점이라 여기 한 곳이면 충분하다(**경로가 늘면 여기로 모아라**)."* 그 지시를 어긴 것이 B1·B2였다.

그 뒤 조건 3건 + 새 조건 1건을 더 해소했다.

## 검증

**테스트 0건 → 35건** (순수 15 + HUD 통합 20). 편집기를 스텁하지 않고 실제로 돌린다 — jsdom에 없는 것(WebGL 렌더러·캔버스 2D)만 갈아끼웠다. 스텁끼리의 약속은 아무것도 보증하지 않는다.

**뮤테이션 — 각 축이 단독으로 깨지는지**

| 뮤테이션 | 깨진 것 |
|---|---|
| ESC 핸들러만 죽임 | ③ ESC **1건만** |
| 배경클릭만 죽임 | ④ 배경클릭 **1건만** |
| 훅 1회성 해제 삭제 | 1건 |
| **진짜 M3**(생산자를 리터럴로) | 미러 검출축 **1건만** |
| `hash` 보존 제거 | 1건 |

**독립 스모크** (executor, `b025ad6`): `EXIT=0 · PASS 17 · FAIL 0 · [-1b] 워킹트리 불변 PASS · [4] 콘솔 에러 0`(`app/index` 포함). *이 커밋(`118c754`)은 주석·문서만 바뀌어 재실행하지 않았다.*

**실브라우저 7세션** — 측정 주체는 **부팀장 본인**. 저장·닫기·ESC·배경클릭 네 경로 전부 `mypage.html` 복귀, `back` 없으면 미술관 유지, `#gd=` hash 보존, 평소 미술관 안 열림, **콘솔 에러 전부 0**. 모든 세션에서 `search`가 비어 있다.

> 배경클릭은 처음 "복귀 안 함"으로 나왔는데 **측정 오류**였다. 카드 374×776 vs 뷰포트 390×844라 여백이 좁아 카드 안을 눌렀고 대기도 짧았다. `elementFromPoint`로 클릭 지점이 오버레이인지 확인하고 `waitForURL`로 이동을 명시적으로 기다리니 `moved`였다.

## 이번 사이클에서 배운 것

**"안 깨진 뮤테이션"에는 두 종류가 있다** — 등가(행동 불변, 축을 늘려도 안 잡힘)와 진짜 사각(축을 만든다). M3은 생산자 출력과 리터럴이 **완전히 같은 문자열**이라 왕복 계약으로는 원리상 못 잡는 등가 뮤테이션이었다. 값 미러링은 **SSOT를 모킹으로 갈아끼우고 생산자가 따라오는지**를 봐야 잡힌다.

그 과정에서 제가 **같은 형태의 거짓 진술을 한 보고 안에서 두 번** 냈고 검수관이 둘 다 잡았다. 원인은 `DELEGATION.md`의 *"「권고 반영」을 적기 전에 `git diff`로 확인한다"* 조항을 **위임자가 직원 보고를 검증하라는 뜻으로만** 읽은 것이었다. **자기신고는 계층을 타고 올라가도 자기신고다.**

## 못 본 것 — 통과로 적지 않는다

실기기·WebGPU·모바일 터치·스크린리더. 저사양 기기에서 두 번째 WebGL 컨텍스트가 실제로 실패하는 경로(`try/catch`+`setStatus`는 넣었으나 재현 미확인).

**CI 스모크는 딥링크 세션을 한 번도 열지 않는다** — 7세션은 1회 수동 실측이지 게이트가 아니다. 백로그 **`G-DL1`**에 처방과 안 고친 이유를 함께 등록했다.

author: edgehero
body:
Closes #104.

Two loose ends the #99 docs audit found and left alone, each being a change to a file that audit did not own.

## 1. `docs/launch-kit.md:125` pointed at packaging steps that did not exist

The pi.dev showcase bullet sent the reader to `docs/demo.md` *"+ the packaging steps"*. `demo.md` is a screen-recording shot list with no packaging section, and the packaging steps were in no file at all, so the reference dead-ended on the one task it exists to support. The word "packaging" appeared exactly once across `docs/`, `specs/` and both READMEs: in that bullet.

**Written rather than dropped**, because the machinery already exists and only the description was missing. The new `## Packaging the extension` section records:

- what makes it a pi package (the `pi` block), and that `extensions` points at the **esbuild bundle** rather than source, with pi as a `peerDependency` so the operator's own pi satisfies it;
- why `files: ["dist", "skills"]` is load-bearing (the build preserves `import.meta.url`, so `../skills` resolves from inside `dist/`), and that `prepublishOnly` is what puts `dist/` in a tarball it is gitignored out of;
- the scoped-name rule and why the bare name can never appear in copyable text;
- what `pi install npm:@edgehero/pi-dispatch-admin` actually needs to resolve, which is why the install line plus `/dispatch` is the whole quickstart;
- how `release.yml` publishes it: gated on `npm view` returning a 404, tagged `admin-v*`, with `--access public` living in the workflow because there is no `publishConfig` in the manifest.

The bullet now points at that section and states what is already true, that the extension ships as a scoped `pi-package` today, so a submission is a pointer rather than work. `demo.md`'s gallery-card bullet, the other half of the pair, gets the same link. The stale version snapshot in the same file (still naming the 0.7.0 release) is refreshed.

## 2. `deploy/pause-windows.json` was read by nothing

The worker resolves this file only through `PI_PAUSE_WINDOWS_FILE`. The empty one an operator runs is scaffolded into the **deployment folder** by `pi-dispatch init`, and the populated example is `pause-windows.example.json` at the repo root. Its presence under `deploy/` implied it was part of the deployment artifacts, and `worker/deploy/` is that set, which it was not in.

Nothing in `worker/`, `admin/`, the tests, the workflows, the Dockerfiles, the compose file, any `files` array or any doc read it. Its entire history is the one commit that added it.

The `.gitignore` comment calling it *"the deployed default (empty)"* was already false and now names `init` instead. The sibling claim about `deploy/triggers.json` is deliberately left alone: that file **is** read, by `receiver/test/start.test.mjs` and `receiver/test/config.test.mjs`.

**The existing sync test could not have caught this.** `publish.test.mjs` enumerates `worker/deploy` and only indexes root `deploy/` *by name*, so a stray there is invisible to it, which is how this file lived unread since the day it was added. Added the other direction: root `deploy/` must hold the mirrored set plus the example triggers file and nothing else. The next config file dropped among the service templates now has to be classified rather than absorbed.

## Checked and unchanged

`INT-PAUSE-WINDOWS-FILE-CONTRACT` describes the file's shape and the `PI_PAUSE_WINDOWS_FILE` resolution, neither of which this touches, and `docs/pause-windows.md` already enumerated the two real files without mentioning the deleted one.

## Verification

- Full suite with a live Valkey in the CI posture: **1958 tests, 0 failures, 0 skipped**.
- The new `deploy/` assertion was verified against a planted stray file, and goes red as intended.
- `grep -rn "deploy/pause-windows"` now returns only the comment in the new test explaining why the assertion exists.

This is also the first PR to prove out #105: it is mostly docs and a deletion, exactly the shape that reported **zero** checks before the trigger fix.

author: shd101wyy
body:
## Summary

Arrays of RC/reference elements were **uncompilable**. `Array(Box(i32), 2)(box(i32(42)), box(i32(7)))` emitted invalid C in both compilers. Three distinct defects, all reached from that one reproducer — and all sharing a root confusion with the Stage-0 marker hole fixed in #79.

This also **unblocks the Stage-0 indexed-borrow regression test** that #79 had to land without, which was the motivation for picking this up.

## The three defects

**1. `Array(T, N)(...)` claimed to be a compile-time constant even with runtime elements.** The constructor path *manufactured* `UnknownValue` placeholders for runtime elements and then stamped the array as a comptime value anyway. Codegen dutifully routed it to the constant emitter, which has no case for an Unknown:

```c
.data = { /* skip generating: <comptime Box(i32)> */, /* skip generating: ... */ }
```

An empty initializer slot → `error: expected expression`.

The array-**literal** path (`values/array.ts`) already guarded with `every(val => !!val)` — which is precisely why `[a, b,]` worked while `Array(T, N)(a, b)` did not. Both compilers had the identical bug, down to the identical placeholder comment. Fixed by mirroring the literal path: an `UnknownValue` means *"type known, value not"* — a runtime element — and does not count as a compile-time value.

**2. Codegen had no dispatch for the runtime constructor shape.** The literal form reaches `generateAnonymousArray` through its `array` head; the type-constructor form has no such head. Now routed by **shape** instead — an array-typed call carrying runtime args and no compile-time value — so both forms share one emitter rather than duplicating logic. `generateAnonymousArray` turned out to be entirely head-agnostic and already handles the per-element deferred dups the constructor path attaches.

**3. The generated RC tracer subscripted the array *wrapper*.** `Array(T, N)` is emitted as `Array_…_N { T data[N]; }`, not a bare C array, so `sizeof(obj->a)/sizeof(obj->a[0])` and `obj->a[i]` produced *"subscripted value is not an array, pointer, or vector"* for any ref struct with an `Array(Box(T), N)` field — the first shape that ever needed such a tracer. Both the count and the access now go through `.data`. (Caught by the self-hosted test run after I'd ported only defects 1 and 2.)

## Root cause worth remembering

All three trace back to the same conflation as #79's Stage-0 hole: **an `UnknownValue` (meaning *runtime*, type known) being read as a compile-time value**. Per AGENTS.md, `$.value == undefined` means runtime while `UnknownValue` means "type known, value not" — so a bare truthiness test on `$.value` is wrong. That's now four bugs from this one distinction, which makes it worth watching wherever `$.value` is tested.

## Tests

Two, both previously impossible to write:

- **arrays of RC elements build at runtime, constructor and literal alike** — asserts the two forms agree on values *and* on element `rc` (they must not diverge in ownership), and that a fully compile-time array still folds to a constant.
- **an INDEXED borrowed argument is protected like a field projection** — the Stage-0 regression test #79 documented as blocked. A fixed-size `Array` field is the only shape that discriminates: `ArrayList` index reads go through the Index trait and yield an *owning* temp, so they were already safe at `+0` and a test built on them passes with or without the fix.

`issues/array-of-rc-constructor-emits-invalid-c.md` moves to `issues/fixed/` with the full resolution; the aliasing issue doc is updated to note the test is no longer blocked.

## Validation

| Gate | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `tests/rc.test.yo` | **33/33 under BOTH compilers** (2 new) |
| Reproducer | constructor and literal now agree exactly (values + element rc); comptime array still folds |
| Guard Malloc | clean |
| Self-hosted battery (hollow detection) | 0 failures, hollow=0 |
| Differential corpus | **155 PASS / 0 DIFF** |
| `check ./std` | 153/153 |
| Stage-2 → clang → stage-3 | **FIXPOINT HOLDS**, hollow=0 |
| TS fast suite | see checks |

body: Change the universe job bucket size from 100000 to 1048576 (1Mi) seeds and label each batch by its seed hex prefix (0x000, 0x001, ...) instead of the old 100k/1M scheme. author: red-sprout
body:
Closes #32

## 배경

정산 공유 링크는 앱을 쓰지 않는 동행자에게 확정 정산 결과를 전달하는 기능이라 인증 없이 조회할 수 있어야 한다. 정책과 서버 구현은 together-trip/togethertrip-server-main#142에서 확정했다.

`application-prod.yml`의 `gateway.security.public-paths`에 `/api/settlement-shares`가 없어 `GatewayAuthenticationFilter`가 401로 차단하고 있었다. main의 `SecurityConfig`만 열어도 gateway에서 먼저 막히므로 양쪽 모두 공개 경로로 지정해야 기능이 동작한다.

## 변경 내용

**공개 경로 추가.** `GatewaySecurityProperties`의 기본 목록과 `application-prod.yml`의 `public-paths` 양쪽에 `/api/settlement-shares`를 넣었다. prod yml이 목록을 통째로 덮어쓰므로 한쪽만 고치면 프로파일에 따라 동작이 갈린다.

**rate limit 적용.** 무인증으로 열리는 경로이므로 제한 대상에 포함했다. 토큰이 32바이트 난수라 추측 공격의 실익은 낮지만, 유출된 토큰을 대량으로 조회하는 트래픽을 막을 수단이 없었다. `SensitiveEndpointRateLimitFilter`가 `resolvePolicy` 진입 직후 POST가 아니면 곧바로 반환하고 있어, GET 경로를 먼저 판정하도록 순서를 바꿨다. 제한 키는 로그인과 동일하게 client IP 기준이다.

한도는 `GATEWAY_SETTLEMENT_SHARE_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE`로 조정한다. 기본값 분당 60회는 링크 하나를 여러 동행자가 함께 열어보는 사용 패턴을 고려한 값이다.

## 검증

`./gradlew test` — 전체 85개 통과, 실패 0. `GatewayProductionSecurityConfigurationTest`가 함께 통과해 운영 프로파일 설정이 유효함을 확인했다.

`GatewayAuthenticationFilterTest`의 main 공개 경로 파라미터 목록에 `/api/settlement-shares`를 추가해 토큰 없이 통과하는지 확인한다.

`SensitiveEndpointRateLimitFilterTest`에 세 케이스를 추가했다.

- 같은 IP의 공유 조회가 한도를 넘으면 429
- 다른 remote address는 독립 key로 취급
- 공유 경로가 아닌 일반 GET은 제한 대상이 아님

기존 인증 필요 경로의 401 동작과 로그인·신고 rate limit에는 회귀가 없다.

## 제외 범위

공유 조회 응답의 캐시 헤더는 main에서 지정한다. 토큰 발급·회전 로직도 main 소관이다.

nginx 접근 로그의 토큰 마스킹은 together-trip/togethertrip-infra#59에서 다룬다.

CORS 허용 origin은 건드리지 않았다. 웹 공개 뷰 페이지 도메인이 확정된 뒤 `GATEWAY_CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS`에 반영한다.

## 배포 순서

이 PR과 main#142는 함께 배포해야 무인증 조회가 열린다. 한쪽만 반영하면 계속 401이 반환된다.

그 전에 together-trip/togethertrip-infra#59(PR together-trip/togethertrip-infra#62)가 먼저 배포되어야 한다. 공유 토큰이 쿼리 파라미터로 전달되는데 nginx access log가 기본 combined 포맷이라 토큰이 평문으로 기록되기 때문이다.

## 관련 이슈

- together-trip/togethertrip-server-main#142 — 무인증 조회 정책과 토큰 회전
- together-trip/togethertrip-infra#59 — nginx access log 토큰 마스킹
- together-trip/togethertrip-client-flutter#68 — 앱 링크 생성·복사·재발급
- together-trip/togethertrip-web#15 — 웹 공개 뷰 페이지

body:
## Summary

You couldn't see Nova because it was only wired to the channel-officer **missed-commercials** page. This puts it on the main **Reconciliations / Summary Sheet** that everyone uses, as a **scope-level** chat (account + channel + month) so a user can ask "which spots didn't match / what happened" and drill into any of them.

## Changes
- **New tool `list_unmatched_spots(account_id, channel, month)`** — lists the spots that didn't reconcile (Not Aired / No Mapping / Programme Mismatch / Late Telecast) from `MatchResult`, with a per-status tally, so Nova can enumerate them and then investigate any one by `schedule_row_id`.
- **`chat_with_nova` now accepts a scope payload** `{account_id, channel, month}` in addition to a single `{schedule_row_id}`. Scope chats are gated by `_account_access` (per-brand); session keyed per scope. Persona explains both entry modes.
- **Widget generalised** — `openNovaScope(account, channel, month, label)` alongside `openNova(spot)`; the submit handler posts whichever base payload.
- **Summary Sheet** — a floating **"Ask Nova"** button (appears once a scope is selected) + the widget include. The button/panel render only when `account_id & channel & month` are set (confirmed the view passes those).

## How it behaves
Open the Summary Sheet for a client/channel/month → click **Ask Nova** → ask "which spots didn't match?" → Nova calls `list_unmatched_spots`, gives a tally ("12 Not Aired, 3 No Mapping"), and offers to dig into any of them — cross-checking LMRB (programme-name-agnostic), the brand mapping, and the whole-system theme search, exactly like the per-spot flow. It still never links a match without your explicit in-chat confirmation (Tier 3).

## Testing
`AgentToolsTest.test_list_unmatched_spots` (excludes matched rows, tallies statuses) and `NovaChatEndpointTest.test_scope_mode_accepted`. All agent tests pass; `manage.py check` clean; widget JS syntax-checked.

> Same live-key caveat as before: `GEMINI_API_KEY` isn't in the sandbox, so real Gemini replies can only be confirmed on the deployed site; the tool layer + endpoint + graceful/no-key paths are covered by tests.
