body:
Implements #11. Drivers declare the subset of registry metric names they produce; `metrics.py` remains the single source of truth for name, unit, scale and bounds. `store/schema.py` generates new tables from the declaration; reads answer from introspected columns so an existing full-registry database is untouched (proven byte-identical by building one with the old code and reopening it — zero ALTERs, history readable, rollups clean); writes are strict against the declaration, and the drift KeyError is documented as collection-fatal by design.

`GET /api/capabilities` reports per device what it produces with a three-state contract (described / present-but-undescribed / no device), shaped for #12's page work. A declaration empty at either level still records failed-poll gaps and skips the rollup it cannot feed. Adding an inverter metric remains a one-line change, proven by test; the per-module pairing with `BatteryModuleSample` is now documented.

Went through two adversarial review rounds (four-lens panel + codex); all findings fixed test-first, including an empty-declaration rollup crash and a gap-recording break for module-only declarations. Gates: 735 tests, ruff check, format, mypy strict.

**Merge after #24** — both touch `routes.py`/`test_api.py`; the combination was gate-checked locally.

author: tmori
body:
## Summary

Fix the Launcher background-session race exposed by the v1.6.6 `test` job.

## Root cause

`claim_session()` held the session preparation lock while calling the existing Launcher's `status` control endpoint. At the same time, the owner control thread could call `persist(force=True)`, which tried to acquire the same lock in fail-fast mode. Depending on scheduling, the owner thread raised `LauncherControlError`, exited, and the control client later timed out.

This was the failure in Actions run `31240245880`, job `93059891143` (`test_live_session_is_not_overwritten`).

## Changes

- Keep competing launch reservations fail-fast by default.
- Allow the existing session owner to use a bounded lock wait while persisting its state.
- Split `claim_session()` into an inspect/probe/revalidate flow so network I/O does not run while holding the preparation lock.
- Re-read and compare `session_id` before replacing a stale session, refusing replacement when ownership changed during the probe.
- Add deterministic regression tests for:
  - probing a live owner without holding the preparation lock;
  - owner persistence surviving a concurrently held preparation lock;
  - a changed owner never being overwritten.

## Validation

Locally exercised the focused race tests and the existing live/stale-session scenarios:

- 7 focused tests passed.
- The previous live-session race reproduction passed 20 consecutive runs.

The repository's full GitHub Actions suite is the authoritative cross-platform validation for this draft PR.

author: devthejo
body:
Ouverte en brouillon : revue adversariale en cours.

## Constat, relevé en production

```
AxiosError: Request failed with status code 404
    at getMetaData (backend/lib/teleservices/demarches-simplifiees.ts:265:20)
    at DemarchesSimplifiees.toInternal (…:281:16)
→ unhandledRejection
→ pm2 tente de le diffuser et échoue : Converting circular structure to JSON
```

**L'erreur disparaît entièrement.** Le processus survit (211 redémarrages inchangés sur 7 h, 2 réponses 502 sur la journée toutes deux imputables à un déploiement), mais rien n'arrive dans Sentry et rien d'exploitable n'est journalisé.

## Cause — l'appelant, pas le téléservice

`backend/controllers/teleservices/index.ts:132` :

```js
return function (req, res) {                    // ← pas de `next`
  return Promise.resolve(createClass(…).toInternal())
    .then(function (fields) { … })              // ← pas de `.catch`
}
```

Express 4.21 **ignore la promesse renvoyée par un gestionnaire**. Le rejet n'a aucun receveur. Effet secondaire : **la requête reste pendante**, aucune réponse n'est jamais émise.

La preuve que c'est bien ce chemin : `getMetaData` est appelé par `toInternal` **et** `toExternal`, mais `toExternal` passe par `exportRepresentation` (`:233`), qui a déjà `.catch(next)`. La trace nomme `toInternal:281`. Les deux sœurs avaient divergé.

**Sur la structure circulaire** : une vraie `AxiosError` définit `toJSON()`, donc `JSON.stringify(err)` ne lève pas. Vérifié avec l'axios du dépôt :

```
stringify(err)    → OK (toJSON utilisé)
stringify({...e}) → LÈVE : Converting circular structure to JSON
```

pm2 **recopie** l'erreur avant `process.send` ; la copie superficielle perd le `toJSON` et expose la boucle `req`/`res`.

## La classe, pas seulement l'instance

Rattrapés au même titre : `routes/proxy.ts:5`, `controllers/simulation.ts:231` (`await` hors du `try`), `controllers/followups.ts:152/166/121`, `controllers/webhook.ts:83`, `controllers/moncomptepro.ts`.

Déjà corrects, et instructifs : `routes/openfisca.ts` porte le commentaire « Express 4 ne rattrape pas les rejets d'un gestionnaire asynchrone ». **Le projet connaissait la classe** ; elle avait seulement été oubliée ailleurs.

## Dégrader ou échouer ? — échouer, en 502

`toInternal` n'existe que pour montrer à l'usager **les champs exacts** transmis au tiers avant son consentement. Sans le schéma, les libellés sont inconnus : dégrader afficherait un écran de consentement vide ou faux, et le `POST` échouerait de toute façon ensuite. C'est le repli silencieux que la règle du dépôt interdit.

`getMetaData` lève donc une `TeleserviceMetadataError` — nommée, plate, copiable, portant `procedure`, `upstreamUrl`, `upstreamStatus`, et un `code = 502` que `httpStatusOf` traduit en statut de réponse.

## Le garde-fou qui manquait

Nouveau `backend/lib/process-error-handlers.ts`, monté depuis `configure.ts` (donc `server.ts` **et** `dev.ts`) : journalise un résumé plat puis remonte à Sentry, sans dépendre de la sérialisation de pm2.

**Volontairement pas de `uncaughtException`** : y poser un écouteur neutralise l'arrêt par défaut de Node et ferait tourner le processus dans un état corrompu. Ce serait le repli silencieux, pas son contraire.

## Le 500 récurrent sur `POST /followup`

**Il n'était pas identifiable depuis les journaux, et c'est là le défaut** : `persist` appelait `Sentry.captureException` **sans un seul `console.error`**. La seule empreinte serveur est la ligne d'accès de morgan. La cause n'a jamais existé côté machine.

Deux défauts réels en sont sortis :

1. **La classification manquait les 4xx.** Le test était `error.message === ErrorType.UnsupportedPhoneNumberFormat`, en égalité stricte. Le refus du fournisseur arrive imbriqué — `SMS request failed. Body: {…"Invalid destination address"…}` — donc jamais reconnu, donc **500**. Or c'est une erreur d'entrée, déterministe : le même numéro donne le même refus. C'est exactement la forme observée cette nuit, `05:49:04` puis `05:52:57` sur la **même** simulation.
2. **`persist` annulait une exclusion Sentry délibérée.** `sms-service.ts:107` porte « Avoid sending invalid destination address error to sentry », puis relance ; `persist` rattrapait et le signalait quand même. Le front traite déjà ce cas par un message dédié. Trois couches d'accord, une qui contredisait.

Corrigé en 422, avec `console.error` structuré, et Sentry réservé aux vraies pannes. Le corps de réponse est inchangé : la détection `invalid-address` du front continue de fonctionner.

**Restant, non corrigé** — si l'usager donne courriel *et* téléphone et que le SMS échoue, le courriel est déjà parti et le suivi créé, mais la réponse est un échec ; il réessaie, et obtient un second suivi et un second courriel. Corriger demande de changer la forme de la réponse et le front : à trancher avec vous.

## Vérification

Fichiers de production remis à `origin/main` **un par un**, tests conservés :

| fichier restauré | résultat |
|---|---|
| `controllers/teleservices/index.ts` | 1 échec — `next` jamais appelé |
| `lib/teleservices/demarches-simplifiees.ts` | 1 échec — pas une `TeleserviceMetadataError` |
| `controllers/followups.ts` | 3 échecs — 422 attendu, Sentry appelé à tort, rien journalisé |

Aucun attendu n'est calculé par la fonction testée. `JSON.stringify({ ...error })` reproduit littéralement ce que fait pm2.

`npx prettier --check .` ✓ · `npm run lint` ✓ · **`npm test` exit 0 — 57 fichiers, 25 082 tests** ✓ · `npm run build` ✓

## Deux changements de comportement assumés, à connaître avant de merger

Un harnais différentiel local a envoyé 54 requêtes identiques aux deux
révisions, sur de vrais serveurs, mêmes stubs et même base : **45 réponses
identiques**, 4 écarts voulus (les requêtes qui pendaient répondent désormais),
5 artefacts de construction. Il a mis au jour deux effets de bord qui ne se
lisent pas dans le diff.

**1. `POST /api/webhook/rdv` répond 500 quand Mattermost est en panne.**
`MATTERMOST_POST_URL` est renseignée en production, donc le cas est réel.
Signature valide, Mattermost injoignable :

| révision | réponse |
|---|---|
| `main` | `200 {"message":"OK"}` |
| cette branche | `500 {"code":"ECONNREFUSED", …}` |

`rdv-aide-numerique` lira ce 500 comme « réessaie plus tard » et **renverra
l'événement**. Le 200 précédent mentait — la notification ne partait pas — mais
c'est bien un contrat inter-services qui change. **C'est assumé** : mieux vaut
un rappel qu'une notification perdue en silence. Signalé ici pour que l'équipe
RDV le sache plutôt que de le découvrir pendant une panne.

À noter : une panne Mattermost prolongée produira des rappels répétés, et des
messages en double dans le canal une fois le service revenu, chaque rappel
republiant.

**2. La veille nocturne des liens ne tombe plus sur une notification ratée.**
`Mattermost.post` propage désormais ses erreurs ; `tools/check-links-validity.ts`
l'appelait sans `await` ni `.catch`, et ce module n'installe aucun gestionnaire
de processus — le rejet arrêtait le programme **après** « Terminé », donc après
une mise à jour Grist réussie, et le cron passait au rouge. Corrigé au dernier
commit. Mesuré, URL vide et URL injoignable :

| révision | sortie |
|---|---|
| `main` | 0 |
| avant le correctif | **1** |
| après le correctif | 0, la cause restant journalisée |

Le premier jet de ce correctif journalisait l'objet d'erreur brut — 186 lignes,
dont **six occurrences de l'URL du webhook**, portée par `path`, `pathname` et
`_header`. Cette URL est le moyen d'authentification du webhook, et les journaux
Actions de ce dépôt sont publics : GitHub ne masque que la valeur *exacte* d'un
secret, pas ses fragments. Le journal passe donc par `formatRejection`, éprouvé
sur 17 formes d'erreur — DNS, TLS, redirections, proxy, corps d'erreur reprenant
l'URL : aucune ne fait ressortir le jeton.

Le partage est délibéré : une panne passagère laisse le compte rendu vert, une
URL absente le fait échouer — aucun réessai ne répare une configuration
manquant

body: `require-error-code-in-thrown-error` tested the *identifier's name* against `ERR_CODE_PATTERN` rather than the value it holds, so a message that plainly starts with an `ERR_*` code was reported as `missingErrorCode` whenever it was stored in an ordinary-named variable first. Unlike its sibling interpolation rules, this rule did no scope/initializer resolution at all. ```js const { ERR_SYSTEM } = require("./error_codes.cjs"); const errorMsg = `${ERR_SYSTEM}: ${result.stderr}`; throw new Error(errorMsg); // reported missingErrorCode — the message is coded ``` ## Changes - **Initializer resolution** — for a plain `Identifier` message argument, resolve its write-once local initializer with `resolveWriteOnceInitializerChain` (the helper already used by `no-exec-interpolated-command` and `no-github-request-interpolated-route`) and evaluate `messageReferencesErrorCode` against the resolved expression. - **Silence over guessing** — only report when the resolved value is statically message-like (`Literal`, `TemplateLiteral`, or `+` `BinaryExpression`). Parameters, reassigned bindings, and call results (e.g. `getErrorMessage(e)` re-thrown behind a `startsWith(\`${ERR_CONFIG}:\`)` guard in `update_release.cjs`) are left alone — false positives are worse than silence for a `"suggestion"`-severity consistency rule. - **Tests** — coded template held in a plain-named variable (including a one-hop alias chain) is valid; unresolvable values are valid; `const msg = "no code here"; throw new Error(msg);` remains invalid. Against `actions/setup/js`, the rule's warning count drops 105 → 97; the three call sites cited in the issue no longer fire, and the remaining warnings in those files are genuinely uncoded messages. body:
## Summary

- reject top-level `null`, arrays, and other non-object JSON bodies across the Claude, Codex, Grok, and Claude Desktop native-toggle routes;
- require a boolean `enabled` field through one shared type guard before any desired-state or artifact mutation;
- restore the live Claude config snapshot when persistence fails, so a lock refusal cannot leave memory ahead of disk or make a same-object retry look idempotent;
- add route-level regressions for all four native toggles and a real-lock same-object retry regression.

## Why

The original Claude route parsed JSON into an object-shaped TypeScript variable and immediately read `body.enabled`. JSON `null` therefore bypassed malformed-JSON handling and raised a TypeError. The same runtime assumption remained in the Codex, Grok, and Claude Desktop sibling routes.

A deeper review found a second Claude-specific failure mode. The route changed `config.claudeCode` before calling the persistence seam. If the config lock returned 409/500, the live object stayed changed even though disk did not. Retrying with that same server snapshot then hit the “already current” branch and skipped persistence entirely.

The shared guard now rejects non-object bodies before every native-toggle mutation. Claude persistence remains the commit point: any thrown save restores the exact prior property state before returning or rethrowing.

## Verification

- Bun 1.3.14: four native-toggle suites **51/51 passed**.
- Bun 1.4.0-canary.1 (`b22e0e6d0`): the same four suites **51/51 passed**.
- The real config-lock regression retries the same live object after 409 and confirms the second request persists the change.
- `bun x tsc --noEmit`: passed.
- `bun scripts/privacy-scan.ts`: passed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- Two independent exact-diff reviews found no remaining P0–P3 issues.
- Windows full suite: attempted, **not passed and not counted as verification**. Bun 1.3.14 terminated after 264.9 seconds with its known `--isolate` internal assertion while entering the storage-policy tests; no test failure was reported before the runtime crash.

## Checklist

- [x] Invalid bodies are rejected before desired-state, config, or artifact mutation.
- [x] A failed Claude save restores the live snapshot and the same object can retry.
- [x] Existing successful toggle semantics remain covered.

Draft pending exact-head upstream CI and fresh maintainer review.

body:
## Summary

The Uploader previously only ever published to YouTube, even though `VideoGen` already writes a `Sidecar` JSON declaring multi-platform targets (`youtube`, `instagram`, `facebook`, `tiktok`) for every vertical short. `Program.cs` carried its own private, YouTube-only config/upload logic and never touched the existing `Sidecar`/`IPublisher` scaffolding, so that multi-platform data was silently discarded on every run.

This PR:
- Adds `YouTubePublisher`, `FacebookPublisher`, and `TikTokPublisher` (`IPublisher` implementations), alongside the existing `InstagramPublisher`.
- Rewrites `Uploader/Program.cs` to dispatch each video's sidecar `Targets` to the matching publisher, track per-platform `Publications`, respect per-platform run quotas, and only move a video to `\done` once every target has reached a terminal state.
- Adds `TikTokTokenCapture`, a one-time OAuth bootstrap console tool (mirrors the existing `TokenCapture` for YouTube), since TikTok had no equivalent flow.
- Adds `appsettings.Local.json` support to the Uploader so secrets never need to touch tracked config (`VideoGen` already had this pattern).
- Adds `GiggleGarden.sln` tying all five projects together for a single build/IDE view.
- Fills in the real (non-secret) Instagram/Facebook IDs in tracked config and adds the licensed background-music asset.

## Bugs found and fixed along the way (not part of the original scope)

- `Uploader.csproj` was missing a `<ProjectReference>` to `Shared` — the pre-existing `Publishing/` folder already depended on `GiggleGarden.Shared` types, so the project would not have built even before this change.
- `appsettings.json` was still the old flat, YouTube-only shape after the config model was redesigned for multi-platform, silently dropping every `Platforms.*` setting.

## What a reviewer should know

- Instagram and Facebook are fully live-tested: a real long-lived Page access token (verified via Meta's `debug_token` endpoint — `is_valid`, correct scopes, `expires_at: 0`) is wired up, and both `IgUserId`/`PageId` are set.
- TikTok is still `Enabled: false` pending the Developer app's Login Kit / redirect URI setup and the one-time `TikTokTokenCapture` run; the publisher code is complete but untested end-to-end.
- `DirectPost` defaults to `false` (drafts-to-inbox mode) since TikTok's Direct Post requires an audited app — this is documented in `AppConfig.cs`.
- The whole solution builds clean (`dotnet build GiggleGarden.sln`, 0 warnings/errors) and the Uploader was dry-run tested against fake videos to confirm the approval-gate and terminal-state/move-to-done logic work correctly without hitting live APIs.
- No secrets are committed — verified via diff review before each commit; real keys/tokens live only in gitignored `appsettings.Local.json` files.
- Note on repo history: `main` was previously just GitHub's auto-generated README commit, unrelated to this project's actual history. It was force-updated to point at this project's real baseline commit (with your explicit approval) so this PR could be opened normally.

author: yambay-steveg
body:
Closes **A3.2**, the last hand-edit in a system whose premise is that cardctl is the single validated writer.

`link` writes the id and date; the note — what that stint actually accomplished — was left to a human or an AI editing the card body directly. Every session wrap-up therefore ended with the one thing the conventions tell sessions never to do.

```bash
cardctl note <card.md> "swept the vaults and retired the buttons"   # the pinned session
cardctl note <card.md> "did the earlier half" --session <id>        # an older entry
cardctl note <card.md> ""                                           # clear it
```

- **Defaults to the pinned session** — "note what I just did" is the whole use case. `--session` targets an older entry, which is what the convention actually asks for when you fill in the stint you just displaced.
- **Preserves the date `link` wrote**; only the note after it is rewritten.
- **Surgical**: rewrites the single matching line, leaving every other byte alone. The history is hand-readable markdown that also carries lines cardctl can't parse — a test asserts those survive byte-identical.
- Same guards as the other writers (card exists, inside a configured `Cards/` folder), and it fails with a *useful* error: no entry for that id tells you to `cardctl link` first, no pin tells you to pin one.

## Tests (238 → 248)
Writes the note, preserves the date, replaces rather than appends, clears on empty, targets an older entry without touching the pinned one, leaves unparsed lines byte-identical, and both failure modes plus both guards.

## The point
The SessionStart hook's conventions block has said for months that `latest` and `## Sessions` "lack a cardctl writer for now — edit those two minimally by hand". With #65 and this, **that exception is gone**: the hook now says nothing on a card needs a hand-edit.

author: pcfreak30
body:
Adds MCP OAuth client registration and protocol requirements needed by OAuth-capable MCP clients such as ChatGPT.

The previous dummy authorization server exposed discovery and authorization endpoints but did not advertise or implement client registration, did not enforce PKCE, did not bind tokens to the MCP resource, and did not issue refresh tokens. ChatGPT reported that DCR and CIMD were unavailable.

Changes:

- Add RFC 7591 dynamic client registration at `/oauth/register`.
- Advertise the registration endpoint, refresh-token grant, S256 PKCE, and `offline_access`.
- Require registered redirect URIs.
- Allow registered HTTPS callbacks for hosted clients and loopback callbacks for native clients.
- Require S256 PKCE on authorization requests and verify `code_verifier` during token exchange.
- Require the RFC 8707 `resource` parameter on authorization and token requests.
- Issue and exchange in-memory refresh tokens with a 30-day lifetime.
- Preserve OAuth parameters in the authorization form.
- Document explicit `--oauth` usage and distinguish ngrok/cloudflared from OpenAI Secure MCP Tunnel.

CIMD is not implemented. DCR is the compatibility fallback supported by current MCP clients; adding CIMD would require fetching and validating client metadata documents from remote URLs.

Build, vet, and the MCP race suite pass.

---

<!-- kody-pr-summary:start -->
Based on the code changes, this pull request enhances the MCP server's OAuth implementation to be fully compatible with remote MCP clients like ChatGPT by implementing complete OAuth 2.0 and RFC 9728/8414/7591 specifications.

## Summary

The changes transform the OAuth implementation from a simplified "dummy" authorization server into a standards-compliant OAuth provider that supports dynamic client registration, PKCE enforcement, and refresh tokens, enabling integration with remote MCP clients.

## Key Changes

### 1. **Dynamic Client Registration (RFC 7591)**
- Added a new `/oauth/register` endpoint for client registration
- Supports registering clients with HTTPS redirect URIs (previously limited to loopback callbacks only)
- Issues client IDs and manages registered client metadata in memory
- Validates redirect URIs, allowing both HTTPS callbacks for web clients and loopback for native clients

### 2. **Enhanced Authorization Flow**
- Strict PKCE enforcement: only S256 code challenge method is supported (removed `plain` support)
- Added RFC 8707 resource binding validation
- Authorization requests now validate against registered clients
- Login page now preserves all OAuth parameters during the authorization code flow

### 3. **Refresh Token Support**
- Added RFC 8414 refresh token grant type
- Access tokens expire after 1 hour; refresh tokens valid for 30 days
- Refresh tokens rotate with each use, issuing new token pairs
- Updated authorization server metadata to advertise `refresh_token` grant support

### 4. **Security Improvements**
- Require PKCE (S256) for all authorization code exchanges
- Validate resource binding per RFC 8707
- Enforce client registration before allowing authorization
- Support registered HTTPS redirect URIs while maintaining loopback restrictions for unregistered clients

### 5. **Documentation Updates**
- Added documentation explaining the OAuth flow for remote MCP clients
- Clarified the distinction between the new OAuth features and OpenAI Secure MCP Tunnel product
- Added usage examples with tunneling options (ngrok/cloudflared)

## Compatibility

These changes make the MCP server compatible with OAuth-enabled MCP clients like ChatGPT by providing:
- Full RFC 9728 protected-resource metadata
- RFC 8414 authorization-server metadata
- RFC 7591 client registration
- PKCE authorization code flow with refresh tokens

The server remains intentionally simple: the shared `--auth-token` is the only credential, entered as the password during authorization, with all registrations and tokens stored in memory.

body:
## Summary

Completes the current Provincial Discovery Experience foundation and validates it across Gauteng and Western Cape.

The province page now acts as a discovery and composition layer while preserving the canonical search authorities introduced through S1-S3.

## What changed

- Extended provincial discovery configuration across all nine provinces.
- Preserved neutral province discovery without silently selecting Buy or Rent.
- Added canonical province/city/suburb handoff through existing search authority.
- Added explicit sibling multi-location OR support.
- Added province search handoff for Buy, Rent and Developments.
- Kept Rent controls limited to supported property type and budget filters.
- Kept Shared Living independent and deferred.
- Kept Commercial and Land/Plots visibly deferred.
- Kept preview Search Areas out of production.
- Reused the established provincial hero, composer and discovery sections.
- Hardened shared location autosuggest accessibility.
- Improved selected-location contrast.
- Disabled noncanonical market shortcuts generically rather than routing invalid geography.
- Added Western Cape cross-province acceptance using canonical Western Cape and Cape Town identities.

## Product behavior

### Neutral

Province visits remain neutral until the customer deliberately selects a property journey.

### Buy

Province + Buy hands off to canonical Buy search.

### Rent

Province + Rent remains Rent through URL generation, reload and search intent reconstruction.

### Geography

Canonical geography IDs are preserved through the provincial composer and search handoff.

### Multi-location

Explicit sibling selections preserve OR semantics rather than collapsing to a shared parent.

### Search Areas

No preview Search Areas were activated and no new production Search Area boundaries were introduced.

### Deferred journeys

Shared Living is not proxied through Rent. Commercial and Land/Plots remain truthful about their deferred state.

## Cross-province acceptance

Western Cape was used as the second materially different province to test whether the architecture contained hidden Gauteng assumptions.

Results:

- neutral Western Cape remains neutral;
- Western Cape Buy produces canonical province-scoped Buy intent;
- Western Cape Rent remains Rent;
- Cape Town canonical identity survives Rent handoff and reload;
- unsupported Rent controls remain absent;
- no Search Areas were activated;
- noncanonical Stellenbosch presentation does not create invalid navigation;
- no Western Cape-specific UX architecture was introduced.

The provincial architecture can therefore be considered cross-province accepted.

The remaining seven provinces require lightweight canonical/data smoke coverage rather than separate feature-development slices.

## Validation

- Focused Vitest: 70/70 passed
- Provincial Playwright: 14/14 passed
- Typecheck: passed
- Targeted ESLint: passed with zero errors
- Prettier: passed
- git diff --check: passed
- Production build: passed

Existing repository build chunk-size advisory remains unchanged.

## Findings

- P0: none
- P1: none
- P2: none
- P3:
  - existing build chunk-size advisory
  - lightweight canonical/data smoke coverage for remaining provinces

## Scope intentionally excluded

This PR does not include:

- city or suburb page redesign;
- Cape Town destination-page redesign;
- new search-engine architecture;
- new Search Area production boundaries;
- Shared Living implementation;
- commercial or Land/Plots implementation;
- unrelated repository cleanup.

## Commits

- `132588492cb7d9e722b8c275554108153a1be631` — generalized provincial discovery continuation
- `f0b5f62ab864b1745b7cfa5b3bdf7b82efaad32c` — Western Cape acceptance and generic hardening

author: westonplatter
body:
## Summary

IBKR FlexQuery credentials move out of the `IB_JSON` environment blob and into a
`flexquery_tokens` table, encrypted at rest with Fernet. Each token carries its
report id, and `accounts` gains a nullable FK recording which token an account
was discovered under — so the token-to-account mapping lives in the database
instead of an operator's head. This is a hard cutover: `IB_JSON` is deleted, and
a job payload can no longer supply a credential.

It also fixes a real bug. `_resolve_flex_credentials(payload, None)` always took
the *first* `IB_JSON` entry, so a second configured token was never used by the
worker. Sync now runs every active token.

Implements `docs/plans/2026-08-07-001-feat-encrypted-flexquery-tokens-plan.md`.

## Features

- `flexquery_tokens` table: name, Fernet-encrypted token, `report_id`,
  `is_active`, `last_used_at`. Additive migration, no backfill.
- `EncryptedString` column type — encryption is transparent at the model
  attribute; the key never reaches the database server (unlike `pgcrypto`).
- Key rotation without downtime via `MultiFernet`: `FLEX_TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY`
  holds a comma-separated key list, first key encrypts, all keys decrypt.
- `scripts/manage_flex_tokens.py` — `add`, `list`, `deactivate`, `rotate-key`,
  `verify`, `generate-key`. The token value is read from stdin or a hidden
  prompt, never argv, and is never printed back.
- Accounts page shows which FlexQuery token each account came from, or
  "Not synced" when it hasn't been seen under one yet.
- Sync stamps `accounts.flex_query_token_id` as it creates account rows.
  Re-stamping is last-writer-wins with a masked warning log.

## Fixes

- Sync uses every active token, not just the first configured one.
- `flex_token` / `query_id` job-payload overrides removed. `jobs.payload` is a
  plaintext JSON column read by the API and frontend; a hand-enqueued job could
  have persisted a live token there. A prod audit found zero such rows, so this
  closed a latent hole rather than an active leak.
- Token values are kept out of error paths: third-party messages are redacted
  before landing in `jobs.result`, and `add` resolves the encryption key
  *before* reading the token, because a bind-parameter failure surfaces as a
  SQLAlchemy `StatementError` that echoes its parameters.

## Refactoring

`src/services/flex_credentials.py` is the single resolution point for both the
trades and positions handlers and `scripts/fetch_flex_trades.py`. The two job
handlers share `_run_flexquery_sync`, which iterates tokens, merges per-account
results into the existing response shape, and records per-token errors.

## Documentation

`docs/getting-started.md` gains a FlexQuery tokens section covering seeding,
verification, and key rotation. `AGENTS.md`, `.env.example`,
`docs/secrets-using-1password.md`, and `docs/trades-and-executions-sync.md` no
longer reference `IB_JSON`.

## Testing

The plan assumed no test framework and built verification around operator
scripts; #128 landed pytest in the meantime, so this adds real coverage instead:
22 tests over key handling, rotation, error hygiene, credential resolution, and
account stamping. The load-bearing one reads `token_encrypted` with raw SQL,
bypassing the decrypting column type, and asserts the stored value is not the
token.

## Additional notes

- Adds `cryptography` as a direct dependency (49.0.0, already present
  transitively). Per the 14-day cooldown in `AGENTS.md`, added with
  `--exclude-newer 2026-07-25`.
- Two generic account IDs (`U8675309`, `U7654321`) were added to the
  `scripts/ibkr_check.py` allowlist and to `prompts/prompt-ibkr-sample-data.md`
  so the demo fixture can show two tokens across four accounts. `U8675309` was
  already documented as a sanctioned value but missing from the checker.

## Deploy order

The cutover has no fallback — a worker without the key, or against an unseeded
table, cannot sync at all.

1. Snapshot, then `task migrate ENV=prod` (additive and reversible).
2. Create `FLEX_TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY` in 1Password, reference it from `.env.prod`.
3. `manage_flex_tokens.py add` per token, then `verify`.
4. Restart `worker:jobs`, run one trade sync, confirm accounts are stamped.

## Open item

`FLEX_TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY` lives in `.env.prod`, so the API process receives it
despite never decrypting a token. Scoping it to `worker:jobs` and the operator
CLI would narrow the exposure; left as-is for now.

author: llongmane584
body:
## 概要

Closes #62

原因は 2 つあった。**1 つ目が障害の本体**で、これがあると変形そのものが起きず、帯は
着地位置でも簡易表示のまま固まる = 計算結果が名前のない 2 つの数字になる。

### 原因 1: `--dock` が初回マウントで一度も書かれていなかった

`useDockMorph` を `ResultBand` (子) の中で呼び、書き込み先として**祖先である** sheet div の
ref を渡していた。React は commit フェーズで ref の attach と layout effect を子から親へ処理
するため、**子の `useLayoutEffect` の時点では祖先の ref はまだ `null`**。フックは
`scope === null` で何もせずに抜け、deps は以後変わらないので二度と走らない。

結果 `var(--dock, 1)` のフォールバックが永久に効き、帯は本来の位置に着地しても 47px の
簡易表示のまま = **見出しもラベルも出ない**。

**前回の検証がこれを見逃した理由**: `playwright-cli` で必ず `open` の直後に `resize` して
いた。既定幅 1280 から 375 への変更が `sm` ブレークポイントを越え、`isCompactViewport` の
反転で `morphSpan` が変わり、**その時だけ** effect が再実行されて `--dock` が書かれていた。
素のロードを一度も確認していなかった。

- `useDockMorph` の呼び出しを **App へ移す**。2 つの ref を所有しているのが App なので、
  App の `useLayoutEffect` が走る時点では両方 attach 済み。観測対象の DOM を所有している
  ところでフックを呼ぶ、が正しい形
- **フォールバックを 1 (簡易表示) から 0 (本来の姿) に変更**。`--dock` が書かれなかったとき、
  1 だと内容を隠したまま固まるが、0 なら最悪でも「ドックしない普通の結果領域」に留まり
  内容は失われない。沈黙して劣化する側に倒れてはいけない

### 原因 2: 切り落としを文字が見えている間に効かせていた

見出しとラベルを `max-height` + `overflow: hidden` で畳む処理を `--dock` 全域に線形で効かせて
いたため、本来の姿に見える領域でも文字が刻まれていた (`--dock` 0.5 で箱 10/20px)。
切り落としは文字が透明になった後でしか使ってはいけない処理だった。

- **見出し**: `max-height` の補間を削除し `font-size` を 14px → 0 で補間。行高を
  `headingLine / 14` の比で持つので箱は文字サイズに比例して縮み、**帯の高さの一次性**
  (ドック維持の不変条件の前提) は保たれ、しかもどの瞬間も切れない。比を 1.5 ではなく
  20/14 にしたのは #59 の `text-sm` と一致させるため —— `headingLine` も `fullHeight` も
  変わらないので、既に実測済みの着地位置をそのまま引き継げる
- **ラベル**: 3 段構えにする。

  | `--dock` | font-size | opacity | 箱 |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | 0 | 14 / 16px (= #59) | 1 | 21 / 24px (= #59) |
  | 0 → 0.3 | 数値と同率で縮小 (= #59 と同じ補間) | **1 (完全)** | 自然な高さ |
  | 0.3 → 0.45 | 同上 | 1 → 0 | 自然な高さ |
  | 0.45 → 0.54 | 同上 | 0 | `max-height` で 0 へ (**透明なので不可視**) |
  | 1.0 | 12px | 0 | 0 |

  **`--dock` ≤ 0.3 では常に完全なラベルが出る。フェードが終わってから畳み始めるので、
  箱が縮む区間では常に透明 —— 見えている間に縮小も切り落としも起きない。**

- 畳む区間を後ろに寄せられるのは、ラベルの箱が `gridMin` がセル実寸を上回っている間は
  帯の高さに寄与しないから。ただし wide ではセル実寸 (`61.5 - 21d`) と `gridMin` (`80 - 54d`)
  が `d = 0.56` で交差するので、その手前の 0.54 で畳み終える

## 維持したもの

簡易表示 **47px**、**遅れ 0** のスクロール追従、量子化なし、変形距離 140/131px、文書高一定。
`useDockMorph` の中身・スペーサー・`DOCK_ABSORB`・`BAND_COMPACT` の寸法・`index.css` は
変更していないので、#60 の 2 つの要求 (干渉低減・移行の高速化) の成果はそのまま残る。

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm lint` / `pnpm build` / `pnpm test`
- [x] **素のロード (リサイズなし) で `--dock` が書かれる** —— 修正前は sheet の `style` 属性
      そのものが存在しなかった。今回の障害を直接押さえる回帰確認
- [x] 375x667 / 900x800 を**いずれも冷間マウント**して 2px 刻みで 131 点走査、違反 0:
  - 見出しは全点で「箱の高さ = line-height」(切り落としが無いことの証明)
  - ラベルは opacity > 0 の全点で「箱の高さ = line-height」(見えている間は切られない)
  - セル実寸 < `gridMin` (余裕は narrow 3.5px / wide 2.9px)
  - `--dock > 0` の全点で帯の下端が画面下端に一致 (ドック維持の不変条件)
- [x] `--dock = 0` の実測が **#59 の定数から計算した期待値と完全一致**:
      見出し font 14 / 箱 20、ラベル font 14 (16) / 箱 21 (24)、数値 font 24 (30) / 箱 30 (37.5)、
      opacity すべて 1、`textContent` も取得できる
- [x] ラベルが完全不透明なのは `--dock ≤ 0.3` の全点
- [x] 現状維持の確認: 簡易表示 47px、`scrollHeight` が `--dock` 1 と 0 で一致、
      131 点で 71 の異なる `--dock` 値 (量子化なし)
- [x] スクリーンショット (375px、ライト/ダーク、`--dock` 0 / 0.15 / 0.3 / 0.45 / 0.7 / 1.0):
      **切り刻まれた文字は 1 枚も無い**。`--dock` 0 は #59 と同じ見た目
- [ ] iPhone SE 3 実機での確認 (依頼) —— 完全表示に見出しとラベルが出ること、遅れが無いこと

body: ## Summary PR #2 was merged into its base (`devin/1786112160-phase1-scaffold`) rather than `main`, so Phase 2 never reached `main`. This PR carries the identical Phase 2 tree, rebased linearly onto `main`. **No new code** — `git diff` between this branch and the merged Phase 2 head is empty (identical trees, `b9ad73e`). Phase 2 delivers authentication in the gateway + frontend: - **Tokens**: short-lived access JWT + rotating refresh token, both in HTTP-only cookies. The refresh token is itself a signed JWT carrying `sub` + random `jti`, so `/auth/refresh` and `/auth/logout` identify the session from the refresh cookie alone — a session survives its full 7-day life instead of dying with the 15-minute access cookie. Only the SHA-256 hash of each refresh token is stored (max 10 sessions/user). - **Reuse detection**: replaying an already-rotated refresh token revokes *all* of that user's sessions: ```js const match = user.refreshTokens.find((t) => t.tokenHash === hashToken(refreshToken)); if (!match) { user.refreshTokens = []; await user.save(); throw ApiError.unauthorized(...); } ``` - **Google login**: rejects tokens with `email_verified === false`, and refuses to sign in when a local password account already owns that email (409) so Google can never bypass a password. - **Endpoints**: `register`, `login`, `google`, `refresh`, `logout`, `forgot-password`, `reset-password`, `me`, `config` under `/api/v1/auth`, all Joi-validated and documented in Swagger, behind an auth rate limiter. - **Reset flow**: reset tokens hashed at rest, uniform response to avoid account enumeration, and a successful reset revokes every session. Email delivery is still stubbed — link logging is off by default and only honored when `NODE_ENV=development`. - **Layering**: thin controllers → services → repositories; `User` model with indexes, timestamps and soft delete. - **Frontend**: Login/Register/Forgot/Reset pages, `ProtectedRoute`, auth slice, and an Axios interceptor that refreshes once on 401 (skipping the auth endpoints themselves, including `/auth/google`). - Tokens are never echoed in JSON response bodies — cookies only. - `COOKIE_SECURE` lets HTTPS staging/preview deploys force `Secure`/`SameSite=None` independently of `NODE_ENV`. CI also now runs on every PR (not just those targeting `main`) so stacked branches get validated. ## Testing 19 gateway tests (Jest + Supertest + mongodb-memory-server) and 7 frontend tests (Vitest) pass; frontend builds clean; lint clean across services. Coverage includes refresh with only the refresh cookie, logout without a valid access token, and replay-revokes-all-sessions. body:
## What

**#884** — the D3D11/D3D12 `*_repaint_pace()` waited for the previous scanout and then wove
immediately: the start of a refresh period, a full period before the pixels reach glass —
exactly the staleness the repaint exists to remove. This ports the VK late-weave logic
(`comp_vk_native_target_repaint_pace`): after the scanout wait, sleep `period − measured_r_ns`,
clamped to a quarter-period floor, weaving immediately when the residual is unmeasured. A late
repaint is a dropped repaint; an early one is merely stale — the clamp never gambles the frame.

**#887** — D3D11 previously emitted a one-shot line only, so runs could not be quantified.
Mirrors the D3D12 leg: bail counters (`armed`/`gate`/`race`), a periodic dump every 240
repaints, and a destroy-time dump.

Plus a one-shot `#884: repaint late-weave pacing engaged` line on both backends — without it a
run cannot distinguish "sleep engaged" from "residual never measured, behaving as before"; the
two are identical in every counter.

## Verification (this box: 60 Hz Leia panel, NVIDIA, SR 1.34.12, leia-sr plug-in confirmed per run)

- **D3D11** `cube_handle_d3d11_win`, `DXR_WEAVE_REPAINT_FORCE=1`: 8-min + 3-min soaks, **0
  `[ERROR]`, 0 device-loss**, steady ~29.5 repaints/s cadence (vsync slots split with the
  forced app), bails flat after warm-up. Engagement line observed:
  `period 16.7 ms, weave residual 16.0 ms, sleeping 0.7 ms`.
- **D3D12** `cube_handle_d3d12_win`, same procedure, 150 s: **0 `[ERROR]`, 0 device-loss**,
  ~29.5 repaints/s steady, bails flat. Engagement within 3 s of start:
  `period 16.7 ms, weave residual 15.6 ms, sleeping 1.1 ms`.
- Note the measured slack on THIS box is small (residual ≈ full period at 60 Hz), so the
  behavioral delta here is sub-millisecond by design; the reclaimed staleness scales with panel
  rate and weave speed, which is the case #868/#884 target. The clamp keeps slow-weave boxes
  unaffected.
- Both soaks ended in an externally-caused freeze: another agent's WebXR/service session took
  the panel full-screen mid-run (service log shows native-res weaves; app's flip-model presents
  stop being consumed and `layer_commit` blocks in `Present(1)` under the compositor lock).
  Reproduced identically on the **pre-change** first soak, so it is not introduced by this PR —
  it is the pre-existing present-under-lock design meeting a contested panel.

## Outstanding before merge

- David's panel eyeball (a mis-tuned late-weave shows as dropped repaints, not log errors).
- A clean throughput A/B on an uncontested box would be nice-to-have; the box was shared with
  another active agent session throughout.

Closes #884. Closes #887.

author: mhaslinsky
body:
## What

`scripts/seed-paks-stage.ps1`, the sibling of `seed-ue4ss-stage.ps1` for pak mods,
plus the S3 object and the `paks-stage/*` IAM grant it needs. Publishes
`D:\PalServer\paks-stage` to `s3://<bucket>/paks-stage/`, and restores it with
`-Restore`.

## Why

`palworld-launch.ps1` (PR #25) restores paks from `D:\PalServer\paks-stage` before
every launch, and D: survives instance replacement, so **the rebuild case is already
covered**. This is not that. It covers losing the *stage itself*: a recreated or
restored EBS volume comes up with no `paks-stage`, and the launcher then starts a
server with no pak mods and nothing anywhere reporting it.

Narrow by design. Worth having because the recovery path is the one you cannot test
when you need it.

## Design notes

**Publish is an overlay; restore is exact.** Publish keeps `seed-ue4ss-stage.ps1`'s
no-`--delete` behaviour, since `--delete` is the one action that can destroy the last
copy of a mod needing a Nexus login. Restore cannot be an overlay: the launcher treats
the stage as authoritative and sweeps live paks it does not list, so a partial restore
landing directly in the stage would **delete working mods** on the next launch. It
syncs to `<stage>.incoming`, verifies it holds every pak S3 lists, and only then swaps.

**The swap holds `Global\PalworldLaunch`**, the launcher's own mutex, so the every-2-min
watchdog cannot observe the moment where the old stage is aside and the new one is not
yet in place.

**Refuses to publish an empty stage.** An empty baseline restores cleanly, exits 0, and
leaves the server modless while every check passes.

**Verifies by content, not by key existence.** Uploading, `s3 sync` compares size and
timestamp, so a rebuilt same-size pak can be skipped while the key sits there looking
healthy - the same trap that made a restage transfer nothing on 2026-07-30, pointed the
other way. ETag vs local MD5; multipart ETags are downloaded and SHA256-compared rather
than size-checked, because size is exactly what the check is trying to catch.

**Exit 2 means published-but-divergent** (S3 holds paks the stage no longer has, which a
later `-Restore` would resurrect and the launcher would then make live). Not a failure,
but a caller reading only the exit code must not record it as clean.

## Verification

`terraform fmt` and `validate` clean. Parse-checked against the box's PowerShell 5.1
(`5.1.20348.5386`) at every revision.

**Not yet functionally exercised, deliberately:** the publish leg needs the
`paks-stage` PutObject grant that is *in this PR*, so it cannot run until this is
applied. Running it on the box is the post-merge verification, and it doubles as
seeding the real baseline.

## Known limitation, not addressed here

The grant attaches to `aws_iam_role.instance`, which the Linux box shares. Real, but
pre-existing rather than introduced: there is exactly one instance role and every
Windows policy already attaches to it, including the `ue4ss-stage` grant this mirrors.
Splitting Windows onto its own role is a genuine improvement and its own change.

## Review

Three `cubic` pre-filter rounds; findings fixed or rejected with reasons in the commit
messages. One of them caught a defect I introduced while fixing an earlier one (a
failed post-swap *validation* left the bad stage active, where only a failed *move* had
been handled).

author: nabaho
body:
내 업무에만 있던 열 접기를 팀 전체에도 넣습니다.

## 열 구성이 달라서 화면별로 나눴습니다

팀에는 「이 주 실적」이 있고 「이번 주」 격자가 없습니다. 그래서 걸러 보기(`fCols`/`fHas`)와 같은 방식으로 화면별(`sc`)로 나눠 담았습니다 — `colHidden(k)` → `colHidden(sc,k)`.

| | 접을 수 있는 열 |
|---|---|
| 내 업무 | 구분 · 업무 · 상태 · 최근 기록 · 다음 할 일 |
| 팀 전체 | 구분 · 업무명 · 상태 · **이 주 실적** · 최근 기록 · 다음 할 일 |

기업/의뢰인 · 담당 · 종료는 두 화면 모두 접지 않습니다.

## 설정을 따로 기억합니다

`work_my_cols` / `work_team_cols`. 내 업무에서 접은 것이 팀 전체까지 접어 버리면 두 화면을 같이 쓸 수 없습니다.

목록도 **한 화면 것만** 열립니다 — `S.colPop` 에 화면 이름을 담아 둘이 겹쳐 뜨지 않게 했습니다.

구분 묶음이 잡는 것은 내 업무만입니다. 팀은 담당(사람)으로 묶으므로 겹치는 열이 없습니다.

## 팀 머리칸에서 손본 두 가지

한 칸에 접기 손잡이·깔때기·정렬이 함께 있습니다.

- **접힌 열의 깔때기 선택지는 세지 않습니다** — 안 그리는데 세면 헛일입니다
- **정렬은 이름 글자에만 걸었습니다** — 예전엔 `<th>` 전체가 정렬 단추라, 접기 손잡이 옆 빈 자리를 눌러도 정렬이 바뀌었습니다

팀도 업무명을 접으면 진행률(3/8)이 기업 칸으로 내려옵니다.

## 검사

580개 통과. `work-my` 144 → 165개.

**칸 수가 어긋나면 표가 통째로 밀립니다.** 두 화면 모두 머리 9칸 · 본문 9칸 · 소제목 `colspan="9"` 인지 검사에 넣었습니다 — 값을 보는 검사로는 안 잡히고 화면을 열어야 보이는 종류입니다.

```bash
node tests/work-my.test.js
```

## 확인해 주실 것

1. 팀 전체 머리줄에 「▦ 열」 칩이 있고, 눌러 목록이 뜨는지
2. 「이 주 실적」·「최근 기록」을 끄면 표가 넓어지는지
3. 띠를 누르면 다시 펴지는지
4. **내 업무에서 접은 것과 팀 전체에서 접은 것이 서로 안 섞이는지**
5. 팀에서 열 이름을 눌러 정렬이 그대로 되는지 (손잡이 `‹` 는 접기만)

author: heshipstech
body:
Closes #133
Closes #47

## What this changes

The page was a flat list of about twenty five lines appended in ladder order, so its visual hierarchy was a fossil record of the build order rather than a design. This regroups the same elements into four zones plus an overlay zone, and makes appending to the page root impossible.

Deliberately minimal. Same elements, same text, same wiring. Elements are held by reference and updated through `textContent` and `hidden`, neither of which cares where the element sits, so no measurement logic is touched and every `data-testid` stays put.

## Why this is a measurement fix, not a cosmetic one

Downward gaze physically lowers the eyelid, and eyelid aperture is what most of this instrument measures. A readout near the bottom of the page therefore changes the number being read while you read it. That feedback loop contributed to the false long closures that forced amendment 5. Sideways gaze is far cheaper: it does not move the eyelid, and a head turn big enough to matter is already caught by the pose gate.

So the zones are ordered by how they are used, not by how they look:

- `notice`: the permanent demo notice and title.
- `measured`: everything read WHILE being measured. Blink measures, the score with its panel and alert slot, state measures. Top band, nearest the webcam.
- `peripheral`: the video preview, camera and gate status, diagnostics. Watched, not read.
- `between`: controls, the feature record count, the sparkline and blink log. Touched only between measurements.
- `overlay`: calibration, heatmap, replay and the sleepiness question.

## The durable part

The arrangement is not the point; the enforcement is. Two new end to end assertions: one fails if any element is appended outside a zone, one fails if the page needs vertical scrolling at 1440 by 900 (scrolling hides the video preview, which is how a person checks their face is tracked at all). SPEC.md gains the zone table and the physical reason behind it, so a future increment asks "is this read while being measured, glanced at, or touched between sessions" rather than "where does this look nice".

This is the third rule in this project made structural rather than remembered, after the CSV column guard and the aliased shut line.

## One presentation change beyond reparenting

A box containing only hidden children rendered as an empty bordered rectangle before the camera starts, which is the first thing a visitor sees. Three lines of CSS collapse those. Flagging it because it is the one thing here that is not pure reparenting.

384 unit tests unchanged, end to end tests 2 to 4. Verified in a real browser at 1600 by 900: five zones, zero orphans, no scrolling.

## Needs a human before merge

Manual item 53: load it on your own monitor, then the test that matters, sit still and read the score and PERCLOS without moving your head, and confirm the aperture reading does not drop while you read.

Merged by me under the overnight authorisation, on green CI.

body:
## Summary
- expand the interactive Product Builder from one reference blueprint to all 18 existing AI Pusula product ideas
- keep one maintainable build engine and feed it product-specific roles, screens, data entities, AI features, security boundaries, and special integrations
- add direct **Ürünü inşa et** actions to idea cards
- generate a professional 14-stage path for every product: scope, UX, project foundation, auth, database, frontend, backend, AI, billing, email, observability, security, deployment, growth
- provide clickable architecture, database explorer, technology profiles, AI coding prompts, acceptance criteria, persistent per-product progress, and Markdown export

## Coverage
Every existing idea in `ideas.json` has exactly one builder blueprint: 18 ideas / 18 builders. The catalog covers cybersecurity, developer tools, education, business SaaS and content products.

## Final verification — all passed on `38a9fb4540e17f6a8edb2fad30da5fbebe888f82`

### Validate product builder — run 11 / `31242795232`
- JS syntax and blueprint JSON parsing
- exact 18/18 idea ↔ blueprint ID match
- product-specific roles, pages, entities, AI features and security focus
- valid minimum / balanced / pro tool profiles
- official HTTPS documentation links
- 14-stage generator contract
- CSP, local fetch and `./public` deployment boundaries
- common secret-pattern scan
- static HTTP smoke test

### Validate AI Pusula — run 161 / `31242795236`
- existing site regression checks passed

### E2E product builder — run 6 / `31242795235`
- Chromium opened all 18 product builders one by one
- every product rendered exactly 14 build stages
- every product rendered at least 10 architecture nodes
- every product rendered at least 6 product-specific database entities
- task completion changed percentage progress
- progress persisted across reload
- professional tool profile rendered correctly
- mobile viewport had no horizontal overflow
- no page or console errors

## Security
- no tokens, API keys, customer PII or CRM records are collected
- progress is localStorage-only and separated by product
- external tools are informational links only; runtime data fetches remain local JSON
- CSP remains self-only for scripts and connections
- production assets remain scoped to `./public`
- each product contributes its own security gates to the generated security phase

## Deployment
`main` and the live Cloudflare Worker remain unchanged. The PR is ready for review and can be squash-merged after explicit production approval.

author: pando85
yoannchaudet
body:
## Motivation
A real run got stuck: the Implementer built a correct scaffold, but the Reviewer kept rejecting on an **environment-impossible** acceptance step ("verify in a real browser") that a headless sandbox can't satisfy. The loop burned all 5 rounds and went to `Failed`, **discarding good work**.

## What changes
Detect when the loop stops progressing and **escalate to `WorkReview`** (a human decides) instead of `Failed`.

- **Stall detection** — after each IM run, content-hash the `implementation/` workspace (skipping `.git`/`.DS_Store`) into a new `workspace_snapshots` table (schema v2→v3). When the RV rejects **and the workspace is byte-identical to the previous round**, the IM demonstrably can't address the feedback → stop early (typically round 2, not 5). Hashing the *files* is robust; comparing the reviewer's prose isn't (it rewords the same objection each round).
- **Escalate, don't discard** — the adversarial loop now goes to `WorkReview` on a stall *or* when `adversarial_max_iters` is reached (replacing the old `Reviewing → Failed`). Escalation **forces** `WorkReview` regardless of the `work_review` gate, so non-converged work is surfaced. `ReviewOutcome::Exhausted` → `Escalated(cause)`; the cause is recorded on the transition.
- `Reviewing → Failed` remains only for genuine step (agent/DB) errors via `fail()`.
- Docs (`agents.md`, `state-machine.md`) updated.

## Rubber-duck review
No blocking issues. Applied its two suggestions:
- `hash_dir` now returns `None` on an incomplete/unreadable tree, so an uncertain snapshot can never trigger a **false** stall (it falls back to the max-iters bound).
- Clarified in the docs that the `WorkReview` gate is for the normal accepted-work path, while escalation always forces `WorkReview`.

Verified: iteration pairing is correct; `WorkReview` is blocked (loop stops for the human); existing v2 DBs upgrade cleanly (missing snapshots → `None` → no false stall); cross-process hash comparison is stable.

## Tests
- Stall escalates at round 2 with the cause recorded.
- A changing workspace escalates only at max-iters.
- `hash_dir` change-detection + `.git` ignore.
- `make verify` → 66 unit; `make verify-full` → 2 integration. Both green, hermetic.

## Impact for the stuck run
With this, the earlier WI would have stopped at `WorkReview` after ~2 rounds with its scaffold intact, for you to approve — instead of `Failed` with the work discarded.

author: siddharth705
body:
The two P1 findings from the codebase quality audit. Both are production exposure; both are small and contained.

## 1. Customer PII out of application logs

`SentryScrubber` is thorough, and `application.yml` deliberately closes the Sentry logback appender because "a log line is the single most likely place for a narration or an amount to appear". That diagnosis was right — but the plain application log never got the matching control. Three sites wrote customer data at levels `application-prod.yml` emits (`com.finora: INFO`):

| Site | Was logging |
|---|---|
| `ImportService` (WARN) | opening/closing balance, credits, debits, expected closing, difference |
| `NoOpSmsProvider` (INFO) | phone number, full SMS body, transaction amount |
| `ResendEmailProvider` (INFO/ERROR) | recipient email address |

`NoOpSmsProvider` is reachable in production because `TWO_FACTOR_API_KEY` is only a startup warning — deliberately so, since a missed alert is a degraded notification rather than a security gap.

New `EmailMasking` (counterpart to the existing `PhoneMasking`) keeps the domain and drops the local part: a whole-domain bounce is a real diagnostic, the local part is the identifying half. Not a hash — a hashed address is trivially reversible by dictionary against any address you already suspect.

`ImportService` keeps only the details map's **keys**. The signal that line exists for is the *count* of these warnings over time, not any one statement's figures.

`NoOpEmailProvider` is deliberately unchanged: a blank `RESEND_API_KEY` is a hard startup failure in prod, so it cannot be the active bean there, and in dev reading the address is the point.

## 2. Production config validated before the web server binds

`ProductionConfigValidator` was an `ApplicationRunner`. Spring Boot starts the web server in `finishRefresh()` and invokes runners *afterwards*, so the real order was: bind, serve, *then* check the JWT signing key, then throw. A crash-looping deployment reopens that window on every restart.

Measured, not assumed — both jars against a real Postgres with `SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE=prod` and the placeholder `JWT_SECRET`:

| Build | `GET /actuator/health` | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| `ApplicationRunner` | **HTTP 200** | served, then refused |
| `SmartInitializingSingleton` | no response | `cancelling refresh attempt` |

A TCP connect succeeds under **both** and is not evidence — Tomcat opens its listen socket during `onRefresh()`, before either callback. Only a real HTTP response separates them.

Pinned as **guardian rule FG-031**, scoped to the `*ConfigValidator` naming convention rather than one file. Falsified: reverting to `ApplicationRunner` fails the build. It also fails when no validator is found, so it cannot go quietly vacuous.

## 3. Encoding repair

Eight double-encoded em-dashes in `application.yml` comments. Comments only; YAML re-parses identically.

## Verification

- Backend **1,689 tests**, 0 failures (303 integration)
- Repository Guardian **31/31** rules
- All 8 Python guard scripts pass, including the PII hygiene check on this diff
- Dependency advisory gate clean

author: shabnam311
body:
### Description
Closes #65796

Added a new `3d-flip-zindex-fix` component to the examples showcase. This submission resolves the infamous stacking context bug where absolute child elements inside a `transform: rotateY()` container get flattened, trapping their `z-index` inside the parent's plane and clipping into backgrounds during 3D rotations.

### What was changed
* Created `submissions/examples/3d-flip-zindex-fix/demo.html` showing a side-by-side comparison of a buggy flattened flip card versus a true 3D flip card.
* Created `submissions/examples/3d-flip-zindex-fix/style.css` which introduces `transform-style: preserve-3d` on the parent to stop the flattening engine, and `transform: translateZ(30px)` on the child badge to physically elevate it off the card's surface.
* Created `submissions/examples/3d-flip-zindex-fix/README.md` explaining why `z-index` completely fails inside 3D transform contexts and why the Z-axis is the only solution.

### Why it matters
Applying any CSS `transform` creates a new stacking context. When doing a 3D flip (e.g. `rotateY(180deg)`), the browser takes all the children of that flipped element and mathematically flattens them onto a 2D plane. This means if you put a `z-index: 9999` on a badge inside the card, it is trapped *inside* that flat plane, causing it to clip through the card geometry during rotation. By preserving the 3D space and pushing the badge forward on the physical Z-axis, it beautifully orbits above the card's surface.

### Accessibility
- Fully respects `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)`.
- Replaces the 3D rotation with a simple opacity cross-fade to prevent vestibular nausea, while ensuring the back panel correctly sits above the front panel in 2D space.

### Verification
- [x] All files isolated to the `submissions/examples/` folder.
- [x] Verified `transform-style: preserve-3d` allows the badge to float above the rotating card geometry without clipping.

author: doctisan
body:
Cierra el hallazgo "prima de colectivas en dos columnas" que quedó ⬜ en la bitácora, ahora que el owner definió la regla. **Sin migración** — prod ya tiene las cinco columnas.

## El bug

Los cinco puntos donde se recalcula la prima de una colectiva escribían **solo `polizas.prima`** (la columna legacy), mientras la UI muestra `prima_neta` / `total_prima`. El recálculo quedaba invisible y las columnas en desacuerdo.

Medido en la póliza de prueba antes del arreglo: `prima = 750.000` (la suma real de afiliados) contra `prima_neta = 5.000.000` y `total_prima = 5.950.000` en pantalla.

## La regla (confirmada por el owner)

La suma de los afiliados **es la prima NETA**; el IVA es 19%.

```
prima_neta  = suma
iva         = round(prima_neta × 0,19, 2)
total_prima = prima_neta + iva
```

## Los cinco sitios

| Archivo | Línea | Caso |
|---|---|---|
| `AfiliadosTab.tsx` | 42 | suma de `prima_individual` |
| `AfiliadosTab.tsx` | 56 | fallback `prima_por_afiliado × count` |
| `AfiliadoModal.tsx` | 74 | suma de la póliza |
| `AfiliadosPorPlan.tsx` | 71 | suma de todos los planes |
| `ImportAfiliadosModal.tsx` | 68 | `prima_por_afiliado × count` |

Los updates a `poliza_planes.prima_plan` quedan intactos: esa tabla no tiene columnas de IVA.

La fórmula vive en `lib/polizas/primaColectiva.ts`, pura y con 7 tests. Devuelve el **payload de update completo**, no solo los números, y los cinco sitios lo pasan verbatim a `.update(...)` — así ninguno puede olvidarse una columna ni escribir su propia fórmula. Es la lección de fase 0.1 aplicada al módulo que ya corrompió la prima en producción.

## Dos decisiones

**Se sincroniza la columna legacy `prima`.** Verifiqué que sigue habiendo lectores reales: `MetasView:33`, `AsistenteView:125`, la tabla de Cumplimiento (`PolizasList:626`) y el propio `AfiliadosPorPlan:93`. Dejarla desincronizada reintroduciría la misma incoherencia por el otro lado.

**Se escribe también `porcentaje_iva: 19`.** Sin eso la fila se contradice sola: `PolizaModal` deriva el IVA del porcentaje almacenado al guardar, así que abrir la póliza y darle guardar sin tocar nada recalcularía un IVA distinto del que dejó el recálculo. Es el mismo patrón del bug que estamos arreglando, en chiquito.

El gating `recalcularPrima` (que excluye las individuales) **no cambia**.

## Verificación

`npx tsc --noEmit` limpio · **136 tests** (7 nuevos) · `npm run build` OK. Los 10 hallazgos de eslint en `components/afiliados/` son preexistentes en `main`, idénticos; los archivos nuevos están limpios.

Contra **producción**, sobre un workspace de prueba aislado:
- El payload del helper es aceptado por el esquema real y la RLS (PATCH 200, las cinco columnas escritas).
- Con 2 afiliados (750.000 + 250.000), `PolizaDetalle` pasó a mostrar **"Prima neta $1.000.000 · Total prima $1.190.000"**. El síntoma —el recálculo invisible— desapareció.

### Alcance de lo verificado

Lo que **no** pude ejercitar fue el clic en la UI que dispara el recálculo: los clics del navegador automatizado dejaron de registrar en esa vista y no quise seguir quemando intentos. Lo que sí está cubierto: los cinco call sites verificados uno por uno por grep, el tipo del payload validado por `tsc`, la fórmula por tests, y el resultado en base y en pantalla. Al revisar, conviene agregar y quitar un afiliado a mano y confirmar que las tres columnas siguen cuadrando.

## Dato de contexto

En producción hay **una sola póliza colectiva, y es la de prueba**. Cero colectivas reales de la agencia, ninguna con `gastos ≠ 0`. O sea que no hay filas históricas que reparar — pero el bug se dispararía con la primera colectiva real que carguen.

body:
## 背景

#2503 で導入した depth-budget センサーの閾値を、**既存コーパスへ実センサーを適用して検証**したところ、Minimal が **26/26(100%)を flag** することが判明しました。

`evaluateDepthBudget` を、`FR-n` を持つ 43 件の `requirements.md` へ各 intent の記録済み Depth とともに適用した実測:

```
Minimal  n=26  min 1346  p25 1738  median 2353  max 6544 B/FR
Standard n=17  min  864  median 2040  max 3354 B/FR
```

| 上限 | Minimal | Standard |
|---|---|---|
| 1,200(変更前) | **26/26 = 100%** | 16/17 = 94% |
| 1,800(本 PR) | 19/26 = 73% | — |
| 2,400(現行維持) | 10/26 = 38% | **3/17 = 18%** |

## 問題

1,200 は**観測最小値 1,346 を下回っていました**。つまり上限がレンジ全体の下に位置し、「全部が長すぎる」としか言えず、**どれが外れ値かという情報を持ちません**。常時赤の信号は測定ではなくノイズであり、これはこのセンサーが未測定の `brief` に対して突きつけていたのと同じ批判です。

Standard(2,400)は既にレンジ内(18% flag)で識別として機能しており、変更しません。

## 変更

**Minimal 1,200 → 1,800**。中央値 2,353 を十分下回るので縮小圧は保ちつつ、最小値を上回るので識別力を持ちます。

## なぜ通ってしまったか(テストの穴)

従来の契約テストは「上限が中央値より下」しか固定しておらず、1,200 はそれを満たしていました。**下限側の制約が無かった**のが原因です。

新しい契約は**両側**を固定します:

```
上限は、その depth の観測レンジの内側に位置すること
  観測最小値 < 上限 < 観測最大値   ← 識別性(今回追加)
  上限 < 観測中央値                ← 縮小圧(従来から)
```

これにより、将来レンジ外の値を設定すると赤くなります。TDD で、変更前に新規2ケースが Red になることを実測してから 1,800 へ変更しました。

## 同期

閾値の記載箇所を全て更新:

- `amadeus-depth-budget.md` — Budgets 節に実測分布(min/median/max/flag 数)と、1,200 が最小値を下回っていた経緯を記録
- `requirements-analysis.md` の `## Sensors` 節
- `docs/guide/05-scopes-and-depth.md` / `.ja.md`

## 検証

body:
## Summary

On datacenter egress, Reddit blocks the keyless shreddit partials (`/svc/shreddit/*`) with HTTP 403. The pipeline's `capture_failures()` sink records those lane-level failures, and `_retrieve_stream` attached the captured failure as the source outcome **even when the source delivered items** — so a healthy Reddit run reported `auth-failed` / `partial after N items: HTTP 403: Blocked`, and the synthesis layer was told to distrust a source that worked.

This PR only attaches the captured-failure outcome when the run produced nothing, or when the impl attached its own explicit outcome artifact (e.g. "primary failed; fallback returned N items"). A swallowed lane failure no longer brands a successful source.

## Testing

- [x] `uv run pytest` (full suite; coverage 88.39% vs the 84% gate — the one failure, `test_setup_wizard.py::TestWriteApiKey::test_unwritable_target_returns_false`, also fails on clean `main` here because the suite runs as root, which bypasses the test's read-only permission setup; unrelated to this change)
- [x] Added regression tests:
  - items delivered + captured lane 403 → no `_source_outcome` attached
  - no items + captured lane 403 → transport-failure outcome still attached (issue #899 behavior preserved)

## Changelog

- [x] Added `changelog.d/+source-outcome-swallowed-lane-failure.fixed.md`

## Agent disclosure

### AI review

Change reviewed against the outcome machinery introduced by #899/#900: the no-items transport-failure reporting is untouched (covered by the existing `test_reddit_transport_outcomes.py` suite plus a new guard test). The `record_failure` → `PARTIAL` conversion in `RetrievalBundle` still applies to explicit impl artifacts, so intentional partial signals ("public fallback returned N items") keep surfacing.

### Security

N/A — no input handling, command execution, or auth changes.

## Notes

Motivated by a real run on a VPS: `"matcha tea trends" --search=reddit` returned 5 threads / 205 upvotes / 266 comments yet the run labeled Reddit `auth-failed: HTTP 403: Blocked` and told the model "do not interpret a failed source as no discussion." Companion PR `feat/reddit-arctic-listing-fallback` makes the shreddit lanes actually recover on such hosts; this fix keeps the outcome honest in the interim and for any future lane that 403s while other lanes deliver.

### Relationship to this change

- [x] None

author: henryperkins
body:
The mobile composer was functionally complete but visually unfinished, and its expanded state was one-way: `app.js` added `.is-expanded` on `focusin`/`input` and nothing ever removed it, so an empty reply that a member tapped once stayed open over the conversation for the rest of the page's life.

## Diagnosis

Reproduced at 390×844 before touching anything:

| Symptom | Cause | Measured |
|---|---|---|
| Expanded reply never collapses | `app.js:729-736` — two delegated handlers add `.is-expanded`; nothing removes it | after tapping a post body: still expanded, `document.activeElement === BODY` |
| Box-in-box | `.composer-box` (`app.css`) **and** `.wysiwyg-composer` (`src/client/wysiwyg/styles.css`) each paint a border, background, radius and ground | outer `1px rgb(148,160,149)` / r12; inner `1px rgb(222,210,184)` / r8, `min-height: 144px` |
| Empty body eats the viewport | `min-height: 9rem` on both the host and its `.ProseMirror`, plus the Source shelf | **308px of 844 (36%)** → now **192px (23%)** |
| Source shelf | `milkdown-adapter.ts` inserted a `btn btn-secondary btn-small` after the textarea | standalone **70×44** band between body and action bar |
| Detached title | `composer_shell.php` emitted `wrapper_slot` *before* `.composer-box`; the title was a plain `.input` with its own border and focus ring | title and body text at different horizontal insets, stacked outlines |

## The state model

`form._rbExpansion = { isExpanded, expand, minimize, collapseIfEmpty }`, living in `composer.js` rather than `app.js` — deciding whether a dock may fold needs the active adapter's canonical Markdown, because the hidden textarea lags behind the Milkdown document. `.is-expanded` stays the single class (server-rendered on 422, already keyed by the CSS and existing tests).

- **Empty** = trimmed canonical Markdown is empty **and** the upload tray holds no cards — an in-flight upload is composer state even while the body reads empty.
- **Folds** on `focusout`, deferred a tick so `document.activeElement` is trustworthy; every composer popover mounts inside the form, so one `contains()` check covers the toolbar, Source, emoji dialog, attachments, suggestions and Preview.
- **Also folds** on a document `pointerdown` landing outside the form — tapping a non-focusable region on mobile Safari moves no focus at all, so focus events alone would leave an empty dock open forever.
- **Stays open** with a draft; the new minimize control folds it by hand and only removes a class. The textarea, Milkdown document, local and server drafts, uploads and editor mode are all untouched, so reopening restores the draft and focuses the writing surface.
- The compact CSS is gated on the controller's own `data-composer-dock` stamp rather than the global `.has-js`, so a shell whose script never loaded stays fully expanded instead of folding into a one-line surface nothing can reopen. That is strictly more robust than before.

One deliberate call worth flagging for review: I first wrote a `document.hasFocus()` guard and removed it. Tabbing past the last control leaves the page for browser chrome, which that signal cannot distinguish from a window blur, and it broke the tab-away case. The attachment picker — the case the guard was meant for — is already covered by `contains()`, since it clicks a hidden input and leaves the trigger button focused.

## Presentation

- **One frame.** `.wysiwyg-composer` loses its border, background, radius and min-height; it is an interior region and `.composer-box` owns the only border and the only focus ring. Body sizing moves into the shell block in `app.css` next to the `.composer-input` rules it has to match.
- **Title inside the box.** New optional `header_slot` renders as the box's first row; New Topic switches to it and the title surrenders its own outline, sharing the body's `10px 12px` inset. `wrapper_slot` is unchanged for the mounts that still need an outside region.
- **Source demoted.** A named `[data-composer-mode-slot]` at the quiet end of the formatting row; the adapter mounts there and falls back to its old position for an older cached shell. Its accessible name still swaps `Source` ⇄ `Rich text`.
- **Minimize** sits beside it, server-rendered `hidden` on the reply mount only and unhidden by the controller, so no inert control ships without JS.

## Scope-adjacent fix

The emoji dialog anchors to `.composer-box` and rises from its top edge, so a shorter box pushed it 10px off the top of the viewport in the centred New Topic modal — caught by the existing `composer-shell` test. Fixing it needed placement to *track* reflow rather than sample once: the modal's `:has()` switch to `overflow: visible` on open, and a late debounced preview response, both move the box after the dialog appears. It now sizes and sides itself against the room actually available and keeps doing so while open.

## A note on the Imladris build

The live composer CSS is not authored in `resources/imladris/components.css`. That file and `docs/design-system/imladris/components.css` are an imported snapshot — "values verbatim from the app's composer shell CSS at the inspected commit" — emitted into `@layer imladris.components`, which unlayered `app.css` always beats. Editing the snapshot would falsify the reconciliation record and have no runtime effect, so the application-owned sources were changed instead.

`templates/**` and `public/assets/**` are inside the baseline digest, so the Imladris obligation is still met: the application-surface digest in `config/imladris-runtime-baseline.json` is refreshed (`LOCAL_RECONCILIATION.md`'s explicit design-contract review step) and the assets rebuilt. The design-system snapshot itself is unchanged. `build-imladris-assets.php --check` and `npm run check:wysiwyg` are both clean on the committed tree.

## Tests

New `tests/browser/composer-expansion.spec.ts` — 19 cases covering all fifteen acceptance items, parameterised over textarea and Milkdown modes, registered in the `evidence` npm script.

- `composer-expansion` + `composer-shell` + `wysiwyg-composer`: **85 passed**, 31 skipped. Composer specs re-run 3× to confirm stability.
- `thread-view-study`: green.
- PHPUnit: **2461 tests, 17525 assertions, 0 failures**.

**Pre-existing failures, not from this branch** — verified identical on unmodified `main` by stashing: 8 in `server-drafts.spec.ts` and 4 in `a11y.spec.ts`, all `toBeVisible`/click timeouts on surfaces this environment's seed does not produce. The other 24 a11y checks pass.

Before/after at the same viewport: `docs/evidence/browser/mobile/90-composer-reply-expanded-{before,after}.png` and `91-composer-new-topic-{before,after}.png`, plus `92` (collapsed dock) and `93` (empty dock folded by an outside tap).

## Deliberately deferred

- **Spec docs untouched.** `COMPOSER.md` §13 has no dock/minimize contract, but the string `COMPOSER.md v0.8` is pinned in `imladris-runtime-baseline.json`, `production-contract.json` and `ImladrisRuntimeAssetTest`. Documenting this properly is a §13 addition plus a v0.9 bump across all four — a separate reviewable change rather than something to fold in here. Happy to do it on request.
- §13 also specifies a full-screen New Thread on mobile; it is a modal in code and stays one per the product decisions for this work. Pre-existing divergence, now more visible.
- `/compose` and the DM mounts keep `wrapper_slot` — their fields carry visible `<label>` text and need their own in-box treatment, so the two New Topic surfaces still differ.
- The mobile action bar remains crowded (`Ano` clips). That ellipsis is asserted as intended by an existing test, so it was left alone.
- The hidden source textarea is still tab-reachable in rich mode. Pre-existing; axe does not flag it.

author: joycai
body:
Adds a second pipeline alongside organize: point the app at a product-page URL, review what it found against the NFO already on disk, and write only what you confirm.

It shares only `AiProvider` with the organize pipeline and is deliberately **not** routed through `OrganizePlan` — only one plan exists app-wide and a second `analyzeFolder` nulls it, so a stray Organize click would discard metadata not yet committed.

## The flow

Right-click a video → **Scrape metadata** opens one panel with three stages: set up, run, review.

Setup takes the URL, an AI backend chosen per scrape (without disturbing the app-wide active profile), free-text instructions for the model, the auto-detected NFO target with a Browse override, and — behind *Advanced* — a per-site cookie box and an HTML paste fallback. With no URL typed and a code detected in the filename, it offers the search sites you curate in Settings; knowing the catalogue number is not knowing the URL.

Two buttons, one destination:

- **Process** walks a four-tier ladder, cheapest first: JSON-LD/OpenGraph (validated against site-wide templates first, or plenty of libraries get identical metadata for every title), then a declarative recipe, then the LLM writing a recipe, then your pasted HTML.
- **Ask the LLM directly** hands the page over. The override, not a fifth tier — a request per title, values that are the model's rather than the page's, nothing verifying them against the document. Every field is stamped `FieldOrigin.llm`, which flags it amber and stops `NfoMerge` letting it overwrite anything on disk.

Review puts the field diff on the left and an artwork grid on the right. Defaults fill blanks, keep conflicts, merge lists — adding information is safe, replacing it is a judgement call.

## Artwork

Jellyfin identifies artwork by **file name**, so right-clicking a thumbnail assigns a role (poster, backdrop, landscape, thumb, banner, logo, clear art, disc, extra backdrop) and the role *is* the file name. Anything unmarked keeps the name the server used. **Save images** is its own operation that writes pictures and touches no NFO at all.

Thumbnails reverse an earlier "URLs only" decision whose reasoning — pre-fetching thirty stills defeats the per-host interval — was sound but lost to the fact that you cannot pick artwork you cannot see. `ScrapeImageCache` makes it affordable: fetches still go through `PageFetcher`, and every byte is kept, so picking three stills out of thirty costs the thirty fetches the grid already made.

## Two decisions worth reviewing

**A learned recipe is never saved automatically.** GIGA's synopsis exists twice, folded and expanded; a model that grabs the folded copy produces a recipe that runs, returns non-empty values and looks entirely healthy while storing truncated text for every title on the site. The self-check can only catch *empty* fields, never short ones — so the decision has to be a human's.

**A static age-gate cookie is not a session.** GIGA answers `old_check=yes` with the gate page and a 200, which is what made the failure so confusing. Recipes now name a `sessionUrl` walked once per host, and `PageFetcher` follows redirects itself — `http` drops `Set-Cookie` on a followed response, which is exactly where a gate puts the cookie, and reports the original URL as the response's own.

## Safety

- Every write goes through `applyOrganizeAction` or `MetadataWriter`, validated with `PathSafety.isWithin`.
- `NfoWriter` replaces only `managedElements`; Jellyfin's own `lockdata`/`dateadded` and probed `fileinfo` survive verbatim, verified against a real library NFO.
- Cancelling any surface writes zero bytes.
- Cookies stay in memory. A browser export can be equivalent to being signed in, so persisting one is an explicit Settings decision.
- Backups and an undo manifest are gated by one checkbox that controls both halves.

## Verification

**325 tests**, `dart format` and `flutter analyze --fatal-infos` clean.

The fetch path is verified **live** against giga-web.jp end to end — title, code, director, cast, runtime, date, poster and the expanded (not truncated) synopsis all correct. The panel, the artwork grid and the role menu have been exercised by hand.

**Not verified:** the direct-LLM path has only ever talked to a scripted provider, so the prompt, parsing, image allowlist and LLM stamping are tested but no real model has read a real page through it. Jellyfin has not been pointed at the NFOs this produces.

**Not included:** the Library section is still a placeholder, and recipe import/export and the scrape→organize title hint are unbuilt.
