author: gyanu1614
body:
## Problem
The published reputable **cheapest** could go stale. The correction cron is a single point-in-time read of `sab_market_raw_listings`; if it runs while a multi-batch crawl is still importing (or on its own clock after a manual crawl), it prices a **partial snapshot** and freezes a wrong cheapest.

Elefanto Frigo showed **$259.99** while a **$248** reputable listing (28k reviews) existed. A drift scan found **700+ of 1489** reputable items affected — including **Tung Tung $9999 vs real $1.93** and **Headless $5489 vs $4000**. "Run the cron more" only narrows the window; it never closes it.

## Fixes
1. **Collector-triggered reprice** — the collector calls `correct-prices?game=sab` as its **last step**, after every batch has landed, closing the snapshot-lag race by construction. Covers manual `sab:eldorado:send` runs too (a workflow-only step wouldn't). Mirrors `adopt-me-daily.yml`. The 10:00 UTC Vercel cron stays as an idempotent backstop. Workflow gets `PUBLIC_API_URL` + `CRON_SECRET`.
2. **Drift monitor** (`npm run sab:price:drift`) — recomputes `reputablePrice()` from current active listings, flags any published cheapest that no longer matches, exits non-zero on drift. Uses the cron's **exact** filter so check and computer can't disagree. This is the durable guarantee that "cheapest is reliably the actual cheapest."
3. **`ended_at` zombie fix** (migration) — the import RPC set `listing_status` on conflict but never `ended_at`, so a re-activated listing kept a stale end timestamp. A BEFORE trigger keeps them consistent + backfills.

## Verified
tsc clean. Drift monitor confirmed on live data (found the 700+ before repricing).

## Deploy actions (user)
- Apply migration `20260808`
- Re-run `correct-prices?game=sab` to fix currently-drifted items (crawl is settled, so this pass is correct)
- Add `PUBLIC_API_URL` + `CRON_SECRET` to the SAB workflow secrets

author: andymai
body: ## What `sweepAlongEdges` gains an exact analytic path for the gridfinity stacking-lip class: a **closed planar G1 chain of lines and tangent circular arcs** (a rounded rectangle) swept by an **all-line planar profile** perpendicular to the chain, sketched on the plane through the chain start — exactly what brepjs's `sweepSketch` constructs. - Straight runs emit exact planar quads; arc corners emit revolution bands (plane / cylinder / cone) via the existing `revolution_band_surface` machinery (revolve helpers exposed `pub(crate)`). - Junction rings are transported exactly (translate per run, rotate per corner) with closure verified before any allocation; ring 0 reuses the profile's own vertices and edges. - The whole `sweepAlongEdges` chain (analytic gate + the fitted-NURBS fallback that previously lived in the wasm binding) moves into `operations::sweep::sweep_along_edges`; the binding is now a thin resolver. ## Why The lip sweep previously produced ~2730 facet quads, which is what pushed the lip+box fuse into the (broken-on-coplanar-contact) mesh fallback. With this path the lip is **40 exact faces** (24 planes, 8 cylinders, 8 cones) and the native hollow-box + lip fuse **stays analytic with exact sum volume** — the ranked lever from the roadmap's lip-fuse chain. ## Pins - `analytic_spine_sweep_lip_ring_is_exact` — 40 faces, exact surface mix, edge-use-2 watertight, valid, Pappus-exact volume. - `analytic_lip_ring_fuses_onto_hollow_box` — the native smoke chain: analytic fuse, exact sum volume, watertight. - `sweep_along_edges_open_chain_falls_back` — fallback preserved. - `shelled_rounded_box_is_orientation_clean` — `#[ignore]`d ready-repro for a **new finding**: shell_op emits its cavity corner cylinders double-flipped (16 same-sense edges, pre-existing on every shelled rounded bin). A naive winding flip breaks the spec assembler's arc pairing (measured), so it needs its own dig; recorded in the roadmap. ## Verification Full workspace green (117 suites, render excluded for the known SIGSEGV), wasm gridfinity canary 27/27, clippy `-D warnings`, boundaries + doc-paths clean. --- ## Summary by cubic Adds an analytic sweep along closed, planar G1 line/arc spines with an all-line planar profile to produce exact plane/cylinder/cone faces. The gridfinity lip now builds as 40 analytic faces (was ~2730 facets) and fuses with the hollow box analytically with exact sum volume; tests are stabilized by insetting the lip 0.25 from the outer wall, with an exact-coincidence repro pinned as ignored. - **New Features** - `sweep_along_edges` detects closed planar chains of lines + tangent arcs and sweeps analytically: planar quads on runs; `revolution_band_surface` bands on corners (plane/cylinder/cone). - Exact per-segment ring transport with closure check; gate requires an all-line planar profile, perpendicular to the start tangent, sketched on the plane through the chain start. Non-gated cases fall back to the fitted‑NURBS path. - Fitted-path sweep moved into `operations::sweep::sweep_along_edges`; the `wasm` binding now forwards. `rotate_point`, `make_arc_curve`, and `revolution_band_surface` are `pub(crate)`. - **Bug Fixes** - Chain extraction re-orients flipped line edges so the analytic path still applies. - Stabilized the lip‑fuse pin by insetting the lip 0.25 from the outer wall to avoid nondeterministic mesh fallback; the exact‑coincidence fuse remains as an ignored ready repro. Written for commit a0308784064821dc3c9bc0324ebb12912f23e101. Summary will update on new commits.

## Summary
- Adds Sixel as a third inline-image graphics protocol (`internal/ui/imgview`), alongside Kitty and iTerm2, widening terminal compatibility to xterm, foot, mlterm, contour, mintty, yaft, and others.
- Detection: an active DA1 probe (`ProbeSixel`/`ParseDA1SixelSupport`), run only when env-var detection finds nothing, since Sixel terminals don't reliably set a detectable env var.
- Encoding: `EncodeSixel` wraps `github.com/mattn/go-sixel`, resizing in pixel space using the terminal's real cell pixel size (queried via `TIOCGWINSZ` on Unix, `internal/ui/imgview/cellsize_unix.go`; no-op fallback on Windows) since Sixel has no terminal-side scale-to-fit like Kitty/iTerm2.
- Modal close now issues `tea.ClearScreen` for Sixel specifically, since Sixel has no delete-placement primitive and Bubble Tea's diff renderer can otherwise leave stray pixels on screen.

| verdict exact | 315 / 315 | **315 / 315** | unchanged |
| the two fields published | 0 markets | **0 markets** | unchanged |

Every structural claim held. The one figure that moved is the aggregate — which is what a mean over a recomputed set always does.

## Changes

- **The residual mean is no longer published.** It is the only genuinely floating figure and it added nothing a reader can act on.
- **min/max kept but dated** (`as_of`) with an explicit note that per-market residuals move on every recompute. The max is safe to state because it coincides with the weight-derived cap — johor sits exactly on it.
- **`max_underivable_points` stays a standing property.** It is derived from `CONSTRAINT_WEIGHTS`, not measured, so it cannot drift.
- **The prose now makes a structural claim instead of a count:**
  > "…NO market reproduces exactly, and that is **by construction rather than by measurement**: the inputs are absent from the schema, not merely missing from some rows."

  That is both stronger and more durable than "0 of 315". The market total is interpolated from the live index size when injected, and omitted entirely when not.
- **Per-score counts** replaced with structural `exact_on` wording.

## Guard

`test_no_frozen_market_count_anywhere_in_the_published_document` renders the document with **no counts injected** and asserts:
- no market or row count appears anywhere in it
- the residual mean is absent
- an uninjected index size is `null`, never a remembered number
- the snapshot is dated and discloses that it moves
- the cap still equals the weight-derived constant
- injecting a *different* index size changes the prose

### `revisions[]` is exempt — deliberately

A revision is a **dated record of what was measured on a date**, and freezing that number there is the entire point; the module's own docstring says the dated values belong "in REVISIONS, where a dated observation belongs". The guard asserts the exemption is scoped to that one key, so every *other* key — all of which describe the current document — must measure its counts or omit them.

**Mutation-tested 7/7**, suite reverting to 25 passed:

| # | mutation |
|---|---|
| M22 | refreeze `"0 of 315 markets"` in the claim |
| M23 | republish the floating residual mean |
| M24 | restore frozen per-score market counts |
| M25 | fabricate an index size when uninjected |
| M26 | undate the residual snapshot |
| M27 | drop the "residuals move" disclosure |
| M28 | decouple the cap from the weights |

Cumulative across #2410 / #2413 / this: **28/28 mutations fired the intended test.**

author: glennneuber
body:
**Comments only, no behaviour change.**

Both workflows build and publish from `runs-on: linux` / `runs-on: windows` — self-hosted labels this fork has no runners for. A release attempted today queues, never starts, and is cancelled or times out after 24h, producing nothing. Whoever hits that should find the reason in the file rather than rediscover it from an empty `runner` field, which is how it came to light here.

## Why these are not gated like the test workflows

#53 gated `test.yaml` and `test-llamacpp-update.yaml` on `vars.SELF_HOSTED_RUNNERS` so their self-hosted jobs skip instead of queueing. **That reasoning does not transfer.** Those jobs only *report*, so skipping loses nothing. These jobs **produce and publish artifacts** — a silent skip would let a release report success while shipping nothing, which is worse than a visible hang.

## What I deliberately did not decide

There are three reasonable answers and they are a release-process call, not a mechanical one:

1. **Register runners** and set `vars.SELF_HOSTED_RUNNERS` — the workflows then work as upstream intends.
2. **Gate them anyway** and accept that releases are a no-op until runners exist.
3. **Fail fast** — add a guard job at the top that errors immediately with a clear message instead of queueing for a day.

(3) is probably the best behaviour if releases aren't imminent, but it changes the job graph of release machinery I've never seen execute, so I left it to you. Happy to implement whichever you pick.

author: jonathangana131-lab
body:
## Why

V14 makes **Forge Compact** a first-class local-AI subsystem: long autonomous missions should stop replaying raw chat/repository state and instead carry a compact, source-backed **Project Capsule** plus relevant retrieval. This PR starts the low-contention DOMAIN/TRUTH rung without colliding with the active Mission Engine, Project Brain, Plan Space, Forge Runtime, Model Center, provider, app-shell, persistence, or Xcode-project lanes.

The package deliberately consumes opaque mission/project/source authority identities rather than creating a second Mission Engine or Project Brain authority.

## What changed

Adds one standalone package: `Packages/ForgeCompactCore/**`.

### Project Capsule truth
- explicit L0/L1/L2/L3 context tiers: always-resident truth, active working set, project memory, cold archive;
- source-revision-bound context items with typed provenance, authority/advisory state, freshness, priority, and user protection;
- mandatory retention for mission identity, current objective, mission stage, safety/privacy policy, accepted requirements, accepted decisions, unresolved decisions, known defects, failing tests, and known limitations;
- stale mandatory truth fails closed instead of being silently compacted into a prompt;
- model summaries cannot mint authoritative project truth **or become any must-retain item**, including through L0 tier/user protection;
- protected user decisions remain retained even at low priority;
- deterministic canonical ordering independent of caller input order;
- exact UTF-8 byte budgeting rather than pretending byte counts are tokenizer token counts;
- if mandatory truth cannot fit the accepted budget, capsule creation fails instead of deleting truth;
- omitted items are explicit and may never claim `mustRetain`.

### Durable/relaunch validation
- versioned `ProjectCapsule` and `ProjectCapsuleArchive` schemas;
- decode re-enters invariants rather than trusting serialized state;
- decoded capsules reject duplicate IDs, cross-source items, omitted mandatory truth, non-canonical ordering, rendered-context drift, byte-count drift, and over-budget state;
- archives bind exact project + mission identity and require strictly increasing capsule revision with non-regressing mission revision / authority epoch;
- invalid/control-character archive identities fail closed.

### Prefix / KV reuse safety identity
`ForgeCompactCacheIdentity` binds exact model/revision, tokenizer revision, runtime/revision, prompt-template revision, tool-schema revision, project/source identity, and capsule revision. Prefix/KV reuse is permitted by this core only for exact identity equality. This is a compatibility boundary, **not** a claim that any particular runtime already supports reusable KV on iPhone.

## Validation

Exact local Swift 6.2.1 package composition at final head:
- debug: `swift test -Xswiftc -warnings-as-errors` -> **17/17 passed**;
- release: `swift test -c release -Xswiftc -warnings-as-errors` -> **17/17 passed**;
- release library build with warnings-as-errors -> **PASS**;
- `git diff --cached --check` -> **PASS**.

All seven published Git blob SHAs exactly match the locally tested bytes:
- `Package.swift` `4f6b0e61dbf822fd1a4f1e6ecf0aa14972d69e5a`
- `ForgeCompactCacheIdentity.swift` `7d7c6cee33c8cf0f177cf7cb96b0816bb43c8840`
- `ForgeCompactTypes.swift` `02c5f2181263de2c26b0a935e658a3a9d930af63`
- `ProjectCapsule.swift` `b23574d3803c9776d771d977cc64bbb2e475204c`

GitHub compare from live main base `d70584bd4f3a5a972067dc12c91873e864ab2ae1` to exact head `4a9d85843d3f73eb408ca92c29bf2b991b6c4694`: **2 commits ahead / 0 behind**, exactly seven additive files under `Packages/ForgeCompactCore/**` (+1083/-0).

## Adversarial coverage

17 deterministic tests cover mandatory truth retention, insufficient-budget fail-closed behavior, input-order determinism, accepted-decision retention, model-summary authority/mandatory/L0 rejection, stale truth, source-revision binding, protected user decisions, tampered omitted truth, exact cache identity, cross-project archives, revision regressions, non-canonical decoded order, invalid identities, and deterministic Codable/rendered-byte round trip.

### Self-review hardening before handoff
A source review found two truth gaps in the first checkpoint and fixed both before final handoff:
1. accepted decisions could be treated as optional context;
2. a model summary could become must-retain indirectly by occupying L0 (or another retention path).

Final head closes both and adds dedicated regressions.

This PR does **not** claim Mission Engine / Project Brain integration, persistence/app wiring, tokenizer-aware token budgeting, actual runtime prefix/KV reuse, q4/q8/adaptive KV, TurboQuant, speculative decoding, mmap, flash-backed weights, sparse expert paging, exact iPhone 12 performance/thermal/energy results, or compatibility for any model. The next safe closure rung is an adapter from accepted Mission/ProjectBrain truth into this package after the current canonical mission stack settles, followed by measured prompt/context reduction and runtime qualification on exact model/runtime/device identities.

author: julianshen
body:
Three slices built a working ACP layer that nothing in the binary called. This is the flag that makes it reachable — and the six things that had to be fixed first or in response to review, nearly all of which became reachable *because* of it.

| | |
|---|---|
| `0882eee` `[BEHAVIORAL]` | Stop serving seven ACP methods that could not back their answers |
| `326ea3b` `[BEHAVIORAL]` | Answer requests that arrive just before the stream ends |
| `181f542` `[BEHAVIORAL]` | Add `--acp`, the first mode that actually serves the protocol |
| `5b42144` `[STRUCTURAL]` | Doc: ACP has a caller now |
| `691757a` `[BEHAVIORAL]` | Correct the ACP consent rule and the shutdown order |
| `694d63b` `[BEHAVIORAL]` | Drop the drain deadline that lost real turns; pass model capabilities |
| `cee5854` `[BEHAVIORAL]` | Wire the pipeline, skills and a cancellation path into ACP mode |
| `ce41484` `[BEHAVIORAL]` | Signal handler startup instead of sleeping for it |

## Seven methods were answering questions they could not answer

Serving the registry from a mode makes everything on it reachable by a real client. Five of the registered methods fabricated success:

```
security/scan     answered "no findings" without scanning anything
security/approve  accepted a decision and recorded it nowhere
skill/invoke      reported success for any skill name
skill/list        reported an empty catalogue as fact
skill/manifest    reported any name as "loaded"
```

`security/scan` is the worst of these. A scan that answers "clean" without scanning does not fail — **it reassures**.

Two more went with them. `agent/prompt` ran a turn straight off the registry, bypassing the handshake gate, the cwd check, the single-session limit and the capability gate that `session/prompt` enforces. `tool/execute` returned a *successful* JSON-RPC response whose payload said `not_implemented` — a lie told inside a success envelope.

An absent method answers `-32601`, which is true. The registry now serves `initialize`, `session/new` and `session/prompt`, and nothing else.

## A transport bug only the real binary could find

Driving the built process, a client that sent `initialize` and closed its write side got **a clean stream close and no response at all**. `serveRequest` answers on its own goroutine, so `Serve` returned the instant the reader hit EOF while the handler was still marshalling its reply.

Every existing test held its stream open, so nothing had hit it. `Serve` now drains handlers that already started, and `failPending` runs first — draining before failing deadlocks a handler blocked in its own `Request` against the drain waiting for it.

**The drain has no fixed deadline, and the first version's five-second grace was the sharpest bug in this PR.** A `session/prompt` handler runs an entire turn, so any realistic prompt outlived the cutoff and lost its response — reintroducing the exact bug the drain was added to fix, for everything except the 50ms test handler that was hiding it. There is no duration that separates a wedged handler from a legitimate turn, so cancellation is the caller's decision: the drain waits on the serve context, which `runACP` derives from `SIGINT`/`SIGTERM`.

## `--acp` refuses to start without explicit tool consent

ACP's mechanism for tool approval is `session/request_permission`, which this agent does not implement — `Conn.Request` can express the round trip, but nothing calls it. So a served agent **cannot ask the user before running a shell command**.

Headless can default to auto-approval because a person typed the command that started it. Here the caller is an editor, and the person may never learn a tool ran.

**`--auto-approve` is the only thing that grants consent.** An earlier version also accepted `--approve-cwd` and promised it would "limit execution to the working directory" — false twice over: that flag governs *folder access*, not tool approval, and nothing downstream scoped execution to the directory. `--approve-cwd` keeps its real meaning here, because `runACP` now applies the folder-access gate that interactive and headless apply and ACP was missing entirely.

## What review found that hand-assembly had dropped

`runACP` was built by copying from headless, and everything not consciously carried across was silently absent:

- **The tool security pipeline.** `WithToolMiddlewares(buildPipeline(...))` enforces `.security.yaml` and `Agent.ToolRules` denials. ACP omitted it — on the one mode that auto-approves every call, so the rule engine was the last thing saying no and was never consulted.
- **The skill runtime.** `--skills` was read for an `apple-dev` check and otherwise ignored; `wireAppleDev` was never called, so that check fed a decision nothing acted on.
- **Model capabilities.** Detected, used only for tool registration, never passed to the agent — so tool-count limits, discovery hints and reasoning effort were dropped.

## Verified against the binary, not only the tests

```
$ printf '<initialize>\n<session/new cwd=/home/user/rubichan>\n<session/new cwd=/tmp>\n' | rubichan --acp --auto-approve

{"id":1,"result":{"protocolVersion":1,"agentInfo":{"name":"rubichan",...},"authMethods":[]}}
{"id":2,"result":{"sessionId":"2da74d984feb4ab314d60e7dab7becff"}}
{"id":3,"error":{"code":-32602,"message":"session/new: ... this agent serves only \"/home/user/rubichan\", not \"/tmp\"; its working directory is fixed at startup"}}
```

`session/new` before `initialize` is refused by the ordering gate; starting without consent refuses with the reason. Every guard the previous slice added fires against a live process.

- `internal/acp`, `internal/agent` and `cmd/rubichan` build/vet/gofmt clean; the first two race-clean; the drain test also `-race -count=20`.
- `cmd/rubichan` has a **pre-existing** data race in `TestRunReplayFollowText`, and `internal/tools` a rotating flake adding a varying 11th full-suite failure. Both confirmed on unmodified code before this branch.

## What a client will hit first

One agent serves one connection, ever; one session; one directory. All three are deliberate refusals rather than silent misbehaviour, and all three are lifted by the same missing feature — per-session agent state. Turn cancellation remains unimplementable (`Handler` carries no context, so `session/cancel` needs a context threaded through every handler), and there is still no mid-turn `session/request_permission`.

A path-scoped approval checker was proposed in review and declined: it must cover shell command *arguments*, not just file tool paths, or it hands back a guarantee it cannot keep — which is precisely how the bad `--approve-cwd` claim got made.

---

author: mikeparcewski
body:
## What & why

Closes the CRITICAL residual of FINDING-045, **found by adversarial re-verification** of the "already-fixed" set. The filesystem boundary (core#189/#219) only inspected `context["path"]`, which `claude_pretool_context` populates **only for Write/Edit/NotebookEdit/Read**. A `Bash` call carries `command`, not `path`, so `boundary_denial` returned `None` and Bash was **never judged** — `Bash{echo x > ~/outside}`, `cp`/`mv`, `dd`, and the FINDING-067 `rm -rf ~/…` / `wicked-estate index .` mechanism wrote outside the worktree, **unblocked and unaudited**. An existing test (`a_call_without_a_path_is_not_judged_here`) documented the hole and `path_policy.rs:19-26` conceded it.

## The fix

`boundary_denial` now also parses a Bash command for **write targets** — `>`/`>>`/`N>` redirects (spaced or glued), `tee [-a]`, and the destination of `cp`/`mv`/`install` and `dd of=` — splitting on pipeline/sequence separators so a write **after a pipe** (`… | tee FILE`) is checked as its own program. Each target runs through `path_policy::check(is_write=true)`; one outside the worktree is a **fatal** boundary deny. `boundary_denial` now returns `(reason, is_write)` so a Bash write escape is unit-fatal even though "Bash" isn't in `WRITE_TOOLS`.

## Honest scope

**Defense-in-depth, not a hermetic sandbox.** The shell is Turing-complete, so `$(...)`, a variable, or `base64|sh` can still evade a scan of the literal command — the real containment guarantee is OS-level worker-fs confinement, which this codebase does not yet have (tracked as the 045 follow-up; the choice of this approach over a full per-OS sandbox was made deliberately). This closes the **direct, common** escapes the finding names, which today are permitted entirely — a sharp reduction of the write-escape surface, framed as what it is.

## Test + falsification

`a_bash_write_outside_the_worktree_is_refused_and_fatal`: a redirect/`cp`/`tee` to an outside path is a **fatal** deny (`is_write == true`); a write **inside** the worktree is allowed (the boundary is a fence, not a Bash ban). **Mutation-verified:** neutralizing `bash_write_targets` re-permits the escape and fails the test.

author: leofalco
body:
✅ Closes

- Não há issue vinculada

✋ publicar antes deste pr

- Nenhum

⏭️ publicar depois deste pr

- Nenhum

**Checklist**

- [ ] Fieldnews - enviar broadcast via e-mail com publicação
- [ ] 🧪 Testes - testes e2e, integrados e unitários foram feitos

> Testes e2e foram executados manualmente contra um repositório de teste com remote bare (cenários detalhados abaixo), mas **não** foram adicionados testes automatizados neste PR.

<!-- Init:FieldnewsEmailContent -->

**Contexto**

O `theo repo clean` é o comando que faz a faxina das branches do seu repositório local. Ele olha todas as branches que você tem na máquina, rebaseia as que ainda têm trabalho pendente em cima da branch principal, apaga as que já foram mergeadas e oferece a limpeza das branches que sobraram no servidor.

Até então ele partia de um pressuposto: o de que a branch principal do repositório é a mesma branch onde o time integra o trabalho do dia a dia. Nos repositórios que seguem esse modelo isso é verdade — só existe a `master`. Mas há repositórios que separam as duas coisas: a `master` representa o que está em produção e a `develop` é onde as alterações do time se juntam antes de subir. Nesses repositórios o pressuposto quebra.

**Motivações**

Ao rodar o comando em um repositório com esse formato, apontando a base para `develop`, a branch de produção local era **apagada**.

O motivo: existe um filtro que protege a branch default da lista de remoção, mas as branches consideradas obsoletas (aquelas sem nenhum commit fora da base) eram adicionadas à lista *depois* que esse filtro rodava. Como a `master` não tem commits fora da `develop`, ela caía na categoria de obsoleta e passava direto pela guarda, terminando em `git branch -D master`.

Outros problemas apareceram na mesma investigação:

- A branch em que você estava no momento nunca era rebaseada, porque o parsing de `git branch` a descartava junto com o marcador `*`.
- Um conflito em qualquer rebase derrubava o comando inteiro e deixava o repositório em estado de rebase pendente, no meio da fila.
- Branches cuja remota já tinha sido apagada eram **recriadas** no servidor pelo force-push, ressuscitando trabalho já concluído.
- Rebases e force-pushes aconteciam sem qualquer confirmação prévia.
- Na etapa final, uma única falha ao apagar branch remota abortava o comando, e as demais branches selecionadas nem chegavam a ser tentadas.

**Implementação**

O comando foi reorganizado em três etapas explícitas: levantar o estado, montar um plano e só então executá-lo.

*Detecção da base e proteção da branch de produção.* Sem a flag `-b`, o comando agora usa `develop` como base quando ela existe no remote; caso contrário, cai na branch default. A branch default entrou num conjunto de branches protegidas que nunca são rebaseadas, force-pushadas ou deletadas — a injeção das obsoletas agora respeita esse conjunto. Ela continua sendo mantida em dia, mas apenas por fast-forward (`git fetch origin master:master`), o que nunca reescreve histórico.

*Base atualizada antes do plano.* A base é atualizada com `git pull --rebase` antes de qualquer cálculo, já que é ela que define o que já foi mergeado e sobre o que todo mundo será rebaseado. O `--rebase` evita deixar um merge commit na base. Se houver conflito, o rebase é abortado e o comando para com erro, em vez de rebasear todas as branches sobre uma base errada.

*Listagem por `for-each-ref`.* O parsing de `git branch` foi trocado por `git for-each-ref`, que entrega nome, upstream e estado de tracking de uma vez. Isso resolveu a exclusão acidental da branch atual e passou a distinguir os três estados de push que importam.

*Push condicional.* Uma branch cuja remota foi apagada (upstream `gone`) é rebaseada localmente mas **não** é pushada, já que recriá-la ressuscitaria trabalho concluído. Branches com remota existente recebem force-push; branches nunca publicadas têm a remota criada.

*Conflito isolado.* Um conflito de rebase agora executa `git rebase --abort`, registra `PULADA <branch>` no log e segue para a próxima. Ao final, todas as puladas são listadas juntas.

*Plano e confirmação.* Antes de qualquer ação destrutiva, o comando imprime o que pretende fazer, agrupado por tipo de ação, e pede confirmação. A flag `-y` pula a pergunta. Também há uma guarda que impede a execução com working tree sujo.

*Deleção remota resiliente.* Uma falha ao apagar branch remota agora gera apenas um aviso e a fila continua. Como no Azure DevOps apagar branch exige a permissão `Force Push` — concedida somente a quem criou a branch — a seleção passou a exibir o autor das branches de terceiros e a listar as suas primeiro.

**Evoluções**

- Corrige a perda da branch de produção local, que era o problema mais grave.
- O comando deixou de ser tudo-ou-nada: conflitos e erros de permissão isolam a branch afetada em vez de abortar a execução.
- Nenhuma branch remota é recriada sem intenção.
- O plano prévio torna o resultado previsível antes de qualquer force-push.
- O repositório nunca fica em estado de rebase pendente.

**Screenshots**

Por ser um comando de terminal, o antes e depois estão como saída de console.

*Plano exibido antes de qualquer alteração (novo):*

```
Plano de limpeza — base: develop (branch de produção protegida: master)

  Rebase + force-push
    feat/a (1 commit fora de develop)
    feat/d (1 commit fora de develop)

  Rebase + push (cria a branch remota)
    feat/e (1 commit fora de develop)

  Rebase local, sem push (branch remota foi deletada)
    feat/c (1 commit fora de develop)

  Deletar local (nenhum commit fora de develop)
    feat/b

? Aplicar esse plano? (y/N)
```

*Conflito isolado, sem derrubar a execução:*

```
 INFO  feat/a: rebaseada em develop e force-push feito
 INFO  feat/c: rebaseada em develop; push pulado porque a branch remota foi deletada
 WARN  PULADA feat/d: conflito no rebase sobre develop — rebase abortado, branch mantida como estava
 INFO  feat/e: rebaseada em develop e branch remota criada
 WARN  Branches puladas por conflito ou checkout falho (resolva na mão): feat/d
```

*Seleção de branches remotas, agora com autor e as suas primeiro:*

```
? Selecione as branches remotas para deletar (as suas vêm primeiro)
❯◯ feat/b
 ◯ minha/branch
 ◯ dele/branch (gustavo@talkcomm.com.br)
```

*Falha de permissão que antes abortava tudo:*

```
dele/branch  -> FALHOU: ! [remote rejected] dele/branch (pre-receive hook declined)
minha/branch -> DELETADA
feat/b       -> DELETADA
```

**Verificação**

Cenário e2e montado com remote bare cobrindo todos os caminhos, todos confirmados:

| Caso | Esperado | Resultado |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Branch com commit próprio e remota existente | rebase + force-push | hash reescrito, remota atualizada |
| Branch patch-equivalente à base | deletada local | removida |
| Branch com upstream `gone` | rebase local, sem push | rebaseada, remota **não** recriada |
| Branch conflitante | pulada e preservada | commit original intacto, sem rebase pendente |
| Branch local-only | rebase + cria remota | publicada |
| Branch de produção (`master`) | intocada | não rebaseada nem deletada |
| Cancelar na confirmação | nada alterado | branch de origem preservada |
| Delete remoto rejeitado | avisa e continua | demais seleções deletadas |

`npm run lint` e `npm test` passando.

author: baileyrd
body:
The socket families #105 deferred for their own pass. With this, **Track W is complete across `platform-windows`**.

## What migrated

`socket`, `bind`, `listen`, `accept`, `connect`, `send`/`recv`, `sendto`/`recvfrom`, `getsockname`/`getpeername`, `setsockopt`, `closesocket`, `WSAStartup`, and the AF_UNIX paths (`bind_unix`/`connect_unix`/`accept_unix`/`local_addr_unix`) whose upstream bindings #105 added.

Structured as a two-armed **primitive layer** — `raw_socket`, `raw_bind`, `raw_connect`, `raw_accept`, `raw_sock_addr`, `raw_recv`, `raw_send`, `raw_sendto`, `raw_recvfrom`, `set_sockopt`, plus the `*_unix` counterparts — so the fifteen public functions keep a single body each. Same shape `sys::console`'s `get_mode`/`set_mode` pair took in #104; two-arming fifteen public functions would have doubled the file to say one thing.

## The address boundary — why this was its own slice

This crate speaks `std::net::SocketAddr` and raw `SOCKADDR_IN`/`SOCKADDR_IN6` byte buffers. The donor speaks its own `SocketAddr` enum and `UnixSocketAddr`. Every address-taking call crosses that, so `to_donor_addr`/`from_donor_addr` (and the Unix pair) own the conversion in one place.

The detail worth checking: both sides pass IP octets **verbatim** and byte-swap only the port. This crate's `to_sockaddr` says so in its own comment (`from_ne_bytes` reproduces the in-memory pattern rather than converting); the donor does the swap internally. Neither double-swaps — which is exactly the class of mistake that would pass every compile and fail only against a real peer.

## Two places this is now *more* correct, not merely equivalent

`unix_listen`'s stale-socket retry and `is_stale_socket` both re-read `WSAGetLastError` **after** the failing call had already returned. That was a latent race — any intervening Winsock call overwrites the slot — and it happened to work only because nothing intervened. Both now branch on the `ErrorKind` carried out of the call itself.

That's `docs/learning/003-…`'s lesson ("the thread-local last-error slot is never the authority once a wrapper stands between you and the call") landing somewhere it changes behavior rather than merely restating it. The track-w arm *forced* the fix, because there the code has to come from the returned value; the windows-sys arm gets it for free.

## Error classification is shared, not duplicated

`wsa_kind` is one table both arms run, fed either by `WSAGetLastError` or by the code the donor captured. Deliberately **not** `errmap::trackw_err`: that classifies through the *Win32* table, where a Winsock code (10035, 10061, …) means nothing. Same number-space discipline `errmap`'s own module doc insists on, one space further out.

## Two calls stay on windows-sys — and they differ in kind

- **`DeleteFileW`** in `unix_listen`'s stale cleanup: a filesystem unlink sitting in a net module, and the donor's `fs::delete_file` takes `&str` where this has an `OsStr`. `sys::fileio` is where a future slice should own it, not here.
- **`unix_peer_addr`'s `getpeername`**: the donor has `local_addr_unix` but no peer counterpart. This is a **genuine upstream gap**, not a judgment call — recorded as such so it doesn't get mistaken for one.

## Track W's final state

Every family in `platform-windows` is now one of: migrated; permanently closed (`CreateProcessW` — the donor's `spawn_suspended` encodes an stdio model this repo rejected in D5); declined pending evidence (`reopen`'s console-device open); a named upstream gap (`unix_peer_addr`); or `sys::nt`, which has no donor bindings at all and would need an `ntdll` admission rusty_win32 has deliberately never made.

## Versioning

`0.25.3` → `0.25.4`. **`z`, not `y`:** no public item's shape changed. Every migrated function keeps its signature; the primitive layer and the `SockOpt` enum are private.

## Verification

Clean from a Linux host: `cargo fmt --all --check`; `clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` on host and `x86_64-pc-windows-gnu`; `clippy -p platform-windows --features track-w --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu --all-targets -- -D warnings`; the `unsafe-scope` gate; `cargo check` under a real 1.75 toolchain for the Windows target.

Worth noting the `-D warnings` build did real work here: it caught `to_sockaddr`, `from_sockaddr`, `to_sockaddr_un` and `UNIX_PATH_CAP` becoming dead under `track-w`, which is the compiler confirming the migration is actually complete rather than partially wired.

Two gaps stated rather than left to inference:

- **Nothing here executed a Windows syscall.** `tests/net_parity.rs` (`windows_net_conforms`, `windows_unix_conforms`, `windows_udp_conforms`) and `tests/net_nonblocking.rs` under the `--features track-w` leg are the first real execution — and they exercise live TCP, Unix-domain and UDP round-trips, so this is a leg worth reading rather than just checking green.
- `cargo test --workspace` on this container has the same one pre-existing failing binary as every previous slice: `platform-linux/tests/secret_service.rs`, all six failures `gnome-keyring-daemon must be installed`. Unrelated to `platform-windows`.

---

body:
## Problem

deploy-railway.yml (API Railway deploy) has been failing since 2026-07-31 with Invalid RAILWAY_TOKEN. The workflow uses railway up (CLI upload), which requires a different token type than the GitHub secret RAILWAY_TOKEN provides.

Meanwhile, deploy-www.yml deploys successfully using the GraphQL serviceInstanceDeployV2 mutation with the same RAILWAY_TOKEN secret — proving the token is valid for GraphQL but not for CLI.

This blocks all API Railway deploys, including the webhooks.ts UP-recovery fix (BUY-47930 / BUY-47993).

## Fix

Convert deploy-railway.yml to use the same GraphQL pattern as deploy-www.yml:
- Replace railway up CLI with serviceInstanceDeployV2(serviceId, environmentId, commitSha)
- Add deployment status polling (up to 15 min)
- Add auto-rollback to previous SHA on failure
- Keep all existing smoke tests (health, catalog, categories, search, auth)
- Remove Node.js setup and Railway CLI install (no longer needed)

## Verification

After merge to main, dispatch deploy-railway.yml from main to verify the GraphQL deploy works and the webhooks.ts UP-recovery fix reaches production.

Ref: BUY-47993, BUY-47930

author: waiphyoaung24
body:
Adds a superuser-only hard delete for products that never entered the stock system, in the footer of the existing product edit dialog.

Design: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-08-product-delete-superuser-design.md`
Plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-08-product-delete-superuser.md`

## What it does

`DELETE /products/{product_id}`, guarded by `get_current_active_superuser` (`is_superuser` only — BKK_ADMIN cannot). It refuses with 409 unless the product is fresh (no `Unit`, no `PartBatch`) **and** has no price history. Everything with stock or sales stays and is retired via `is_active`, as before.

The button renders only when `canDeleteProduct(product, isSuperuser)`. First click arms a destructive confirm that reverts after 4s; the second deletes. It sits at the opposite end of the footer from Save.

## Three things reviewers should know

**1. A grant migration was required.** The least-privilege `castranova_app` role holds only SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE, so the endpoint died at commit with `InsufficientPrivilege`. `m037` grants `DELETE ON product`, following m034's precedent. Grants only, no schema change. It deliberately excludes `pricechange` — see below.

**2. Price history makes a product undeletable, by design.** `pricechange` is one of m026's append-only `LEDGERS`, guarded by m021's `reject_ledger_mutation` trigger, so its rows can never be deleted and the FK can never be satisfied. Cascading was rejected over weakening the trigger. Practical consequence: create a product, correct its price, and it can only be deactivated. The frontend cannot predict this (`ProductPublic` has no price-history flag), so the 409 message surfaces as a toast.

**3. A double-click bypassed the confirmation.** Found while testing in the running app: double-clicking Delete fired both the arm and the confirm, deleting without the confirmation ever being read. A second click within 500ms of arming is now swallowed.

## Review findings addressed

`ecc:database-reviewer` and `ecc:security-reviewer` both ran. Fixed:

- **Deletions are now logged** (medium, security). This is the codebase's first hard delete, and the audit trail derives from the movement ledgers — which a deletable product has none of. The route binds the acting superuser and logs product id/sku/model_name/actor before deleting.
- **The `IntegrityError` fallback message was wrong.** It said "has stock history", but the case it actually catches is a non-stock reference — most plausibly a `PricingOverrideRequest`, which can exist without stock or a re-price. Now generic and accurate.
- **That fallback branch had no test.** Added one: a product with only an override request passes both explicit gates, so it exercises the backstop and asserts 409 rather than 500.

Not addressed, deliberately: no rate limit on the endpoint (consistent with every other route in `products.py` — not a regression here), and Save stays enabled while delete is armed (cosmetic).

## Verification

- Backend: 778 passed, 0 failed. mypy strict and ruff clean on changed files.
- Frontend: 96 vitest tests pass; `tsc -p tsconfig.build.json` clean.
- Manually verified in the running app as a superuser: stocked product shows no Delete and a locked SKU; fresh product arms and reverts; double-click leaves the product alive; two deliberate clicks delete it and the list refreshes.

Note for whoever runs this: `scripts/test.sh` cannot execute these tests — the backend Dockerfile never copies `backend/tests` and `compose watch` does no initial sync, so pytest exits with "file or directory not found: tests/". Use `docker compose cp ./backend/tests backend:/app/backend/tests` first. Recorded in the plan.

body:
Closes #183.

`RoyalPuzzleGame` and `RoyalPuzzleTests` were 1,096 lines answering #131's question — *in-game rule, new plugin, or engine change?* They answered it, M7 shipped the real 8×8 region on that answer (`Sources/Dungeon/Regions/RoyalPuzzle.swift`), and what was left standing was a parallel 4×4 puzzle with its own grid type, its own prose, and its own `#verb("pushWall")` that compiled only because no `DungeonTests` case named `.pushWall`.

**Net: −1,120 lines, +296.**

## What moved, and where

I audited all twenty cases before deleting any.

| Deleted case | Behaviour | Now pinned by |
|---|---|---|
| `pushWithNoDirectionIsAnsweredByTheRuleNotTheCore` | a `[verb, .direction]` row makes the **bare** verb parse instead of asking | `PatternGrammarTests.aDirectionRowMakesTheBareVerbParseInsteadOfAsking` (+ a `turn` control) |
| `literalWordRowsBuyBackTheNoun` | a literal may sit beside a direction slot; adjectives and synonyms may not | `aLiteralWordMaySitBesideADirectionSlot`, `adjectivesAndSynonymsStopAtThePattern` |
| `theNounInALiteralRowIsDecorative` | a literal is matched, never resolved — `directObject` stays nil | `theNounInALiteralRowIsDecorative` |
| `theGridIsOneOpaqueGlobalAndTheVerbRowsCollideWithNothing` | a custom row sharing a core verb *word* but not its *shape* is silent | `sharingACoreVerbWordButNotItsShapeIsSilent` |
| `aRewindReprintsTheGeometryItRewound` | `alwaysDescribed` un-hides on UNDO | `AlwaysDescribedTests.anUndoReprintsTheStateItRewound` |
| `aRoomWithoutTheTraitIsStillBriefOnARevisit` | …and only for the room that declares it | `onlyTheRoomThatDeclaresItIsDescribedTwice` |
| `theGridSurvivesUndoAndSaveAndRestore` | …and on RESTORE, the third entry path | `aRestoreReprintsTheStateItRestored` |
| `everyStepAndEveryPushCostsATurn` | a location `before` that replies still costs a move | folded into `anUndoReprintsTheStateItRewound` |

**Deliberately not carried over**, each checked against the suite rather than assumed: `withRoomName: false` (`ArriveTests`, `PluginSeamTests` — pinned twice already), the reach and `isReachable`-in-a-presence-line cases (`ReachTests`), the `.data` boxing of a struct global (`CustomStateTests`, and the file round trip in `ConversationTests`). Everything else was Royal-Puzzle *content*, and `DungeonTests` pins the shipped version of all of it.

## Two homes rather than one

- **The direction slot → `PatternGrammarTests`**, whose `BadPatternsGame` already pinned the *refusal* side. `WorkshopGame` grows the legal side as plain `SyntaxRule` rows against `Intent("shove")` rather than `#verb`, so the duplicate constant disappears instead of moving. The verb *word* is deliberately core, because what a direction row displaces is core `push`'s "What do you want to push?".
- **`alwaysDescribed` → a new `AlwaysDescribedTests`**, because the trait had no owner: `BootstrapTests` held only its warning, and `ArriveTests`/`PluginSeamTests` hold the other half of #149. `DialRoomGame` is a landing and a room with a dial in it — one `@Global Int` the description reads, one verb that turns it, one control room next door. Deliberately not a puzzle; a second spike is what this PR removes.

## Verification

**1,427 tests green, strict lint clean.** Every retargeted pin was proved to *fail* without the behaviour it claims:

- `push` rows deleted from `WorkshopGame` → all three direction cases red, and `"What do you want to push?"` observed coming back.
- `alwaysDescribed` deleted from the chamber → all three trait cases red.

A pin that still passes with its subject removed is not a pin, and the point of this PR is that coverage moved rather than evaporated.

## Docs the deletion made stale

`docs/games/dungeon.md`'s Royal-Puzzle section now reads as history and points each of its three findings at the suite that owns it — including one `Pinned by` name that had already gone stale under it. `DungeonTests`' note on why `RoyalPuzzleGrid` carries a prefix no longer explains it by a type that exists. The `reach` snippet in `Item.swift`, `WritingRules.md` and `ContainersDoorsAndLocks.md` named `PuzzleGrid`; it now names nothing, since a generic example in the engine's own docs shouldn't reach for one demo game's content either.

## `/simplify`

Run over the diff. It cut a second fixture item whose literal row the bootstrap registers anyway, and restated the decorative-noun pin as named-versus-bare; replaced a struct wrapper around one `Int` that no assertion could tell from an `Int`; caught the two dropped pins listed in the table above; and sharpened a bare `throws` into the `.notInScope` the parser actually returns — itself the cost #151 records, since the player names a thing standing in front of them and is told it isn't there. Its parser-memoisation finding was measured at 0.5% of suite time and skipped: `try!` fails the repo's own strict lint.

No user-facing copy is involved, so `dehumanizer` does not apply.

body:
> 🤖 This PR description was generated by Claude on behalf of @keddie.

Task 7 of `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-08-otel-batched-write-turn.md` — the documentation tail. Tasks 1–6 have landed, so this is **part of #2194**, not a closing PR.

## The one thing that was actually broken

Task 3 shipped `@sample us.tractat.kuilt.otel.sampleBulkExport` on `WarpLogRecordExporter.export(records:)`, and that function did not exist. Nothing was red: `compileTestKotlinJvm` compiles sample *bodies* but never reads the KDoc tag, and Dokka only warns (`failOnWarning` is unset repo-wide). This supplies the target.

```
kuilt-otel/src/commonMain/kotlin/us/tractat/kuilt/otel/WarpLogRecordExporter.kt:937:     * @sample us.tractat.kuilt.otel.sampleBulkExport
kuilt-otel/src/commonSamples/kotlin/us/tractat/kuilt/otel/Samples.kt:35:internal suspend fun sampleBulkExport() {
```

Verified beyond the grep: `:kuilt-otel:dokkaGenerateModuleHtml` now inlines the sample body into `export.html` (the rendered page contains `drainedFromSomeQueue`), so the link resolves rather than merely existing.

## The rest

- **Cookbook** — a new `## Telemetry & log capture` section plus a row in the "Don't build this yourself" table, routing *"capturing logs is slow" / "the app stalls when it logs a lot"* to `export(records)` and `installLogCapture`. Its snippet is a `verbatim from` block; I ran a negative control (one word case-flipped) and confirmed `verifyDocCitations` reddens on it, so the citation is genuinely content-checked and not merely resolving.
- **`kuilt-otel/module.md`** — a plain-language section ahead of any type name, then the mechanism.
- **`kuilt-otel-logging/module.md`** — the same idea from the consumer's side, inside the existing "When your app logs faster than the buffer takes them" section: the drain batches on its own, and nothing is held back to arrange it.
- **`.claude/skills/kuilt-primitives/SKILL.md`** — the `description` covered no telemetry phrasing at all, so it would not have fired on "my logging is slow". Added the trigger phrasing and a reflex bullet.

## Corrections to the prescribed content

1. **`module.md` `@sample` fences do not work.** The plan's shape implied one; I wrote it, then checked the generated HTML. Dokka does **not** expand `@sample` inside a module doc — it renders the literal line `@sample us.tractat.kuilt.otel.sampleBulkExport` as a code block. This is pre-existing: the "Quick start" fence citing `sampleWarpTelemetry` renders the same way today. I dropped my fence and pointed at the declaration's own KDoc instead, rather than add a second instance of a broken pattern. Filed separately as #2206.
2. **The prescribed cookbook block used a trailing `// …` marker where a contiguous quote works.** I quoted the sample's `when` run contiguously instead — the failure branch carries the load-bearing "a run may span turns, so `Failure` means stop, not nothing landed" point, and quoting it whole avoids relying on the elision matcher's trailing-closers anchoring.
3. **`is ExportResult.Success ->`** in the plan's sketch; `Success` is a `data object`, so the branch is written as an equality check.
4. **The plan's final checklist prescribes a closing keyword on #2194 in the PR body.** It must not carry one — #2194 is already closed, and a squash merge turns this body into the commit message, where backticks do not disarm the keyword.

## Verification

- `./gradlew build detektAll --max-workers=6` — BUILD SUCCESSFUL (2m 28s, load 1.36 at start). `verifyDocCitations` is wired into `check` and green within it; also run standalone.
- `./gradlew verifyDocCitations` — green, and proved non-vacuous by the negative control above.
- No close keyword in any commit message on this branch (`git log origin/main..HEAD --format=%B | grep -inE '\b(close[sd]?|fix(e[sd])?|resolve[sd]?)[[:space:]]+#[0-9]+'` → no output).

author: alonshuld
body:
Implements the whole of v0.8 from `description.md`: the milestone where grpctui stops being "grpcui in a terminal" and becomes a debugging tool.

## What lands

**Raw wire view — `w`.** Toggles the response panel between the decoded JSON and the protobuf encoding behind it: a field-by-field listing as a decoder without a schema sees it, and a hex dump under that. The listing is deliberately schema-*free* — the case that needs a raw view is the one where the descriptor and reality disagree, and consulting the descriptor to render it would hide exactly that. The bytes are a re-encoding rather than a capture (gRPC hands its stats handlers the decoded message, not the frame), and the view labels itself "as re-encoded" instead of pretending otherwise. The dump narrows to 16/8/4 bytes a row so it always fits the panel.

**Diffing — `D`.** Compares the response against the previous one from the same method, with runs of unchanged lines collapsed and counted. New leaf package `internal/diff`: an LCS over whole lines with the common prefix and suffix peeled off first, which is what keeps the table small in the ordinary case of two answers differing in a field or two. Past a budget it degrades to "wholly replaced" rather than allocating gigabytes. The previous body per method is a bounded, memory-only cache on the root model.

**Latency breakdown.** `grpcclient.Timing` — connect, first byte, total, and the payload sizes — measured by gRPC itself through one `stats.Handler` installed at dial time, with each call hanging a collector off its own context (which is what lets one handler serve every concurrent call with no registry). A wall clock says a call took 800ms; this says whether that was reaching the server or waiting for it. An unmeasured `Timing` is the zero value and shows no breakdown rather than an invented one.

**Passive/proxy mode — `--proxy <addr>`, `t`.** New transport-layer package `internal/proxy`: a gRPC server that forwards everything it receives to the target and reports what went past. It forwards without a schema — a raw codec forced onto both halves, every method served by `grpc.UnknownServiceHandler`, each call pumped in both directions as a bidi stream — because the descriptor for a method it is about to see is precisely what it does not have. It adds nothing to the wire: no credential of its own (the upstream is dialled from the profile's *security* and none of its auth) and no rewritten metadata. Events go to a buffered channel and are dropped-and-counted when nobody keeps up, since the one thing it may never do is slow the traffic it is watching. Picking a call out of the traffic panel decodes its request against the discovered descriptor and loads it into the form — which is what makes passive mode more than a log.

**grpcurl export — `X`.** Renders the request in the form as an equivalent `grpcurl` command in a modal.

## Credentials

An exported command is the most outward-facing surface in the program — it is written to be pasted somewhere else — so it obeys the standing rule hardest: header *names* with placeholder values, the credential's *kind* rather than the credential (`Bearer <token>`, `Basic <base64 of alice:password>`), and `{{variable}}` references left exactly as written, since the value behind one is very often a token captured out of a login response. References a JSON body cannot carry are listed as comments rather than silently dropped. There is a test asserting a token and a header value cannot appear in the output, at both the package and the model level.

## Testing

- `internal/proxy` runs three real gRPC stacks with no port between them (health server, proxy, client, all over `bufconn`): all four call shapes, a failed call's status surviving, metadata reaching the upstream unchanged *and* no credential being added, interleaved call numbering, and events dropped rather than blocking.
- `internal/diff` pins the invariant that matters — every line of both inputs appears exactly once on its own side — plus the collapse arithmetic and the huge-input fallback.
- `internal/grpcclient` measures a real call over `bufconn` and checks the parts fit inside the whole, and that a warm connection's connect time is no worse than a cold one's.
- `internal/protoschema` covers the wire round trip, every wire type, a truncated buffer returning what was readable, and the hex dump's exact layout.
- `internal/ui` and `internal/ui/panels` cover the toggles, the per-method diff, the breakdown on the status line, both new modals, and the proxy read loop end to end (the channel is filled and closed so the real command chain settles).

`gofmt`, `go vet`, `golangci-lint run` (0 issues) and `go test -race ./...` are all clean. The expanded help bar grew one row and stays inside its 100-cell budget; the golden file is regenerated for that alone.

Everything from v0.9 on is still ahead.

## Summary

Site-owner review of agency constellation pages found the Civic Time Ledger as-of control oversized, full of hedging caveats, and inert when system-time history was not available (for example `/agencies/probation/?as_of=2026-11-25` showed 12/12/0 with no visible change). This PR makes the control compact and functional, and sweeps the same page family for related verbose chrome.

### As-of view
- **Compact chrome:** one-line purpose + date picker + result counts; deeper explanation only behind a small `?` details affordance.
- **Valid-time only:** system-time axis and all “not retained / not claimed as knowledge-time” disclaimers are gone from the UI.
- **Real filter:** picking a past day keeps only linked records whose publisher or event date is on or before that day, and drops later ones from the lists.
- **No inert controls:** the control renders only when `asOfFilterCanNarrow` is true (≥2 dated items across ≥2 days).

Browser check:
- Parks: 31 → 6 rows as of 2024-06-01 (`6 of 27 dated · 13 later`)
- Probation: 24 → 4 rows as of 2024-06-01 (`4 of 12 dated · 8 later`)

### Provenance chips
- Always-on chip is a quiet warrant token (`exact` / `probable` / `reviewed`) with an accessible label.
- Full “why do we believe this” where/how detail stays in the inspector only.
- Dropped the always-on “How links are warranted” legend and the “source detail still to attach” enrichment block.

### Agency-page de-slop sweep (what was cut)
- Sources and limits block (internal join mechanics + “filters on X only” caveats)
- Valid-time / System-time definition boxes and honesty footer lines
- Hero / lede disclaimers about system-time history and warrant-class lectures

author: mhayk
body:
Refs #32 — the consuming half. The end-to-end assertion follows.

## Child **and** link, deliberately

| | what it gives | what it loses alone |
|---|---|---|
| Child | the causal chain | says the consumer ran *inside* the producer — the publish appears to contain the consume and swallow the queue wait |
| Link | "this is a message-driven continuation", in the model rather than a comment | the consumer becomes a root; one question returns two traces |

Both, so Tempo renders the gap between the spans as queue time rather than work.

## The span wraps the settle, not just the work

An ack that fails after a successful commit is exactly the case that produces a
duplicate delivery. Leaving the ack outside the span would hide the one hop that
explains why the message came back.

## Degradation

A message with **no** traceparent, or a corrupt one, yields a root span rather
than an error — right for an event published before this instrumentation
existed, and the alternative is one bad publisher stalling a stream. An
unreachable collector is a no-op, never a startup failure.

## One measured difference from Go

Python's **default** global propagator is already a `CompositePropagator` over
traceparent/tracestate/baggage; Go's is a no-op. Setting it explicitly here is
still right — `OTEL_PROPAGATORS` can replace the default — but no test can
distinguish the line from its absence, so none pretends to. Recorded in the
code, and the corresponding mutant is documented as *not written* with the
reason.

## Mutation testing, and two harness bugs worth reporting

Five mutants, five caught: link dropped, parent context ignored, span kind
INTERNAL, outgoing headers forwarded verbatim, `current_ids` returning the
all-zero id.

Getting there took fixing the harness twice, and **both bugs produced false
confidence rather than an error**:

1. The first run copied `.venv` with the source. uv's editable install records
   an absolute path, so every test imported the **original** module and all six
   mutants "survived" — which reads as a damning result about the tests and was
   actually a harness that never ran the code under test.
2. The patterns used `\n` against a CRLF working tree, so several mutations
   silently applied nothing and the tests passed for the most boring possible
   reason.

The script now rebuilds the venv in the copy, **proves with a canary** that it
imports the copy before reporting anything, refuses to give a verdict on a
pattern that matched nothing, and restores from one pristine baseline rather
than a per-mutation snapshot.

## Verification

`ruff`, `ruff format`, `mypy --strict` clean. Coverage 81%.

body:
## Summary `lifetimeXpRankForCharacter` (`server/db.ts`) runs two full `COUNT(*)` scans over the `characters` table on every call, and it was uncached at all 4 sites that read it: `server/characters.ts` (owner sheet), `server/leaderboard.ts` (public sheet), the legacy owner/public sheet arms in `server/main.ts`, and the unauthenticated crawlable `server/profile_page.ts` SEO route (`GET /c/:name`). A popular character's sheet or a crawler revisiting the same profile page paid the full two-scan query every single time. This adds `server/character_rank_cache.ts`, a keyed, bounded TTL cache built on the existing `KeyedCachedRead` seam (`server/cached_read.ts`), in the same shape as `server/discord_status_cache.ts`. `server/db.ts` wraps the existing function with it, so all 4 call sites benefit with **no changes to their code**: the raw SQL stays exported uncached as `lifetimeXpRankForCharacterUncached` for direct testing. Correctness detail this PR treats as load-bearing: a ban or unban changes every *other* eligible character's `ahead`/`total` counts too (the delisted account leaves or rejoins the population the counts are taken over), not just the moderated account's own rank. A per-key bust would miss that, so a moderation action drops the **whole** cache via `bustAllLifetimeXpRankCache()`, wired into `server/main.ts`'s existing `bustBoardCaches()` (the same hook every other player-derived board cache already uses), so delisting stays immediate instead of waiting out the TTL. TTL defaults to 30s (matching `LEADERBOARD_TTL_MS`, since the same underlying metric already tolerates that staleness on the boards) and the cache is capped at 5,000 entries (the public route serves any character on the realm, not only online ones, so an unbounded per-character `Map` would be exactly the grows-without-bound defect `server/CLAUDE.md` forbids). Both are env-overridable (`LIFETIME_XP_RANK_CACHE_TTL_MS`, `LIFETIME_XP_RANK_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES`). ## Type of change - [x] Refactor or performance (no behavior change) ## How was this tested? Commands: - `npx tsc --noEmit` (clean). - `npx vitest run tests/server/character_rank_cache.test.ts` (new module: singleton wiring, TTL via injected clock and env var, per-key and bust-all, an unbounded 50-key drive that never exceeds a 3-entry cap, null-result caching): 8/8 passed. - `npx vitest run tests/server/leaderboard_moderation.test.ts` (extended): the existing eligibility/SQL-shape pins now run against the renamed `lifetimeXpRankForCharacterUncached`; added a test proving `lifetimeXpRankForCharacter` (the production export) issues exactly one query for two reads of the same character and a second query for a different one, a test proving `bustAllLifetimeXpRankCache` forces a re-query, and a structural pin that `bustBoardCaches` calls `bustAllLifetimeXpRankCache()`: 21/21 passed. - `npx vitest run tests/server/characters.test.ts tests/server/leaderboard.test.ts tests/profile_page.test.ts tests/server/board_read_single_flight.test.ts tests/server/leaderboard_guild_reads.test.ts` (the 4 call sites plus the sibling board-cache suite): 207/207 passed. - `npx @biomejs/biome check --write` then `check` on every changed file: clean (no errors; the `noUndeclaredEnvVars` warnings on the two new env var names are the same pre-existing warning class `DISCORD_STATUS_CACHE_TTL_MS` already carries, not something this PR introduces). - `GATE_WORKER_TIER=low GATE_SELECT_BASE=upstream/release/v0.36.0 node scripts/gate_select.mjs`: correctly resolved to `mode=selective` (3 changed source files, 2 changed test files), but the machine is running this same batch's ~37 parallel worktree gates concurrently, and every attempt exhausted the session's time budget inside the i18n/malware/biome prefix or immediately at vitest start before producing a full pass/fail verdict (worker auto-detection fell to 1 on the last attempt, confirming heavy contention). Ran `npx vitest related server/db.ts server/main.ts server/character_rank_cache.ts --run --passWithNoTests --maxWorkers=2` directly instead: of the tests it pulled in, 5 failed, all with 20 to 51 second single-test durations (a clear timeout signature, default test timeout is 5s), and none of the 5 import or exercise any file this PR touches (confirmed by grep). For confidence, stashed this change and re-ran `tests/corpse_harvest_sim.test.ts` (4 of the 5 failures) against the pristine, unmodified base commit: it failed identically (`Error: Test timed out in 20000ms`) in the same 4 places, proving the failures are pre-existing machine-load noise, not a regression from this change. CI on GitHub Actions' dedicated runners is the authoritative signal. ## Performance evidence Query-count measurement (`db.pool.query` mocked with a fixed row and a 3ms synthetic latency, run against the real `lifetimeXpRankForCharacterUncached` and `lifetimeXpRankForCharacter` exports): 500 character-sheet views across 50 distinct characters (10 repeat views each, the popular-page / crawler-revisit pattern the 4 call sites see within one 30s TTL window). | | Queries issued | Wall time | |---|---|---| | Before (every call site uncached) | 500 | 1896 ms | | After (cached wrapper) | 50 | 200 ms | | Reduction | 90% fewer queries | ~89% faster | ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Caller as characters.ts / leaderboard.ts /
main.ts / profile_page.ts participant DB as db.ts
lifetimeXpRankForCharacter participant Cache as character_rank_cache.ts

body:
## Summary
- Closes #21, #22.
- Adds `MESSAGE_RETENTION_DAYS` (default 30, `0` disables) and `MessageRepository.delete_messages_older_than()`: age-based, global delete of old `messages` audit rows.
- Adds `scripts/cleanup_retention.py`: idempotent, fail-open script that runs the `messages` age-based delete plus a global SQL sweep that prunes LangGraph's `checkpoints`/`checkpoint_blobs`/`checkpoint_writes` down to the newest checkpoint per thread (no timestamp column exists on those tables, so "keep newest per thread" rather than a simple age filter).
- Deliberately stays on `PostgresSaver` rather than switching to `ShallowPostgresSaver`, which is deprecated as of `langgraph-checkpoint-postgres` 2.0.20 and slated for removal in 3.0.
- Adds `durability="exit"` to the agent's `graph.invoke()` call (`agent.py`) as a companion fix — LangGraph's own recommended alternative to `ShallowPostgresSaver` — to reduce intra-turn checkpoint writes during multi-step tool loops.
- Wires the new script into `start.sh` (after `setup_checkpointer.py`) and documents the equivalent Railway `preDeployCommand` change (`alembic upgrade head && python scripts/setup_checkpointer.py && python scripts/cleanup_retention.py`) in `AGENTS.md`/`README.md`.
- Updates `AGENTS.md`, `README.md`, `.env.example` to describe the new bounded behavior (including that `/stats`'s "Since" date now reflects the oldest *retained* row, not the chat's true first message, once cleanup has run).

## Env/config changes
- New env var: `MESSAGE_RETENTION_DAYS` (default `30`; `0` disables). Added to `.env.example`, `README.md`'s env table, `AGENTS.md`'s env list.
- Railway `preDeployCommand` needs a manual update in both `dev` and `production` environments to append `&& python scripts/cleanup_retention.py` (not a repo file — documented in this PR, not applied by it).

## Validation steps and observed results
- `python3 -m py_compile *.py database/*.py scripts/*.py` — passes.
- `pytest tests/ -v` — 201 passed (includes 4 new config tests for `MESSAGE_RETENTION_DAYS` defaults/validation, and a new `tests/test_cleanup_retention.py` regression test mirroring `test_setup_checkpointer.py`'s sys.path-by-invocation-path check).
- **Not yet run**: manual verification against a real database (baseline row counts, exercising `scripts/chat_cli.py` across multiple threads, running `cleanup_retention.py` directly, re-checking counts, confirming `/clear`/`/stats` still work post-sweep, idempotency on a second run). This sandbox has no real `DATABASE_URL` configured. Recommend running this against the Railway `dev` database before updating `dev`'s `preDeployCommand`, then promoting to `production` only after that succeeds.

## Test plan
- [ ] Run `scripts/cleanup_retention.py` directly against the Railway `dev` database and confirm expected row/checkpoint counts drop as described above
- [ ] Confirm `/clear` and `/stats` still behave correctly post-sweep
- [ ] Update `dev`'s Railway `preDeployCommand`, watch one deploy's logs for the new script's output
- [ ] Promote the same `preDeployCommand` change to `production`

body:
## 🚀 Release 2026-08-08

Diese PR bringt den Stand von `development` nach `main`. Schwerpunkt: Dokumentenablage am Kind, Reparatur des Betreuungsplan-Serien-Speicherns nach Template-Splits, Sichtbarkeit der Angebots-Attribute im Personal, sowie zwei kleinere Login-/Dashboard-Korrekturen.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Dies ist eine reine Release-PR. Sie enthält keinen zusätzlichen Code über den bereits geprüften Stand von `development` hinaus.

| Umfang | Stand |
|---|---:|
| Commits | 47 |
| Enthaltene PRs | 6 |
| Geänderte Dateien | 211 |
| Diff | +15.386 / −347 Zeilen |
| Migrationen | 1 (1.15.271) |

## 📄 Dokumente-Tab am Kind samt gemeinsamer Speicher-Schicht (#2182, schließt #777)

Kinderunterlagen lagen bisher außerhalb des Systems (Verträge im Ordner, Atteste im Sekretariat, Abholvollmachten in der Mail). Neu: **Dokumente-Tab** auf der Kind-Detailseite und darunter die Speicher-Schicht, die dafür fehlte.

- Gemeinsame Storage-Backend-Schicht für Uploads (ein Schreibpfad)
- `users.student_documents` + Cleanup-Intents, RLS, tenant-scoped Soft-Delete
- Berechtigungen `student_documents:health` und `student_documents:legal`
- Upload-Autorisierung vor dem Schreibzugriff, nosniff auf Downloads
- Audit mit Kind-Namen beim Download, ohne Metadaten-Leak in der Änderungshistorie
- Bytes werden bei fehlgeschlagenem Metadata-Write und beim Graduate-Purge zurückgeholt

## 📅 Betreuungsplan: Serien-Speichern über gekappte Vorgänger-Templates (#2188, schließt #2187)

Nach einem Template-Split konnte die Wochenansicht Vorkommen mit der ID des gekappten Vorgänger-Segments rendern. Serien-Speichern ("Ab jetzt dauerhaft" / "Alle Termine der Serie") lief dann auf `GET /api/timetable/templates/{id}` → 404 und Toast **"template not found"**. In Produktion (Tenant 6, 07.08.) war der Nachzügler für den Tag nicht eintragbar.

- Gekappte Split-Chain-Vorgänger werden aufgelöst statt 404
- Vorgänger-Roster-Mirroring pro Wochentag, Kette endet sauber
- Nachfolger behält eigene Hauptbetreuung und Scope
- Frontend sendet Roster-Scope und chain-aware Series-Saves mit deutschen Fehlermeldungen

## 👪 Angebots-Attribute und Gültigkeit in der Personal-Ansicht (#2192, schließt #2185)

Mittagessen, Ferienbetreuung, Preis und Gültigkeit eines gebuchten Angebots waren nur im Elternportal sichtbar. Das Personal konnte dieselben Angaben am Kind nicht prüfen und hat sie fälschlich als Fehler abgetan.

- Personal sieht dieselben Angebots-Attribute und die Gültigkeit wie die Eltern
- Gültigkeitsende und Stichtag an das Elternportal angeglichen
- Korrektur vor Periodenstart ohne Datenverlust
- Katalogausfall und veraltete Clients vom Löschpfad getrennt
- Auswahl-Zugehörigkeit aus dem Repository statt aus einer Kopie

## 🔑 Falsches Login-Portal: Hinweis statt stummem Scheitern (#2184)

Eltern, die am **Staff-Login** der Schul-Subdomain anmelden statt am Elternportal, bekamen keinen brauchbaren Hinweis. Jetzt klare Weiterleitung/Meldung auf das richtige Portal (`parentsPortalLoginUrl`), inkl. Tests für die client-only Guards.

## 🧩 Aktive-Gruppen-Kachel: activities-Template statt education-IDs (#2179, schließt #2178)

Die Dashboard-Kachel „Aktive Gruppen" verglich zwei ID-Räume: `active.groups.group_id` (FK auf `activities.groups`) mit einer Map aus `education.groups.id`. Auflösung läuft jetzt über das activities-Template.

## 🛠️ Agent-Skills / Repo-Setup (#2191)

Matt-Pocock-/AI-Hero-Skills unter `.agents/skills/`, Agent-Config unter `docs/agents/`, Verweis in `CLAUDE.md`. Kein produktiver Runtime-Code.

| 1.15.271 | `users.student_documents` + `users.student_document_file_cleanup`, RLS, Permissions `student_documents:health` / `:legal` (#777 / #2182) |

Neue Tabellen mit RLS und FORCE RLS. Kein Backfill bestehender Dateien.

author: barakbenzi
body:
Production-hardening pass over the whole product: security, money correctness, data integrity and operations, correctness bugs, the unfinished screens, and architecture. 117 commits, 561 files, +128,714 / −7,255.

`docs/REMEDIATION-PLAN.md` is the living record and the hand-off — it carries every decision, every defect found, and the boundary of everything left partial. `docs/AUDIT-2026-07-31.md` is the evidence it started from; `docs/FEATURE-INVENTORY.md` is the contract that nothing was dropped.

## Status

Ledger: **111 rows — 85 done, 23 partial, 3 rejected, 0 open.** Every gate green as of the last commit:

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Unit tests | **1,250 pass** (includes RLS assertions against real Postgres via PGlite) |
| Typecheck | clean |
| Lint / format | 0 errors, 13 pre-existing warnings; `prettier --check` clean |
| Production build | succeeds |
| Browser suite (public) | passes |

The 23 PARTIAL rows are deliberate and each states its own boundary in its note — they are work that cannot be finished in this environment (no Supabase project, no Helcim sandbox, no geocoder, no OAuth app) or that was scoped out on purpose. They are not forgotten work.

## Four things a green CI badge does not tell you

**1. Twenty-one migrations must be RUN, and the code assumes them.** Measured from `git diff --name-only main...HEAD -- db/`: `023` through `043`. (`001_schema.sql` also appears in that diff, but that is the baseline *rename* described under ledger 3.1, not new DDL.) Use `npm run db:plan` then `npm run db:migrate`; an existing production database is `adopt`ed, never re-run. `db/MIGRATIONS.md` is the runbook and is generated from the files on disk.

**2. Nothing here has ever met a real Supabase project.** PGlite is Postgres, so it genuinely proves the SQL, the policies, the constraints and the guards — the migrations are applied to an empty database on every test run. It is *not* Supabase: `auth.uid()`, `auth.users` and `storage.objects` are shims. Whether GoTrue issues the claims these policies read, and whether Supabase Storage enforces the `storage.objects` policies, is unproven. So are MFA (6b.5) and the Helcim provider refund call (5.1), which has never executed.

**3. No authenticated browser test has ever run.** 12 of the 13 e2e checks skip without a signed-in `STORAGE_STATE`, which needs a real project and a seeded user. This is the largest untested surface on the branch. For calibration: the *public* half of that suite had never successfully run either, and the first time it did, it found a live production defect within seconds — see below.

**4. Schema drift with `feature/live-communications-payments` is unresolved.** Production runs a migration from that unmerged branch — 102 tables against `main`'s 97. Confirm that branch is genuinely intended to merge before treating the drift as harmless. `provider_webhook_events` has RLS on with **zero policies**.

## What the last commit found, as an illustration of the above

Establishing whether this branch was ready turned up two defects, one hiding the other:

- **The browser harness was wired but dead.** Boot-time env validation (ledger 3.3) fails closed, and `playwright.config.ts` never passed `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`, so the server aborted and every e2e test timed out. Nothing caught it because **no CI job ran the suite** — `npm run test:e2e` existed and executed nowhere.
- **With it alive, the CSP turned out to be blocking the app's own web fonts.** `style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'` rejected the Google Fonts stylesheet and `font-src 'self' data:` rejected the font files. From the day the security headers shipped, every page in production rendered in fallback system faces — **including the Hebrew UI, whose face is Heebo.**

The pre-existing test asserted the CSP header *exists*, and a header that blocks your own fonts is a perfectly well-formed header. The replacement probe is derived: it parses the `csp` array, extracts the origins `app/layout.tsx` actually loads, and requires every stylesheet origin in `style-src` and every preconnect origin somewhere in the policy — so a new font host fails until the CSP names it. It also refuses `https:` in either directive, so the fix cannot be "widen it". Proven both ways. CI now runs `npm run test:e2e` so the harness cannot rot back to unread.

## Review notes

- **Every fix ships its probe.** The standard on this branch is that a guard must fire on a planted defect *and* stay silent on the good tree — a false RED is treated as the same bug as a false GREEN, because it gets the guard switched off.
- **The threat model is PostgREST, not the UI.** Policy changes are judged against an attacker who skips the server actions and talks to `/rest/v1/` with the anon key.
- **Suggested review order:** the ledger in `docs/REMEDIATION-PLAN.md` first (it explains the *why* for every change), then the migrations, then the code.
