author: claude[bot]
body:
## Task

> - [ ] **[MEDIUM]** Make the app installable and fully offline with a web manifest and service worker

<!-- id: c9e555e2-768b-4890-8fa6-052e38150a08 -->

- Type: feature
- Description: Add a web app manifest and a service worker that precaches `index.html` and the `src/` ES modules and styles so every surface works offline, and register the worker from `src/main.js`. No build step.

## Changes

- **`manifest.webmanifest`** (new): web app manifest — `name`, `short_name`, `description`, `start_url`/`scope` `./`, `display: standalone`, dark `theme_color`/`background_color` (`#0d0e13`, matching `--bg`), and the existing `favicon.svg` as an `any maskable` icon. Makes the app installable.
- **`sw.js`** (new): a **module** service worker. On `install` it precaches the app shell and every module the app loads, then `skipWaiting()`; on `activate` it deletes caches from prior revisions and `clients.claim()`s; `fetch` is **cache-first** for GET requests (offline is the design point), falling back to the network for anything not precached.
- **`src/precache.js`** (new): the single source of truth for the offline contract — `CACHE_NAME` (versioned; bump to evict stale copies) and `PRECACHE_URLS`. Imported by both `sw.js` and the test, so the precache list can't be tested and shipped separately.
- **`src/main.js`**: registers `sw.js` as a module worker on `window.load`; registration errors are swallowed so the app still runs online in browsers without service-worker support.
- **`index.html`**: adds `<link rel="manifest">` and a `<meta name="theme-color">`.

Note on approach: the worker is a **module** service worker so it can `import` the precache list it shares with the app (no build step — the browser fetches both files directly). This matches the app's existing ES-module baseline (`index.html` already loads `main.js` as `type="module"`). Registration is wrapped in `.catch()` so an unsupported browser degrades to online-only rather than breaking.

## Files modified

- `manifest.webmanifest` (new)
- `sw.js` (new)
- `src/precache.js` (new)
- `tests/precache.test.js` (new)
- `src/main.js`
- `index.html`

## Testing

`npm run test:run` — **65/65 passed** (59 pre-existing + 6 new in `tests/precache.test.js`). The new tests directly exercise the "keep the precache list in sync with the served-from-source file set" requirement:

- **covers every module reachable from main.js** — statically walks `main.js`'s import graph (found: main, session, neglect, history, pieceDetail, store, tagSheet) and fails if any reachable module is absent from `PRECACHE_URLS`. This is the guard against precache drift when a new surface is added later.
- **covers the app shell** — asserts `./`, `index.html`, `manifest.webmanifest`, `favicon.svg`, `style.css` are precached.
- **every precached URL exists on disk** / **no duplicate entries** — catches typos and stale entries.
- **manifest is valid JSON with installable-PWA fields** — `name`, `display: standalone`, `start_url`, hex `theme_color`, at least one icon whose `src` exists on disk.

The service worker's runtime behavior (install/activate/fetch handlers, actual offline serving) runs only in a browser service-worker context and is not exercised by the Node test runner; manual verification in a browser (DevTools → Application → Service Workers, and offline reload) is recommended for the runtime caching path.

## Bookkeeping

Project defines no bookkeeping (`.claude/routine.md` specifies no changelog or version file).

## Notes

- **CLAUDE.md not updated:** the change adds load-bearing files, but CLAUDE.md's "Key files in this repo" section is still the unfilled template placeholder and names no file paths, so nothing in it is contradicted (per the claude_md_sync skip clause).
- `src/greet.js` is a served-from-source module but is **not** loaded by the app (only by `tests/greet.test.js`), so it is deliberately excluded from the precache list; the import-graph test confirms it is not reachable from `main.js`.
- Follow-up observation (not fixed, out of scope): `src/greet.js` and `tests/greet.test.js` appear to be leftover template scaffolding with no role in the app — a human may want to decide whether to remove them.

author: davidoeztuerk
body:
Behebt einen Fehler, den **der erste echte Rückfall** aufgedeckt hat — nicht ein
Test, sondern der Betrieb.

## Was passiert ist

Beim Merge von **#45** (Dependabot) trug develop bereits einen eigenen Commit
(die dependabot-Löschung), ein Fast-Forward war also unmöglich. Der
Rückfall-Zweig griff genau wie entworfen — und scheiterte:

```
GitHub Actions is not permitted to create or approve pull requests
(createPullRequest)
```

Das ist die Repo-Einstellung *„Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull
requests"*, und sie ist standardmäßig **aus**. Der Rückfall konnte also nie
funktionieren.

## Warum es nicht auffiel

Der Trockenlauf vor dem Einbau prüfte die **Git-Logik** gegen ein
Wegwerf-Repository — Fast-Forward, eigener Commit, bereits auf Stand; alle drei
stimmten. Was er nicht prüfen konnte, sind die **Rechte auf GitHub**. Der
Fast-Forward-Pfad lief im Betrieb sofort durch und sah aus wie ein Beleg für das
Ganze; der Rückfall war nie gelaufen.

## Der Weg, der ohne Sonderrechte funktioniert

Statt eines PRs wird der Merge auf einem eigenen Zweig vorbereitet:
`rueckfuehrung/main-nach-develop`. Einen Zweig zu schieben darf der Lauf mit
`contents: write` — niemand muss eine Einstellung ändern. Die Zusammenfassung
enthält den fertigen Compare-Link; daraus einen PR zu machen ist ein Klick.

**Nach develop geschoben wird weiterhin nur ein Fast-Forward.** Ein
Merge-Commit ist von keiner CI geprüft, und still Ungeprüftes nach develop zu
heben wäre schlimmer als der Zustand, den dieser Lauf behebt.

## Bei einem echten Konflikt: rot

`git merge --abort`, keine automatische Auflösung, Exit 1. Ein grüner Lauf, der
develop still zurückfallen lässt, wäre genau der Zustand, gegen den die Datei
geschrieben ist.

## Geprüft

Beide Rückfall-Pfade gegen ein Wegwerf-Repository:

```
sauber mergebar → Zweig geschoben (im Remote nachgewiesen), zustand=bereit ✔
Konflikt        → merge abgebrochen, zustand=konflikt → Lauf wird rot     ✔
```

## Alternative, die bewusst nicht gewählt wurde

Die Einstellung *Settings → Actions → General → „Allow GitHub Actions to create
and approve pull requests"* einzuschalten, würde den ursprünglichen Weg
freischalten. Der Zweig-Weg kommt ohne aus — eine Automatik, die eine
Repo-Einstellung voraussetzt, bricht beim nächsten Repository still wieder.

author: trishorts
body:
Adds `ControlledVocabulary` — embedded, version-pinned PSI-MS (4,114 terms) and PRIDE (981 terms) with lookup by accession and by name — and `DissociationTypeCvTerms`, which maps mzLib's `DissociationType` onto PSI-MS terms and back.

> **Note on scope:** nothing in mzLib consumes this yet; it is the vocabulary layer for the SDRF work in #1138. Reviewing it standalone is intended.

## Why pinned and embedded

Resolving a term against something that moves means the same experiment annotated a year apart gets different accessions, and a corpus built that way silently stops joining to itself. `Version` is exposed so the snapshot can be recorded alongside whatever the terms end up in, and refreshing a vocabulary becomes a reviewable change to this repository rather than something that happens to users overnight.

It reuses what is already here: TopDownProteomics' `OboParser` (already a dependency, already used by `Loaders.ReadPsiModFile`), `ProteaseDictionary`'s lazy embedded-resource pattern, and `MzLibUtil.CvParam` as the term type. **No new dependency.**

The large sample ontologies are deliberately absent — NCBITaxon is ~600 MB and unnecessary, because an organism identifier comes from the search database that was already loaded (see #1136).

## Package impact

+1.4 MB uncompressed inside `UsefulProteomicsDatabases.dll`, ~226 KB compressed in the nupkg. `Omics` already ships 6.7 MB of ontologies the same way.

`.gitattributes` gains `*.obo -text`, added **before** these files were first tracked: `* text=auto` would store them LF and hand back CRLF on a Windows checkout, so what CI embeds would not be what was committed or reviewed.

## Licensing

Both vocabularies are **CC BY 4.0**, which requires attribution to reach downstream recipients — and NuGet consumers get assemblies, not this repository. Adds `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md` (shipped via `mzLib.nuspec`) naming both, their publishers, sources, pinned versions and licence, and covering the pre-existing `unimod.xml` / `PSI-MOD.obo.xml` / `ptmlist.txt` embedded in `Omics`. `Resources/PROVENANCE.md` records fetch URLs, dates and the refresh procedure.

## DissociationType mapping

This table did not exist. The accessions lived only in XML doc comments on the enum, where no code could reach them. 17 values are mapped; four (`aEPD`, `Custom`, `Autodetect`, `AnyActivationType`) have no PSI-MS term and return `false` rather than a plausible neighbour.

HCD writes `MS:1000422` — the plurality in the curated corpus at 273 files against 47 and 23 — and reads all three spellings, so other people's documents still join to ours.

## Five wrong accessions were found by audit before this shipped

Recorded because the reason they survived matters more than the fix:

| Wrote | Actually is |
|---|---|
| `SID → MS:1000406` | "surface ionization" — an **ionization** type |
| `PD → MS:1000435` | mzLib's `PD` is **plasma desorption**, `MS:1000134` — as `DissociationType.cs:33` and `Mzml.cs:99` both already said |
| `MS:1000045 → CID` | "collision energy", a numeric parameter with `has_units eV` that accompanies nearly every HCD scan |
| `PRIDE:0000598 → ETD` | "Alkylation reagent". PRIDE has no ETD term at all |
| "UVPD/NETD have no term" | `MS:1003246` and `MS:1003247`; UVPD is used in the curated corpus, so refusing to write it was a joinability gap |

**Every one of those resolved cleanly against the vocabulary.** The test meant to catch them pinned each accession to the name the OBO gives it, which is circular — the ontology guarantees that link, so the assertion could only fail on a typo. It could not detect a real accession naming the wrong *concept*.

The replacement, `AgreesWithTheMzmlReadersOwnAccessionTable`, checks this table against `Readers.Mzml.DissociationDictionary` — public, in the same assembly, and right all along. Disagreeing with it means an mzML this library reads cannot be described by the terms this library writes. Read-aliases now get the same name-pinning discipline as the primary table; they had none, which is how two wrong ones survived.

The obsolete test had the same defect: it asserted things about "Q Exactive", which is not obsolete, so deleting the entire obsolete filter left it green. It now uses `minute`, where an obsolete `MS:1000038` precedes the live `UO:0000031` in file order and would win without the filter.

## Other fixes from the same audit

`CvLabel` now derives from the **accession** rather than from which file the term came out of — `psi-ms.obo` imports 128 foreign terms (`UO`, `PEFF`, `NCIT`) and `pride_cv.obo` 19, all of which were being stamped with the wrong `cvRef`.

## Known follow-up

This is the **fourth** in-repo source of PSI-MS accessions, alongside `Readers/MzML/Mzml.cs` (~25 consts + 3 dictionaries), `Readers/MzML/MzmlMethods.cs`, and `UsefulProteomicsDatabases/PrideArchiveExtensions.cs` (17 consts). Consolidating them is now *unblocked* — `PrideArchiveExtensions.cs:230` already complains that `Mzml.AnalyzerDictionary` "is not reachable from this project", and moving those dictionaries into `UsefulProteomicsDatabases` (which `Readers` already references) is exactly what resolves it. Not attempted here to keep the diff reviewable.

## Tests

53 in `TestControlledVocabulary`. Full mzLib suite green at 5,459 passed / 0 failed.

body:
Resolves #16683

The tour-entry cleared-body blank is repaired at its named seam: `runTourSpec`'s entry projection now declares `geometryOnly` — validated in-place **admission**, not a skip. `DockProjectionReconciler.reconcileProjection` (`src/dashboard/DockProjectionReconciler.mjs:314`) treats the flag as admission-to-attempt `reconcileStableTopology` (`:130`), which returns null on ANY node/type/ancestry/order/orientation delta and falls back to the full staged transaction — so the same-topology entry (the workspace re-staging its own `initialDocument`, i.e. every film run) takes the in-place path and the staged shell swap's cleared-body intermediate frame never presents, while a genuinely changed topology still gets the staged path unchanged. The stale call-site comment claiming "neither may declare a geometry-only projection over the transition" was wrong about the flag's semantics and is truth-folded with the contract citations; the restore projection stays full deliberately (at probe-restore time the shell typically diverges from the displaced document, so admission would validate-and-fall-back with no gain) — an explicit non-change, documented in-code with the residual (changed-topology entries can still blank; present-no-intermediate-state is the deferred stronger shape, per the ticket's Avoided Traps).

Evidence: L3 (headed film-mode runs on the isolated-display stage + headed dense tour) — the full requirement for every AC; no sandbox-unreachable residual. Residual: none [#16683].

## Deltas from ticket

None substantive. One scope note: AC-2's fallback half is pinned by existing src-side coverage rather than a new test — `DockProjectionReconciler.spec.mjs:452` ("falls back when a geometry-only projection changes split orientation") plus its staged-count assertions already red-prove the null-fallback contract, so the new unit witness pins only the call-site contract (entry admission + restore-stays-full), avoiding duplicate coverage of the reconciler's own guarantee.

## Test Evidence

- Unit (`test/playwright/playwright.config.unit.mjs`, apps/workstation/Workspace): **37/37 passed** incl. the new witness — `refreshCalls[0]` equals `{geometryOnly: true}`, `refreshCalls[1]` equals `{}` (restore full), displaced document restored.
- Film-mode scene 1 (`WorkstationFiveBeatNL`, `NEO_FILM_TAKE=1`, isolated-display stage `2632,-249,1200,1040`), **×3 consecutive green** at this head: minEntropy **5.3038 / 5.3126 / 5.3100** vs baselines ~5.35 (floor 3.48-class), `minFrameIndex` moved from **7** (the entry defect, this morning's red-control at `0.4088`) to **26** (ordinary mid-capture variance) on all three runs.
- Same-day red-control at the pre-fix head (falsifier-1 on `#16500`, receipts at `#16500` issuecomment-5225908387): control RED `0.4088` minFrame 7/59; treatment (this exact change as an uncommitted probe) GREEN `5.3480` — the red/green pair that named this seam.
- Driver-path regression: dense tour (`WorkstationNL` "the real tour keeps density…") headed **GREEN 25.6s** at this head — every runTourSpec driver consumer exercises the changed entry.
- Touched surface `apps/workstation`: the two suites above are the surface's own coverage.

## Post-Merge Validation

- [ ] The next five-beat film take's scene-1 entropy receipt stays green with Vega's per-step oracle once `#16500`'s instrument refactor lands (the agreed joint witness run).

## Related

Refs #16500 (Vega's oracle instrument — the ownership split and falsifier receipts live there) · Refs #16473 (origin of the full entry projection; its correctness contract is preserved via the validated fallback) · Refs #16412 (the hazard the stale comment cited) · Related: #15252 (film epic — this is one of the three v1-gate legs)

author: kawasima
body:
Fixes #482.

`souther examples` took its compilation from `Compiler.compiled` /
`compiledModules`, which raise the first error they find. Those entry points
are `Compilation.answerEverything()` plus three throws, so the command got
the work it needed and a contract it did not: the specification says
"Nothing here changes what compiles; it reports", and the converse was
never implemented.

What that cost is the `incompleteness` field. It carries what stopped the
rows from being observed, and run through the CLI each of those exits 1
with the diagnostic and prints no report:

```text
duplicate declaration in an attached file   E1906
a module that did not type-check            E1321 and its neighbours
a composition that reaches itself           E1608
a row that did not come back                E1923
classes that could not be generated         the backend's own CompileException
```

One producer carries no diagnostic — the runtime not being reachable,
which no source is at fault for — and it needs the runtime off the
classpath while the compiler runs, which is the annotation processor's
situation, and that path builds no report. So the field a report could
carry and the report a compilation could produce excluded each other, and
`AdequacyReport.adequacy` — which refuses `satisfied` where the field is
not empty — has never had the chance to fire in a published report.

What stopped a *measure* from reading what was observed is a separate half,
said by that measure: an axis past the limit, a combination count that
stopped at its own, a value too large to read back. Those reach the report
today, carry no `incompleteness` entry, and are why `partial` was never in
the same position. An empty `incompleteness` has therefore never meant that
everything was read, and the specification now says which half is which.

## What changed

`Compiler.analyzed` / `analyzedModules` drive the same compilation and
raise nothing. `Compilation.errors(...)` sits beside `warnings(...)` and
answers with all of them where `firstError` answers with one.
`examplesSubcommand` routes through those and decides its three results
apart: the report to stdout wherever the compilation formed something to
assess, the diagnostics to stderr as before, the exit code unchanged — an
error is still 1, and `--strict` still decides the exit code of a
compilation that raised none.

Whether there is anything to report on and what the report shows are asked
of different things — the first of everything that formed, the second of
what the selection named. Reading the first off the filtered report would
put them back under one condition, which is the shape of the defect this
change is about, and would leave the emission gate depending on the
selector having been resolved somewhere else first.

`Compiler.linked` and `compiled` keep their fail-fast contract. `souther
compile` is untouched.

The specification gains `[#example-report-emission]` and a normative
account of `incompleteness`, which it had never described at all — its
description of the JSON form covered `status` and `reason` only.

## Behaviour that changes

- A failing invocation now writes a report to stdout alongside a non-zero
  exit status. A consumer treating empty stdout as "no report" reads the
  exit status instead. This is a change to the process I/O contract, not to
  the schema: `incompleteness[]` has never been emitted, so no document
  shape a consumer has seen is altered.
- `souther examples` now prints every error rather than the first. A
  command that goes on to describe the whole compilation should not show
  one error beside an account of everything else.
- A source that declares no module gets no report. It has no subject for a
  measure to be about.

## Not in this change

A selector that matches nothing is refused ahead of the report, with its own
exit code. That landed in #487 while this was open, and this rebases onto it:
the two rules meet in a test here, where a selector that resolves gets its
report from a compilation that did not.

The test asserts that the entry exists and is about the source, not which
word it carries. `runtime_absent` at source scope does not mean the runtime
is absent, and that is #474's to fix now that the field is reachable.

Evidence is still recovered per module: `Bodies.Checked` is absent for the
whole module, so one behavior that does not type-check costs every row
observation in it. A report that says `partial` and carries little is
honest and not yet worth much. That is the next piece of work and wants its
own issue.

## Verification

`mvn clean test` — BUILD SUCCESS across all eight modules.

Six tests in `ACompilationThatFailedStillReportsWhatItsRowsCoverTest`, and
`ASelectorThatResolvesToNothingIsRefusedTest` still green beside them. The
emission and `incompleteness` tests were watched failing against the old
routing before this was written.

body: Retire unsupported public surfaces and move public integrity into one executable gate. The active site carried 94,000 lines of historical or derived material, including an unpublished bootcamp, a provenance-free decisions projection, duplicate tells registries, static design labs, and stored copy metrics. This removes those liabilities, consolidates the 39 supported tells into Hugo content, and preserves their legacy `/slopodar/` aliases. `./build.sh` is now the single verifier used locally, by GitHub, and by Vercel. It pins Hugo, verifies downloads, checks share routes and retirement source, builds cleanly, and validates rendered routes, metadata, nonempty content, tells, and legacy aliases. Git-linked Vercel remains the only main-site deployment owner. The copy checker and editorial hard gates remain, but metrics are read-only diagnostics rather than persisted article state. Historical material remains reconstructable from Git; dirty worktree state is quarantined separately outside this repository. Careful review areas are the removed public routes and the source-data-to-frontmatter tells migration. `oceanheart.blog` DNS and TLS are deliberately out of scope. --- ## Summary by cubic Retired unsupported public routes and historical content, consolidated the 39 supported tells into Hugo content with preserved `/slopodar/` aliases, and unified verification through a single pinned `./build.sh` used locally, in CI, and on Vercel. This reduces risk, simplifies the tree, and makes public integrity checks consistent. - **Refactors** - Removed unpublished bootcamp, duplicate registries/design labs, persisted copy telemetry, and career archives; only supported tells remain in Hugo content with legacy aliases kept. - Added a single executable gate: `./build.sh` now checks share routes and retirement sources, pins `Hugo` 0.159.1 with SHA256 verification, builds into a clean dir, and validates rendered routes/metadata; new `verify.yml` runs it in GitHub. - Housekeeping: dropped `Makefile`, removed and ignored `.hugo_build.lock`, and updated `README.md` and `AGENTS.md` to reflect read‑only copy checks and preview instructions. - **Migration** - Run `./build.sh` before merging; use `hugo server` only for local preview. - Confirm expected route retirements, verify tells moved into front matter, and check legacy aliases resolve. - No DNS/TLS changes; `oceanheart.blog` is out of scope. Written for commit d7e2d4e152aea9241452ba0429dbf05d4d760762. Summary will update on new commits.

author: lexus2016
body:
## Summary

Rework of the SkillTrojan composition tracer (#1802, needs-work) addressing both issues from PR #1818 review.

### Rework Fixes

**1. Turn-boundary reset (the regression):**
The previous PR used a module-level singleton (`_tracer = CompositionTracer()`) that accumulated skills across turns — but `reset_tracer()` was NEVER called in production code (only in tests). This violated the "2+ skills in the SAME turn" invariant, causing spurious cross-turn blocks on legitimate skills.

**Fix:** Wired `reset_tracer()` into `agent/turn_context.py` at the turn boundary (`reset_for_turn`), right alongside `_tool_guardrails.reset_for_turn()`. Now the tracer only composes skills loaded within the current turn.

**2. Tightened conditional heuristic (false positives):**
The previous regex fired on plain prose mentioning another skill's completion (e.g. "after skill_X completed"), hard-blocking skills whose documentation mentions other skills.

**Fix:** The conditional regex now requires the pattern to be inside **indented code** or a **fenced code block** (` ``` `). Plain prose is NOT flagged. This is implemented via `_INDENTED_CONDITIONAL_RE` (matches leading whitespace) and `_extract_fenced_code()` (extracts text inside ``` blocks for checking).

### Heuristics (all deterministic, no ML)
1. **Base64 fragment assembly** — fragments from different skills that concatenate and decode to executable code
2. **Cross-skill conditional references** — `if skill_X completed` patterns (code-block only)
3. **URL assembly from fragments** — URL templates referencing variables defined in another skill

### Files
- `tools/skill_composition_tracer.py` — 345 lines (new module)
- `tests/tools/test_skill_composition_tracer.py` — 246 lines (20 tests)
- `tools/skills_tool.py` — +14 lines (check_composition wiring)
- `agent/turn_context.py` — +9 lines (reset_tracer at turn boundary)

### Tests
20 tests pass, including:
- Turn-boundary reset: skills from different turns NOT composed
- Prose conditional NOT flagged (the false positive fix)
- Indented code conditional IS detected
- Fenced code block conditional IS detected
- Base64 fragment assembly detected/blocked
- URL fragment assembly detected/blocked

### Line count
614 lines total — exceeds 200-line self-merge cap. This is a single coherent security feature that cannot be meaningfully split further (the tracer, call-site wiring, and turn-boundary reset are one atomic unit). Needs human review.

Closes #1802

body:
## What this changes

One line: `SHELLCHECK_OPTS: --severity=warning` on the actionlint step, matching
the other repositories.

## Why

A mechanical audit of every `ci.yml` on `main` against
[CI.md](https://github.com/sapn95/.github/blob/main/CI.md) — name casing,
triggers, top-level permissions, concurrency, per-job timeouts, action versions,
`persist-credentials`, the two hygiene jobs — came back clean everywhere except
this: seven repositories set `SHELLCHECK_OPTS` and five did not.

Nothing fails either way today, because there is no shell script here that trips
an info-level shellcheck note. That is exactly why it would have stayed
different until the day it mattered.

The setting is now written into `CI.md` (sapn95/.github#2) so the next
repository does not have to be reverse engineered from a working one.

## How it was verified

`actionlint` and `yamllint` exit 0 locally.

author: agustinreiden
body:
## El problema

Para `aplicar_orden_ruta` el transportista es parte de la **identidad** de la ruta: la busca por `(transportista_id, fecha, estado, sucursal_id)`. Elegir otro chofer en el selector y volver a armar no movía la ruta — armaba una **segunda** y dejaba la original viva, con sus pedidos en `asignado` y fuera del pool de disponibles. Una ruta armada a nombre equivocado solo se corregía cancelándola y rehaciéndola.

El caso que lo destapó: en Taco Pozo la ruta del día se arma la tarde anterior. Se armó a nombre del transportista que estaba en el picker y media hora después se le habilitó a Juan —preventista que acompaña al camión— la capacidad `transportista` (mig 155). La ruta quedó a nombre de quien no la iba a repartir.

## La solución

**Mig 172** — `cambiar_transportista_recorrido(recorrido_id, transportista_id)` mueve el recorrido y el `transportista_id` de los pedidos de sus paradas en una sola transacción, conservando el orden de entrega, la optimización y las polylines.

Los pedidos se actualizan además del recorrido porque `pedidos.transportista_id` es lo que leen la PWA del chofer, las policies de `pagos` (mig 155) y la rendición: sin eso la ruta cambia de nombre en el listado y el chofer nuevo no la ve.

### Guardas

| Guarda | Por qué |
|---|---|
| `es_encargado_o_admin()` | Mismo gate que `aplicar_orden_ruta` |
| Ruta y destino de la sucursal activa | Aislamiento multi-tenant |
| Destino habilitado como transportista ahí | Rol base o capacidad extra (mig 155); espeja `fetchTransportistas()` del front, server-side |
| Ruta `en_curso` | Una completada ya se rindió: reabrirla no es un cambio de chofer |
| **Cero entregas hechas** | Si el chofer ya entregó y cobró, la plata del día es suya: mover la ruta partiría la rendición entre dos personas |
| Destino sin otra ruta esa fecha | `uq_recorrido_vigente`, chequeado explícito para dar un mensaje útil en vez de un `23505` crudo |

Idempotente: reasignar al mismo chofer devuelve el id sin tocar nada, así un doble click no es un error en pantalla. Las paradas marcadas "no entregado" **no** bloquean: no mueven plata, y el caso real (se rompió el camión a media mañana) es justamente ese.

### UI

El panel sale en el aviso de *"ya hay una ruta armada para X"* de **Armar ruta del día**, que es donde ya se edita la ruta in-place (agregar/quitar paradas). Al confirmar, el modal queda parado sobre la misma ruta bajo su nuevo dueño.

## Verificación

- **8 escenarios contra la base**, simulando sesión autenticada y revertidos al terminar: happy path, no-op idempotente, transportista de otra sucursal, usuario sin la capacidad, ruta de otra sucursal, ruta con 17 entregas hechas, destino con ruta duplicada esa fecha, y preventista sin permisos. Los 8 se comportan como corresponde.
- **4 tests unitarios** del hook: firma de la RPC (`p_recorrido_id` es bigint — mandarlo como string falla en runtime, no en compilación), que el mensaje del `RAISE EXCEPTION` llegue a la UI tal cual, fallback genérico, e invalidación por prefijo de las queries indexadas por transportista.
- Suite completa: **1048 tests en verde**. `tsc --noEmit`, `eslint` y `npm run build` limpios.

## Notas

- La mig 172 **ya está aplicada en producción** (ledger: `20260808122237`). Solo agrega una función: no modifica ni una fila, todo su SQL corre cuando el usuario dispara la acción desde la UI.
- `MANIFEST.md` actualizado (próxima migración: 173).

author: jingi723
body:
## 요약

증분 수집 창(`default_window`)이 **UTC 날짜**로 계산되는데, 그 날짜 문자열은 **KST 달력을 쓰는 벤더 질의에 그대로 실린다** — BigKinds `search_page` 의 `startDate`/`endDate` 가 그 자리다. 정규화는 이미 그 벤더가 KST 벽시계임을 알고 있다(`normalize_news._KST`, "UTC 로 라벨하면 사건 τ가 9시간 밀려…"). 창만 프로세스 시계로 날짜를 뽑고 있었다.

KST=UTC+9 이라 **09:00 KST 이전에 도는 슬롯에서 창이 하루 밀린다.** 지금 안 깨지는 유일한 이유는 모든 스케줄 슬롯이 09:00 KST 이후이기 때문이고, **그 불변식은 어디에도 적혀 있지 않았다.**

⚠️ 잠복만이 아니다 — **공시 09:00 슬롯은 그 경계에 정확히 서 있다.** 08:59:59 에 창을 뽑으면 `[D-2, D-1]` 이 되어 그날 공시를 한 건도 안 가져온다. 안전 마진이 단방향 수 초에서 9시간이 된다.

## 변경 사항

- `window_calendar_tz(step, source)` 신설 — 창을 쓰는 **11개 (스텝, 벤더) 조합마다 달력을 선언**하고 호출부 3곳(`load-disclosure`·`tag-news`·공통 ingest 6스텝)이 그걸로 `datetime.now(tz)` 를 만든다.
- **기본값을 두지 않는다.** 이 레포엔 축이 다른 관례가 둘이다 — **순간은 UTC**(`make_run_id`·`started_date` 파티션·원장 타임스탬프·`_scheduled_time`), **시장 날짜는 KST**(`dart_disclosure` 가 "파이프라인 전체가 KR 시장 기준이라 KST 다"로 명문화, `assemble_events`·`dart_values` 동일). 어느 쪽을 기본으로 삼아도 다음 사람이 반대로 읽고, 조용히 떨어진 창은 **하루가 밀린 채 성공**한다. 미선언은 `SystemExit`.
- **기준은 벤더 국적이 아니라 그 데이터가 어느 시장의 날짜인가다** — `yahoo` 는 미국 서비스지만 `index_map` 이 `^KS11`·`^KQ11` 뿐이라 KST 다. 테스트로 못박았다.
- 분기의 기본 벤더(`args.source or "fmp"`)도 같은 표를 읽게 해 **리터럴 두 벌을 없앴다**(리뷰 지적 — 아래).
- 오타난 `--source` 는 "달력 미선언"이 아니라 **"알 수 없는 --source"** 로 진단한다. 창 계산이 분기보다 앞이라, 안 고치면 같은 오타에 `--from/--to` 유무로 **다른 메시지**가 나오고 시킨 대로 표에 넣어도 아무것도 안 고쳐진다.

## 검증

- 전 스위트 **2308 passed**.
- **변이 12종 전부 red** — 표 4항목 반전 · fail-loud 제거 · 기본 벤더 교체 · KST 오프셋 +9→+8 · 호출부 3곳 각각 UTC 되돌리기 · 분기 리터럴 부활 2종 · 오타 진단 되돌리기.
- **현행 동작 무변경**: 리뷰어가 terraform 에서 실제 슬롯을 뽑아 **9슬롯 × 11조합 × 6날짜경계 = 594 조합**을 변경 전/후로 대조해 **차이 0건**. 네 레인 모두 `flexible_time_window OFF` 라 조기 발화도 없다. 움직이는 건 00:00~08:59 KST 의 KST 벤더뿐 — 의도한 범위와 정확히 일치.
- 창을 쓰는 스텝 집합이 닫혀 있음을 정적 전수 확인(50개 step choices 양방향 차집합 0, 끝은 `AssertionError("unreachable step")`).

## 실측 (라이브 콜)

이 변경의 명제 전체가 **"BigKinds 가 `startDate`/`endDate` 를 KST 달력 날짜로 해석한다"** 하나에 걸려 있어서, 추론으로 두지 않고 벤더를 직접 쳤다.

**① 질의 날짜 == 기사 DATE, 그 달력의 하루 전체**
`startDate=endDate=2026-08-05` → `totalCount=6223`, 반환행의 DATE 필드 distinct = `['2026-08-05']` 하나, 시각 범위 `00:00:20 … 23:59:29`. UTC 기준이었다면 KST 로는 이틀에 걸쳐(09:00 → 익일 08:59) 나왔을 것이다.

**② 그 달력이 KST 임을 지금 시각으로 앵커**
지금 UTC `2026-08-08 12:49:35` / KST `21:49:35` 인 시점에 최신 기사 시각 = `2026-08-08 21:45:43` → **KST 대비 +4분**, UTC 대비 −536분(9시간 미래 기사라 불가능). **KST 벽시계 확정.**

**③ 옛 코드가 실제로 몇 건을 놓치는가 — 08:10 KST 슬롯 기준**

| | |
|---|---|
| 2026-08-08(토) 경제 카테고리 | 770건 |
| 그중 08:10 KST 이전 발행 | **259건** (`00:02:01 … 08:07:51`) |
| 옛 코드의 창(UTC) | `[2026-08-06, 2026-08-07]` — **그날이 없다** |
| 새 코드의 창(KST) | `[2026-08-07, 2026-08-08]` |

옛 코드로 08:10 런을 돌리면 **그날 259건 중 0건**을 가져오고 8시간 전 런이 이미 훑은 창을 다시 긁는다. 토요일(저뉴스일) 수치이고 평일은 하루 6,223건(08-05 수요일 실측)이라 규모가 다르다.

⚠️ 아직 실측 안 한 것: **dev 실런**. 이 PR 은 현행 슬롯(전부 09:00 KST 이후)에서 무변경이라 dev 에서 드러날 차이가 없다 — 실효는 08:10·00:10 슬롯이 생길 때 나온다.

## 리뷰 — ⚠️ Codex 아님

Codex 한도 소진(재개 2026-08-10 15:36)으로 CLI·PR 봇이 둘 다 죽어 있다. 사용자 승인을 받아 **작성 맥락 없는 서브에이전트 1라운드**로 대체했다(직전 사이클과 달리 변경이 1파일 규모라 1각도·1라운드로 줄였다). 결과 **P0/P1 0건 · P2 2건**, 둘 다 수용해 반영.

그 리뷰가 **내 변이 8종이 못 잡은 구멍**을 찾았다: 표가 아니라 **분기 쪽** 기본값만 바꾸면 전 스위트가 초록이었다 — 창은 이 벤더로, 질의는 저 벤더로 나가는, 정확히 이 PR 이 죽이려는 그 버그다. 고침은 테스트 추가가 아니라 **중복 제거**였다.

그리고 내 주석의 **근거가 틀렸다는 것도 잡았다** — "이 레포 기준시는 다 UTC" 라고 적었는데 `dart_disclosure.py:112` 가 정반대를 명문화하고 있었다. 결론(무기본+fail-loud)은 유지하되 근거를 두 축 프레이밍으로 고쳤다.

## 잔여 (비블로킹)

1. **달력의 임자는 사실 벤더 어댑터다.** KST 어댑터 10여 개가 이미 자기 `_KST` 를 들고 있고 `dart_disclosure._window_segments` 는 그걸로 창 끝까지 채운다. `_WINDOW_CALENDAR` 는 그 사실의 재진술이고, 창이 어댑터 생성 **전에** 계산되기 때문에 존재한다. 창 계산을 분기 뒤로 옮기면 표가 통째로 사라진다 — 6분기를 건드리는 일이라 별건이다(`ponytail:` 주석으로 남김).
2. `test_window_does_not_move_for_todays_slot_times` 는 terraform 을 안 읽고 슬롯 시각을 하드코딩한다 — 살아있는 불변식이 아니라 **스냅샷**이다. 이 변경 후엔 09:00 이전 슬롯이 구조적으로 안전해져서 지키는 게 아니라 기록하는 성격이라 그대로 뒀다.
3. canonical 뉴스 파티션은 **달력이 섞여 있다** — normalize 가 BigKinds 는 KST, FMP 는 UTC 로 라벨한다. `tag-news` 는 벤더가 안 갈려 한쪽을 골라야 하고 실제로 도는 KR 레인 기준 KST 가 맞다. 조치 불필요이나 표 주석을 "이 파티션 축은 KST"로 읽으면 안 된다(주석에 명시).
4. `("ingest-raw-inav", None)` 은 그 분기가 창을 쓰지도 않는데(`--from/--to` 를 거부한다) 표에 없으면 CLI 가 죽는다 — 아무도 안 쓰는 값이 load-bearing 이다.

## 후속

이 티켓은 **뉴스 슬롯 재배치(08:10 / 15:30 / 00:10)의 선행**이다. 그 자체는 별건이고, 15:30 유지 여부는 EOD analyze 소유권 결정에 묶여 있다.

body:
## Summary
- migrates `/dashboard` from live Spotify saved-tracks loading to the persisted MuseVault library snapshot in PostgreSQL
- uses full-library SQL aggregates for Liked Songs, unique artists, total duration, and average track length
- fetches only the five newest persisted saved tracks for Recently Saved
- resolves users through the authenticated Spotify account identity and does not expose internal database identifiers
- requires a completed authoritative full-sync baseline and returns safe `sync_required` / `sync_in_progress` states instead of falling back to live Spotify data
- avoids presenting transient partial full-sync state as final dashboard data

## Dashboard data flow
Before:
`session -> Spotify GET /me/tracks -> first 50 tracks -> dashboard`

After:
`session identity/profile -> PostgreSQL persisted snapshot -> SQL aggregates + 5 recent tracks -> safe dashboard view model`

## UI changes
- replaces first-page metrics with full-library metrics: Liked Songs, Artists, Library Duration, Average Track Length
- sidebar now shows persisted track count, persistent snapshot wording, and last-sync information
- statistic badges use persisted/synced wording instead of implying live Spotify requests
- Recently Saved is now sourced from the persisted library
- stale preview copy was updated so analytics cards no longer claim that a full-library sync is still missing
- preview analytics remain clearly unimplemented; no analytics engine was added

## Safety / scope
- dashboard rendering no longer imports or calls the Spotify saved-tracks loader
- no internal HTTP request to a MuseVault Spotify route
- no migration or schema change
- no OAuth/session redesign
- no synchronization algorithm changes
- no new Spotify scopes
- no Rediscover, Wrapped, mood analysis, recommendations, playlists, AI, or background jobs

## Validation
All Milestone 3D validation passed before commit:
- `pnpm format:check`
- `pnpm lint`
- `pnpm typecheck`
- `pnpm test` — 145 tests across 20 files
- `pnpm build`
- `git diff --check`

Focused preview-copy follow-up:
- 1 focused test file, 2 tests passed
- `git diff --check` passed

## Manual verification
- dashboard loaded successfully from the persisted PostgreSQL snapshot
- unsynchronized Spotify changes did not change dashboard values
- after `Sync changes`, persisted counts updated and dashboard reflected them after refresh
- Liked Songs updated from 2,936 to 2,937 after a confirmed incremental sync
- Library Duration updated from 177h 7m to 177h 10m
- Recently Saved showed the newly persisted track first
- no-change incremental sync continued to work
- `/library` and existing sync behavior remained functional

## Known limitation
The dashboard reflects the latest synchronized MuseVault snapshot, not unsynchronized Spotify changes.

author: smaug123
body:
Follows #808 (which merged while this was in flight, so this targets `main` directly rather than stacking).

CoreCLR reads the four `USHORT` version columns of the manifest's single `Assembly` metadata row (`PEAssembly::GetVersion` → `GetAssemblyProps` on `TokenFromRid(1, mdtAssembly)`) and widens each to `INT32`. PawPrint's `DumpedAssembly.Name` is `AssemblyDefinition.GetAssemblyName()` over that same row, and its `Version` is built from those same four columns, so this is an exact implementation like `GetSimpleName` before it — no `docs/divergences.md` entry.

Values outside what a `USHORT` column can hold fail loudly rather than reaching the guest. That includes the `-1` a `System.Version` reports for an absent `Build`/`Revision`: CoreCLR can never produce either here, so seeing one means we read the version from somewhere other than the Assembly row.

## Test-layout change

`TestAssemblyNativeSimpleName.fs` becomes `TestAssemblyNativeQCalls.fs`. `Assembly.GetName()`'s six QCalls all want the same scaffolding — guest preparation, `QCallAssembly` construction, handler invocation — and four more are still to come, so they now share it in one fixture rather than growing six copies. The alternative considered was a separate shared harness module with one fixture per QCall; that keeps the same reuse but adds a module boundary for what is already a single coherent subject.

## Testing

Still no end-to-end guest coverage: the guest now gets past `GetVersion` and stops at `AssemblyNative_GetLocale`, so `sourcesPure/AssemblyGetNameSimpleName.cs` stays parked, with its comment updated to name the new blocker.

The guest fixture is built with `[assembly: AssemblyVersion("4.3.2.1")]` — four distinct non-zero components, unlike Roslyn's `0.0.0.0` default, which every transposition would survive — and the four `out int` slots are separate arrays seeded with a negative sentinel, so "never written" is distinguishable from "wrote 0". Each claim was mutation-tested:

| mutation | caught by |
| --- | --- |
| transpose build and revision | metadata-columns test |
| ignore the `QCallAssembly` argument, always answer corelib's version | per-assembly + metadata-columns tests |
| never write the out params | per-assembly + metadata-columns tests |
| fall back to corelib on an unloaded handle | unloaded-assembly test |

Full suite: 2139 passed, 0 failed. `codex review` returned no findings (run before the rebase; the rebase was clean and the fixture re-run green afterwards).

author: mmedum
body:
Closes #38. **Worth landing before the v1.1.0 tag** — that tag is exactly what
would otherwise publish ungated.

## The gap

`release.yml` triggers on `push: tags: ['v*.*.*']` and has no dependency on the
`ci` workflow — no `workflow_call`, no `needs:`, no required status check.

A tag is just a pointer. Nothing stopped one landing on a commit whose CI never
ran, or ran and failed. Everything below it writes somewhere irreversible: GHCR,
a GitHub release, and PyPI, where an upload can be yanked but never replaced.

This is the same blind spot that let `uv.lock` sit stale with CI red for months
(#35) — applied to the path with the worst blast radius.

## The change

A `verify-ci` job queries the `ci` workflow's conclusion for the exact tagged
SHA and fails loudly if it isn't `success`. `docker-build` — the only job that
had no `needs:` — now depends on it, so the whole chain is gated.

Scoped `contents: read` + `actions: read`, no extra secrets.

## Verified

`actionlint` clean. The query run against real commits:

| Commit | Result |
|---|---|
| current `main` (green ci) | `success` → proceeds |
| a SHA with no ci run | `none` → blocks |

## Note

Chose to gate on the existing `ci` result rather than re-running the jobs inside
`release.yml`. It's cheaper and keeps one definition of "green", but it does
mean the gate trusts the recorded conclusion — if you'd rather it be
un-bypassable, re-running test/audit/container inside the release workflow is
the stronger form.

author: susumutomita
body:
## Summary

npm package [`ever-better`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/ever-better) (作者: isamu / ありもとさん) の導入を検討し、**read-only 診断のみ**を配線した。依存追加は root devDependency 1件 (exact pin `0.4.0`)、呼び出しは `make ever-better-diagnose` の1 target のみ。`GATE_CHECKS` にも `.github/workflows/ci.yml` にも載せていない。

### 何を検査/実行するツールなのか

`ever-better` はリポジトリの品質ツール構成を診断し、ESLint 本体の bulk suppressions (`--suppress-all`) を使った ratchet (= 違反件数の天井を固定し、増えたら CI を落とす) を運用するための CLI。今回配線した `diagnose` subcommand は書き込みを一切せず、次の3つを報告する。

1. 品質ツールの検出結果と不足している層 (formatter / test runner / knip / jscpd / CI の内容)
2. 600行超の file 数とその上位 (= split & DRY の backlog)
3. `eslint --print-config` を引いて **実効設定で off / warn-only になっている high-value rule** — config の source を読むのではなく実際に適用される値を引くので、preset 同士の上書きで黙って off になった rule を検出できる

3 が本命。このレポでは 13 rule が off と報告された (`@typescript-eslint/no-unsafe-assignment` / `no-unsafe-member-access` / `no-unsafe-call` / `no-unsafe-return` / `no-unsafe-argument` ほか)。type-aware の block が `scripts/**` に限定されているため、それ以外の file では unsafe-* 系が実際に無効という指摘で、これは正しい。

### なぜ「診断のみ」で、ratchet 部分を採用しなかったのか

**ratchet 機構は素の ESLint に既にある。** インストール済み ESLint 9.39.5 で確認済み:

```
--suppress-all / --suppress-rule / --suppressions-location
--prune-suppressions / --pass-on-unpruned-suppressions
```

`ever-better` の README 自身が「ratchet の再実装はしていません」と明記しており、追加されるのは gap 診断・config 生成・`QUALITY.md` 描画・state 台帳・Claude Code plugin skill。つまり ratchet を入れたいだけなら**新規依存はゼロで足りる**。

加えて、このレポで ratchet が意味を持つのは ESLint の実行範囲を広げた時だけ。現ゲート `make lint-ts` (= `eslint scripts`) は exit 0 = 緑なので、`freeze` を今の範囲に当てても**空の suppressions file ができるだけ**で無意味。範囲を広げる判断は別作業なので、このPRでは触れていない (実測値は下の Validation に記載)。

### なぜ gate と CI に載せていないのか

`ever-better` は 2026-08-08 00:05Z 公開の新規 package で、3時間半のうちに 0.1.0 → 0.4.0 の4版。npm downloads API は `package not found` (= download 実績ゼロ)、GitHub star 0 / open issue 2件。公開後72時間は無条件に unpublish 可能で、その窓を抜けた後も「public な dependent が無く download が少なく単独 owner」の条件を満たす限り unpublish 対象のまま (このレポは private なので dependent には数えられない)。**消え得る package を `bun install` の必須解決対象かつ gate の依存にはしない**。

supply-chain 面の素性そのものは良い (下記 Validation で実測)。gate に載せない理由は malice ではなく churn と存続性であり、そこは混同しないこと。

### `bootstrap` は実行していない

`ever-better bootstrap` はこのレポと正面衝突するため使わない。Makefile のコメントにも残した。

| bootstrap の挙動 | 衝突 |
| --- | --- |
| Prettier を devDependency に入れる | このレポの formatter は Biome |
| ESLint 10 を要求 | このレポは `eslint ^9` + `typescript-eslint ^8` |
| 生成 workflow が `npx --yes` を使う | このレポの npx / bunx 禁止に反する |
| `dependabot.yml` / `.gitattributes` / 3プラットフォーム workflow を書く | 不要 |

`npx` は生成される workflow file の中だけで、**CLI 自身は runtime で npx を呼ばない** (`dist/util/exec.js` は `spawn` を `shell: false` で使用、ESLint は `node_modules/eslint/bin/eslint.js` を直接起動)。生成 workflow を使わない限り npx 禁止には触れない。

## Validation

すべて実行済み。

| 検証 | 結果 |
| --- | --- |
| `make before-commit` | **赤。ただし原因は既存 flake で、この diff とは無関係 (下記に実測)** |
| `make harness` / `lint-md` / `lint-text` / `lint-format` / `lint-ts` / `dead-code` | 全て緑 |
| test (infrastructure / packages / 他 SPA) | 505 + 30 + 11 + 19 file 全緑、8,000+ test passed |
| `make audit-deps` (追加後) | `OK 92 package(s) ... No new packages or hooks vs baseline` — **baseline 無変更** |
| `ever-better` の transitive dep | **0件** — lockfile entry に `dependencies` object が無い / `node_modules/ever-better/node_modules` 不在 |
| install 時 lifecycle script | **なし** — published manifest は `prepack` のみ (= publish 時。auditor の `LIFECYCLE_SCRIPT_KEYS` 対象外) |
| license | MIT |
| npm 署名 | あり (`keyid SHA256:DhQ8wR5APBvFHLF/+Tc+AYvPOdTpcIDqOhxsBHRwC7U`) |
| `make ever-better-diagnose` | exit 0、レポートを出力 |
| `diagnose` が read-only か | **確認済み** — 実行後の `git status` は自分の dep 追加2 file のみ。`.ever-better/` も `QUALITY.md` も生成されない |
| `make help` / `make help-ja` | 新 target が英日どちらにも表示される |

### `make before-commit` が緑にならない件 (既存 flake、この diff とは無関係)

`apps/participant-portal` の `src/components/MultiFlagSubmissionPanel.test.tsx` が負荷下で `Test timed out in 5000ms` を出す。**`origin/main` を素で checkout した別 worktree で再現させた**ので、この PR の変更とは無関係。

| 実行 (同一コマンド `vitest run` を `apps/participant-portal` で) | 結果 |
| --- | --- |
| origin/main (変更なし) run 1 | 91/91 passed ← 外れ値 |
| origin/main (変更なし) run 2 | **3 failed** |
| origin/main (変更なし) run 3 | **3 failed** (run 2 と同一テスト) |
| このブランチ run 1〜3 | 2〜4 failed、上記3件を必ず含む |

毎回落ちる中核の3件:

- `MultiFlagSubmissionPanel > should score all six rows through the real multi-flag path and show the handoff`
- `MultiFlagSubmissionPanel > should restore all mock-solved rows after reopening the problem`
- `multi-verify extensions (issue #2252) > should complete wp-exposed-backup and retain all four checkpoint hint histories`

無関係と言える根拠:

1. **同じ失敗が変更なしの origin/main で再現する** (3回中2回)。
2. このブランチの base (3680d047) と比較対象 (5b0f8e0a) の間の2コミット (#2941 / #2937) は `apps/participant-portal` を1行も触っていない = テスト対象コードは同一。
3. この diff は devDependency 1行・lockfile 1 entry・Makefile の target とコメントのみで、SPA の component test に到達する経路がない。
4. 失敗ファイルが実行ごとに変わる (participant-portal / admin-console の `EventCreate.flow` / `EventDetail.force-archive` / `App.test.tsx`) = timing 依存。
5. 該当2ファイルだけを実行すると **52/52 passed**。並列度を上げた時だけ落ちる。

このファイルは 36 test で 41〜49秒かかる重量級で、直近も #2914 / #2881 / #2874 と修正が続いている。**flake 自体の是正はこの PR の範囲外**として別途起票する (テスト側の `testTimeout` かポーリング待ちの見直しが必要で、devtool 追加と混ぜるべきではない)。

参考として測定した (このPRでは変更しない) 数値:

| 計測 | 結果 |
| --- | --- |
| `make lint-ts` (現ゲート範囲 `eslint scripts`) | exit 0 = 緑 |
| `eslint .` (同じ config、リポジトリ全体) | **1,612 errors / 551 files** (1,993 file 中) |

内訳上位: `consistent-type-assertions` 336 / `sonarjs/assertions-in-tests` 224 / `no-empty-function` 214 / `array-type` 178 / `no-explicit-any` 109。

この 336 は [`eslint.config.js`](eslint.config.js) に残る #2861 / #2862 の経緯 (「`assertionStyle: "never"` は105件出てゲートが永久に緑にならないので `as` に戻した」) と同じ rule で、ratchet がまさに解く問題ではある。ただしこのレポの確立パターンは「清算してから配線」(knip #2866、ESLint #2862 の2回) であり、1,612件の grandfathering は方針転換になる。**その判断はこのPRの範囲外**として据え置いた。

### 診断結果の false positive (追いかけないための記録)

9 gap のうち4件はこのレポの構成による誤検出。Makefile のコメントにも同じ内容を残した。

| 報告 | 実態 |
| --- | --- |
| "No TypeScript" | 同じ出力内で `99% TypeScript` と報告しており自己矛盾。root に `tsconfig.json` が無く `tsconfig.scripts.json` / 各 workspace 側にあるため |
| "No formatter" | Prettier の有無だけを見ており Biome を知らない |
| "No test runner" | vitest が root devDependency でなく workspace 側にある |
| "CI does not run lint" | CI の step が全て `run: make <target>` なので直接の tool 呼び出しを見つけられず `[no known steps]` になる。実際は `make lint-text` / `lint-format` / `lint-ts` を実行している (ci.yml:104 / 108 / 116) |

残る5件 (600行超47 file、13 rule が off、CI が macos/windows で走らない、`format` npm script 不在、`ever-better check` 未配線) は事実。うち「13 rule が off」が実際に価値のある指摘。

## Regression analysis

- **既存 gate への影響なし**: 追加したのは独立した `ever-better-diagnose` target 1つで、`GATE_CHECKS` (`harness lint dead-code test`)、`ci-local`、`.github/workflows/ci.yml` のいずれにも参加させていない。既存 target の recipe は無変更。
- **`audit-deps` baseline**: 無変更を実測で確認 (92件のまま)。ever-better は install hook をゼロ追加なので `scripts/audit-baseline.json` の更新は不要。
- **`knip` (`make dead-code`)**: `knip.json` は `devDependencies: "off"` / `binaries: "off"` なので、Makefile からのみ呼ばれる devDependency を未使用として検出しない。
- **lockfile**: `bun.lock` の差分は ever-better の1 entry と root devDependencies への1行のみ。他 package の解決は動いていない。
- **`.PHONY`**: 新 target を登録済み (同名 file が生まれても壊れない)。
- **ロールバック**: `package.json` / `bun.lock` / `Makefile` の3 file を戻すだけ。生成物・設定 file・CI 変更が無いので副作用は残らない。

## Physical impact

**NO-OP** — AWS リソースの変更なし。infrastructure/ に変更がなく、CDK template にも影響しない (CREATE / UPDATE / REPLACE / DELETE いずれも該当なし)。開発者ツールのみの変更。

## 残る risk と未検証事項

- **package の存続性 (最大の risk)**: 公開当日・download 実績ゼロ・単独 maintainer。unpublish されると `bun install --frozen-lockfile` が失敗し得る。gate/CI に載せていないので**ゲートのロジックは落ちない**が、install する全 workflow が影響を受ける点は残る (この risk を消すには依存を持たない選択肢しかない)。数週間後も放置されているなら、この target と依存は削除して構わない (ロールバックは3 file)。
- **version churn**: 3時間半で4版。exact pin なので勝手には動かないが、bump 追従の価値があるかは実績を見て判断。
- **未検証の subcommand**: `bootstrap` / `freeze` / `check` / `prune` / `migrate` / `catalog` / `emit-diff` は**一切実行していない**。`bootstrap` は上記の衝突があるため意図的に未実行。`catalog` (`docs/shared-h

author: hyzxn
body:
Supersedes #35.

Fixes URL encoding, payload cleanup, and worker exit handling on the Rust side; improves stereo panning balance and fixes a couple of UI bugs.

## Changes

**`src-tauri/src/commands/app_cmd.rs`**
- Add `percent_encode_query()`: URL-encodes `workflowId` query parameters
- `open_workflow_node_editor_window()`: apply `percent_encode_query()` to `workflow_id`
- `close_current_window()`: remove duplicate emit of `pymss://workflow-node-editor-closed` — the `Destroyed` window event handler already sends this event, so the command-side emit was redundant

**`src-tauri/src/python/worker.rs`**
- `run_worker_with_payload()`: clean up the payload file if `spawn()` or `wait()` fails
- `spawn_worker_background()`: same cleanup on spawn failure
- Stderr handling: scope to a single `task_id` instead of looping over all registered tasks
- Worker exit without a terminal event: previously silent, which could leave a task stuck as "running" in the UI indefinitely; now emits a typed error ("worker exited without reporting results") so the failure surfaces to the user

**`src/composables/useEditorPlayback.ts`**
- `stereoGainForPan()`: replace linear panning with equal-power panning (`Math.cos`/`Math.sin` gain curves) for a more natural playback preview balance; add an `abs(normalized) <= 1e-6` guard returning `{ left: 1, right: 1 }` so center panning keeps full level — mirrors the worker-side guard in `_apply_stereo_pan()`

**`src/utils/workflowDefinition.ts`**
- `safeWorkflowStemDir()`: replace `|| stem` with `|| 'stem'` — when the sanitized result is empty (e.g., empty or whitespace-only stem), `|| stem` falls back to the raw input, which can still be empty/whitespace; the literal `'stem'` guarantees a stable, usable directory name

**`src/views/SeparateView.vue`**
- Add a `durationTick` ref + `setInterval(1000)` for real-time task duration display
- `taskDuration()`: switch from `updatedAt`-based to `Date.now()`-based elapsed time — previously the displayed duration only updated when the task object itself was updated
- `onMounted` / `onBeforeUnmount`: start/clean up the interval

## Notes

- For single-task payloads this is behavior-preserving; for multi-task batch payloads it changes attribution — stderr goes only to the payload's primary `task_id`. Batch separation (`startSeparation`/`startWorkflowInference` in batch mode) sends multiple tasks per payload via `tasks[]`, so batch runs are affected. The backend API itself doesn't preclude multi-task payloads.
- The `Destroyed` window handler is confirmed to emit the same event; the old command-side emit is removed, so the event is now emitted from a single place (exact ordering vs. the previous emit is runtime-dependent).
- `percent_encode_query()` is currently applied only to `open_workflow_node_editor_window()`'s `workflowId`; no other query params are affected.
- `stdout.take()` failure (unexpected in practice — the pipe is always configured) isn't followed by payload file cleanup — same as the original code; besides the new `spawn()`/`wait()` failure cleanups, the pre-existing end-of-function cleanup still removes the file on the success/worker-error paths.
- `taskDuration()` uses `Date.now()` for every non-terminal state (`queued`, `preparing`, `validating_input`, `downloading_model`, `ensuring_model`, `loading_model`, `separating`, `writing_output`) — live count-up via the 1-second `durationTick` interval — and falls back to `updatedAt` for terminal states (`done`/`failed`/`cancelled`) so the elapsed time freezes at completion. This means a `queued` task's duration counts up from creation while it waits, not only once it starts running. For `failed` tasks specifically, `updatedAt` reflects the last progress update rather than the exact failure time, so the displayed duration can be marginally shorter than the actual run time.

author: vibecoderst
body:
# PR Summary — Scope the JUnit merge step's write grant (Issue #3681) ## Summary The `merge` job of `.github/workflows/coverage.yaml` ran the in-repo script `scripts/merge_junit.ts` with an unrestricted `--allow-write`, ahead of two steps in the same job that hold `secrets.CODECOV_TOKEN`. A same-repo pull request controls what executes at that step, and an unrestricted write grant reaches `$GITHUB_ENV` and `$GITHUB_PATH` — both honoured by later steps in the same job — which is enough to shim a binary onto `PATH` or set an environment variable the Codecov action reads, and thereby observe or redirect the token. The grant is now scoped to exactly the file the script writes (`--allow-write=junit.xml`), matching the already-narrow `--allow-read` treatment of `coverage_merge_gate.ts` and the SBOM step's `--allow-write=sbom.cdx.json` (Issue #3668). Fork PRs never receive the secret, so the exposure was limited to branch PRs, but the ordering still put PR-authored code with unrestricted write ahead of the token. `Closes #3681`. ## Evidence Backend/CI-only change — there is no web interface to screenshot. Verification is the new test file, run below. ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph merge["merge job (holds CODECOV_TOKEN)"] A["Merge JUnit reports
deno run scripts/merge_junit.ts"] B["Upload test results to Codecov
token: ***REDACTED*** C["Upload coverage to Codecov
token: ***REDACTED*** A --> B --> C end A -. "before: --allow-write
can write \$GITHUB_ENV / \$GITHUB_PATH" .-> X["Token observable
or redirectable"] A == "after: --allow-write=junit.xml
write denied outside the report" ==> Y["Token out of reach"] ``` Test run (`deno test test/ci/CoverageMergeStepLeastPrivilege.ts`): ```text the JUnit merge step scopes --allow-write to its output (Issue #3681) ... ok no secret-bearing job grants unrestricted write to repo-authored code (Issue #3681) ... ok the committed permission set still merges the shard reports (Issue #3681) ... ok the committed permission set blocks writes outside the report (Issue #3681) ... ok ok | 4 passed | 0 failed ``` All four fail (bar the first behavioural one) against the unfixed workflow — they were written first and confirmed red before the workflow was changed. ## Test Plan New file `test/ci/CoverageMergeStepLeastPrivilege.ts`: - **`the JUnit merge step scopes --allow-write to its output`** — parses the committed workflow and asserts the merge step grants exactly one `--allow-write`, qualified with a path equal to the step's `--output` value. - **`no secret-bearing job grants unrestricted write to repo-authored code`** — the regression guard the issue asks for: any job in `coverage.yaml` that references a secret must not run `deno run/test/bench/eval` with a bare `--allow-write`, `-A`, or `--allow-all`. This catches permission drift back to unrestricted, which never fails at runtime. - **`the committed permission set still merges the shard reports`** — executes `scripts/merge_junit.ts` in a throwaway directory under the *exact* flags parsed out of the committed workflow, over two fixture shard reports, and asserts the merged `junit.xml` aggregates both (`tests="5" failures="1"`). Narrowing the grant too far turns this red instead of failing CI later. - **`the committed permission set blocks writes outside the report`** — same flags, but asks the script to write a different path; asserts a non-zero exit with a Deno permission error and that no file was created. This proves the narrowing is actually binding, not cosmetic. Existing `test/scripts/MergeJunit.ts` (the script's own unit tests) is unchanged and still passes; the script's behaviour is untouched. ## Files changed - `.github/workflows/coverage.yaml` — `--allow-write` → `--allow-write=junit.xml` on the merge step, with a comment recording why. - `scripts/merge_junit.ts` — CLI usage comment updated to the scoped invocation. - `test/ci/CoverageMergeStepLeastPrivilege.ts` — new tests (above). ## Milestone This PR is part of the **Scan 20260807** milestone and targets the `milestone/scan-20260807` feature branch. --- 🤖 Processed by: VibeCoderST 🏷️ Run id: `vibe-mskaumhd-9622f2`

## What this changes

One line: `SHELLCHECK_OPTS: --severity=warning` on the actionlint step, matching
the other repositories.

## Why

A mechanical audit of every `ci.yml` on `main` against
[CI.md](https://github.com/sapn95/.github/blob/main/CI.md) — name casing,
triggers, top-level permissions, concurrency, per-job timeouts, action versions,
`persist-credentials`, the two hygiene jobs — came back clean everywhere except
this: seven repositories set `SHELLCHECK_OPTS` and five did not.

Nothing fails either way today, because there is no shell script here that trips
an info-level shellcheck note. That is exactly why it would have stayed
different until the day it mattered.

The setting is now written into `CI.md` (sapn95/.github#2) so the next
repository does not have to be reverse engineered from a working one.

`actionlint` and `yamllint` exit 0 locally.

author: quintonhogshead
body:
## What

The term-consistency scan (`find_inconsistencies`) tokenized with an ASCII-only `_WORD`, so any accented word split mid-token — `Rían` → `R` + `an`, `fiancée` → `fianc` + `e`. Every accented term was invisible to the compound scan, and the stray fragments paired with their neighbours into phantom open compounds. This migrates the term scan to the Unicode-aware pattern the name scan already used, and folds the two into one shared `_WORD`.

## Details

- **One shared tokenizer.** `_NAME_WORD` is deleted; both scans now use `_WORD = re.compile(r"[^\W\d_](?:[^\W\d_]|[̀-ͯ'’-])*")`.
- **Decomposed accents are read whole.** Python's `re` does not treat combining marks as word characters, so NFD-normalized text (anything pasted through a tool that decomposes accents) still split under a plain `\w` class. The pattern allows the combining-diacritics block (U+0300–U+036F) after a letter, and `_key`/`_structure` NFC-normalize first, so a composed and a decomposed `café` share one key, one structure, and one `min_length` count. This also fixed latent NFD blindness in the name scan.
- **No accent-folding.** `café` against `cafe` may be a loanword against its anglicization — two deliberate choices — so the term scan leaves accents standing. Whether an accent difference is drift stays `find_name_drift`'s question, asked only of proper names. `_key`/`_structure` do NFC canonical folding only, never accent-stripping.
- **`min_length` unchanged.** Keys count NFC-composed characters, so `fiancée` is 7 — accented words face the same bar as ASCII ones.
- **ASCII behavior is bit-for-bit identical** to the old pattern on pure-ASCII input, so no existing manuscript behavior shifts.

## Tests

Five added in `tests/test_consistency.py`: an accented hyphen-that-comes-and-goes, an accented open-vs-closed compound, accent-only difference is *not* flagged, NFC/NFD group as one term, and an all-NFD manuscript still gets its name drift corrected. Consistency suite: 41 passed; full suite: 998 passed.

## Note

Based on `feat/name-diacritic-consistency` (the name-drift scan), not `main` — this builds directly on that work. A follow-up is still open for `docproof/spellscan.py`, which has its own ASCII tokenizer with the same disease.

author: marccampbell
body:
## Summary

`elasticclaw hub upgrade` printed:

```text
Remote: unknown  →  Target: 2026.8.8-beta.2
```

even when the remote hub was running a real build.

**Cause:** `parseVersionFromOutput` required a leading `v` (`elasticclaw v…`), but `elasticclaw version` prints CalVer without it:

```text
elasticclaw 2026.8.8-beta.2 (commit: …, built: …)
```

**Fix:** Parse CalVer and legacy `v`-prefixed lines (and JSON). Also probe `/usr/local/bin/elasticclaw` and `sudo` when checking the remote version.

## Test plan

- [x] `go test ./cmd/ -run TestParseVersionFromOutput`
- [ ] `elasticclaw-beta hub upgrade --profile …` shows the real remote version before upgrade

author: umairnadeem
body:
## What changed

`Template.systemPrompt` and `Template.exampleText` are read in exactly one place — `createTemplateModePlugin` — and are never rendered by any UI. They were 160KB of the 174KB in `lib/templates/templates.ts`, which `TemplateGallery`, `ComposerCopilot` and `ConfigProvider` all import eagerly, so every editor page load downloaded and parsed them.

They now live in `lib/templates/prompts.ts` behind `getTemplatePrompt(id)`, which the plugin reaches through `import()` on the first template-mode generation. `templates.ts` keeps the gallery metadata it always owned.

## Why it matters

Measured across two `npm run build` runs, the shared client chunk carrying the templates:

| | raw | gzipped |
| --- | --- | --- |
| before | 971,072 | 277,167 |
| after | 804,447 | 224,991 |
| delta | **-166,625 (-17%)** | **-52,176 (-19%)** |

The prose now sits in its own async chunk that appears in neither `build-manifest.json` nor `app-build-manifest.json`, so it is never part of the initial load. It is fetched when a template generation starts — next to an LLM call that already takes seconds — so interactivity is unaffected.

No behavior change: same prompts, same plugin contract (`beforeGenerate` already accepted a `Promise`), and `getTemplatePrompt` throws on an unknown id exactly like `getTemplate` does.

## Open PR overlap check

One open PR at the time of this run: **#531** (`refactor: nightly maintainability 2026-08-08`), which touches `ARCHITECTURE.md` only. This PR touches `lib/templates/*` and `lib/connectors/llm/plugins/template-mode.ts` — no overlap in files or theme.

## Considered and skipped

Profiled the runtime hot paths first, per the runbook order, and found nothing worth shipping:

- **Slate**: every consumer already uses `useSlateStatic` (never `useSlate`), `renderElement` is a stable `useCallback`, and there is no custom `decorate` or `normalizeNode` overreach. Chunking targets 1000+ node documents; scripts here are tens of nodes.
- **Remotion**: `VideoComposition` memoizes its sequence nodes, transition timing and presentation; `Captions` binary-searches word timestamps via `sortedLastIndex` over memoized data; `motionTransform` is pure per-frame arithmetic.
- **Player/timeline**: frame subscriptions go through `useSyncExternalStore` with derived snapshots, and `ScrubBar` moves the playhead through CSS variables instead of React renders.
- **Queue**: `SnapshotStore` hands out stable snapshot references, so `useQueueSelector` consumers re-render only on real changes.

`PlayerPositionContext` builds an unmemoized context value, and `MotionLayer` subscribes to `useCurrentFrame()` even when its effect is `"none"`. Both are single-component re-renders with no measurable cost — left alone rather than shipped as micro-churn.

## Validation

`npm run lint`, `format:check`, `typecheck`, `knip`, `npm run build`, and `npm test` (1111 tests, 128 files) all pass.

author: heshipstech
body:
Owner feedback within minutes of running the first real clip through stepping: **a progress line that never changes is indistinguishable from a hang.**

Stepping a 3 minute 20 second recording takes ten minutes or more, and the status said only `Measuring every frame...` for the whole time. A long wait is acceptable. A silent one is not.

## What changed

The line now reads like `Measuring every frame: 1200 done, 20% of the clip, about 4 min left.`

The estimate is deliberately withheld until a twentieth of the clip is measured. The model's first inference is far slower than the rest, so an estimate from the first few frames would be wildly high and then visibly shrink, which reads as a broken estimate rather than an improving one.

It is written every fifteenth frame, roughly twice a second of wall time. Writing it on every frame costs a layout for a number nobody can read that fast.

## Also a stop button

Without one, the only escape from a long run started by accident was reloading the page, which throws away everything measured so far. Stopping keeps the records, and the export already states the measurement mode and the frames measured, so a partial run cannot be mistaken for a complete one.

424 unit tests, 5 end to end tests.

author: mw-aqa
body:
Closes #61. Enforcement follows in **#62**, filed rather than folded in — see below.

`Scan` returns every item and `Selection` narrows the **payload**, never the reach, so a caller wanting *"the items whose Status is Shipped"* had no way to say so: it read the whole board and discarded most of it. On `arqtiqa`'s board 1 that is twelve round trips to answer a question about six.

This is the gap that made `arqtiqa/arqtos-connectors#189` unbuildable.

## The shape — a real fork, with two in-house precedents pointing opposite ways

Operator ruling 2026-08-08, after measuring both:

| | outcome |
|---|---|
| a fourth parameter on `Scan` | **compile error** for every implementer — louder than the silent break `arqtiqa/arqtos-cli#1169` paid for today. But **77 files** across three repos, sequenced through the release diamond, for a feature most callers never use |
| an optional tier behind a capability | `Scan` untouched; the shape `TrainAdmin` and `SchemaAdmin` already establish |

⚠️ **It does not breach `#49`'s five-operations rule**, and the source says why, because the precedents look contradictory. `#49` refused a sixth operation *named after a vendor mutation* — `addProjectV2ItemById` becoming `PlaceItem` — because that is how `internal/tracker` grew one method per vendor API to fifteen. A filtered read is a general capability of a tracker, like administering its delivery buckets.

## The predicate is in the contract's terms

`query:` is GitHub's UI grammar. A contract carrying its text would make every other tracker translate **from GitHub** — the defect `OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN` is named for in another seam. So a `Predicate` names a field by the name `Catalogue` publishes and a value from the vocabulary that field published, and each connector renders it in its own grammar.

**No OR and no nesting**, as a decision rather than an omission. A conjunction is expressible by every backend worth supporting — and by a client-side loop where the backend offers none — whereas disjunction and grouping are where grammars diverge and a connector starts approximating. A contract a connector can only approximate is one whose answers a caller cannot trust. A caller needing OR issues two reads, which is honest about costing two.

## `Filter.CheckAgainst` — for a measured hazard

`arqtiqa/arqtos-connectors#168` found GitHub answers `nosuchfield:x` with `totalCount=0` and **no errors**. A mistyped predicate is indistinguishable from *"no items match"* — a wrong answer wearing a correct one's clothes. It refuses an unresolvable field, a comparison nobody chose, values that would be silently ignored or are missing, and a value outside a published vocabulary — the last **only** where the field published one, or text fields would be unfilterable.

**Honour it or refuse it, never widen it**: a connector ignoring the filter answers with a **superset**, which a caller can detect no more easily than a subset. The refusal is legitimate, and is what lets a host fall back to `Scan` plus a client-side filter.

## Falsifiers, each RED on its own row

| mutation | goes red |
|---|---|
| drop the unknown-field branch | the unresolvable-field row, and the empty-catalogue row |
| drop the empty-`Options` guard | *"any value on a field that published NO vocabulary"* |
| `quotedOrNone` renders empty as `""` | `ARefusalNamesTheVocabularyEvenWhenItIsEMPTY` |
| delete a `matchNames` row | `EveryValueRendersAndTheZeroIsNamed` |

That third row is `arqtiqa/arqtos-connectors#230`'s shape caught one repo earlier: a refusal listing the available set and rendering nothing when it is empty reads as truncated, and blames the value when the cause is a board that published none.

`KnownCapabilities` gained `server_filter`, and `TestKnownCapabilities_IsTheClosedSet` was updated **deliberately** — that test exists so a capability cannot be added quietly.

## ⚠️ Enforcement is #62, and this ships obligations nothing else holds yet

`#62` carries the `trackerconform` check and the reconciliation of `scan/paged-to-exhaustion`. The second changes what an **existing load-bearing check means**, and the failure mode to design against is a reconciliation that admits the filter by *weakening* the comparison — removing the truncation guard rather than scoping it. That deserves its own review rather than trailing edits at the end of this diff, which is the reasoning that split `arqtiqa/arqtos-connectors#244` out and found the same thing.

A connector implementing `ScanWhere` before `#62` lands is one whose filter nothing holds to the contract, and `#62` says so where its consumers can read it.

## Verification

- Whole suite green `-count=1` — **23 packages, 0 FAIL**
- `gofmt`, `go vet`, `staticcheck` clean, exit captured directly rather than after a pipe

author: michaelbyrne
body:
A `title` attribute is slow to appear, cannot be styled, and on a touch screen
there is no hover at all — so on a phone the names could not be reached. The markup
was right and the mechanism was not.

## Why the browser's own popover

This list sits inside an `overflow-y-auto` box, so anything absolutely positioned
in it is clipped by the scroll container. A popover renders in the top layer and is
not. Light dismiss and escape-to-close come with it rather than being written here.

The panel names the fund and the amount too, because a panel opened from a list of
batches should say which batch it belongs to.

Every name is listed and the panel scrolls. Capping at fifteen was the answer when
there was nowhere to put the rest; in a panel there is somewhere.

## Two stylesheet rules, both needed

```css
[popover] { display: none; }
[popover]:popover-open { display: block; }
```

A supporting browser hides a closed popover from its own stylesheet, but an author
rule beats a UA rule — so `display: none` alone would keep it shut for ever, and
`:popover-open` is what opens it again. A browser without the API drops that second
rule as invalid and keeps the first, so the panel stays hidden rather than every
payee list on the page rendering inline under the batches.

None of that is visible from a template test, so there is one that reads the built
stylesheet.

## Verification

Mutation-tested: going back to a title, giving every panel the same id, dropping the
scroll so a long list is cut off, and removing the rule that hides the panel where
the API is missing each fail a test.

## Support

The Popover API is Chrome 114+, Safari 17+, Firefox 125+ — 2023 onwards. Older
browsers get a button that does nothing rather than a broken page.

body:
Closing the Mac window left the app running with no window (the macOS default).
For a single-window game that's almost always wrong — you expect it to quit.

Adds an `NSApplicationDelegate` via `@NSApplicationDelegateAdaptor` returning
`applicationShouldTerminateAfterLastWindowClosed = true`. Kept as a
`WindowGroup` (not a single `Window`) so a challenge deep link can still open
its own window; the app only terminates when the **last** window closes.

macOS-only change; iOS unaffected. Both platforms build, lint clean.
