## Description

Fixes #1033.

Email addresses beginning with digits were incorrectly interpreted
as numeric user IDs because `parseInt()` only parses the numeric prefix
of a string.

For example:

`12345@example.com` → `12345`

This caused the original email value to be used against the integer
`links.user_id` column.

## Changes

- Replace `parseInt()` based user ID detection with strict numeric validation.
- Treat values such as `12345@example.com` as email addresses.
- Apply the fix to both `getAdmin()` and `totalAdmin()`.

## Testing

Tested locally through the admin links page:

- `12345@example.com` → no database error, treated as email search.
- `12345` → no database error, treated as numeric user ID.

author: grimblaz
body:
Closes #1017.

Chunk 1 of 3 for designed parent #1015, executed from the `plan-variant: brief` in [comment 5226737652](https://github.com/Grimblaz/agent-orchestra/issues/1017#issuecomment-5226737652) via the bare `/goal` lane.

## The defect

The shipped `agent-memory-compaction` policy made its own budget arithmetically unreachable — standing entries never retired, so the protected floor grew monotonically past the size the index can actually load — and the checker was blind to exactly that: `RESULT: clean` on a store whose tail the harness was silently truncating.

## What ships

**The supersession is stated where the ratchet's reader reads.** The canonical policy text now names the never-retire ratchet as superseded and states the three rules replacing it: no silent exits; an exit is lawful only when its destination verifiably carries the lesson at landing; destructive acts execute only behind an owner-present slate.

**A store may split.** A compact stanza in the index carries the three write rules in operative form plus a pointer; the full policy text and that store's own values live in a policy file beside it. The policy file's path rides the stanza's opening marker — an instance value, deliberately outside every compared region, so naming a different file is never a divergence.

**The checker reports four axes.** The new size axis measures the index in characters against `fraction × the freshest recorded limit observation` (0.80 of a 24,978-character observation dated 2026-08-06). The budget never renders as a bare number — the formula and the dated observation travel with it on the same line, so it cannot be copied back into an absolute. The axis is data-driven: `not evaluated` without recorded inputs, `could not verify` on inputs it cannot use, and per-axis so the other three still count.

**No store is obliged to migrate, and it is demonstrated rather than asserted.** A legacy full-header store reports present-but-diverged — never absent, never a refusal — with an explanation naming the onward paths and obliging none. The pre-supersession text ships at `skills/agent-memory-compaction/templates/policy-pre-supersession.md`; passing it with `-PolicyReferencePath` returns the same `RESULT: clean` such a store got before.

Verified on the real artifact, not a fixture — the live store this was measured against:

```text
default reference          -> exit 1, "in-index header - present, INCOMPLETE"
pre-supersession reference -> exit 0, "in-index header - present, complete"
```

## Review

Standard pipeline: 5-pass prosecution panel (2 generalist + 3 specialist, none degraded) → defense → judge. **27 findings merged, 23 sustained, 4 defense-sustained** (Prosecution 91, Defense 12). Then two further adversarial passes over the fixes themselves, because the first fix cycle did not hold.

Every sustained finding traces to an outcome. Highlights of what the review caught that the run had shipped:

- A **whole-index stanza scan**: an index that merely *quoted* the shipped adoption snippet was read as a split store, and the preserved-text route then refused, blaming the shipped template for the index's own content. This took **three rounds** to close — header-region scoping, then column-0, then fence tracking each left a way for quoted text to answer the shape question, and the fence tracker broke it in the other direction too (an unclosed fence hid a *real* stanza and silently switched the size axis off). The rule is now positional: **the opening marker must be the index's first non-blank line.** An index cannot quote something at its own first line without that line being its first line.
- A **future-dated observation** governed the budget permanently — the freshest date wins and the format is append-only, so a mistyped year outranked every honest re-observation while the store read clean. That is the exact vacuity the axis exists to prevent.
- `budget_fraction: NaN` survived `TryParse`, passed a range guard (every comparison against NaN is false), reached an `[int]` cast and **threw** — exiting 1, the "defects found" code, with no report and an empty `-Json` payload.
- An **adapted store mid-migration was refused** with the one message the brief's AC2 verbatim forbids — and that is the state chunk 3 puts every store through.
- A **one-line residue threshold failed four lawful stores**, including one carrying the shipped check command, which the live index carries today.

Two guards that could not fail were found and repaired (one fixture short-circuited before the code path it named; one threshold was self-defeating). Each fix round's guards are verified red against the tree that preceded them.

## Suite state

Differential against baseline `7b204e6`, which predates this change:

- `memory-index-policy.Tests.ps1`: **32 → 106** tests
- Full CI selection — 59 suites, glob minus `ci-quarantine.json`, driven through the workflow's own selection code:
  - baseline `7b204e6`: **1630 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped**
  - head `5355bd6`: **1704 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped**
- **No pre-existing failures at baseline, and none introduced.** The baseline was run in a real `git worktree`: an earlier attempt using `git archive` reported one failure, which turned out to be that suite's own non-vacuity guard firing because an archived tree has no `.git` for its `git ls-files` to read. The artifact was in the measurement, not the tree.

One pre-existing defect was repaired while the file was open and is named as pre-existing rather than claimed as this change's: a markdown link nested inside another link's text computed a negative substring length and threw. It is byte-identical at `origin/main`; links now return in starting order and an overlapping pair routes to the exit-2 refusal the shipped description already claimed.

## Two owner rulings, recorded on the parent

Both questions the review surfaced were escalated rather than decided in the chunk, and both are now ruled ([#1015 comment](https://github.com/Grimblaz/agent-orchestra/issues/1015#issuecomment-5227809317)).

**A split store may record no budget inputs and stay clean — the opt-out is intended.** The budget is a fraction of an *observed* limit, and that observation belongs to the installation. A downstream store with no size problem has no reason to run a truncation-boundary test, so a mandatory values block would push it toward copying this skill's example `24978` — one installation's measurement wearing another's name, which is exactly the hand-picked absolute the formula rule forbids. No AC conflict: AC2's conforming store is defined as carrying per-store values, so a values-less split store is not its subject. No code change; the behaviour is now documented as a decision and pinned by a test so it is not later "repaired" as a defect.

**Amendment A-C24 gains a forward-compatibility clause.** Appending a key this version does not know produced `could not verify - unrecognized key 'last_swept'` — a defect on a store that is fine — and the local plugin cache holds 17 co-resident per-version directories, so stores really do outlive checkers. The bind was structural: A-C24 assigns the format to chunk 1, so with no growth path chunk 2 would have to change a format it is forbidden to change. Keys written `x-...` are now ignored and **reported** (size-axis line and `size.ignored_keys`); every other unrecognized key stays a hard error, because blanket tolerance would silently swallow `budget_fracton: 0.5` and apply the default.

Carried to chunk 2 as procedure rather than checker code: the sweep must **append** to the values region, never rewrite it — losing it silently returns a measured store to `not evaluated`, and after chunk 3 that store is the one whose problem is being over budget.

## Resting state

Better policy and checker shipped; no store obligated to migrate. The live store and user-global `CLAUDE.md` are untouched — migration is chunk 3'

author: dineshmittal-neosmith
body:
## Why

No contributor doc existed, and this material doesn't belong in the customer-facing README.

## What's in it

The question that keeps coming up — build the complete npm package locally and test it end-to-end **without uploading to the registry** — at three fidelity levels, with the tradeoff stated for each:

| Approach | When | Tradeoff |
|---|---|---|
| `npm pack` + global install | pre-release gate | the exact tarball `npm publish` would upload; **the only option that validates the `files` allowlist** |
| `npm link` | iteration | bypasses `files`, so a module you forgot to ship works perfectly right up until release |
| Verdaccio | registry behavior | only when testing the registry interaction itself |

Also: testing against a throwaway HOME (all four of `HOME`/`USERPROFILE`/`APPDATA`/`XDG_CONFIG_HOME` — setting only `HOME` on Windows leaves paths pointing at the real profile), the test suite and pre-push hook, requirements for adding a command or harness, and the release flow.

**Troubleshooting** covers failures actually hit, with root cause rather than just the fix: the stale `~/.local/bin` launcher shadowing an npm install, bash's command hash cache surviving the fix, "a global install is a copy, not a symlink", and why a new env var is invisible to a running editor.

## Two CI fixes — same drift class

- **`publish.yml`** ran a hand-maintained list of test files that had gone stale: `env-preservation` and `originals` were both missing, so **the publish gate was weaker than the PR gate that admitted them**. Now runs `scripts/run-contract.js`, matching `test.yml`.
- **`package.json`** had the same stale list. `test` and `test:all` both route through `run-contract.js`, so a new contract file is picked up everywhere with nothing to register.

## Verification

`node scripts/run-contract.js` → 99/99 on this branch standalone. All relative links resolve.

> One link points at `packages/cli/lib/envsetup.js`, which lands in #18 — resolves once that merges.

author: abhinav-jain09
body:
## The problem

`scripts/deploy/service-deploy.sh` had this:

```bash
NAMESPACE="options-edge"
```

A constant. That was correct while options-edge was the only namespace — but now `fullfunding` exists, and **a build has no way to know which application a service belongs to.** Every service would deploy into options-edge regardless of where it belongs.

## The change

The namespace comes from `services.yaml`:

```yaml
- name: some-service
  namespace: fullfunding      # unset means options-edge
```

**Unset means `options-edge`**, so all 51 existing entries keep their exact behaviour and nothing needs back-filling. A tenant service sets the field and the same job deploys it to the right place.

## Two guards, because this crosses an application boundary

**1. The namespace must already exist.** A service deploy never creates one — that is a platform action with its own job and credential (`k8s/tenants/<tenant>/bootstrap`). Without this, a typo in the registry silently creates a namespace and deploys into it.

**2. The render must target the registered namespace.** A service whose manifests say `options-edge` while its registry entry says `fullfunding` — or the reverse — is refused *before any apply*, naming each offending object and where it was headed. Separate namespaces are pointless if a mistake in one can still reach the other.

## Verified against the live prod cluster, all three cases

```
A) existing service, unchanged
   === service-deploy: web -> namespace options-edge (env=production) ===

B) registered for a namespace that does not exist
   FATAL: namespace 'nosuchns' does not exist. A service deploy never creates one —
          run the owning tenant/infra job first.

C) registry says fullfunding, manifests say options-edge
   FATAL: web is registered for namespace 'fullfunding' but its render targets another:
     Service/options-edge-web -> options-edge
     Deployment/options-edge-web -> options-edge
```

**(C) is the one that matters** — it is exactly the mistake that would deploy one application's service into the other.

## What did not change

No Jenkins job, no credential, no existing service. The options-edge deployer already holds rights in `fullfunding` (granted in #758), so the same `service-deploy` job serves both — routed by the registry, with the guards keeping it honest.

author: tweggen
body:
Reverts the functional half of #48. **The physical system is unstable from the very start** with the real model height — worse than the zero-height disc, not better.

## Why this was the wrong change to make

The typo is real: the cylinder **length** argument reads `BB.Y` minus itself, so the player ship's collision body is a flat disc. But fixing it is not a bug fix, it is a **physics retune**. `MassShip`, the hover forces, the self-righting gain and the damping have all been tuned against a zero-height body, and changing the shape invalidates every one of them at once. That is a far larger change than the one-line diff made it look, and it should not have ridden along on a diagnostic push.

It was also never *proven* to be the cause of the angular runaway. The evidence was circumstantial — angular velocity in the hundreds against a limit of 0.8, recovering within frames of being clamped to zero, and no `Too fast` warning on the controller's own impulse (limit 500), which is consistent with impulses arriving from the solver rather than from our code. **Consistent is not demonstrated**, and acting on it changed behaviour before the root cause was established. That was the wrong order, and the instability is the cost of it.

## Kept from #48 — neither changes behaviour

- **The finding**, as a comment at the site, explicitly marked as a known bug that is *deliberately not fixed*, with the reasons above. So the next reader does not "correct" it and rediscover the instability the hard way.
- **A `Trace` at body creation** printing the radius, the height the body is *actually* built with, and the model Y extent it was meant to derive it from — so the discrepancy shows up in a log instead of only in the source.

The emergency clamp from #46 keeps the runaway survivable meanwhile.

## Verification

- The cylinder call is byte-for-byte the pre-#48 expression.
- `Karawan` and `Wuka` build, 0 errors.
- 192/192 tests pass.

author: sjwan01
body:
## Summary

Streamlines the CI and publish workflows to eliminate noise and waste:

**ci.yml**
- `push` narrowed to `branches: [main]` — feature-branch pushes are covered by `pull_request`, so the same commit no longer runs CI twice; tags no longer trigger CI.
- `paths-ignore` for docs-only changes (`**/*.md`, `LICENSE`) — documentation PRs skip the full matrix entirely. `.github/` is deliberately NOT ignored (CI changes must be verified by CI).
- `actions/cache` for the venv (key: python version + `pyproject.toml` hash, with restore-keys) — `make bootstrap` goes from minutes to seconds on cache hit.

**publish.yml**
- A "Check version changed" step gates the whole flow: a merge to `main` without a version bump (e.g. docs) skips bootstrap/check/build/twine/upload. Version-changing merges and manual `workflow_dispatch` runs run the full flow. `skip-existing` remains as a second guard on TestPyPI.

## Behavior after merge

- PR: CI runs (re-runs on each push to the branch).
- Merge to main: CI runs (merged state).
- Version-changing merge: publish runs full flow → TestPyPI.
- Docs-only merge: no CI, publish triggers but skips everything except the version check.
- Tag push: no CI, no publish.

author: dlipicar
body:
Nix below **2.26** discards an overridden input's own lock and resolves its children from the **parent's** lock instead. Every doc-test that passes `--override-input` — which is all of them under `--workspace-pins` — therefore builds that input's dependencies from a stale snapshot, and can silently compile months-old code **while reporting green**. `v27` shipped Nix 2.22.

## Not theoretical

On #99 this produced two failures whose builds are clean on a local Nix 2.34.6 with the **identical** pins:

| job | CI (Nix 2.22) | local (Nix 2.34.6) |
|---|---|---|
| `doctest logos-basecamp` (both platforms) | `#include "logos_async_result.h"` — file not found | `nix build .#logos-basecamp` **succeeds** |
| `doctest logos-tutorial` (both platforms) | 6 failures, all downstream of the basecamp build | — |

The basecamp artifact built locally carries the expected new-protocol symbols (`ModuleHandshakeProxy` ×160, `seedHandshakeTrustAnchor` ×10), so the pins are sound; CI just could not resolve them. Same pins, opposite outcomes, decided entirely by the Nix version.

The same root cause also forced an otherwise-unnecessary pin on #99: `logos-lidl` had to be bumped because cpp-sdk's own lidl pin was being discarded in favour of the parent's stale one.

## Why it matters beyond #99

The workspace job exists to catch cross-repo drift. Under Nix 2.22 it can build a dependency at a commit the workspace does not pin and still pass — the failure mode `--workspace-pins` was introduced to eliminate. This silently under-tests every doc-test that overrides an input.

## Scope

Version bump only — `v31` keeps the `extra_nix_config` interface, and the diff is 3 lines of `uses:` plus a comment explaining the ≥ 2.26 floor so it is not casually reverted.

Applied to **all three** workflows (`tests-and-doctests.yml`, `ci.yml`, `nightly-bump.yml`) deliberately: a doc-test that resolves its inputs differently in `ci.yml` than in `tests-and-doctests.yml` is its own trap.

## Verification plan

Merge this first, then rebase #99 onto it and re-run `tests-and-doctests`. Expected: both `logos-basecamp` jobs and the 6 remaining `logos-tutorial` failures clear. The other reds on #99 are independent and will remain — `logos-storage-module` (86/1, identical pre-existing), `logos-execution-zone-module` (10/13 pre-existing; Metal Toolchain on macOS), and `logos-evm-wallet-ui` (logos-co/logos-doctest#12).

author: azouel4me
body:
The unscoped gallery selected every non-rejected photo with no visibility join, so any guest opening /gallery saw photos from hidden projects — the ones reachable only by link/QR — and from private projects too. Replaced with ListPublicGalleryPhotos, which joins projects and restricts to public.

?project_id=N had no visibility check either. It now 404s for anything not public: project ids are sequential, so serving a hidden project's gallery by id would defeat the unguessable slug that makes it hidden. A nonexistent id returns the same 404 as a non-public one so the response can't be used to probe which ids exist.

Also stops publishing session_id in the same response. Guest sessions are accepted verbatim from the fineprint_guest cookie and are exactly what DeleteOwnPhoto authorizes against, so handing out every photo's session id let any guest set that cookie and delete another guest's photos. Ownership is now returned as an is_mine boolean computed server-side from the requester's own cookie.

That also fixes the ownership UI, which had been silently dead: the gallery page tried to read the guest session via document.cookie, but the cookie is HttpOnly, so isOwn was always false and a guest never saw the delete affordance on their own photo.

Tests cover each visibility class in the unscoped listing, the scoped 404s, 404 indistinguishability, that rejected photos stay excluded, that no session id appears in the payload, and that is_mine tracks the requester's cookie. Reverting the query makes the first test fail on both hidden and private.

author: alvarolobato
body:
## What & why

Two owner-reported UI bugs in the candidate feed filter bar (`dashboard/components/candidates/CandidateFilterBar.tsx`), both purely presentational — no filter semantics changed.

### 1. "Más filtros" popover renders off-screen
> "Cuando selecciono mas filtros el popup se sale de la pantalla."

**Cause:** the `Popover.Panel` was positioned with `position: absolute; left: 0; top: calc(100% + 6px)` and a fixed `width: 300`. Because the "Más filtros" trigger sits toward the right of a `flex-wrap` row (after the segmented control, search box, source, bajo-mercado, alerts toggle), on a wide feed it opens near the right edge and the 300px panel spills past the viewport; on narrow widths the wrapped bar puts it in unpredictable spots and it clips too.

**Fix:** anchor the panel viewport-aware via headlessui v2's `anchor={{ to: "bottom end", gap: 6 }}` (Floating UI flip/shift under the hood, already a dependency), and cap size: `width: min(300px, 92vw)`, `maxWidth: 92vw`, `maxHeight: min(70vh, var(--anchor-max-height))` with `overflow: auto`. The panel now opens right-aligned to the trigger and Floating UI shifts it back on-screen at any width; it never exceeds the viewport and scrolls internally instead of clipping below the fold.

### 2. "Limpiar todo" jumps the layout
> "Limpiar todo hace un efecto raro que salta la pantalla, déjalo siempre visible."

**Cause:** the button was conditionally rendered (`{anyActive && (...)}`), so it appeared/disappeared as filters were toggled, shifting the bar.

**Fix:** always render it. When no filter is active it stays visible but `disabled` and muted (`opacity: 0.5`, `cursor: not-allowed`, `--fg-subtle`); clear-all behaviour is unchanged when active. The bar layout no longer shifts.

Everything else about the popover (grouped filters, active-count badge, chips, Limpiar todo behaviour) is intact, using the existing redesign tokens.

## Tests (D-041)

New spec `dashboard/e2e/mas-filtros-popover-overflow.spec.ts` (real Next.js server + self-seeded Postgres, admin-session pattern):
- opens "Más filtros" at **1920×1080** and **480×800** and asserts the panel bounding box is fully inside the viewport (`x>=0`, `x+w<=vw`, `y>=0`, `y+h<=vh`);
- asserts "Limpiar todo" is visible **with and without** active filters, and toggling a filter changes neither the primary row height nor the button position (no layout shift);
- asserts no error surface throughout.

## Local CI (from `dashboard/`)
- `npm run typecheck` ✅
- `npm run lint` ✅ (no warnings/errors)
- `bash scripts/check-llm-context.sh` ✅
- e2e: `mas-filtros-popover-overflow.spec.ts` + `filter-bar-url-state.spec.ts` → **6 passed**

Scope limited to `CandidateFilterBar.tsx` + the new e2e spec. No `.github/workflows/` changes (D-029).

author: axdeontour
body:
**Eingegangen · Bestätigt · Eingeplant · In Arbeit · Erledigt · Verworfen**

## Warum sechs

Die ersten drei sind eine **Leiter der Verbindlichkeit**: „wir haben es" — „wir machen es" — „wir wissen wann". Auf einem geteilten Board meldet der Kunde etwas, und jede Stufe ist ein Vorgang, den jemand auslöst. Fielen sie zusammen, sagte schon das Anlegen eines Tickets eine Zusage zu, die niemand gegeben hat.

## Warum nicht „Backlog"

Der Begriff bezeichnet üblicherweise den **unsortierten Eingangsstapel** — also die *erste* Spalte. An zweiter Stelle, für „bestätigt", läse ihn falsch herum, wer ihn kennt, und gar nicht, wer ihn nicht kennt.

Dazu passt das Benennungsprinzip des Produkts: §7 benennt „nach dem Publikum, nicht nach der Technik" (so heißen auch die Sichtbarkeitsstufen), und §8 verbietet kundenspezifische Spaltennamen — der Kunde sieht dieselben wie die interne Seite. Fachjargon aus der Softwareentwicklung steht damit auf einem Schirm, für den er nicht gemacht ist.

## Keine Spalte „Wartet auf Kunde"

Der Wartezustand liegt laut §9 **quer zu den Spalten** und ist ein Filterschalter, kein Ort. Ein Test verbietet eine solche Spalte ausdrücklich — sie wäre die naheliegendste falsche Ergänzung, wenn jemand die Vorgabe später überarbeitet.

## Übersetzt wird einmalig

Beim Anlegen, in der Sprache der anlegenden Person. Danach sind es normale Daten und jederzeit umbenennbar. Bei jeder Anzeige zu übersetzen wäre falsch: Dann sähe ein englischsprachiger Kunde andere Spalten als die interne Seite, und §8 verlangt ausdrücklich dieselben.

## Die Prüfung ist geteilt

Weil jede Ebene nur weiß, was sie wissen kann:

- `DefaultColumnsTest` prüft die **Quellwörter** containerfrei — nötig, weil die Testumgebung auf Englisch läuft und die Spalten dort übersetzt entstehen.
- Die Integrationssuite prüft, dass **sechs Spalten in der richtigen Reihenfolge und übersetzt** angelegt werden.

Zwei Gegenproben, beide fallen: „Backlog" an zweiter Stelle, und eine ergänzte Warte-Spalte.

- handle $d=0$ by proving that no projective ray exists, and handle $d=1$ with the separate formula $\chi_{P_p+P_q}(X)=X-2$

body:
## O bug que você achou

O print mostrou que **"Bitcoin above ___ on August N"** é um mercado de **vários strikes** (acima de 60k? 62k? 64k? ...), cada um com **Yes/No** — não um binário Up/Down como o SPY. Meu código só pegava o **primeiro strike** e tratava como Up/Down, então o **64000 Yes 97,9¢** (dentro da faixa) nunca virava sinal. Você estava certo.

## A correção

- O `Mercado` ganha **`kind`**: `"binary"` (SPY) ou `"strikes"` (Bitcoin).
- **Captura de strikes**: percorre **todos** os markets do evento — um contrato por strike (a `faixa`), com Yes→up e No→down por posição.
- **Estudo** agrupa por **(dia, faixa)**: cada strike é um contrato; **qualquer lado na faixa (95–99,8¢) vira parcela**, com o intervalo de 10 min por contrato. O SPY (binário) fica com uma faixa `"—"` e resultado **idêntico** ao de antes (segue com 8 parcelas).
- **Dashboard**: para strikes mostra a **tabela dos strikes** do último snapshot com a coluna **"Na faixa"** (marca quais entrariam); o gráfico de preço binário fica só para o SPY.

## Testes
`python -m unittest discover -s tests` → **122 OK** (novos: strike na faixa vira sinal; `daily_summary` agrega os strikes do dia). Smoke test: SPY mantém as 8 parcelas; Bitcoin lida com vazio.

## Nota
Não consegui validar contra a API da Polymarket daqui (bloqueada), então a captura de strikes foi escrita a partir da estrutura do seu print (multi-strike Yes/No via `groupItemTitle`). Rodando no Actions, o **64000 Yes 97,9¢** deve virar parcela na próxima captura — vale conferir o log da primeira rodada.

author: cataggar
body:
#369 took `tryAdd` from 5 allocations per event to 2. Both survivors were
`encodeMessage`'s dynamic buffer, measured directly rather than inferred:
a temporary `encodeMessage ONLY` benchmark case reported 2.00 allocs/op
and 192 B/op for one event. `Buffer.ensureCapacity` grows by
`@max(len * 2, needed, 64)`, so an ~80 byte message allocates 64, then
reallocs to 128 — two allocations and 192 B requested to hold 80 B. The
`ArrayList` append was never the problem; it amortises to about 0.01.

So the per-event allocation was the *encoder's* buffer, not the batch's
storage. Two changes follow from that:

  - `EventDataBatch` keeps one `scratch` buffer and reuses it for every
    event, via a new `encodeMessageIntoBuffer`. Once it has grown to fit
    the largest event seen, encoding allocates nothing.
  - `marshaled: ArrayList([]u8)` becomes `blob: ArrayList(u8)` plus
    `ends: ArrayList(usize)`, so an adopted event is a memcpy into space
    already reserved rather than an owned slice per event.

Encoding into scratch first also means the fit check happens before
anything is committed, so a refused event needs no rollback: it is simply
never copied out of scratch. `blob` and `ends` are both reserved with
`ensureUnusedCapacity` before either is touched, so a failed growth
cannot leave the batch holding half an event.

  case                       allocs/op          B/op
  batch.tryAdd x1000    2010.00 ->  19.45   230158 -> 134851
  encodeBatchTransfer   2011.00 ->  20.20   320188 -> 203856
  send x1000            2051.00 ->  60.90   603189 -> 539381
  send x8x100           1716.15 -> 180.05   400817 -> 409301
  sendPipelined x8x100  1716.00 -> 180.00   386507 -> 404531
  batch.tryAdd x100      206.00 ->  14.00    21710 ->  23963
  batch.tryAdd x1          5.00 ->   6.00      430 ->    677
  send x1                 43.00 ->  44.00    21808 ->  22055

Both sides re-measured for this table rather than carried over from
#370, interleaved and repeated three times under one fixed launch
environment; every figure above repeated exactly. That control matters
more than usual here. `blob` grows geometrically — `ArrayList` takes
`minimum + minimum / 2 + init_capacity`, not doubling — and the counting
allocator charges a reallocation only when the block moves, so both
`B/op` *and* the second decimal of `allocs/op` depend on the heap layout
the process starts with. The same head binary reports `batch.tryAdd
x1000` anywhere from 110830 to 181382 B, and 19.15 to 20.05 allocations,
depending only on how it was launched; the base, which allocated exactly
per event, reported 2010.00 / 230158 in every environment tried. Only
the thousand-event and eight-batch rows move; the one-event,
hundred-event and receive rows were identical in every launch
environment tried. The benchmark's module comment now says all of this.
(Every figure here is ReleaseFast, which is what the benchmark
documents; figures taken under another optimisation mode are not
comparable to these.)

The marginal cost of an event is now (19.45 - 6.00) / 999 = 0.013
allocations. That is the number this change was aimed at.

Two regressions, both real:

A one-event batch costs one allocation and 247 B more than before. The
cause is one growable container becoming two: `marshaled` was itself a
growable `ArrayList([]u8)` that over-allocated to capacity 9, so it cost
1 allocation and 144 B, while `blob` plus `ends` cost 2 and 391 B. The
two sides decompose exactly — 430 = 192 encoder + 94 envelope + 144
marshaled, and 677 = 192 scratch + 94 envelope + 255 blob + 136 ends —
which also shows `scratch` is neutral rather than part of the
regression: it replaces `encodeMessage`'s buffer one for one at 2
allocations and 192 B. `send x1` inherits the same +1 allocation.
Anything sending single events in a batch of one pays that.

Bytes rise wherever batches stay small: +10% at 100 events and +4.7% on
the eight-batch cases, because geometric growth overshoots where exact
per-event allocation did not. It inverts well before 1000 events, where
one growing buffer beats 1000 separate 2.4x-overshooting allocations and
bytes fall 41%.

The eight-batch figure needs its own note, because the two rows in the
table disagree with each other (+2.1% and +4.7%) and neither is the
change. Both rows carry some number of the scripted peer's own
`MemoryTransport.outbound` growths, which `benchSendSequential` already
documents as the test peer's buffer rather than the send path. Each is
worth 95400 / 20 = 4770 B/op, and every eight-batch figure I measured
decomposes onto a fixed steady state plus a whole number of them:
400817 = 386507 + 3, 409301 = 404531 + 1, 499931 = 404531 + 20. Against
the steady states the trade is 386507 -> 404531, +4.7%, in every
environment. The apparent range was the artifact, not the change.

Allocation count is the stated regression gate and it improves 9x to
100x on every case with more than one event, but the byte trade is a
trade, not a free win.

Reusing one scratch buffer has a third cost, which is fixed here rather
than disclosed. The buffer keeps the high-water mark of every event
*offered*, not every event adopted, and an event is encoded in full
before its size is checked — so refusing one 10 MiB event would park 10
MiB on the batch until `deinit`, where the per-event allocation this
replaces freed it on the spot. `tryAdd` now releases `scratch` on the
refusal path when it exceeds `max_size_bytes`, which no acceptable event
can need.

`marshaled` was a public field and is gone. `count()` and `sizeInBytes()`
are unchanged; `payloadAt(i)` replaces indexing it. Slices it returns
point into `blob` and are invalidated by any later `tryAdd`, which is
documented on both. No caller outside the package used `marshaled`.

`encodeDataSections` had no caller left once `encodeBatchTransfer`
switched to `encodeDataSectionsFromBlob`, so its two tests were guarding
a function the send path no longer runs — including the one that pins
`dataSectionSize` against what is actually written, which is the
invariant a disagreement would truncate a payload over. The dead
function is deleted and both tests now drive the blob form.
`encodeMessage` is now unreachable in the same way, but is kept: it
delegates to `encodeMessageSectionsInto`, the live batch path, so its
tests cannot drift away from what ships. `encodeDataSections` had its
own independent loop, which is what made it a hazard.

Five tests, all mutation-verified rather than assumed to work:

  - "a rejected event leaves no trace in the encoded transfer" fills a
    batch to refusal and asserts its encoded transfer is byte-identical
    to a batch that was never offered the refused event, and that its
    `blob` is the same length. Moving the whole commit before the fit
    check fails it with `expected 8, found 10`; committing only into
    `blob` fails the length assertion with `expected 456, found 570`.
  - "an event accepted after a refusal carries only its own bytes" is
    the shape that makes a `blob` half-commit observable at all. A
    refusal at the end of a batch leaves stray bytes outside every
    section, so the encoded transfer cannot see them; a refusal between
    two accepted events puts them inside the next event's section. The
    mutation that appends to `blob` before the fit check while leaving
    `ends` after it fails three tests: this one, the blob-length
    assertion above, and the oversized-refusal test below. Before those
    assertions existed it passed the entire suite, which is what made it
    worth adding them.
  - "a refused oversized event does not park its encoding on the batch"
    covers the scratch release. Dropping the release fails it alone.
  - "scratch is reused across accepted events rather than released"
    pins the optimisation itself. Releasing on the accept path as well
    is harmless for correctness and passed every other test, while
    quietly restoring the per-event allocation this change removes.

body:
## Summary

Implements **Sprint 5 — Render Batching** to minimize `SpriteBatch.Begin/End` state changes by grouping entities by texture.

## Changes

### API Changes
- **`Sprite.Texture`** — new public getter for the underlying `Texture2DAsset`
- **`Entity.BatchTexture`** — renamed from `Texture`
- **`Entity.BatchTextureDirty`** — renamed from `TextureChanged`
- **`Entity.RegisterForInstancedRendering(Texture2DAsset)`** — renamed from `SetTexture()`
- **`Entity.RegisterForInstancedRendering(Sprite)`** — new overload that extracts texture from sprite

### Core Logic
- `EntitySystem.Draw()` now groups entities by `BatchTexture` before rendering
- Single `SpriteBatch.Begin/End` per texture group
- Sort order preserved within each texture group
- Entities without textures render in a separate group

### Testing
- 13 new unit tests for render batching behavior
- All 486 tests passing (2 pre-existing skips)

### Documentation
- Sprint 5 documentation marked complete
- Sprint 20 created for Z-Order Render Layers (follow-up work)

### Playground
- `Ball.cs` demo entity uses clean `RegisterForInstancedRendering(_sprite)` API
- No more reflection hacks ✨

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Entities are sorted by texture before drawing
- [x] SpriteBatch is begun/ended per texture group
- [x] Sort order is preserved within texture groups
- [x] Project builds cleanly — 0 errors, 0 warnings
- [x] All existing tests pass + new batching tests added

## Known Limitations
- Z-order rendering may be incorrect when entities with different textures interleave
- Sprint 20 addresses this with z-aware batching (group by z-layer + texture)

author: satoshi-34
body:
Closes #202

#195 の A/B 比較で選定者が選んだ **候補A（Bravura engravingDefaults 準拠）** を、アプリの既定値として適用しました。実装仕様は本Issueの**トリアージコメント**（2026-08-09）に従っています。順序制約（PR #198・#201 のマージ後）は両PRがマージ済みのため解けています。

## 変更の骨格: 値の正本を1ファイルに集めた

太さ・文字サイズが App.css と5つの描画ファイルに散らばっていて「いま何 sp か」を追えなかったので（#195 §5 の指摘）、**`src/utils/engravingDefaults.ts`** を新設し、**sp（五線間隔比）のまま**値を持たせました。`spToUnits()`（1 sp = 10 u）で換算します。

`src/utils/engravingDefaults.test.ts` が、**この定数・App.css の数値・`ab-preview.js` の `PRESETS.a` の三者が一致していること**を見張ります（片方だけ直すと崩れる箇所なので機械で担保）。

適用した値はトリアージ表のとおりです（対応表と実装場所は設計書 §10）。

## トリアージ表を解釈した3点（レビューで追認いただきたい点）

### 1. 「ブラケット 0.12 → 0.16」は**サブ括弧**に適用しました

調査したところ、総譜左端の**太いメイン括弧**は VexFlow が**幅 3 u（= 0.30 sp）の塗り矩形**で描いていました。表の「現状 0.12」に一致するのは、アプリが SVG で直接描く**サブ括弧**（Vln.I / Vln.II をまとめる細い括弧）で、Bravura の `subBracketThickness` も 0.16 と整合します。

メイン括弧に 0.16 を当てると **0.30 → 0.16 と細くなり**、「総譜の楽器グループが読み取りにくい」（#195 の乖離5）を悪化させるため、メイン括弧は**変更していません**。Bravura 推奨の `bracketThickness` 0.50 sp へ太らせるかは**未決定事項として残しています**。

### 2. cresc./dim. とテンポ表記も、強弱記号と同じ 1.25 倍にしました

表が名前を挙げているのは「強弱記号 1.6 → 2.0」だけですが、`ab-preview.js` の `classifyText()` は **Times イタリック全部**を `dynamics` と判定して 1.25 倍していました。つまり**選定者が見て候補Aを選んだ画像では、cresc./dim.（1.2 sp）とテンポ表記（1.2 sp）も 1.5 sp になっていました**。受入条件1「`engravingAB('a')` を当てた表示と同等」を優先し、同じ倍率を当てています。表より広い範囲なので、意図と違えば戻します。

### 3. 一律 `stroke-width: 1.2` は「フォールバック」として残しました

トリアージの「一律指定を対象ごとの個別指定へ分解すること」に対し、**対象7つを個別指定へ分解した上で、一律指定自体は残して**います。

`ab-preview.js` は一律指定の**上に** `!important` でかぶせる作りなので、**承認された比較画像は一律指定が生きたままの状態**でした。いま撤去すると、スラー・タイの弧（1.6〜2.2 u）、終止括弧、連符の括弧、ペダル線、オッターバ線が**いっせいに元の属性値へ戻り**、比較画像に写っていない箇所まで太さが変わります。撤去は段3以降の作業として、参照値つきで設計書 §11-1 に残しました。

なお一律指定を残した副作用として、**符幹には 1.2 u の明示指定が必要**でした（属性は 1.5 u なので、上書きしないと据え置きのはずが太る）。

## トリアージが警告した「ブラケットのアーティファクト」— 原因を特定しました

> A/B ライブ確認時にブラケットの stroke 描画に副作用（枠状のアーティファクト）が出た

**アプリ側の不具合ではなく、A/B スニペット固有の副作用でした。** 本実装では発生しません。

原因は2つ重なったものです。

1. **括弧の上下端が豆腐（□）になる**。`StaveConnector` は BRACKET の上下端を Bravura の **U+E003 / U+E004**（SMuFL の `bracketTop` / `bracketBottom`）を `<text>` で描きますが、この2つは `g.vf-*` の**外**（SVG直下）に出るため、スニペットの `g[class^="vf-"] text` による Bravura 復帰が効きません。結果セリフ体で描かれ、**空の四角**になります（実測: 正しいグリフ 19px に対し豆腐 40px）
2. **メイン括弧の縦棒が細くなり左へずれる**。スニペットの rect 書き換えが「幅 3 以下」を対象にするため、幅 3 のメイン括弧まで 1.6 へ縮めて x も 0.7 ずらしていました

そのため本実装では、**書体を CSS で SVG の text 全部に当てず**、アプリが自分で描く `<text>` にだけ渡しています（VexFlow が描く文字には触りません）。メイン括弧の rect も触りません。

| 画像 | 中身 |
| --- | --- |
| `docs/qa/engraving-defaults/images/adopted-a-bracket.png` | **本実装**。Bravura の括弧の上下端が正しく描かれ、縦棒の太さは変更前のまま（受入条件4） |
| `docs/qa/engraving-defaults/images/preview-a-bracket-artifact.png` | 比較用。変更前 + `engravingAB('a')` で**括弧の上下に空の四角**が出る（=警告された症状） |

## 検証結果

### 受入条件1: 4譜種の初期表示（画像添付・localStorage 空で実測）

1ページ全体の画像を `docs/qa/engraving-defaults/images/adopted-a-{single,piano,quartet,windband}.png` に置きました。数値は `engravingAB('a')` を当てた main（別 worktree・別ポートで並べて実測）と一致します。

| 実測項目 | main + `engravingAB('a')` | 本実装 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 五線 | 1.3px | **1.3px** ✅ |
| 小節線 rect 幅 | 1.6 | **1.6** ✅ |
| 段の左右の縦線 | 1.6 | **1.6** ✅ |
| パート名（弦楽四重奏） | 17 | **17** ✅ |
| タイトル | 26px / 字間 0.52px / Century Schoolbook | **同じ** ✅ |
| 作者欄 | 13px | **13px** ✅ |
| 段数/ページ | 4段・1ページ | **4段・1ページ** ✅ |
| メイン括弧 | 1.6（**豆腐あり**） | **3（変更なし・豆腐なし）** ⚠ 上記の意図的な差 |

音符を置いた状態でも実測しました: **符幹 1.2px**（属性 1.5 を上書き）、**加線 1.6px かつ黒**（属性 2 / #444 を上書き）、**強弱 `f` が font-size 20 の Century Schoolbook italic**。

### 受入条件3: テスト・lint

- `npx vitest --run src --no-file-parallelism`: **130ファイル / 1446テスト 全緑**（変更前の main は 129 / 1432 で全緑。増えた1ファイル・14テストは本PRで追加したぶん）
- `npm run lint:ratchet`: **OK・基準値ちょうど（エラー 326 / 警告 5）**
- `npm run build`: **成功**（`tsc -b` も通過）

### そのほか確認したこと

- **表示ウェイトが生きている**: 細/普通/太のボタンで五線が 0.867 / **1.3** / 1.95px と比例（標準がちょうど候補Aの値）。個別指定を `calc(1.3px * var(--score-stroke-scale))` の形にして、印刷時の細線化（0.8）も従来どおり効かせています
- **REGRESSION.md G節**（小節選択のハイライト）: 4パートの小節1を選択して青枠 3px ＋ 薄青の塗りが見えることを確認（`.vf-hit` を壊していない）
- コンソールエラーなし
- **連符・終止括弧の括弧は巻き込んでいません**。これらも「幅 1 の rect」で描かれるため、SVG 全体を掃くと縦のカギだけ太って横棒が細いままの不揃いな括弧になります。そこで小節線は `g.vf-stavebarline` 直下に限定し、段の縦線は「その描画で増えた要素」だけを対象にしています

## 自信の無い点・申し送り

1. **パート名の拡大でラベル余白がわずかに広がります**（弦楽四重奏 74 → 76.9 u）。増えたぶんは小節の幅が吸収し、**4譜種すべてで段数/ページは変化なし**（実測）。既存テストが「余白が従来値から変わらない」を等値で見張っていたので、**「+4 u 以内かつ上限未満」へ緩めました**（意図＝段割りを動かさない、は維持）
2. **フル名が長い総譜のパート名は拡大されません**。余白の上限（110 u）に収まらない長さだと `fontSize = usable / ratioSum` へ縮められ、この式が基準サイズに依存しないためです（吹奏楽で 8.90 u のまま＝変化なし）。**略称を使う2段目以降は 1.7 sp になります**。#195 の乖離2が総譜で残るので、「余白上限の見直し」を別Issueにする価値があります（本Issueのスコープ外と判断）
3. **印刷プレビューでは線が細くなりません**。`.print-preview .print-page` の `--score-stroke-width: 0.8` が `.score-area` のインライン style に負けるためで、**main でも同じ**ことを実測しました（本実装による退行ではありません）。実印刷（`@media print`）は `!important` で当たるので効きます
4. **README.md は更新していません**。AGENTS.md の「README はユーザーから見える操作・画面が変わった場合のみ」「実装のポイント・Issue の経緯を書かない」に従い、操作の追加が無いためです。開発者向けの変更手順は `docs/DEVELOPMENT.md` に追記しました
5. **`CLAUDE.md` と `AGENTS.md` の内容が同一でなくなっています**（両ファイルの冒頭に「常に同一に保つ」ルールがあります）。README の扱いが CLAUDE.md では旧方針（実装のポイント・最小チェックも README へ）、AGENTS.md では #138 以降の新方針です。本PRでは新しい AGENTS.md に従いましたが、**どちらを正とするかは運用者判断**なので同期は行っていません

body:
## Purpose

Fix the false-negative immutable merge-result certification for long-lived staging PRs.

## Root cause

The trusted QA workflow treated `pull.base.sha` as the current staging tip.

For PR #219 this produced:

- stale PR base SHA: `ebb09ef3819e9126f07a52e0f5f48b72f53f3343`
- trusted staging SHA: `f42c63d807614b3ef6cb3ae817f16a6b8065231c`

GitHub's merge ref was correctly based on current staging, but the workflow rejected it because it compared that merge result against the stale PR base SHA.

## Fix

Pin the certification base to immutable workflow-dispatch `context.sha` in both:

1. Candidate / immutable merge-result validation
2. Release certification

The existing later fetch of `origin/staging` remains unchanged, so a genuine staging movement during certification still fails closed.

## Scope

- `.github/workflows/lbfl-ci.yml` only
- 1 commit
- +6 / -2
- No Worker changes
- No Cloudflare configuration changes
- No secrets
- No production deployment
- No PR #219 changes

## Exact head

`734734a9b9bb85d4ba103f9cb918d5334935a753`

## Validation

- repair commit directly descends from trusted staging `f42c63d807614b3ef6cb3ae817f16a6b8065231c`
- branch is 1 commit ahead and 0 behind staging
- only `.github/workflows/lbfl-ci.yml` changed
- stale `pull.base.sha` removed from both certification paths
- immutable `context.sha` used in both certification stages

PR #219 remains Draft until this trusted-control repair is validated and merged.

O roteiro de consertos publicado hoje de manhã acusou escassez falsa e promoções fantasma na loja. Verificado no HTML servido: **as quatro strings estão com `display:none`** e são placeholders que o JS do tema só revela com dado real, que não existe (`"stock":null` nas 10 variantes, `"has_promotional_price":false` em todas, `"promotions":[]` no carrinho). A auditoria leu o código-fonte, não a página renderizada. O dono estava certo ao dizer que não via nada disso.

Mesma correção no telefone: ele está no HTML, mas nosso próprio CSS o esconde desde 16/07, com o comentário `/* Telefone pessoal: remove contato publico */`.

`consertos-loja-2026-08-08.md` substitui o roteiro anterior (marcado `status: superado` com o aviso do que estava errado) e traz, além da correção:

- **Ordem de execução por fases**, porque os títulos das colunas do rodapé são injetados por `nth-child` e mexer no CSS antes dos menus quebra o layout.
- **Uma única colagem de CSS** cobrindo os quatro itens que tocam o mesmo campo, com o aviso de que o arquivo compacto é *gerado* e editar só ele é trabalho perdido.
- **Correções técnicas**: o selo powered-by tem duas regras escondendo (uma de grupo); o CNPJ não renderiza no rodapé porque `.contact-info` está oculto; não existe editor de textos de tema na Nuvemshop (a troca Carrinho/Sacola é FTP em `translations.txt`); o "aquí" não está no `cart.tpl`; não existe link literal do Google Fonts (é `google_fonts_url('400,700')` em dois pontos do `layout.tpl`); e a div `#nimbus-aviso-ecobag` **já existe** na linha 68 do `cart.tpl`, dentro do ramo de carrinho não vazio (testar com carrinho vazio dá falso negativo).
- **Portão de hash** corrigido: o hash conhecido vale como partida, não como chegada, já que os itens editam os arquivos.
- **Nota de que `Disallow: /loja/` não é bug**: é `VITRINE_INDEXAVEL = false`, decisão registrada em código.

author: komediruzecki
body:
Two small polish items found after v0.8.1, plus the Wrangler warning they surfaced alongside.

## Credits: "Buy" was offered to visitors who cannot buy

`startCheckout` needs a real identity — the db-worker 403s an anonymous or absent token, deliberately, because a receipt without an account is useless. So a signed-out visitor clicking **Buy** on a credit pack could only reach a "Checkout failed" toast.

The label now reads **Create account** until an account is held, and the click opens the shared sign-up dialog. `Soon` and `Unavailable` still outrank it — neither has a checkout to reach either way.

The predicate is `accountHeld()`, not a `/me` fetch: it decodes the stored token, so it is right on the first paint and corrects itself the moment someone signs in. Gating this on a fetch is the mistake documented in `auth-service.ts` that made the app look like it did not know you were signed in.

## Supporter tiers: the account CTA linked to the panel it was already in

`DonatePanel`'s signed-out fallback was `<a href="#/settings/account">`. Reached from Settings → Credits — where these cards live — that click reads as doing nothing, and the visitor is left to find the sign-in button themselves. It is a `<button>` now, opening the same `AuthModal` on its register pane, like every other sign-in entry point.

Both CTAs gained `font-family: inherit`. There is no global button reset, and the donate one becomes a `<button>` here, so without it the two would have rendered in different fonts side by side.

## The Wrangler warning

> `"r2_buckets" exists at the top level, but not on "env.preview"`

A named Wrangler environment inherits nothing from the top level, so `env.preview` had **no** bindings at runtime. Both entries added here **reference dev's existing stores** — verified against the account, a preview deploy provisions no new Cloudflare resource of any kind: no bucket, no KV namespace, no Worker script, no DNS record. It uploads an immutable *version* of two Workers that already exist.

| Binding | Real effect of its absence | Warned? |
|---|---|---|
| `SHARE_STORE` | `share-handler.ts` reads it unguarded, so `/api/share/*` 500s — but `tryShortenUrl` returns null on any failure and the caller **falls back to the long URL**. The symptom is a share link that never gets shortened, not a broken share. That silence is why it went unnoticed. | No — there is no top-level `kv_namespaces` for Wrangler to compare an env against |
| `UVR_INPUT_BUCKET` | None today. Server separation **cannot run on a preview at all**: the `mercurypitch-preview` Worker holds only `JWT_SECRET`, while dev holds `RUNPOD_API_KEY`, `RUNPOD_ENDPOINT_ID_GPU` and `BILLING_SERVICE_KEY`. Declaring it is for the warning plus the day preview gets those secrets. | Yes — this is the warning above |

`RUNPOD_STEM_PREFIX` was in the first commit and has been dropped: it is read only on the RunPod path, which cannot run here.

Worth recording, since it is the obvious alternative: **`"r2_buckets": []` does not silence the warning.** Wrangler compares binding *names*, so it switches to complaining that `UVR_INPUT_BUCKET` is missing from the env. Removing the top-level block is not an option either — it exists so plain `wrangler dev` has the staging bucket locally. Binding dev's bucket or living with the warning are the only two choices.

Verified by loading the config both ways: the version on `main` prints the warning, this branch prints nothing.

Prettier reformats `wrangler.jsonc` wholesale on first touch (trailing commas, inlined single-element arrays), which is most of that file's diff. The behavioural change is the `env.preview` block alone.

## Tests

- `PricingPanel`: signed out offers an account and opens the dialog, the unpriced pack still reads "Soon", and "Unavailable" still outranks the account offer.
- `DonatePanel`: the CTA carries no `href` and its click sets the auth modal to `register`.
- Both new tests were confirmed to fail against the old behaviour before being kept.
- Full suite green: 6058 passed, 0 failed. `pnpm check` and `pnpm pr:validate` clean.

Not verified in a browser — the preview server in this session runs from a different worktree.

body:
## Motivation Closes #34135. Krea-2 accepts a quantization configuration, but the configuration was not propagated to its transformer linear layers. As a result, eligible tensor-parallel linear layers remained unquantized when online FP8 was requested. This PR adds online FP8 support for the Krea-2 transformer architecture. The implementation also applies to Krea-2 Turbo because it uses the same transformer architecture with distilled weights. ## Modifications - Propagate `QuantizationConfig` through `Krea2Transformer2DModel`, `SingleStreamBlock`, `TextFusionTransformer`, `TextFusionBlock`, `Attention`, and `SwiGLU`. - Pass stable checkpoint-compatible prefixes to eligible `ColumnParallelLinear` and `RowParallelLinear` layers. - Preserve native precision for numerically sensitive boundary layers, including the image input projection, time-modulation projection, final output layer, and text-fusion projector. - Support `ignored_layers` using stable layer names. - Add a unit test covering FP8 method selection, ignored layers, and unquantized boundary layers. ## Accuracy Tests Krea-2 Turbo was tested in BF16 and online FP8 on an NVIDIA H100 with identical settings: - Resolution: 1024x1024 - Inference steps: 8 - Seed: 42 - Same prompt for both runs Both runs completed successfully. The FP8 result had no obvious visual degradation compared with BF16 in this smoke test. The output hashes differed, as expected from the precision change: - BF16 SHA256: `bd2cb461aca4c07f20abd340a643da3070854d6e46ff522ca9e5b9a8891888d2` - FP8 SHA256: `5a09dda0df58867e1223b6c980642b40115c718df9e87b64398848f793578871` The added unit test passed: ```text 1 passed, 17 warnings in 0.13s ``` This is a single-prompt visual smoke test rather than a comprehensive image-quality evaluation. Krea-2 Raw has not yet been benchmarked separately. ## Speed Tests and Profiling
BF16 FP8
Each precision was warmed up independently before measurement on an NVIDIA H100. | Metric | BF16 | Online FP8 | FP8 improvement | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Denoising time per step | 0.2284 s | 0.1982 s | 15.2% faster | | Subprocess elapsed time | 63.745 s | 56.351 s | 1.13x speedup | | Transformer size | 23.88 GB | 12.25 GB | 48.7% lower | | SGLang peak memory | 38,086 MB | 26,218 MB | 31.2% lower | | Observed GPU peak | 44,524 MiB | 32,656 MiB | 26.7% lower | These results represent one Krea-2 Turbo workload on one H100 and are not intended as a comprehensive performance benchmark. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (Not applicable: no user-facing API or configuration change.) - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci` 4. body:
## Qué hace

Última pieza para que el flujo teléfono → reloj funcione de punta a punta: hasta ahora el reloj recibía y guardaba canciones sueltas, pero un `WearPlaylistSync` (enviado por PR4/PR5 antes que el audio) caía al suelo sin persistirse ni mostrarse. Este PR:

1. **Recepción**: `WearDataListenerService` enruta `PLAYLIST_SYNC` a `WearTransferRepository.onPlaylistSyncReceived`, que hace upsert de la playlist y sus cross-refs (orden preservado) en una transacción. Re-sincronizar reemplaza membresía/orden en vez de mezclar con lo obsoleto, y preserva el `createdAt` original.
2. **ViewModel**: `WearLocalPlaylistViewModel` resuelve la disponibilidad de cada canción cruzando el orden de la playlist contra `LocalSongDao.getAllSongs()` — reactivamente, así que una canción que termina de transferirse mientras la pantalla de detalle está abierta pasa de "pendiente" a reproducible sin salir y volver a entrar. Expone también `playlistIdsReceiving` para el indicador "recibiendo…" en la lista.
3. **UI**: `LocalPlaylistsScreen` (lista, con indicador de recepción) y `LocalPlaylistDetailScreen` (canciones en orden de sync, las pendientes se muestran deshabilitadas con "Waiting to transfer…" en vez de ocultarse). Entrada nueva "Playlists" en `DownloadsScreen`.

Con esto, el flujo completo de la Fase 1 funciona: playlist → "enviar al reloj" → estimación → confirmar → notificación de progreso → salir de la app → escuchar en el reloj en cuanto llega la primera canción, incluyendo las playlists ya guardadas localmente.

## Una corrección sobre mi propio trabajo

Al escribir `LocalPlaylistsScreen`/`LocalPlaylistDetailScreen` usé por reflejo `items(items = list, key = {...})` asumiendo la API estándar de `androidx.compose.foundation.lazy.LazyListScope`. No compilaba: `ScalingLazyListScope` (de `androidx.wear.compose.foundation`, no Horologist) no expone esa forma como miembro — existe como función de extensión en `ScalingLazyColumnKt`, así que hacía falta importarla explícitamente (`import androidx.wear.compose.foundation.lazy.items`). Confirmado con `javap` sobre el AAR de `wear-compose-foundation:1.6.2`. De paso, esto sí resuelve el hallazgo #2 de la auditoría (listas sin `key` estable) para estas dos pantallas nuevas — el resto del módulo sigue con `items(n){}` sin key, deuda preexistente que no toco aquí.

También corregí en el mismo commit un `Icons.AutoMirrored.Rounded.QueueMusic` referenciado sin calificar (bare `QueueMusic`) en `DownloadsScreen.kt` y `LocalPlaylistsScreen.kt` — el import por sí solo no basta, hace falta la referencia calificada (mismo patrón que ya usa `SongListScreen.kt`).

## Verificado

- `./gradlew :wear:compileDebugKotlin :app:compileDebugKotlin :shared:compileDebugKotlin` — `BUILD SUCCESSFUL`, sin warnings.
- `./gradlew :wear:testDebugUnitTest` — `BUILD SUCCESSFUL`, 15 tests nuevos en verde:
  - `WearTransferRepositoryPlaylistSyncTest` (6): primer sync fija `createdAt == updatedAt`; re-sync preserva `createdAt` y sube `updatedAt`; re-sync con canciones distintas reemplaza (no mezcla) los cross-refs; orden/posición se preservan; lista vacía sigue haciendo upsert; nombre/playlistId se propagan.
  - `WearLocalPlaylistViewModelTest` (9): `playlists`/`playlistDetails` reflejan el DAO; disponibilidad de canciones en orden de sync; una canción pasa de pendiente a disponible sin recargar; `playlistIdsReceiving` reacciona a transferencias activas; `playAll`/`playFrom` respetan el guard de canciones pendientes y activan `WearOutputTarget.WATCH` cuando corresponde.
- Todo el grafo de dependencias (`WearLocalPlayerRepository`, `WearPlaybackController`, `WearTransferRepository`) se construye **real**, no mockeado: son clases `final` de Kotlin, y MockK solo puede mockear clases finales vía su agente de inline-mocking, que cuelga indefinidamente en este sandbox (mismo hallazgo que en PR4 con los clientes GMS). Documentado en el doc-comment de cada clase de test.

## Sin verificar (necesita dispositivo/emulador)

- Recepción real de un `WearPlaylistSync` vía `ChannelClient`/`MessageClient` entre dos dispositivos emparejados.
- Renderizado real de `LocalPlaylistsScreen`/`LocalPlaylistDetailScreen` en Wear Compose (tamaños, scroll, rotary).
- `WearLocalPlayerRepository.playLocalSongs` → `MediaController` → `WearPlaybackService`: en JVM puro, esta ruta falla al intentar `Uri.fromFile` (no stubbed sin Robolectric/dispositivo). Los dos tests que ejercitan `playAll`/`playFrom` sobre una canción disponible verifican el guard clause y el cambio de `WearOutputTarget` explícitamente vía `assertThrows<NullPointerException>` alrededor de ese fallo esperado — la reproducción real en sí no es verificable aquí, solo en dispositivo.

## Migración Room 5→6, DAO instrumentado

Sin cambios en este PR — ya entraron en PR2. `LocalPlaylistDaoTest`/`WearMusicDatabaseMigrationTest` (`androidTest`) siguen pendientes de ejecutar en dispositivo/emulador real.

author: keilynrp
body:
Phase 7 of #209 — **the first string in this track that reaches someone outside the organisation.**

Everything migrated so far is read by logged-in operators. A password-reset email goes to whoever asked to recover an account, and until now every one of them received Spanish regardless of who they were.

## The language question is at its hardest here

No session, no stored preference, and the reader may open the mail on a different device than the one that asked. The only signals are the `Accept-Language` of the triggering request and an explicit parameter the frontend can pass — it knows the UI language the user actually chose, which is better evidence than the browser's guess.

That is exactly the chain `language_dependency` already implements, so nothing new was invented for this case.

## Two keys, not four

The body is **one message with a `{link}` placeholder**, not three concatenated fragments. A translator needs the whole sentence; fragments produce text that fits English grammar and no other language's. `{platform}` and `{link}` interpolate verbatim.

## Two things nearly went wrong

**Newlines almost did not survive the catalog.** The body has real line breaks and a `translations.ts` literal cannot span lines. Hand-rolled escaping dropped them *silently* and the generator rejected the file. Fixed by emitting the literal with `json.dumps`, then verified end to end — the projection reads back **5 real newlines** with `{link}` intact.

**These tests broke a neighbour before they passed.** The endpoint allows **10/hour per IP** and every test here goes through it, so the file exhausted the quota and `test_auth.py`'s long-standing reset test failed with **429 while passing in isolation**. An autouse fixture resets the limiter around each test.

> On a rate-limited endpoint, **test count is a shared resource**.

## Mutation-checked

| mutation | result |
|---|---|
| subject hard-coded in English | 3 tests fail |
| resolved language ignored | 2 tests fail |

## `DEPLOY-NOTE.md`

Covers the outward-facing half: **who is affected** (anyone with no Spanish language signal now gets English; Spanish speakers keep their exact wording), **why it is safe** (nothing depends on the current subject — confirmed with the product owner 2026-07-31), what to watch after deploy, and how to roll back.

## The contract moved again

Third router to gain the dependency, third time `sdk/openapi.json` changed: **+37 lines** plus the Python client for this endpoint. The plan put that work in phase 8 (task 8.6) as though it happened once at the end — it happens **wherever a router gains the dependency**.

## Verification

- Full backend suite: **3771 passed, 9 skipped, 0 failed**.
- `openapi-drift`, `sdk-clients-drift` and the i18n parity gate all exit 0.
- `openspec validate --strict` passes.

## Related

- #209 — 41 of 47 tasks after this. Phases 8 and 9 remain, plus the separate change owed for the 15 strings in modules that persist their text.

author: that-guy-40
body:
## The defect

`tools/check-harness-net.sh` §1 enforces the rule that no test may install its own `trap … EXIT` (bash keeps one per shell, so doing it silently replaces `lib.sh`'s safety net). It matched `^[[:space:]]*trap`.

It therefore never saw:

```bash
tmp="$(mktemp -d)"; trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT
```

— the trap after a semicolon, on a line beginning with an assignment. That is the single most common way to open a test in this repo. **It printed `no test overrides lib.sh's EXIT trap` across six suites while twenty tests did.**

The anchor was deliberate: it dodged a false positive from a test that *writes* a trap into a fixture and greps for it. It bought that with a false negative twenty times the size — the cheap question (*does a line START with trap*) standing in for the real one (*is a trap installed here*).

## The fix

Match `trap` at a **command position**: start of line, or after `; && || | ( ) { }`. A `trap` inside quotes is preceded by a quote or a `^`, neither of which is a command separator — so the fixture-writing lines stay unmatched **without needing an anchor at all**. Whole comment lines are skipped: prose about the rule is not an installation of one.

## Verified

Negative controls, all run:

| fixture | want | got |
|---|---|---|
| comment mentioning `trap 'cleanup' EXIT` | not flagged | rc=0 ✓ |
| `printf 'trap reap EXIT\n…'` (fixture write) | not flagged | rc=0 ✓ |
| `grep -q '^trap reap EXIT'` (fixture grep) | not flagged | rc=0 ✓ |
| `tmp="$(mktemp -d)"; trap … EXIT` | **flagged** | rc=1 ✓ |
| `trap 'echo x' EXIT` (line-anchored) | **flagged** | rc=1 ✓ |

`examples/metal-as-a-service/tests` — the suite the anchor existed for — stays green, so the false positive did not come back.

The 20 offenders (phase2 ×8, phase3 ×4, micro-linux ×4, phase4 ×2, phase5 ×1, zfsbootmenu ×1) converted to `on_exit`. **Verified by outcome, not by exit status:** `/tmp` entry counts are unchanged across a run of each, so the temp dirs really are still being removed — by `lib.sh`'s net now rather than by their own trap. 19 passed, 1 skipped (docker), 0 failed.

Out of scope, classified not missed: `tools/tests/`, `kali-packer-vagrant`, `almalinux-packer-images` have **no lib-owned net and no checker** — those tests supply their own `_on_exit`, which is a different arrangement, not a violation of this one.

body:
Two changes touching the same strings, so done together rather than over the same lines twice. **425 tests, typecheck clean, lint unchanged at 14 problems.**

## Spelling, at David's ask

`enrol` → `enroll`, `enrolment` → `enrollment`. One rule does it — **`enrol` NOT followed by `l`** — which is the only form that actually differs between dialects:

- `enrolled` and `enrolling` are identical in both, and are left alone
- the lookahead is what stops the already-correct `enroll` (including the CLI subcommand it quotes) becoming `enrolll`
- an all-caps `ENROLMENT` escaped the first pass and needed its own case

`device-enrolment.tsx` and its test are renamed with it.

## And a command that runs

The screen displays `armillary-engine enroll --name <device> --grants sync,push`, which until today exited with *"the following required arguments were not provided"* because `--root` was a required global on the engine. Fixed there in [core#26](https://github.com/studiozojer/armillary-core/pull/26); the comment added here records why the flag is deliberately absent, so nobody helpfully adds it back.

The copy now says the command runs **on the host** — a phone cannot run it, and that is the whole reason this screen is a paste field rather than a button.

`projects/harness/specs/2026-08-07-principal-on-the-wire-plan.md` keeps its two `Enrol`s. It is a dated, executed plan, and the studio's rule for those is *fix a live surface on touch, leave a frozen record as written* — rewriting one edits history to agree with a decision made after it.

author: taciturnaxolotl
body:
First slice of **Workstream E** (sound threading). Removes the two most dangerous threading defects the audit flagged.

## What was wrong
Both message-drain sites (`threadLogic::checkMessages`, `MainFrame::OnIdle`) held `mexMessages` across the whole `parseMessage` loop and acquired it with `while (mexMessages.TryLock()==BUSY) wxYield();`:
- On the **GUI thread**, `wxYield` pumped the event loop while waiting on the logic thread, letting a menu action (undo/redo/paste) re-enter mid-drain — the crash class the sim-timer guard (#32) worked around.
- On the **logic thread**, `wxYield` was called off the GUI thread, which wxWidgets doesn't support.
- It only worked because `parseMessage`'s STEPSIM path re-locks `mexMessages` via `sendMessage` — i.e. it silently relied on the mutex being recursive.

Separately, **New/Open cleared the queues with no lock held** (`MainFrame.cpp`), racing the logic thread that drains `dGUItoLOGIC` on its own 1 ms loop (which `pauseTimers()` doesn't stop).

## The fix
Swap the pending deque into a local under the lock, release, then process the local. `mexMessages` is now held only for an O(1) swap — no busy-spin, no yield, no recursive-mutex reliance, and `parseMessage` can re-take the lock freely. The two flushes now clear under the lock.

Both drains remain serialized by `m_critsect` exactly as before, so this **adds no concurrency between them** — it only shortens the lock hold and removes the reentrancy + the illegal cross-thread yield. The threading-model doc on `MainApp.h` is updated to describe the new protocol.

## Scope / not included
This is the **minimal, low-risk** slice. It does **not** replace the logic thread's 1 ms poll with a condition-variable wakeup (the plan's 'condvar on both ends') — that's a larger, higher-risk follow-up.

## Testing
- Clock circuit stable untouched; **survived a hard interactive stress run** (sim running while pasting / undo / redo / New / Open / tab-switching) with no hang or crash; plus 20 scripted maximize/restore repaint cycles under the sim.
- **Caveat, disclosed:** one `0xC0000005 execute at 0x0` null-call was seen on a first-launch foreground+screenshot and could **not** be reproduced in ~40 subsequent iterations or the interactive stress. By analysis it isn't introduced here (this change narrows the unsafe window rather than widening it), so it's most likely a pre-existing rare startup/paint race — worth keeping an eye on, not a regression from this PR.

author: thodson-usgs
body:
Phase 0 cleanup from #1. Bug fix, no API additions.

## Reproduce on `master`

```python
from owslib.etree import etree
from owslib.iso3 import FC_FeatureCatalogue, NAMESPACES_V2

XML = b"""<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<gfc:FC_FeatureCatalogue
    xmlns:gfc="http://standards.iso.org/iso/19110/gfc/1.1"
    xmlns:cat="http://standards.iso.org/iso/19115/-3/cat/1.0"
    xmlns:gco="http://standards.iso.org/iso/19115/-3/gco/1.0"
    uuid="test-catalogue-1">
  <cat:name><gco:CharacterString>Hydrography</gco:CharacterString></cat:name>
  <gfc:featureType>
    <gfc:FC_FeatureType uuid="ft-1">
      <gfc:typeName><gco:LocalName>River</gco:LocalName></gfc:typeName>
      <gfc:carrierOfCharacteristics>
        <gfc:FC_FeatureAttribute uuid="attr-1">
          <gfc:memberName><gco:ScopedName>discharge</gco:ScopedName></gfc:memberName>
        </gfc:FC_FeatureAttribute>
      </gfc:carrierOfCharacteristics>
    </gfc:FC_FeatureType>
  </gfc:featureType>
</gfc:FC_FeatureCatalogue>"""

element = etree.fromstring(XML)

# as owslib/catalogue/csw3.py:489 calls it
FC_FeatureCatalogue(element)
# AttributeError: 'FC_FeatureCatalogue' object has no attribute 'namespaces'

# as owslib/iso3.py:243 calls it
FC_FeatureCatalogue(NAMESPACES_V2, element)
# TypeError: __init__() takes from 1 to 2 positional arguments but 3 were given
```

**Both call sites fail**, in different ways. The ISO 19115-3 feature catalogue
path is unreachable today.

## Cause

`FC_FeatureCatalogue`, `FC_FeatureType`, `FC_FeatureAttribute` and
`FC_ListedValue` all read `self.namespaces` but never set it, and take no
`namespaces` argument — while every other class in the module does:

```python
class MD_ImageDescription(printable):
    def __init__(self, namespaces, img_desc=None):
        self.namespaces = namespaces
```

The two-argument call at `iso3.py:243` was already written for that signature, so
these four definitions appear to have been missed when the rest of the module was
converted.

There is also an undefined name at `iso3.py:1436` — the
`carrierOfCharacteristics` loop passes a bare `namespaces` instead of
`self.namespaces`. It was unreachable behind the earlier failure.

## Fix

Give the four classes a `namespaces` parameter, thread it through the nested
constructions, and update the `csw2`/`csw3` call sites to pass `NAMESPACES_V2`.

## Why CI did not catch it

`owslib/iso3.py:10` carries `# flake8: noqa: E501`. That reads as "ignore long
lines in this file"; it actually disables **every** check in the file, including
the undefined name:

```console
$ printf '# flake8: noqa: E501\nx = 1   \n' > /tmp/a.py && flake8 /tmp/a.py | wc -l
0
$ printf 'x = 1   \n' > /tmp/b.py && flake8 /tmp/b.py | wc -l
1
```

Narrowing those directives is left to a separate PR so this fix stays reviewable
on its own.

## Verification

```
tests/test_iso3_feature_catalogue.py    9 passed
full offline suite                    246 passed (was 237)
flake8 owslib/                        clean
ruff check --select F821 owslib/      All checks passed
```

author: slachiewicz
body:
The first run that got past authentication failed at the very last hurdle, on plexus-utils:

```
M  apidocs/org/codehaus/plexus/util/StringUtils.html
M  apidocs/org/codehaus/plexus/util/SweeperPool.html
...
##[error]Process completed with exit code 141
```

**141 is SIGPIPE**, and it is my bug, in this line:

```bash
git status --short | head -50
```

`head` exits after 50 lines. `git status` is then killed writing to a closed pipe. Under `set -o pipefail` that becomes the pipeline's exit status, and `set -e` makes it fatal.

Reproduced exactly:

```
$ bash -c 'set -euo pipefail; seq 1 500000 | head -50 >/dev/null'   # exit 141
$ bash -c 'set -euo pipefail; seq 1 500000 | sed -n "1,50p" >/dev/null'  # exit 0
```

It only bites when the output exceeds the pipe buffer, so this would have published a small site perfectly well and failed on a large one — plexus-utils regenerates thousands of apidocs files. A nastier failure mode than a consistent one.

The fix uses `sed`, which reads to end of input instead of exiting early, and says how many files were omitted from the listing.

### The good news

**Nothing was published, and everything before this worked.** The step died before the commit, and the log shows the clone, the token authentication and the rsync all succeeded — the run had a fully populated `gh-pages` checkout with the new site staged. So the approach in #66 is sound; this is the last thing between it and a working publish.

Worth saying plainly: two failed runs, both mine, both found by actually running it rather than by reading it. The `dry-run` input has paid for itself twice now.

body:
## What changed
- Adds a single `ATLAS-GLOBAL-CORE` regional navigation registry instead of duplicating ATLAS by geography.
- Adds Global, North America, Central America, Caribbean, South America, Europe, Africa, Asia, Oceania, and Antarctica/Research layers.
- Adds region and country selectors directly to the ATLAS sidebar.
- Persists active regional context locally and emits `atlas:region-changed` for dynamic module adaptation.
- Keeps the full global module catalog shared by default while exposing a policy registry for future country/regulatory overrides.
- Adds the new runtime to the PWA app shell and JavaScript validation.
- Adds a structural regional-navigation validation script and architecture documentation.

## Why
ATLAS needs one global product with regional and country layers, not separate cloned applications. This establishes the resolution hierarchy `Global Core -> Region -> Country -> Organization -> User` while preserving the existing ATLAS shell and current modules.

## User impact
Users can switch ATLAS regional context from the sidebar without changing applications. Regional modules can now listen to `atlas:region-changed` and adapt currency, language, compliance, public-sector workflows, design, and integrations without creating separate navigation trees.

## Validation
- New runtime is included in `npm run check:js`.
- `npm run check:regional` verifies all required regional layers, global-core identity, runtime loading, regional event support, and PWA caching.
- Cloudflare build already copies root JavaScript assets automatically.

author: ibennet
body:
## What's the vibe

Ingredient names mentioned in a recipe's **steps** are now hover/tap targets — hover (desktop) or tap (mobile) any ingredient in a step to see its measurement in a little popover. No more scroll-back-up-to-the-ingredients-list energy while you're mid-bake.

Builds directly on the structured `{name, qty?, unit?}` ingredient shape from #19, so no schema change or content migration was needed.

## How it works

- **`src/lib/ingredients.ts`** — build-time, pure, fully tested. Builds a `name → [{measurement, group}]` index from a recipe's ingredients, then rewrites each step's HTML to wrap ingredient mentions in a popover trigger.
  - Longest-match-first (`brown sugar` beats plain `sugar`), case-insensitive, word-boundary safe (won't light up `salt` inside `salted`).
  - Singular/plural both directions (`apple` ↔ `apples`).
  - Strips leading prep adjectives so `softened butter` / `medium apples` still match `butter` / `apples`, while keeping type qualifiers (`brown`/`powdered`) distinct.
  - **Ambiguity handling:** a name measured differently across groups (e.g. `vanilla extract` = 1½ tsp in Bread layer, ½ tsp in Icing) shows **all** measurements with group labels.
  - Runs on post-markdown HTML, skipping `<a>`/`<code>` and entities so it never corrupts tags.
- **`RecipeLayout.astro`** — indexes the recipe, links each step, loads the popover script.
- **`src/scripts/ingredient-popover.ts`** — hover/focus reveal is pure CSS; this only adds tap-toggle, `Escape`, and outside-click dismissal. Degrades gracefully if JS is off.
- **`global.css`** — accent dashed underline + card popover, with dark-mode variants.

## Testing

- ✅ `npm test` — 17 Vitest unit tests (index, matching, longest-match, plurals, prep-alias, ambiguity rows, HTML/tag/entity safety).
- ✅ `npm run build` — all 18 recipes + 25 pages build clean; inspected generated HTML for `apple-bread` (duplicates → both amounts with labels) and `chocochip-cookies` (longest-match).
- ✅ `astro check` clean for the changed files (one pre-existing unrelated `KVNamespace` error in `worker/`).
- ⚠️ Live browser hover/click/keyboard/dark-mode not automated (no browser tooling in this env) — verified the CSS reveal selectors and toggle/Escape script are bundled and referenced by the recipe page. **Worth a quick manual eyeball before merge.**

author: arthefacte
body:
## Ce que le dernier rapport a révélé

`?cine=3d&sans=nu` gèle encore 14 s. Mais son rapport dit autre chose :

```
cine-embleme : 33932 ms      ← alors que le gel court de 19 954 à 33 977 ms
```

La timeline n'avance pas pendant le gel (le pas de temps est plafonné). Le jalon `t = 8,4 s` n'est donc atteint qu'à la **sortie** du gel — ce qui situe le déclencheur à **t = 8,2 s**, l'instant exact où l'opacité bascule de 0 à 1.

Or `nu` **et** `fondu` conservaient tous les deux cette bascule. **Le cas « canvas visible dès le début » n'a jamais été testé** — c'est pourtant celui de l'écran de connexion, où le même canvas tourne à 60 fps : il y est visible dès son montage, jamais réintégré après huit secondes d'invisibilité.

Second angle mort : `sans=fond,halo` ne retirait que **deux calques sur sept**. Restaient les scanlines, le balayage, les éclairs, la convergence (16 lignes de 80vmin en `mixBlendMode: screen`) et 30 particules animées avec `boxShadow`.

## Les deux variantes

| paramètre | effet |
|---|---|
| `?sans=apparition` | canvas visible d'emblée, sans transition 0 → 1 |
| `?sans=deco` | canvas seul, tout le décor retiré — test symétrique de `sans=3d` |

Aucun effet par défaut, à combiner avec `?cine=3d`.
