author: toddwbucy
body:
Closes #198 — but **do not merge until the reinstall has actually run**. The rebuild is the test.

## What this adds

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `scripts/install/hades-preserve.sh` | Run **before** the wipe. Captures what the reinstall destroys. |
| `scripts/install/hades-install.sh` | Idempotent installer. Fresh install or restore-from-preserve. |
| `docs/install/reinstall-runbook.md` | The ZFS-aware sequence, start to finish. |
| `services/systemd/arangodb3-hades.conf` | The arangod drop-in, finally in version control. |

Plus: `hades-embedder.service` / `hades-extractor.service` de-hardcoded onto `@SERVICES_DIR@`, new `make install-embedder|install-extractor|install-units`, README wired to the script, CHANGELOG entry.

## The framing that shaped it

The instinct is "install fresh, then restore the data". That is wrong here and would waste a day. `dbpool/arangodb` is mounted at `/var/lib/arangodb3`, so every database, the `hades` ArangoDB user, and every per-database ACL grant survives the wipe untouched — all of it lives inside the data directory, not in the OS.

What the wipe destroys is the **host identity** that makes the surviving data usable: the password in `/etc/hades/daemon.conf`, the systemd units, and the numeric UIDs the ZFS files are owned by. This is a restore-identity problem. The runbook is organized around that.

## Four defects this surfaced

**1. The arangod drop-in was never tracked.** Three hand-written files under `/etc/systemd/system/arangodb3.service.d/` carry the socket `chmod 770` and the `Type=`/`PIDFile=` overrides. One set `Type=` twice (`notify` then `simple`; last wins). Without them ArangoDB reports `active (running)` and every HADES command fails to connect. Consolidated into one tracked file, and added to the README prerequisites — its absence there is precisely why it went unnoticed for so long.

**2. `SupplementaryGroups=weaver-admin` makes the daemon unstartable on a clean machine.** systemd refuses to exec a unit naming a group that does not exist, and `weaver-admin` is created by WeaverTools, which will not have run yet on a fresh OS. The error does not obviously point at the group. HADES adapts rather than creating it (that group is WeaverTools' to own): the installer filters the sysusers membership line and writes a drop-in clearing the entry, then removes that drop-in on a later run once the group exists.

The container harness never caught this — the README notes it validates only the manual-daemon path, not systemd. This is exactly the class of bug a real systemd install finds.

**3. `arangodb` UID versus ZFS numeric ownership.** `/var/lib/arangodb3` is owned by 997:986. The Debian package allocates its system UID dynamically, so a rebuilt machine that lands elsewhere has a service that cannot read its own 78 GB of data. The runbook avoids this by creating the account *before* `apt-get install`; the installer detects it after the fact and offers `--arango-uid-fix adopt` (fast, moves the account) or `chown` (slow, rewrites every inode).

**4. Two units pinned to one workstation.** `hades-embedder.service` and `hades-extractor.service` hardcoded `/home/todd/olympus/HADES-Burn/services` while `hades-trainer.service` already used `@SERVICES_DIR@`. Now consistent.

## Testing so far

Both scripts were dry-run against the live workstation, which is the only place the real state exists. That caught a defect in my first cut of the installer: converging a running machine silently replaced `/etc/hades/embedder.conf` with the repo default, moving `HF_HOME` off the shared Weaver cache at `/opt/weaver/huggingface` and sending the next embedder start off to re-download the model. It now keeps any differing config as `.preserved`, reports it in a follow-ups summary, and only restarts arangod when the drop-in actually changed.

The dry run also correctly identified real drift on the current box: `/etc/hades/hades.yaml`, `embedder.conf`, and `trainer.conf` all differ from the repository, and all three legacy arangod drop-ins are flagged for removal.

Not yet tested: the restore path (`--from-preserve`), the UID reconciliation branches, and the whole runbook. Those need the actual reinstall.

## Sequence

1. Before the wipe: `sudo scripts/install/hades-preserve.sh` (with `ARANGO_ROOT_PASSWORD` set, to record grants for later comparison). Check the last line of output says `zfs` — otherwise the secrets are on the disk about to be erased.
2. Reinstall, import pools, create `arangodb` with its preserved UID before installing the package.
3. `cargo build --release`, then `sudo scripts/install/hades-install.sh --from-preserve .../latest.tar.gz --dry-run`, review, run for real.
4. Fold every manual intervention back into the script and runbook. A step that needed hands is a gap in the installer, not a fact about the machine.
5. Then merge.

author: jcfischer
body:
Implements [#582](https://github.com/the-metafactory/soma/issues/582), the containment half of [#529](https://github.com/the-metafactory/soma/issues/529), on the tree [#580](https://github.com/the-metafactory/soma/issues/580) made explicit.

## What was false

DD-16 Amendment A ungates `git-ref-exists`, `git-merged-into` and `artifact-exists` as *"argv, no shell, no egress, bounded to existence checks in a local tree"*. The last clause was false as written. `repo` and `path` are **tracker content** resolved against the runner's base cwd with no bound, so a node body could name any directory on the closing machine — and the receipt publishes the answer.

Verified live at `dfea720`, before this change:

```
artifact-exists path:"/etc/passwd"                   → pass | /etc/passwd exists
artifact-exists path:"~/.ssh/id_rsa"                 → pass | …/.ssh/id_rsa exists
git-ref-exists  ref:HEAD repo:"../../.."             → pass | HEAD → 6887d503…
git-ref-exists  ref:main repo:"/Users/fischer/.soma" → pass | main → a4ca03e4…
```

And after, at this branch's HEAD:

```
artifact-exists path:"/etc/passwd"                   → fail | probe refused — outside the probe tree …
artifact-exists path:"~/.ssh/id_rsa"                 → fail | probe refused — outside the probe tree …
git-ref-exists  ref:HEAD repo:"../../.."             → fail | probe refused — outside the probe tree …
git-ref-exists  ref:main repo:"/Users/fischer/.soma" → fail | probe refused — outside the probe tree …
artifact-exists path:"src/work-graph-probes.ts"      → pass | …/src/work-graph-probes.ts exists
git-ref-exists  ref:HEAD                             → pass | HEAD → dc9bcdf9…
```

**The premise correction:** #529 asked whether **`repo`** is bounded. It is not the only escape — `artifact-exists.path` resolves against the cwd too, so an absolute `path` escapes with **no `repo` at all**. A containment check that saw only the probe directory would have been the defect being fixed, not the fix.

## Shape

- **One predicate, before dispatch, beside `authorizeProbe`**, exhaustive with no `default` — for the reason #526 put the gate there: a probe type added later must be classified, not inherit "contained" by omission.
- **Contained** = the resolved absolute path is the stated probe tree or a descendant, by a separator-aware prefix test, so `/base-evil` is not a descendant of `/base`.
- **Both resolutions** pass through it: the probe directory, and `artifact-exists`'s `path` in the no-`atRef` branch. With `atRef` the path is a repository-relative object name for `git cat-file` and never touches the filesystem, so only the directory is contained there.
- **Escape is a failed probe** — never an exception, never a skip — so `assertClosable` refuses through the path it already owns. Same shape as a registry refusal, with its own prefix, because the two have different fixes.
- The refusal **names the resolved path and the tree**, home-collapsed: the node's literal field and the path the runner would touch are different strings (#526's `cwd` lesson).
- The **pre-flight tree read** skips uncontained directories before spawning `git status` in them — that read runs in a directory a node body names, ahead of any gate.
- **`command` and `url` stay uncontained**, deliberately: a `command`'s resolved `cwd` must already match an absolute directory the adopter declared in soma-home, and a `url` names a host and no tree. Containment on top would forbid the adopter's own deliberate act.
- Nothing reads a node's autonomy class — uniformity stays structural.

**Lexical, not `realpath`**: a symlink inside the tree pointing out of it still escapes. Resolving links would mean filesystem I/O in a predicate that runs before the runner has decided to touch anything, and would still race the probe. Recorded in the spec rather than implied away.

## Spec

`docs/work-graph.md` §2.2's gate row is rewritten to what is now true, plus a *Containment of the ungated probes* subsection. A **spec** amendment, not a DD one — DD-16 delegates mechanics to the spec and no normative clause moves (precedent: #549, #530, #579).

It carries #529's tested-negative honestly: the exemption rests on **containment**, not on a proof that `git`'s config surface is inert. Five exec-capable knobs were pointed at a marker script and none fired under the three verbs' exact argv on git 2.40.0 — a negative result on a tested set, which on this map has four times looked identical to a positive one (#557, #510, #561, #579).

## Tests

Each of the three types refused on a relative escape, on an absolute `repo`, and — for `artifact-exists` — on an absolute `path` with no `repo`; the sibling-prefix case refused; contained probes still pass, including a `repo` naming a subdirectory; the refusal is a `probed`/`fail` result and `assertClosable` refuses on it; the pre-flight never reads an uncontained tree.

`bun test` 2351 pass / 0 fail · `bunx tsc --noEmit` clean.

## Not in scope

A registry `repoRoots` list for cross-tree probes (#529 ruled it fog — no consumer, and #579 found the registry's existing worktree entries had never once been used), bounding the `observed` string (useless against a chosen-path oracle; containment removes the oracle instead), and output volume bounds (#527).

author: aeon-7
body:
The pins were the thing that rotted — both npm versions we shipped had stopped resolving — and now that operators build the images themselves, a rotted pin breaks *their* run instead of our CI. openclaw and opencode track `latest`; hermes keeps tracking the default branch. The build args still pin a version for reproducing an old result, and now they actually work.

## What makes a floating tag safe

The version is never assumed. `run_harness2.discover` runs `docker run --rm <image> --version` against the built container, and that string is disclosed as `harness_version` on the submission — so the tag floats but the result still names the exact release that produced it.

Verifying that end to end turned up four defects, three of which only bite once the tag floats:

| | defect | consequence |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `discover()` queried the version **before** anything built the image, and cached the result | first agentic run on any new machine disclosed `harness_version = null` |
| 2 | `ensure_image` passed no `--build-arg` | `AEON_OPENCLAW_VERSION` / `AEON_OPENCODE_VERSION` / `AEON_HERMES_REF` pinned nothing — the documented way to reproduce an old score did nothing |
| 3 | the version regex dropped a CalVer pre-release suffix | openclaw's *current* latest, `2026.7.1-2`, would have been recorded as `2026.7.1` — a release that didn't run |
| 4 | `ensure_image` built only when the image was **absent** | `latest` would mean "latest as of this machine's first bench", permanently |

For (4): `AEON_HARNESS_REFRESH=1` rebuilds `--no-cache --pull` — a cached layer would re-resolve to the old release and make "refresh" a no-op — and an image older than 45 days says so at the start of a run. It never rebuilds mid-run on its own; a harness change moves agentic scores, so that stays the operator's call.

## The one that proves the point

**openclaw `2026.7.1-2` requires Node ≥22.22.3, and `node:22-slim` currently ships v22.22.2.** `latest` built a perfectly good image whose CLI refused to start — which would have scored the entire openclaw harness at **zero, with no error anywhere**:

```
openclaw: Node.js >=22.22.3 <23, >=24.15.0 <25, or >=25.9.0 is required (current: v22.22.2).
```

Two fixes, the second mattering more:

1. base images → `node:24-slim` (v24.19.0), which both npm harnesses accept.
2. the smoke `RUN <cli> --version` loses its **`|| true`**. That swallowed exactly this failure. The image can no longer be built unless the harness actually starts. hermes gets the equivalent import gate.

Tracking `latest` means upstream can raise its requirements under us, so the build has to prove the thing runs. This is what the build-validation CI catches now.

## Verified

On a DGX Spark (arm64), from the shipped Dockerfiles:

- openclaw → `2026.7.1-2` (suffix intact — the regex fix)
- opencode → `1.18.15`
- hermes → `3.46.1`
- pin override → openclaw rebuilt back to `2026.6.11`

Test images removed; the rig's working images untouched.

## Known, not addressed here

`scoring.harness_board()` pools case scores across harness versions with no separation, and the Harnesses matrix labels a cell with whichever result row it saw first while showing a mean over all versions. Drifting harness versions make that visible sooner. Flagged for a separate decision — it changes ranking semantics.

body:
## Summary

- Added a reusable, structured GIMP layer-mask gateway with mask identity/state inspection, safe creation/attachment, and mask enable/disable control.
- Added bounded `isolate_subject` subject-isolation service/MCP tool. It duplicates an explicit source layer, uses border-seeded contiguous-color selection, and applies a non-destructive selection-derived mask.
- Added baseline/refined observable matte metrics, deterministic unit coverage, a deterministic live synthetic-mask check, Forge verifier wiring, and documentation of the current fallback envelope.
- Hardened `export_image` to refuse the unsafe `gimp-file-save` fallback when the tested Script-Fu bridge lacks `gimp-file-export`.

## Live benchmark

- GIMP: 3.2.0
- Script-Fu: 127.0.0.1:10009 (the repository default remains 10008)
- Image: `[Vulpes_vulpes_ssp_fulvus] (imported)`, 1280x960, fox against snow/light background
- Benchmark image ID: 5; source layer ID: 13; final working layer ID: 153; final mask ID: 154
- Source layer had no mask before the run, remained pixel-intact, and was left available beneath the selected `MCP Subject Isolation` layer. The source visibility was changed from visible to hidden only to make the isolated duplicate inspectable.
- Border evidence: 40 perimeter samples, 31 high-key, high-key ratio 0.775, mean luminance 202.789, spread 221.574. The selected policy was `all-perimeter-samples` because the high-key evidence was strong.
- Baseline: border transparency 0.9821; transparent 0.7919; opaque 0.1403; partial alpha 0.0679; coverage 0.2081; non-pathological.
- Refined/final: border transparency 0.9107; transparent 0.6380; opaque 0.3484; partial alpha 0.0136; coverage 0.3620; foreground-retention proxy relative to baseline confident samples 1.0; non-pathological; runtime about 27.9s.
- These are bounded mask observables, not ground-truth segmentation accuracy. The first visual preview showed the fox silhouette mostly retained but also exposed residual snow/branch regions and soft edge uncertainty; no claim of perfect removal is made. A contrast preview was used via a temporary PNG path during evaluation.

Native foreground extraction was probed and is unavailable through this GIMP 3.2.0 Script-Fu bridge. The current production strategy is therefore a bounded high-key/border contiguous-color fallback with conservative threshold refinement and modest feathering; it is not a general semantic segmentation solution.

## Validation

- Ruff format/check: PASS
- Unit suite: PASS, 71 passed, 5 skipped without the live endpoint
- Live integration: PASS, 5 passed with GIMP 3.2.0 at 127.0.0.1:10009
- Synthetic live mask verifier: PASS
- Forge provider checks: individual Ruff, unit, live, synthetic live-mask, and pip checks PASS when run serially against the configured endpoint.
- Joern 4.0.583: before/after CPGs captured. Post-edit focused CFG evidence covers `isolate_subject`, validation branches, try/except/finally cleanup, duplicate-layer/undo grouping, ownership validation, mask gateway calls, and the serializer/evaluate boundary. Dynamic Python dispatch and some generated Scheme strings remain unresolved by the frontend; absence of extra call-path/dataflow edges is not treated as proof of absence.
- Forge epoch: `epoch:ce8cd54dcd30520a6f8ecccf28c2553d8e2f4ae012707edff174fb2fe350f253`
- Forge candidate: UNKNOWN. The installed Forge MCP control plane is currently configured for an unrelated project and rejected this repository's paths during candidate registration; the committed repository provider and individual records remain the authoritative project-local evidence. Its aggregate state is UNKNOWN, with the known selection-policy/control-plane comparability limitation preserved.

## Security/safety

- No raw Script-Fu MCP tool, cloud processing, generated pixels, arbitrary GEGL execution, or unsafe IDs were added.
- IDs and image/layer ownership are validated; existing masks are refused rather than silently replaced; malformed pixels, non-finite values, pathological masks, and serializer injection attempts are covered.
- No original source file was overwritten. During the live benchmark, the pre-existing export path was found to use `gimp-file-save` and changed the open document's temporary file association; this was not allowed to overwrite the original JPEG, and the code now refuses that fallback. The final open document still contains the untouched source layer and masked working result.

## Roadmap

Add a supported GIMP-side foreground-extraction/trimap adapter when an environment exposes one, then compare it against this fallback on fur/snow and other difficult high-key benchmarks.

author: pierrefiorellipro
body:
## Le problème

La révision d'un mot servait **toujours la même carte** : `vocabTypeExercise` produisait invariablement `traduction FR → tape le mot en japonais`, en saisie, quel que soit le niveau de maîtrise.

Et **toujours dans le même ordre** : `buildSessionDue` finissait par `out.sort((a, b) => (a.due ?? 0) - (b.due ?? 0))`, or `allVocab()` rend les items dans l'ordre des clés IndexedDB (alphabétique) et le tri est stable — les cartes neuves, qui partagent toutes la même échéance, retombaient donc sur cet ordre. Mêmes mots, même séquence, session après session.

## Le triangle

Un mot porte trois **faces** — kanji, furigana, traduction — et se révise dans l'une des **six directions**, tirée au hasard en évitant celle du passage précédent (`app/src/lib/vocabFaces.ts`). Une face n'existe que si elle apporte quelque chose : pas de face kanji pour un mot en kana, pas de face française sans sens connu.

Le mode d'entrée suit la face demandée et la maîtrise :

| Face demandée | Mode |
|---|---|
| furigana | **QCM** tant que ce n'est pas su, **saisie** ensuite |
| kanji | **QCM** toujours — le champ convertit romaji → kana, on ne peut pas y taper de kanji |
| traduction | **QCM** toujours — les synonymes rendraient la saisie injuste |

Le seuil est un compteur de **réussites consécutives** (`VocabItem.streak`, seuil 2), pas un intervalle : lisible, et affichable plus tard. Un échec ou un « Difficile » le remet à zéro ; un élément difficile (leech) repasse au QCM même au-dessus du seuil.

Les distracteurs sont tirés sur **la même face que la réponse**, en préférant le même niveau JLPT. Sans trois distracteurs plausibles, une cible « furigana » bascule en saisie plutôt que de servir un QCM à deux options.

## L'ordre

Le tri par échéance ne sert plus qu'à **choisir** les items qui tiennent dans le plafond de session ; le deck est mélangé (`lib/random.ts`) avant d'être servi, en révision comme en bilan de leçon.

## Un seul assembleur

`buildSession` gagne un périmètre `"story"` : le Lecteur le consomme au lieu de son deck maison. Effet de bord appréciable — ses exercices ne dépendent plus du Worker pour s'afficher (la reconstruction de phrase, qui a besoin de la traduction alignée, devient best-effort).

Dans la foulée, et comme demandé, l'inventaire d'exercices se réduit : suppression du **quiz de particules**, du **QCM de compréhension** et du **drill de conjugaison** (`conjugation.ts` et `particleDistractors.ts` supprimés). Restent le triangle, l'écoute, la grammaire et la reconstruction de phrase.

> ⚠️ La piste `comprehension` est retirée **de la couche exercices seulement** — plus aucune carte servie, et le store est purgé au montage de session. Le reste du pipeline (génération LLM, podcast, sync, download) est intact : le démonter entièrement touchait 8 modules et sortait du cadre.

## Format visuel

- **Face avant** (`JpFront`) : un mot japonais isolé passe en `text-6xl`/`text-7xl` ; une face française prend la sérif latine plutôt qu'une Noto Serif JP incongrue. La consigne passe sous la face avant — celle-ci montre le contenu, jamais la question.
- **QCM en grille 2×2 de grandes tuiles** quand toutes les options sont des formes japonaises courtes ; sens français et règles de grammaire restent en liste, qu'une tuile carrée tronquerait.
- **Correction** (`WordFeedback`) : le mot en ruby, son mnémo et sa décomposition en kanji.

Au passage, un défaut d'affichage corrigé : les options de QCM passaient par `kit/Button`, dont `variant="ghost"` fixe `border-hairline-strong`/`text-text` — utilitaires de même spécificité que `border-accent-2`/`text-accent-2`, si bien que l'ordre de la feuille Tailwind décidait du gagnant et **la bonne réponse restait grise**. Les tuiles posent maintenant leurs propres couleurs d'état.

## Vérification

- `npm test` — **514 tests verts** (49 fichiers), dont `vocabFaces.test.ts` (nouveau), et les mises à jour de `exerciseBuild` / `exercise` / `reviewSession`.
- `npm run build` et `tsc --noEmit` propres.
- App pilotée en local (Vite + Playwright/Chromium) :
  - 6 sessions successives → **6 ordres distincts** ;
  - les **6 directions** sont servies, à peu près à égalité (35 à 45 tirages sur 240) ;
  - carte fraîche → QCM ; après 2 réussites, seules les cibles `*>kana` passent en saisie ;
  - une carte `猫` → « Quelle est la lecture ? » avec les options `ねこ / とり / みず / やま` en grille ;
  - correction vérifiée : ruby `水みず`, décomposition et mnémo présents, bonne réponse en `--accent-2` (`rgb(46,67,116)`) et choix erroné en `--accent` (`rgb(192,57,43)`).

## Migration

`streak` et `lastDir` sont des champs **optionnels** sur `VocabItem`, sans index : pas de bump de `DB_VERSION`, lus avec `?? 0`. Les bases existantes repartent simplement du QCM.

body:
## Summary

- Add a conservative source-level fast path that skips comment collection, comment-block construction, and parser-based candidate analysis when a file cannot contain commented-out Rstest registrations.
- Preserve the existing exact parser-based analysis for every potential candidate.
- Add regression coverage for regex, template, TSX, and JSX source contexts.

## Performance

Measured with `--timing` over all `*.test.*`, `*.spec.*`, and configured in-source test files in six Rstack repositories. Each result is the median rule time from seven runs using the same `2190a4f6` baseline. Diagnostics are identical before and after the optimization.

| Repository | Test Files | Before | After | Speedup |

author: iderex
body:
Part of #64. It does not close it; what is left is at the bottom.

The section a reader consults to find out how much of the page above is real had
gone stale, and it had gone stale in the direction that understates the plugin.
It said the HTTP endpoints and the configuration page were planned and not yet
built. Both are in the tree, read at `1b51b40`:

    git grep -nE 'Route\("Watchlist"\)|HttpGet|HttpPost|HttpDelete' \
      -- Jellyfin.Plugin.Watchlist/Api/WatchlistController.cs
    Jellyfin.Plugin.Watchlist/Api/WatchlistController.cs:44:[Route("Watchlist")]
    Jellyfin.Plugin.Watchlist/Api/WatchlistController.cs:100:    [HttpGet("Items")]
    Jellyfin.Plugin.Watchlist/Api/WatchlistController.cs:132:    [HttpPost("Items/{itemId}")]
    Jellyfin.Plugin.Watchlist/Api/WatchlistController.cs:166:    [HttpDelete("Items/{itemId}")]

    git grep -n 'IHasWebPages' -- Jellyfin.Plugin.Watchlist/Plugin.cs
    Jellyfin.Plugin.Watchlist/Plugin.cs:15:public class Plugin : BasePlugin<PluginConfiguration>, IHasWebPages

That section exists so the description above it is not read as a description of
what the code does today. A stale copy of it does that job in reverse, and the
reader it misleads is the one who came to the README to find out where the work
had got to.

## What the section says now, and what backs each part

Three endpoints, one to read a user's list and one each to put an item on it and
take an item off, pointing at `docs/api.md`. The configuration page, pointing at
`docs/settings.md`. The export format, its writer and the rule that matches an
imported entry onto this server's items, pointing at `docs/export-format.md`,
with the sentence that no endpoint carries a file out or takes one in yet, which
is the route list above: three routes and none of them an export.

The projection is not built and the section says so as the thing a user would
notice, because until it exists the list is reachable over the API and appears on
no client:

    git grep -c 'IPlaylistManager' -- Jellyfin.Plugin.Watchlist/ ; echo "exit=$?"
    exit=1

The shared list is not built either, and the section says that too, because the
opening paragraph describes one.

## Two conditions of the issue that were nearly met and are now met

The first condition asks the opening paragraph to say three things: the list is
held on the server, it appears on clients that were never modified, and it
appears as a playlist owned by the user. It said the first two. The third was a
screen lower, under `## Where the list appears`, so a reader who stopped at the
first screen did not have it. It is in the opening sentence now.

The third condition asks for one short section saying what the plugin does not
do: no external service is contacted, no client is modified, and no user's
private list is visible to anyone else. All three were in the README and no two
of them were in the same place, so somebody deciding whether to install had to
assemble the answer from three sections. They are now one section, `## What it
does not do`, and the two places that stated one of them a second time point at
that section rather than carrying their own copy, so the two cannot drift apart.

What backs the three:

    git grep -nE 'HttpClient|Socket\(|WebRequest' -- 'Jellyfin.Plugin.Watchlist/*.cs' ; echo "exit=$?"
    exit=1

    git grep -c 'CallingUser.IdOf' -- Jellyfin.Plugin.Watchlist/
    Jellyfin.Plugin.Watchlist/Api/WatchlistController.cs:3

Three endpoints, one function answering who the caller is, and no second reading
of it. The "no client is modified" half is not a grep; it is what the plugin
ships, an assembly and a configuration page, and `docs/coexistence.md` is where
the neighbouring promise is argued.

## The means

Prose in the file that already holds it. Nothing here is a new artefact, no
format and no tool is introduced, and the one thing a machine could hold about
this file, that the settings it names match the configuration class, is already
held by `SettingsDocumentTests` over `docs/settings.md` rather than over this
page. Nothing refuses a README that has gone stale again, which is the residual
this change repairs by hand and does not remove.

## The suite

    DOTNET_CLI_UI_LANGUAGE=en DOTNET_ROLL_FORWARD=LatestMajor \
      dotnet test Jellyfin.Plugin.Watchlist.sln --configuration Release
    Passed!  - Failed:     0, Passed:   238, Skipped:     0, Total:   238

Two bounds on that run, both stated rather than left to be found. It rolled
forward: the machine carries the 10.0 runtime and no 9.0 one, so it says the
suite passes and says nothing about the runtime either server line uses.

    dotnet --list-runtimes | grep 'Microsoft.NETCore.App'
    Microsoft.NETCore.App 10.0.9 [C:\Program Files\dotnet\shared\Microsoft.NETCore.App]

And no test in this suite reads `README.md`, so a green suite is not evidence
about this change at all. It is evidence that this change broke nothing, which
is the smaller claim and the only one available.

    git grep -l 'README' -- Jellyfin.Plugin.Watchlist.Tests/ ; echo "exit=$?"
    exit=1

## No second reader

There is no second reader for this change. The evidence above stands in place of
one, and it is weaker than a reader: every command in it was chosen by whoever
wrote the change, so it shows what was checked and cannot show what was not
thought of.

## What is left on #64, and why this does not close it

Three conditions, and none of them can be met from this file today.

The shared list is described as something an administrator turns on. There is no
such setting and no shared list; that set is fixed on #32.

The README names which artifact a server of each line receives. Neither artifact
has a name because neither is packaged; that is #73.

A screenshot or a walk-through of where a user finds the list on a client, taken
from a real run. There is no run to take it from, because the projection is not
built, and describing the walk from the code is the substitution that condition
was written to refuse.

author: rozzeo
body:
## Context

Profiling a static audit on a 401-file / 3.6 MB target (one MCP server with 40 tools, plus 400 ordinary Python modules — the shape of a server living inside a larger repo) showed `ast.parse` accounting for ~35% of total runtime, on files whose parse results were then thrown away.

No detection logic changed. The serialized report fingerprint is identical before and after (`d2b17e864d0fae1b`), so findings are byte-identical.

## Changes

**1. Gate on the MCP SDK signal before parsing** (`extractor.py`)

`_extract_python` computed `sdk` from a cheap regex, ran `ast.parse`, and only *then* returned `(False, [])` when the signal was absent. Both orderings return the same thing on that branch, so the gate moved ahead of the parse.

```
parse-then-gate:  0.950s   — 401 files parsed
gate-then-parse:  0.100s   — 1 file parsed        9.5x
```

**2. Split source lines once per file instead of once per tool** (`extractor.py`)

`ast.get_source_segment` re-splits the entire source on every call, making body capture O(tools × file size) — a server with dozens of tools in one module pays it repeatedly.

```
ast.get_source_segment x40 :  0.0619s
pre-split + slice          :  0.0000s        ~2165x
```

The replacement mirrors the stdlib exactly, including the two things that are easy to get wrong: the parser's line splitting ignores form feed and the Unicode line separators that `str.splitlines()` breaks on, and AST columns are UTF-8 **byte** offsets, not character offsets. Verified by differential test against `ast.get_source_segment` over **8146 nodes in 230 files** (project + stdlib), plus explicit CRLF / form-feed / Cyrillic / emoji / U+2028 cases — 0 mismatches.

**3. Stop re-encoding every file just to count bytes** (`loader.py`, `fetcher.py`)

The total-size cap called `len(text.encode("utf-8", "ignore"))` on each decoded file, copying the whole corpus for a number already reported by `stat()`, the tarball member, or the tree listing. `_read_one` now returns `(text, size)` instead of a single-entry dict, which also removes the `(key, content), = chunk.items()` unpacking at the call site.

## Result

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Audit (401 files, 3.6 MB) | 1.844s | **0.938s** (1.97x) |
| Test suite | 13.24s | **6.13s** |
| Findings | 241 | 241 (identical fingerprint) |

Test suite: 176 passed, 2 skipped. The 2 `test_acceptance.py` failures are pre-existing and unrelated — the subprocess CLI tests don't inherit `pythonpath = ["src"]` from `pyproject.toml`, so they fail with `ModuleNotFoundError` on both branches.

author: jimdc
body:
## Summary

This CI-only change keeps the local public demo-link contract blocking on pull requests while making that same sub-check advisory only for `merge_group` runs. The queue still runs the contract and records its output, but a combined-revision visibility timeout no longer ejects an otherwise-green pull request.

## Diagnosis

Five observed failed `merge_group` runs — `31274445302`, `31273307857`, `31272372561`, `31271405071`, and `31259078665` — failed inside `Accessibility + language gate (axe on every PR)` at `test/functional/20_demo_links.py`. Each failure was a Playwright `Locator.wait_for` timeout while waiting for a rendered demo state; none was an axe violation.

Performance was not the cause: the corresponding merge-group performance jobs passed. Downloaded 20-sample artifacts from successful runs measured `home.cold` wire-byte p95 values of 440478, 440868, and 440880 against a 445000 budget; LCP p95 stayed between 88 and 96.6 ms against 2500 ms, and contract settled-time p95 stayed between 764 and 769 ms against 1200 ms.

## Why this fix

The PR context remains fail-closed for the full demo-link regression contract, preserving the regression signal before queue entry. The merge-group context continues to execute the same contract but treats this environmental combined-revision failure as advisory, preventing queue ejection from a sub-check that is not a required merge rule on its own.

## Validation

- `node --test test/ci_no_prod_origin_gates.test.mjs test/ci_path_fast_path.test.mjs test/changelog_queue_checks.test.mjs`
- `make prepush`
- No product or site behavior changes.

author: shinraxtensei
body:
ENG-37 and most of ENG-38. CONTEXT.md wants this wired in **from day one**, because the risk it guards is real from the first command the pipeline runs: burning cash generating designs for niches that never sell (RSK-04, rated High/High).

## The design point: authorize *before*, record *after*

```python
with metered.metered(CostCategory.IMAGE_GENERATION, usd("0.04"), reference=asset_id):
    api.generate()          # never reached if the cap is breached
```

A ledger that only *records* has already lost the money by the time it notices. So the guard sits in front of the API call. Tested with a fake API that counts invocations — on a breached cap, `calls == 0`.

A vendor failure inside the block records nothing: a call that errored wasn't billed and shouldn't eat budget.

## Threshold behaviour, which is the whole value

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| 124 × $0.04 = $4.96 against a $5 cap | not paused |
| **125 × $0.04 = exactly $5.00** | `BudgetCapReached` + `PipelinePaused` |
| `authorize($0.01)` sitting exactly on the cap | refused |
| Late cost arriving while already paused | **no repeat alert** |

Fires at exactly the cap, not one cent past. `authorize` refuses *at* the cap — a ledger sitting on its cap has no room for the next call, however small. And the cap event fires only on the transition, so late-arriving costs can't drown the alert that mattered.

## Decisions worth reviewing

**Daily and monthly caps, both.** A daily cap alone lets a slow leak run all month; a monthly cap alone lets a runaway loop burn the month in an hour. A monthly cap *below* the daily one is rejected — that config typo would silently disable the tighter guard.

**`record` never refuses.** The money is already gone. A ledger that rejects reality is worse than one reporting an overspend.

**Etsy listing and transaction fees are not metered.** They're consequences of selling, not discretionary spend — counting them toward a generation cap would pause generation *because something sold*, which is exactly backwards.

## Two things the tests caught

`roll_to` had a dead no-op branch that looked like month handling and did nothing. Crossing a month now clears the monthly total — without it, a breached monthly cap would keep the pipeline paused **forever**.

A test asserted spending resumed after a day rollover while recording a cost still dated the previous day. The code was right and the test was wrong; it now documents the real constraint — a stale ledger undercounts the daily total, which is why `SpendLedgerRepository.current` is specified to roll forward.

## Verified

```
ruff          clean
mypy          clean (94 files, strict on domain/)
lint-imports  3 kept, 0 broken
pytest        220 passed
```

## Not done

**Persistence and the budget dashboard (ENG-39).** And the real remaining risk on ENG-38: **a paid call that never goes through `metered()`**. The guard can't catch what doesn't use it, so every new paid adapter needs checking by hand until there's an automated way to prove coverage.

This also makes **DEC-02** a measurable decision rather than a guess — per-model spend is now attributable by category and reference.

author: athrvk
body:
## Description

Every action in every collection-tree row menu stopped working when #367 landed (#403). "Run collection" and "Move to..." are simply the two most recently added, so they are the two that got noticed - Rename, Duplicate, Add Request, Add Folder and Delete were dead in the same way and for the same reason.

**Root cause.** A row renders its own ⋯ menu, and Radix renders that menu's items through a **portal**: a React child of the row whose DOM lives on `document.body`. React bubbles synthetic events through the *component* tree, not the DOM tree, so pressing a menu item arrives at the row's own `onPointerDown` - which #367 added. That handler starts a press and calls `setPointerCapture` on the row, and the capture retargets the `pointerup` the menu item was waiting for. The item never activates.

Nothing looks broken while it happens: the menu opens, the item highlights, the menu closes on dismissal. Only the action is missing.

**The fix.** `closest("[data-tree-menu]")`, which already excluded the trigger, cannot catch this - portalled content is not inside the trigger it belongs to. DOM containment is exactly the distinction between "this row's own box" and "this row's portalled child", so `currentTarget.contains(target)` now guards every pointer handler a row spreads. The click-capture takes the same guard: a suppression left armed by a finished drag would otherwise swallow the very menu action the user chose next.

**The alternative I rejected** was stopping propagation inside `RowActionsMenu`. It fixes the symptom for this one menu and leaves the trap set for the next portal a row ever contains (a tooltip, a popover, a context menu), and it puts the knowledge in the shared primitive rather than in the handler that actually has the constraint.

## Type of Change
- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Breaking change
- [x] Documentation update

## Testing

`cd app && pnpm test && pnpm type-check && pnpm lint && pnpm format:check` - **343 files, 3265 tests, all passing** (137s). One new test; the baseline was 3264. `mkdocs build --strict -f .github/mkdocs.yml` passes. No engine files touched, so no engine run.

**Why the existing suite was green through all of this.** Both the runner's tests and the drag tests activate a menu item with `fireEvent.click(item)`, which dispatches a click straight at the item - and jsdom does not retarget captured pointer events, so the capture that breaks the real browser is invisible to that style of test. The regression test therefore presses a real menu item and asserts **the row did not capture the pointer**, which is the mechanism itself rather than a proxy for it:

| Mutation | Reddens |
|---|---|
| remove the containment guard from the press (i.e. restore the bug) | 1 - the new test, and only it |

Verified by actually reverting the guard and re-running, not by inspection.

Verification is by mechanism plus that test, **not** by driving the packaged app: the repo has no e2e harness and I did not stand one up for this. The chain being asserted - portalled press reaches the row, row captures the pointer, capture eats the item's `pointerup` - is the whole of the defect, and the guard is what breaks it.

## Checklist
- [x] My code follows the style guidelines
- [x] I have performed a self-review
- [x] I have added tests (if applicable)
- [x] I have updated documentation

## Related Issues

Regression from #367 (PR #403). No issue was filed - this was reported directly.

Docs: `docs/design-system.md`'s collection-tree section gains the rule, since any future pointer handler on those rows walks into the same trap.

author: kyzcreig
body:
Two independent defects in `hermes_cli/kanban_db.py`. Both fired in one incident chain on 2026-08-08: a worker's repro escaped its sandbox and wrote 6 cards to a live board, the dispatcher correctly picked one up and spawned a real Opus worker against it, and the cleanup hard-deleted that card mid-run.

## Defect 1 — `delete_task()` had no live-claim guard

`delete_task()` deleted a `running` task holding a live `worker_pid` exactly as readily as a `todo` one, and cascaded away `task_runs` + `task_events` — the only record the run ever existed. Grepping the old function body for `status` / `claim_lock` / `worker_pid` / `current_run_id` / `running` returned zero matches.

Reachable unguarded from the UI at `plugins/kanban/dashboard/plugin_api.py` `DELETE /tasks/{task_id}`. **One dashboard click on a running card amputated that worker.**

Observed downstream, in order, from the real incident:

- `kanban_show()` → `task <id> not found`
- `kanban_heartbeat` → `could not heartbeat <id> (unknown id or not running)`
- `kanban_comment` → `kanban_comment: unknown task <id>`
- the worker process **kept running for 9+ minutes**, burning tokens against a card that no longer existed, and exited with no terminal state — there was no row left to write one to.

**Fix.** `delete_task(conn, id)` now raises `TaskRunningError` when `status='running'` and `worker_pid` is alive, unless `force=True`. Deliberately distinct from the existing "not found → `False`" return: those are different conditions and must not look alike. The liveness check runs *inside* the write transaction so a concurrent claim cannot slip between check and delete. The guard keys on a **live** pid, so a crashed worker's stale claim stays deletable without `force`. The dashboard maps the refusal to **409** and accepts `?force=true`.

## Defect 2 — `HERMES_KANBAN_DB` defeats `HERMES_HOME` sandboxing

`kanban_db_path()` checks `HERMES_KANBAN_DB` before anything `HERMES_HOME`-derived, and the dispatcher pins that var into every worker env on purpose (defense in depth). Correct for board work; live ammunition for a worker writing tests against kanban internals. The standard hermeticity move — `HERMES_HOME=$(mktemp -d)` — yields false confidence while writing production rows. The docstring advertised the override purely as a safety feature and never mentioned the edge.

**Fix.** `HERMES_KANBAN_SANDBOX=1` neutralises every `HERMES_KANBAN_*` path pin (`DB`, `HOME`, `WORKSPACES_ROOT`, `ATTACHMENTS_ROOT`), so all kanban paths resolve from `HERMES_HOME`. All five read sites route through one `_kanban_path_override()` choke point, so the flag cannot be honoured by some resolvers and silently ignored by others; a test asserts every var in the declared pin list is actually neutralised, which fails if a future pin is added without routing.

Chose the flag over docs-only because the incident's proximate cause was a *correct-looking* sandbox producing production writes — the only pre-existing remedy was a non-obvious, undocumented `os.environ.pop` loop. Default resolution is unchanged (the override still wins), so this is additive for every existing caller. Both escapes are now documented in the module docstring and in `kanban_db_path()`.

Also: an override that resolves outside the `HERMES_HOME`-derived kanban root now logs a warning **once** — the resolution is unchanged, but the escape is no longer silent. The check memoizes on the raw env strings because `kanban_db_path()` is on the `connect()` path.

## Verification

Suite from the incident report's verify command, run with the kanban env stripped and a scratch home:

```
env -u HERMES_KANBAN_DB -u HERMES_KANBAN_TASK -u HERMES_KANBAN_BOARD \
    -u HERMES_KANBAN_RUN_ID -u HERMES_KANBAN_WORKSPACE -u HERMES_KANBAN_WORKSPACES_ROOT \
    -u HERMES_KANBAN_CLAIM_LOCK HERMES_HOME=$(mktemp -d) \
    venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_db.py \
        tests/plugins/test_kanban_dashboard_plugin.py -q

389 passed, 8 warnings in 39.13s   (exit 0)
```

Plus 8 neighbouring kanban suites (`test_kanban_boards`, `test_kanban_cli`, `test_kanban_core_functionality`, `test_pin_kanban_board_env`, `test_kanban_worker_hermeticity_anchor`, `test_kanban_worktree_isolation`, `tools/test_kanban_tools`, `tools/test_delegate_kanban_isolation`): **436 passed, 1 skipped**.

**RED-proof.** With only the two impl files stashed and the tests kept, **9 of the 11 new tests FAIL**, including the dashboard arm asserting `assert 200 == 409`. The 2 that pass are deliberate controls: dead-pid-still-deletable, and the `force=True` path.

**Live-board tripwire.** `select count(*) from tasks` on the real `ban-forensics` board read **107 before and after every test run** in this session.

**Incident A/B reproduced**, resolve-only then for real:

```
case A: worker env + HERMES_HOME=<scratch>, no flag
  resolved -> .../boards/ban-forensics/kanban.db     LIVE BOARD (now with a warning)
case B: same + HERMES_KANBAN_SANDBOX=1
  resolved -> <scratch>/kanban.db                    SANDBOXED
  (init_db + create_task run for real; the live path is never created)
case PROD: untouched dispatched-worker env
  resolved -> .../boards/ban-forensics/kanban.db     no warning (override is inside the root)
```

**Perf.** `kanban_db_path()` is on the `connect()` path: 1.4 µs baseline → 58.4 µs unmemoized → **3.2 µs** after memoizing the escape check. The pid probe only runs for `running` rows, so deleting a non-running task stays at 0.5 ms.

## Notes for review

- `tests/conftest.py` gains `HERMES_KANBAN_SANDBOX` to the existing kanban strip list — a developer shell exporting it would otherwise silently flip path-resolution tests.
- The dashboard frontend (`dist/index.js`) already surfaces errors via `.catch(...) → setError(...)`, so the 409 detail renders without a bundle change. A dedicated "archive instead?" affordance would be a follow-up, not this diff.
- Considered and rejected for scope: making the dashboard `DELETE` a soft-delete/archive by default. `archive_task` already exists and is the better UI verb, but flipping the endpoint's semantics is a behavior change beyond the guard this card asks for.

author: mrhegemon
body:
A polish pass on the film the fleet review called *"the only film that is unambiguously an
argument rather than a tour, and the shortest"*. Two narration/copy lines and one alt string.
The arc, the focus moves and the degradation beat are untouched.

## The film did not need a cold open

The brief for this pass expected the concrete moment of pain to be missing before the question
lands. It is not missing — [`02fc11c`](https://github.com/companionintelligence/JustInCase/commit/02fc11c)
already moved it into the intro's narration, so the first nine words of the film are:

> There is no signal. How long do you boil creek water?

That is the pain, told concretely, spoken before the product is named. What the pattern asks for
is a sequence of ideas, and 4.5 seconds is short enough to carry *pain, then name* inside one
card — the voice lands first, the eye lands on the title second.

Giving it its own card would buy ordering, not information, and would cost 4–5s of screenless
picture in a 51s film whose brevity is the asset. Three concrete reasons not to:

1. **No camera.** This pipeline shoots product screens through Playwright and nothing else, so a
   cold open here could only be type.
2. **`split` is not the instrument.** It lays out two real captures side by side and the build
   refuses a `split` scene with no shots — it is the fix for view-enumeration (the review's
   finding 6), not a typographic card.
3. **Screenless scenes are where frozen picture lives** (AUTHORING.md). Adding a type card pushes
   the frozen fraction up against a <8% bar on a fleet currently at 24/24, in exchange for a beat
   the film already delivers.

## What changed

### `recap` — the "what stays yours" beat, sharpened in place

Three of its four chips already were about what stays yours. The fourth named a mechanism rather
than a stake, and was the only one a viewer could not check against anything the film had shown:

| | was | now |
|---|---|---|
| chip 3 | `Retrieval · Hybrid search` | `Data leaves home · Never` |

That is MESSAGING.md's sanctioned **"ownership tally"** shape for a closing `feature` scene.

**It is a claim, so it was verified rather than assumed** — the fleet review caught this exact
chip being false on Spellbook, whose published image bakes a Sentry DSN. For this repo:

- `CMakeLists.txt:125` — `option(JIC_SENTRY ... OFF)`
- `Dockerfile:28` — `ARG JIC_SENTRY=0`, and in that state it *"downloads nothing, links nothing,
  and produces binaries with no Sentry code in them at all"*
- `.github/workflows/docker-publish.yml` — passes **no** `build-args`

So the published image is the no-Sentry build, and the DSN is never baked in. An `_itemsNote` in
the storyboard records this and says what to re-check if `docker-publish.yml` ever grows a
`build-args:` block — it is the one line in this film a build-system change can silently falsify.

### `recap` narration — re-cut, and transcribed to prove it

The old line opened with its own caption read aloud, verbatim, while that caption was on screen.

```
was:  One Docker stack. No accounts, no cloud. It keeps working when the network does not.
now:  Your documents, your questions, your answers. It keeps working when the network does not.
```

The three nouns are the film's own arc in the order the film showed it — the shelf, the typed
question, the cited answer — so the recap recaps something the viewer watched instead of
introducing a fourth claim in the last six seconds.

`narrate --stale` re-recorded `recap.mp3` and nothing else (1 generated, 9 already present).
**whisper base.en transcribes the new file back word for word.** edge-tts exits 0 while writing
silence, so the mp3's hash changing is not evidence that it speaks.

### `question-typed` alt — a count that was never true of both plates

The alt claimed *"the six suggested-question chips"*. The app renders six at desktop width and
three at portrait (`.chip-extra { display: none }` under 620px), and this one string is read
against both. Confirmed three in the 9:16 cut. The count is gone rather than corrected, because
no single number is true of both.

No re-capture: alt is composition-level and no shot changed.

## What was deliberately left alone

- **The intro.** Re-authored one commit ago; re-cutting it again would be churn.
- **`ask-a-question` / `check-the-sources`** — the 0:30–0:36 focus moves the review called *"the
  shot every other film should be copying"*. Verified still intact at full resolution: three
  filenames and their matched passages, legible.
- **`no-model-no-panic`** — the degradation beat, the most credible seconds in the fleet.
- **The `cut` transition** into `check-the-sources` and its `_transitionNote` reasoning.
- **Scene count and chapter structure** — 10 scenes, three chapters, unchanged.
- **The notch inset and caption plate** — real defects, but kit-level and fleet-wide (ranked
  backlog items 1 and 5). Out of scope for one film's polish pass, and touching them here would
  risk the 24/24.

## Verification

- kit **0.13.1**, asserted from a fresh CI-Common worktree (`origin/main` @ `8b64629`). Note the
  brief said 0.13.0 — 0.13.1 is 0.13.0 plus the thenable-`eval` fix and is what `origin/main`
  carries.
- Rendered on core-1 via `render-on.sh --ref just-in-case=video/cold-open-and-keep`;
  `RENDERED-FROM.txt` stamps `origin/video/cold-open-and-keep @ dd27179c6`.
- Contact sheets read for both formats, and the before/after landscape sheets differenced:
  amplified 12×, the only non-zero pixels are the chip-3 position in the two recap frames.
  Nothing else in the film moved.

### Scored — `score-videos`, kit 0.13.1

```
product                cut        dur   LUFS    dBTP   dead    worst   frozen  verdict
just-in-case           landscape  50    -14     -2.6   2.8%    0.50s   0%      pass
just-in-case           portrait   50    -14     -2.6   2.8%    0.50s   4%      pass

24/24 cuts pass the bar
bar: -14.5..-13.5 LUFS · <=-0.9 dBTP · <6% dead air · no gap >1.5s · <8% frozen · 45-105s · 0 slates
```

Every clause with margin, and the film is **0.3s shorter** than before (50.65s → 50.35s) — still
the shortest in the fleet by seven seconds. The fleet stays at 24/24.

author: tigerblue77
body:
Closes #289. **The bug is live on `master`** and the suite is green while it happens.

## Problem

#167 (merged as #175) gave a profile whose `ipmitool` call was refused a `(not applied)` suffix, so the table stops naming a profile the server is not running. That makes the string longer than the column reserved for it, and `printf`'s `%*s` (`functions.sh:1398`) pads without truncating:

| string | length | column |
|---|---|---|
| `Dell default dynamic fan control profile (not applied)` | **54** | 40 |
| `User static fan control profile (100%) (not applied)` | **52** | 40 |
| `User static fan control profile (5%) (not applied)` | **50** | 40 |

Two consecutive rows of the same table, before this change:

```
08-08-2026 20:45:38   22°C   39°C   38°C     28°C      User static fan control profile (5%)                                              Enabled   -
08-08-2026 20:45:38   22°C   39°C   38°C     28°C  Dell default dynamic fan control profile (not applied)                                              Enabled  CPU temperature is too high
```

The `Enabled` of the second row lands **14 characters** right of the first's — exactly `54 - 40`. It is #170's misalignment, on the one row reporting that the safety profile could not be applied.

Monitoring only mode is unaffected: the apply functions return before touching `ipmitool` (`functions.sh:5-7`, `29-31`), so that mode only produces the `(monitoring only, not applied)` badge, which its 71-wide column fits exactly.

## Change

**`constants.sh`** — `FAN_CONTROL_PROFILE_COLUMN_WIDTH` 40 → **54**, with the reason recorded next to it.

**`tests/cases/60_cpu_topologies.sh`** — the guard now derives both forms per mode instead of appending a suffix only in monitoring only mode:

```bash
if [ "$IS_MONITORING_ONLY_MODE" == "true" ]; then
  VARIANTS=("$PROFILE$MONITORING_ONLY_MODE_BADGE")
else
  VARIANTS=("$PROFILE" "$PROFILE$NOT_APPLIED_BADGE")
fi
```

This is the part that matters beyond the number. `test_no_fan_control_profile_can_outgrow_the_column_reserved_for_it` was written for #170 and its comment claims to walk "every profile the code can actually produce", but it built its list by hand and never constructed the normal-mode `(not applied)` forms — so the strings it measured were not the strings `functions.sh` assigns. The guard passed, and the overflow shipped.

The four golden headers move with the width. The integration assertion that pinned the gap between the exhaust column and the profile (`90_integration.sh:105`) is now matched rather than compared, that gap being the width guard's business rather than that test's.

## Verification

The new guard fails on the old width, which is what makes it a guard rather than a restatement of the constant:

```
$ sed -i 's/=54$/=40/' constants.sh && ./tests/run_tests.sh --filter test_no_fan_control_profile_can_outgrow_the_column_reserved_for_it
  fail no fan control profile can outgrow the column reserved for it
       MONITORING_ONLY_MODE=false : "Dell default dynamic fan control profile (not applied)" (54) must fit in 40
       MONITORING_ONLY_MODE=false : "User static fan control profile (1%) (not applied)" (50) must fit in 40
       ...
```

And the rows line up after the change — measured, both `Enabled` cells at the same offset.

Full suite with `master` (61b5cda) merged in, no conflict: **318 test cases passed (1799 assertions)**, against 1793 on `master` — same case count, six more assertions, being the `(not applied)` variants the guard now walks.

#2163 landed with the submodules pinned to the branches it was developed against. Those have since been merged, and **rebased in the merging**, so the commits master records don't exist on `libossia/master` or `avendish/main` — they exist only on the source branches.

```
score master records          on upstream master?
  libossia  b167d39b7           NO  (only on fix/backwards-playback-dataflow)
  avendish  948d21d25           NO  (only on fix/quantification-backwards)
```

It resolves today **only because those branches still exist**. Delete either and a fresh clone of score can no longer check out its submodules.

```
libossia  b167d39b7 -> cdeb2619e   build: version Boost.Asio's global symbols on Windows
avendish  948d21d25 -> cb3d29191   halp: one quantification grid, walked once

I checked rather than assumed — the trees are *not* byte-identical, but the entire difference is `.github/workflows/*`, which upstream changed while the branches were open:

git diff b167d39b7 cdeb2619e -- . ':(exclude).github'   # empty
git diff 948d21d25 cb3d29191 -- . ':(exclude).github'   # empty
```

So no source change, and score stops pinning both projects to their pre-merge CI as a side benefit.

## Summary

This PR introduces the new **Explore the Library** experience for Just A Thought and establishes a clearer discovery path beyond chronological browsing.

The goal is to make it easier for readers to enter the library by theme, move into longer reading paths, or search for a specific idea without treating the site like a traditional date-first blog archive.

## What Changed

- Added a new `/explore/` landing page titled **Explore the Library**
- Added **Explore** to the primary navigation
- Simplified the primary nav by removing separate top-level links for Posts and Series

  - Faith

  - Leadership
  - Technology
  - Culture
  - Creation
- Reused the existing collection hero images and icon system for visual continuity
- Added automatic reflection counts for each collection
- Added a **Go Deeper** pathway into Series
- Made the featured Series image dynamic based on the most recently published reflection that belongs to a series
- Added compact pathways for:
  - Search the Library
  - Browse All Reflections
- Added dedicated responsive and dark-mode styling for the Explore page
- Updated the Jekyll workflow so `explore-library-v1` validates automatically on push

## Reader Experience

This creates a clearer discovery hierarchy:

**Explore → Collection → Series / Reading Path → Reflection**

Readers can still browse the full chronological archive, but the new Explore experience makes topic-driven discovery the more intentional entry point.

## Design Intent

The page follows the existing Just A Thought visual system:

- warm editorial layout
- restrained use of imagery
- consistent collection icons
- responsive cards
- dark-mode support
- compact secondary pathways rather than oversized utility sections

- Responsive behavior checked during development
- Jekyll validation workflow enabled for this branch

## Next Phase

After this PR is merged, the next planned discovery feature is **Related Reflections**, which will use series, collections, and tags to help readers move naturally from one article to another.

author: cscheid
body:
## Summary

Interim support for Q1's dual-theme map form, `format.html.theme: {light: [...], dark: [...]}` (bd-o76p01wb, discovered from #474's Connect-docs testbed work): the map now **parses**, only the **`light:` half is applied**, and a new **Q-14-3 warning** marks the ignored `dark:` entry — anchored at the `dark:` key with an ariadne span, coalesced across documents sharing the offending config. Previously every document using this form hard-failed with Q-14-1; on the Connect docs testbed that was all 351 files. Full dual-theme support (compile both CSS variants + toggle wiring) remains tracked separately (bd-0pic6).

Plan with design decisions and phase-by-phase evidence: `claude-notes/plans/2026-08-08-theme-light-dark-interim.md`.

## Design

- **quarto-sass** parses the pair: `ThemeConfig::from_config_value` recognizes a non-empty map whose keys are only `light`/`dark` (mirroring `extract_brand_ref`'s brand-pair precedent in the same file). The light half runs through a shared `from_theme_value` helper (null / `none` sentinel / string / array), so `{light: none}` suppresses Bootstrap, unknown names still raise Q-14-2, and nested maps stay Q-14-1. A `dark`-only map renders default Bootstrap. Maps with extra keys keep the Q-14-1 error (message now names the accepted shapes).
- **Warning carried as data, emitted by the stage**: quarto-sass stays diagnostics-free — the ignored `dark:` key's `SourceInfo` rides on the new `ThemeConfig::dark_theme_ignored` field, and `CompileThemeCssStage` converts it into the Q-14-3 warning via `ctx.add_diagnostic` (once per document; not emitted by `BootstrapJsStage`, which parses the same config). A light-only map is a fully-honored spelling and does not warn.
- **Latent bug fixed for free**: `BootstrapJsStage` treated the map form's parse failure as `suppress_bootstrap`, silently shipping themed CSS without Bootstrap JS.
- `highlight-style: {light, dark}` needs no interim work — Q2 currently has no `highlight-style` reader (tree-sitter highlighting), so the map passes through inert. Wiring it up belongs to the full-support strand.

## Test plan

- TDD: 11 quarto-sass unit tests, 2 stage tests (`compile_theme_css`, `bootstrap_js`), Q-14-3 catalog registration, and 3 integration tests driving the real `render_to_file` path — all written first and observed failing.
- Full workspace suite: 11,135 passed. Full `cargo xtask verify` (including hub-client/WASM leg): green, re-run after rebasing onto post-#474 `main`.

## Real-world verification

- Minimal fixture through `q2 render`: exit 0; `Warning: [Q-14-3]` with a span pointing at the `dark:` key in `_quarto.yml`; compiled CSS contains the light marker rule and no dark rule. Output inspected directly.
- Connect docs testbed with the posit-docs extension's theme map **unflattened**: **351/351 files render, exit 0**, Q-14-3 printed exactly once ("Affected files: … (and 348 others)"), light theme (Open Sans / posit orange) in the site CSS, dark-only background absent. (quarto-openapi's contributed pre-render was temporarily neutralized — its Deno-style `.ts` failing under Node is the separate bd-wch2dotq gap.)

Noted for follow-up (in the plan, not blocking): the Q-14-3 warning renders span-less when the offending map lives in an extension's `_extension.yml` (print-time source repair only covers `_quarto.yml`), and quarto-openapi's manifest uses `contributes: format:` (singular), which Q2's manifest validator rejects — possibly relevant to bd-of20unsb.

author: toddawhittaker
body:
## The defect

`doCopy` set "Copied!" on success and had **no `else`** — and the inline Copy SQL handler had the identical shape. Both `copyText` and `copyHtml` **swallow** their errors and return `false` (a denied clipboard permission, an insecure context, or the `execCommand` fallback refusing), so a failure was indistinguishable from success: no toast, no state change, the trigger still reading "Copy".

The user believes the answer is on their clipboard, and pastes something else.

**Two call sites, not one.** A fix applied only to `doCopy` would have left Copy SQL silent, so each has its own test.

## The wording

> Couldn't copy to the clipboard. Select the text and copy it manually.

It names the escape hatch rather than guessing at a cause, because the cause is genuinely unknown at the call site — both helpers have already discarded it. Lives in `announce.js` next to `DELETE_FAILED`.

`CopyMenu.jsx` is untouched: the outcome is known in `doCopy`, and threading a promise back into the ARIA menu button would add a state machine for nothing.

## The test blocks both clipboard routes

That is the part that matters. `copyText` falls through from `navigator.clipboard` to a `document.execCommand` fallback, so stubbing only the first would still succeed and the test would prove nothing.

Verified by removing both `else` branches: two red, failing on the toast's error class.

## Verification

- Full local gate green: 366 Playwright specs (up from 364).
- `frontend/types/` regenerated for the new export — the derived-contract guard caught it before CI did.

author: arasz
body:
## Defect

Issue #200: an old binary opening a bank a *newer* binary already migrated to schema v2
silently no-oped past `EnsureAsync`'s version check (`storedVersion >= CurrentVersion`
covered both "current" and "ahead") and went on to write through write paths that
predate WP3's chunk-column recompute. That is how the live-bank drift happened: 193 rows
across ~10 `source_file` groups left with `chunk_index`/`total_chunks` at their `0/0`
defaults, written 21:29-22:28 CEST on 2026-08-08 by 1.2.0-era stdio servers after the bank
had already migrated to v2.

## Two changes

1. **Forward-version write guard.** `MemorySchema.EnsureAsync` now throws
   `UnsupportedSchemaVersionException` (new, `AiRaccoon.Core.Memory`) when
   `storedVersion > CurrentVersion`, naming both versions:
   `"bank schema v{stored} is newer than this binary supports (v{current}); update ai-raccoon"`.
   **Guard-surface choice**: `EnsureAsync` is invoked from exactly one place —
   `SqliteConnectionFactory.InitializeAsync`, called by both bank-opening paths
   (`OpenBankWithResolvedKeyAsync`, `OpenBankWithKeyAsync`), both opened
   `ReadWriteCreate`. The codebase has no separate read-only open that reaches
   `EnsureAsync` — the one place `SqliteConnectionFactory` opens read-only
   (`MigrateLegacyKeyAsync`'s current-key probe) explicitly never calls `InitializeAsync`,
   by comment and by an existing test
   (`SqliteConnectionFactoryEncryptionTests:251,275`). So guarding in `EnsureAsync` itself
   *is* guarding every writer — there is no narrower surface to pick.

2. **v3 ladder step.** `CurrentVersion` 2 → 3. The new hard step (`MigrateToV3Async`, same
   `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` / rethrow pattern as `MigrateToV2Async`) reuses
   `MemorySql.RecomputeChunkColumnsBankWide` — already a shared `internal` constant used by
   both `SyncService.MergeRemoteAsync` and the v2 migration backfill, so no SQL duplication
   was needed. This deterministically heals any bank written during the mixed-version
   window described in #200.

## Red evidence

Both new checks were watched failing before the fix, on this commit's test additions to
`MemorySchemaVersionTests.cs`:

- `EnsureAsync_WhenStoredVersionIsAheadOfCurrent_ThrowsNamingBothVersions` — before the
  guard, `EnsureAsync` no-oped silently (`storedVersion >= CurrentVersion`); the test failed
  with "should throw UnsupportedSchemaVersionException but did not".
- `EnsureAsync_OnAV2Bank_WithDriftedChunkColumns_HealsThemBankWide` — before the v3 step,
  a v2 bank with a drifted 3-chunk group stayed at `[(h1,0,0),(h2,0,0),(h3,0,0)]` instead of
  `[(h1,0,3),(h2,1,3),(h3,2,3)]`.

Also added: `EnsureAsync_OnAStampedV3Bank_SkipsTheRecomputeStep` (idempotence — a second
`EnsureAsync` on a stamped v3 bank does not re-run the recompute) and
`EnsureAsync_OnAV1Bank_RunsTheFullLadderThroughV3` (full v1→v3 ladder, reusing the existing
`SeedV1BankAsync` harness).

## Gates

- `dotnet test --filter "Speed=Fast"` — 1328/1328 pass (excluding
  `VersionContractTests`, which was already broken on `origin/main` before this branch:
  the `chore(release): bump version to 1.3.1` commit bumped `PackageVersion` only, leaving
  `InformationalVersion`/`AssemblyVersion` at 1.3.0 against the test's hardcoded
  `"1.3.0"` expectation — pre-existing, unrelated to this change, not touched here).
- `dotnet test --filter "Speed=Slow"` — 331/331 pass.
- `dotnet test --filter "Category=Retrieval"` — 41/41 pass.
- Golden files byte-identical:
  `reference-topk.json` = `34b0c0a7ed42dd59fdff525930c1f50d9e09d80e`,
  `manifest.json` = `e9a583dd1b3b7a4ee72ba9410596a3e9f40ce94e`.

## Test plan

- [x] Red test for the write guard, watched failing, now green
- [x] Red test for the v3 recompute, watched failing, now green
- [x] Idempotence test at v3
- [x] Full v1→v3 ladder test
- [x] `Speed=Fast` / `Speed=Slow` / `Category=Retrieval` all green
- [x] Golden files unchanged

author: maildej
body:
Notes only — no website changes.

## The change

An attorney no longer has an office in this database. The office is recorded on the case, and only there.

This replaced a usual-office-plus-per-case-override arrangement that carried a real hazard: someone looking at one case could click through to the attorney, see the office sitting there editable, correct it, and silently rewrite that attorney's office on every other case they had.

Recording it per case removes the hazard rather than warning about it, and is truer to the work — panel attorneys sit on several counties' panels, so "their office" was never a single fact. The override existed precisely because the underlying claim was false. Three fields go, one arrives.

All 44 cases were backfilled from the attorneys' affiliations before anything was dropped.

## Corrections and limits recorded

- **The three cases carrying two offices are not an error.** Each has two attorneys from two different offices, correctly recorded. An earlier note wrongly described them as attorneys with two affiliations.
- They do expose the model's one limitation: the office attaches to the case rather than to the attorney-on-the-case, so co-counsel from different offices cannot be told apart. Acceptable — co-counsel are in practice always from the same organisation, and doing it properly would need a junction table for a situation that does not arise.
- **Seeding the office from the intake form is not worth doing yet.** The intake collects affiliation as free text against a linked target, so matching would fail silently or mis-match; and case creation is manual anyway, so a person is already there. The useful first step is making the intake field a picker.
- **A rollup's aggregation formula cannot be updated** through the API, and fields cannot be deleted — so a rollup's aggregation is effectively fixed once created.

author: ripnrip
body:
## Summary

Three fixes that unshackle non-Claude agents from hook-layer bugs that prevented SessionStart context injection and memory persistence.

### BIN-256: Remove version-check.js gate from Codex SessionStart (Critical)
**Was:** `codex-hooks.json` ran `version-check.js` BEFORE the context hook. When `.install-version` mismatched (happened after every marketplace `autoUpdate`), it emitted an upgrade hint to stdout and `exit(0)` — **the real context hook never ran**. Codex users got "run `npx claude-mem install`" instead of memory observations after every update.

**Fix:** Removed the version-check gate entirely. The context hook now always runs directly, matching Claude Code's pattern (which has no such gate).

### BIN-257: Add worker start hook to Codex SessionStart (High)
**Was:** Claude Code has TWO SessionStart hooks: `start` (bootstraps worker daemon) + `context` (injects memory). Codex only had `context`, which had to lazy-spawn the worker AND inject memory within its 60s timeout. On cold boot, worker spawn + Chroma warming (~7s) frequently exceeded the timeout → soft-fail to empty context.

**Fix:** Added a dedicated `worker-service.cjs start` hook as the FIRST Codex SessionStart hook, matching Claude Code's dual-hook pattern. The worker is now guaranteed running before the context hook fires.

### BIN-258: Fix Cursor adapter discarding all context (Critical)
**Was:** `cursorAdapter.formatOutput()` returned only `{ continue: true }`, stripping ALL `hookSpecificOutput` and `systemMessage`. Even when the context handler produced rich observations, Cursor never saw them. Context injection relied entirely on a file-based `.cursor/rules` mechanism.

**Fix:** `formatOutput()` now passes through `hookSpecificOutput`, `systemMessage`, and `suppressOutput` — same as the Claude Code and Codex adapters.

## Test plan
- [x] `bun test tests/cli/cursor-adapter.test.ts` — **5 pass, 0 fail**
- [x] Validated `codex-hooks.json` is valid JSON with proper dual-hook SessionStart structure
- [ ] Manual: fresh Codex session → SessionStart fires → context injected → marker recalled in session B
- [ ] Manual: fresh Cursor session → SessionStart context appears in model context

## Linear
- [BIN-256](https://linear.app/binary-bros/issue/BIN-256/fix-codex-sessionstart-suppressed-by-version-checkjs-gate)
- [BIN-257](https://linear.app/binary-bros/issue/BIN-257/fix-codex-missing-worker-start-sessionstart-hook-cold-boot-race)
- [BIN-258](https://linear.app/binary-bros/issue/BIN-258/fix-cursor-adapter-discards-all-sessionstart-context)

author: heke99
body:
Remediation of the 2026-08-06 system consistency audit, plus every production bug found while verifying it.

**Test state:** unit 6175/6175 (main: 53 failing across 10 files) · pg-real 640/640 (was 509) · typecheck, lint, guards, build green.

Note: no workflow in this repository has ever run — all six report zero runs. This PR is the first CI execution, so there is no prior green baseline for `main`.

## Security findings (all four verified by exploit, then fixed)

**#17 — cross-tenant data leak through views.** A PostgreSQL view runs with its *owner's* privileges unless created `security_invoker = true`. Four superuser-owned views carried no tenant predicate and were granted SELECT to `authenticated`. Measured as an ordinary member of one company:

| View | Foreign rows visible |
|---|---:|
| `customer_ar_balances` | 388 (all of them) |
| `company_commercial_usage_v` | 4 433 |
| `company_effective_commercial_limits_v` | 22 165 |
| `agency_commercial_usage_v` | 104 |

`customer_ar_balances` exposes customer ids and outstanding receivables per company — every tenant's order book, readable by every other tenant. Fixed in `20260808150000`; three other definer views are kept deliberately, each for a checked reason (own tenant filter, public catalogue, service-role only).

**#18 — `commit_journal_entry` had no authorization.** SECURITY DEFINER, EXECUTE granted via PostgreSQL's implicit PUBLIC grant, and `auth.uid()` used only as an attribution fallback. An authenticated member of *any* company could post another company's draft voucher. Posted entries are immutable by law (BFL 7 kap), so the victim can only storno it — both vouchers stay in their ledger permanently. The same call as `anon` also reached voucher-number assignment, stopped one statement later only by an unrelated table grant, which is an accident rather than a control. Fixed in `20260808160000`.

**#19 — 147 write policies authorized on read-level membership.** `company_id IN (SELECT user_company_ids())` means "is a member", which a viewer is. 57 tables let a read-only user INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE: supplier invoices, payments, salary runs, the chart of accounts, fiscal periods. The application's `requireWrite` is not the control here — Supabase publishes PostgREST with the user's own JWT, so a viewer can PATCH `/rest/v1/supplier_invoices` directly. Fixed in `20260808170000`.

**#16 — third `commit_method` mismatch.** `__year_end_prior_result_transfer` commits with `'system'`, which the CHECK constraint forbade. It fires on the *second* consecutive year-end close of an aktiebolag (the routine 2099→2098 omföring) — every existing year-end test closes a first year, the same success-path blind spot that hid the two settlement incidents. Found by the drift guard built to catch this class.

## Original audit findings

H-03 payment atomicity, H-05 test matrix, H-01/H-02/H-04/H-06, M-01…M-06, L-01/L-02, R-01 (iXBRL entitlement short-circuiting the actor/period check, letting a viewer finalize an annual report).

## H-03 — settlement creates its own voucher

The settlement RPCs took a draft voucher the application had already committed in a *separate* transaction, then cancelled it if the settlement rolled back — compensation that is best-effort by construction. `settle_customer_invoice_v2` / `settle_supplier_invoice_v2` now take the voucher as `p_journal` and create it inside the settlement transaction, so nothing economic exists before the RPC. Line-derivation logic stays in TypeScript (`plan*` variants); the RPC persists a plan and never decides which accounts a payment hits.

## H-05 — concurrency, failure injection, lifecycle

- **Settlement concurrency:** two transactions held open simultaneously, with `pg_blocking_pids` asserting the second genuinely blocks before the first commits. Same key concurrently, key reuse with a different payload, first-attempt rollback, and all four overlap shapes — each pinning the exact guard that fires rather than accepting either.
- **Failure injection:** ten stages per side, via real BEFORE triggers so the rollback under test is PostgreSQL's own. Plus the one case that must *not* roll back: commit succeeded, response lost, client retries.
- **Bank concurrency:** legitimate fan-out, forbidden duplicate `(transaction, invoice)`, parallel workers, cross-company refusal.
- **Stripe lifecycle:** idempotency, refunds that sum rather than overwrite, disputes, stale/out-of-order events, parallel delivery of one event.
- **Year-end + SIE matrices**, including the R-01 access shape driven as a real authenticated user.

## Permanent guards

Each reads the **live catalog**, not migration text, so it judges the definition that survived every later redefinition:

- `check:redefinition` — fails when a tracked critical object's definition count changes, listing what to diff. Verified to fire.
- `commit-method-provenance` — every `commit_method` literal any function writes vs the CHECK constraint.
- `security-definer-search-path` — every SECURITY DEFINER pins `search_path`; pgcrypto callers keep `extensions` on it.
- `view-tenant-isolation` — no new definer view readable by a tenant role.
- `tenant-isolation-matrix` — no write policy authorizing on read-level membership.

## Migration redefinition review

253 objects are defined more than once; 41 critical ones are now tracked. Two passes — chronological token diff, then history-vs-live, which separates "moved" from "lost". Four flagged, all four verified individually as benign. Recorded in `docs/audits/2026-08-08-migration-redefinition-review.md`.

## Database / deployment

Production is **12 migrations behind** this branch, so the four security fixes are not yet live. Ledger dry-run: 358 RECORDED, 69 APPLIED_BUT_UNRECORDED, 12 NOT_APPLIED, 0 CHECKSUM_MISMATCH, 0 AMBIGUOUS. The 12 are exactly this branch's migrations and are correctly unapplied.

Deployment order matters — running `db:migrate` first would try to re-apply the 69 already-applied files. Exact commands in `docs/audits/2026-08-08-supabase-advisors-and-ledger.md`.

**External operator actions:** enable leaked-password protection (dashboard-only), and the `mark-through` that must precede deploying these migrations.
