author: mcritchie-agent[bot]
body:
Task: https://mcritchie.studio/tasks/fix-engine-migration-command

Hub half of a self-caught defect. Engine half: [studio-engine#73](https://github.com/McRitchie-Studio/studio-engine/pull/73) (0.30.1).

## The command didn't exist

Both docs I shipped earlier today (#725) told agents to run:

```bash
bin/rails studio:install:migrations   # Unrecognized command
```

The real task is **`studio_engine:install:migrations`**, and copied files land with a **`.studio_engine.rb`** suffix, not `.studio.rb`.

I inferred the wrong spelling from mcritchie-industries' installed migration, which turned out to have been **hand-copied with a hand-written suffix mimicking the convention** rather than generated by the task. A file that looks like tool output isn't evidence of the tool's name.

## The advice was also unsafe

"Install the engine migrations" read as blanket guidance. The task copies **four reference migrations**, and `allow_null_image_cache_owner` runs `change_column_null :image_caches` — which fails outright on an app without that table.

moms-app hit exactly this and kept **one of the four**. Both docs now say to review what was copied before migrating, and name the failure rather than leaving it to be discovered.

## Files

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `docs/agents/modules/email-operations.md` | Correct task + suffix in the install block; added the review-before-migrate step; corrected the troubleshooting-list reference |
| `docs/agents/system/new-app-onboarding-sop.md` | Correct task + suffix; review-before-migrate with the failure mode named |

Verified empirically while building `moms-app-inbox-standard` — I ran the wrong command, read Rails' own "Did you mean?", ran the right one, and inspected what it produced.

author: conqueror-mod
body:
Salvaged from #132, which I closed as superseded — it solved the same starvation from the query side rather than the worker side, and that half was worth keeping.

## The pair

- **#136 (merged)** — the worker walks past a batch that stamps nothing. General: covers collections, and anything with no provider configured.
- **This** — music never enters the queue. Specific, and it is what makes the count honest.

## Measured on your real library

```
PendingCount: 2198  →  7
  still queued: collection  6
  still queued: movie       1
```

That number read 2,198 and never fell — indistinguishable from a stuck backlog, for work that was never going to happen. Seven is a number that can reach zero, which is the only kind worth showing.

## Two decisions carried over from #132

**A filter, not a stamp.** Marking music as "enrichment has run" would be a lie about what happened, and the day a music provider exists this one line changes and those rows become eligible — with no migration to undo the lie.

**Collections stay queued.** No provider handles them today either, but that is a *gap*, not a permanent fact, and excluding them would hide it. The filter names what can never be matched, not what merely is not matched yet.

Credit where due: the filter and the reasoning came from the other session's PR, not from me.

author: ericolimaeducador-ux
body:
Fecha os achados de `infra/AUDITORIA-2026-08-08.md` que dependiam **só de código**. O que restou depende de execução na nuvem ou é trabalho de escopo próprio — está mapeado em `infra/PRODUCTION-BACKEND.md`, o guia que a auditoria referenciava em seis pontos mas que não existia.

## Achados fechados

| # | O que era | Correção |
|---|---|---|
| C2 | `ThrottlerModule` registrado **sem `APP_GUARD`** — o limite só valia em 2 controllers; `telemedicina/acesso` (público, sem autenticação) rodava sem limite nenhum | `GlobalThrottlerGuard` como `APP_GUARD`, 300/min por IP + limites por rota |
| C4 | `/health` respondia 200 com o Redis fora, enquanto **toda** requisição autenticada falhava | indicador de Redis no health check, com timeout de 2s |
| M1 | Possível subir em produção com `JWT_ACCESS_SECRET=change-me-...` (valor do `.env.example`) sem aviso | fail-fast no boot |
| M3 | `autoIndex` do Mongoose ligado em produção | desligado fora de dev |
| M4 | Sem `enableShutdownHooks()` | hooks + `quit()` do Redis |
| C3 | 33 vulnerabilidades, 1 crítica | 28, **0 críticas** + gate no CI |

## Decisões que merecem revisão

**Os 300/min do teto padrão são deliberadamente altos.** O limite é por IP e uma clínica inteira atrás de um NAT compartilha o bucket. Apertar isso depende antes de resolver o M2 (ver abaixo).

**O gate do CI ficou em `critical`, não `high`.** Restam 5 highs sem correção disponível, todas presas na migração Nest 10 → 11 (`multer` via `@nestjs/platform-express`; `js-yaml` e `lodash` via `@nestjs/swagger`). Com `high`, o CI ficaria permanentemente vermelho — e um gate sempre vermelho é um gate que todo mundo aprende a ignorar.

**O rate limiter de login continua fail-open** (M5). É tradeoff deliberado e documentado; mudar para fail-closed transformaria queda de Redis em "ninguém loga". Fica alerta especificado no guia, não mudança de comportamento.

## Limitação conhecida

O storage do `@nestjs/throttler` é em memória, então o limite vale **por instância** do Cloud Run — com N instâncias o teto efetivo é N × limite. Protege a CPU de cada instância (que é o risco do polling da telemedicina), mas não é teto global. Storage no Redis acoplaria o throttling à disponibilidade do Redis, o que merece decisão explícita.

## Ainda aberto — não dá para fechar por código

- **C1**: os secrets do CI estão vazios; 100% dos deploys falharam desde 2026-08-07. **Cadastrar antes de mergear**, senão os workflows disparam e falham de novo.
- **M2**: atrás de um Load Balancer do GCP a última entrada de `X-Forwarded-For` é o balanceador, constante para todos. Se for o caso, o rate limiting agora global compartilha um bucket único. Só dá para determinar com tráfego real — medir no primeiro deploy.
- **M6**: rotacionar a chave da Anthropic.

## ⚠️ Mudanças de comportamento

1. **A API passa a recusar subir** em produção com segredo fraco ou placeholder. Se o `CLOUDRUN_ENV_YAML` tiver valor copiado do `.env.example`, o container não sobe — falha com a lista completa no log.
2. **Índice novo não nasce mais sozinho em produção** (`autoIndex` off). Ao adicionar índice num schema, criar explicitamente.

## Verificação

- 25 → **35 testes**, todos passando; `tsc` e build limpos em `apps/api` e `apps/web`.
- Cada commit intermediário compila (`bisect` continua útil).
- `bcrypt` 6 mantém o formato `$2b$` — **senhas já gravadas seguem validando**, verificado e não presumido.
- Um bug foi encontrado pelos próprios testes: o payload do health usava a chave `status`, que sobrescrevia o campo `up`/`down` do terminus — o `/health` mentiria de novo por outro caminho. Corrigido, com teste travando a regressão.

author: avel123111
body:
Codex нашёл два **P2** на уже смерженном #736. Оба реальны, оба воспроизведены прогоном **до** починки. Общее у них одно: измеритель не падал и не предупреждал — он отвечал «чисто» над непроверенным местом.

## 1. Форма экспорта — хуже из двух

Сборщик читал только `export const X`. На модуле вида

```js
const Row = () => null;
export function Col() { return null; }
export { Row };
```

он печатал **«НЕ ИЗМЕРЕНО»** при живом `Layout.jsx`. То есть рефактор формы экспорта **выключал бы гейт целиком** — и ровно молча, потому что «не измерено» я сам объявил законным состоянием для отсутствующего модуля.

Замер до починки:

```
{"measured":false,"nodes":0}     ← узлов там 2
```

Лечится переиспользованием соседа: `exportedNames(ast)` вынесен из `dsExports`, который все четыре формы уже умел. Собственно дырой и был мой урезанный сборщик, написанный в двух метрах от полного — рунг 2 лестницы, который я пропустил.

## 2. Алиас импорта

`import { Row as Stack }` → в разметке стоит `Stack`, узел пропускался. Обратный `import { Btn as Row }` → **ложное срабатывание**: имя тега совпало, но рисует его не примитив. `imports` хранит только путь модуля и на вопрос «что это за экспорт» не отвечает — добавлена карта локальное→экспортированное имя.

```
до:  Row as Stack → 0 узлов (должен 1)
     Btn as Row   → 1 узел  (должен 0)
после: 1 и 0
```

## Живое число не съехало

```
ДВОЙНОЕ ВЛАДЕНИЕ раскладкой: 56 узлов · 32 классов
```

Обе починки расширяют охват, а не пересчитывают — на текущем дереве ни алиасов примитивов, ни иных форм экспорта нет. Это и означает, что дефекты были **латентными**: сегодня они не врали, но выключились бы от первого же безобидного рефактора.

## Доказательство

3 теста, обе починки проверены обратным прогоном. Каждая мутация подтверждена **до** чтения вердикта:

| мутация | что упало |
| --- | --- |
| вернуть урезанный сборщик экспортов | тест форм `export {…}` / `export function` |
| игнорировать алиас импорта | оба алиас-теста — и пропуск, и ложное срабатывание |

Зелёные: `lint` · `typecheck` · `npm test` (819) · 2o «пол держится».

## Что осталось открытым и названо вслух

`import * as ds` + `<ds.Row className="…">` под `member` не попадает. В `src` таких обращений к примитивам сейчас нет ни одного, но появятся — и это будет **тихий пропуск**, а не ошибка. Записано комментарием в коде, чтобы следующий не искал.

Reuse audit: reused — `exportedNames` вынесен из существующего `dsExports` (тот же разбор, а не второй), `astOf`, `importTarget`, фикстурный стенд теста; new: none.

## Summary

- make bare `claude` plus TUI `/login` the default remote-login flow
- recognize and safely advance the known theme, workspace-trust, ready-prompt, and login-method screens

| Mode | Scopes |
| --- | --- |
| TUI `/login` (default) | `org:create_api_key`, `user:profile`, `user:inference`, `user:sessions:claude_code`, `user:mcp_servers`, `user:file_upload` |

author: amroksaleh
body:
Closes part of #713.

## What this PR does

Fixes **item 4** of #713 — the delete-before-hook ordering hazard — and nothing else. Items 1–3 (plugin-registrable setting keys, `resource_settings`, jsonb values) are **deliberately left out**; a written plan for each is at the bottom.

## The bug, and the half of it the issue did not mention

`OusApiHandler::delete()`, `TenantsApiHandler::delete()` and `RolesApiHandler::delete()` all ran:

```
dispatch('*.deleting')  →  DELETE (autocommit — no transaction)  →  dispatch('*.deleted')
```

So a `*.deleted` listener ran against a row that was already **committed** gone, and if it threw, the generic `catch (\Exception)` returned **500 after the delete had landed** — the caller saw a failure, the row was gone anyway, and a listener had no way to veto or undo. Core's own tables shrug this off because they carry real `ON DELETE CASCADE` constraints; plugin-owned tables have no FK, so this hook is their only cleanup mechanism.

While reproducing it I found the hazard is worse than #713 describes. `PluginLoader::wrapHookCallback()` wraps every plugin hook in a per-plugin error boundary that **catches all Throwables and returns `$data` unchanged**. So a plugin listener could not fail the operation *at all*: its objection was logged, its lifecycle error counter ticked toward the 3-strikes breaker, and the delete committed regardless. Wrapping the delete in a transaction alone would not have fixed anything for plugins — the exception never reached the handler. Both halves are fixed here.

## The fix

**1. Deletion is one transaction** (`OusApiHandler`, `TenantsApiHandler`, `RolesApiHandler`):

```
*.deleting  →  DELETE  →  *.deleted        [ ONE transaction ]
                                             ↓ commit
                                         *.deleted.async
```

- Uses the repo's established own-transaction idiom (`$ownTransaction = !$this->db->inTransaction()`; see `UsersApiHandler::update()`, `DomainEventStore::append()`), so it composes safely if a caller already has one open.
- The transaction opens *after* the existing 400/403/404/409 guards, so no early return can leak an open transaction.
- `*.deleted.async` moved to **after** the commit. `HookManager::dispatchAsync()` is non-critical by contract (a failure to persist must not break the caller's primary action) — keeping it inside would have inverted that, since a failed outbox insert poisons a PG transaction and would take the delete down with it. After the commit it also can never announce a deletion that rolled back.
- Bonus on the role path: `deleteRolePermissionsScoped()` and `deleteRoleScoped()` were two independent autocommitted statements. A failure between them stripped a role's grants but left the role — a silent privilege change. They are now atomic with each other.

**2. A real veto contract** — `Whity\Sdk\Hooks\HookVetoException` (SDK **1.15.0**, additive):

- The one Throwable `wrapHookCallback()` re-throws instead of swallowing. Everything else stays isolated exactly as before (the existing `testFailingHookCallbackIsIsolated` still passes unchanged).
- A veto does **not** tick the lifecycle error counter: it is a healthy plugin doing its job, and counting it would trip the breaker and disable a plugin for behaving correctly. Logged at INFO instead, so "why did that delete refuse?" is visible to an operator.
- Handlers turn it into **409 Conflict** with the plugin's `reason()` under `details.reason` — matching the shape of the existing child/member/assignment guards, and mirroring how `SettingsApiHandler` surfaces `SettingsValidationException::reason()`. The raw exception message is never surfaced, so the WC-186 leak guard stays satisfied (it forbids `getMessage()` in a `Response::error()`, not a vetted accessor).
- `reason()` is plugin-authored text that reaches a client, so it is normalised: control chars collapsed, whitespace squeezed, empty → generic, and capped at 300 **code points** using a PCRE `/u` pattern rather than `mb_substr` — the SDK's package-contract test pins it to requiring nothing but PHP, and a byte-wise cut would hand the client a broken UTF-8 sequence (Arabic is a first-class content language here).

## Reproduced before fixed

`tests/Api/DeleteHookTransactionRealEngineTest.php` (17 tests) drives all three handlers with a **real** `HookManager` and **real** listeners, against a real engine seeded from the production migrations. The sibling `*RealEngineTest` classes all `createMock(HookManager::class)` and stub `dispatch()` away — which is precisely why this bug survived in a suite that already covered these delete paths heavily.

Verified by stashing only the three handler files and re-running:

- **before the fix: 10 of 17 fail**
- **after the fix: 17/17 pass**

A `plugin_owned_rows` table (no FK, no cascade) stands in for a plugin's private store, so the "cleanup rolls back with the delete" case is tested as the issue describes it rather than in the abstract. `tests/Core/PluginIsolationTest::testHookVetoExceptionCrossesTheErrorBoundary` pins the boundary passthrough and that a veto does not count as a plugin fault.

## Not changed, on purpose

`UsersApiHandler::delete()` has the same autocommit-then-notify shape, but it is deliberately left alone: there is no `user.deleting` counterpart, and its core listener (`EmailNotifications::onUserDeleted`) sends mail — which must neither hold a transaction open nor be able to undo a membership removal because SMTP was down. This is stated in the SDK docblock so the asymmetry is intentional and documented rather than an oversight.

## Verification

Run locally in a throwaway container (`--network none`, no `.env`, so no database was reachable — staging was never touched):

- `phpstan analyse src tests plugins sdk` — **no errors**
- `scripts/ci-tenant-predicate-guard.php` — **OK, no unscoped tenant-table queries**
- `scripts/ci-plugin-tenant-conformance.php` — **OK**
- `scripts/ci-plugin-smoke.php` — **OK, 4 plugins loaded**
- `tests/Api/DeleteHookTransactionRealEngineTest.php` + `tests/Core/PluginIsolationTest.php` + `tests/Sdk/SdkPackageContractTest.php` — **45 tests, 339 assertions, all pass**

**Left to CI**, and why:

- The **whole** SQLite suite (~3.5k tests, which is where `RouteCatalogueCompletenessTest` and the OpenAPI drift test live). A local run over a Windows Docker bind mount is far slower than the CI runner; the targeted files above plus PHPStan cover the changed surface, and CI is the authoritative gate.
- The **real-PostgreSQL** job (Integration + Security suites, migration idempotency). No migration is added here and the new tests live in the SQLite `default` suite, but transaction semantics differ enough between engines to be worth CI's word — a failed statement poisons a PG transaction where SQLite is more forgiving.

---

# Plan for the rest of #713

Each of the three remaining items needs new SDK surface and/or a migration, and each is independently reviewable. Bundling them behind this fix would hold a real data-integrity bug hostage to a feature epic.

## Item 1 — plugin-registrable setting keys

The issue proposes "mirror `PermissionRegistry`". That is not a copy-paste: `PermissionRegistry` is an **instance** service (wired in `index.php`, called from `PluginLoader::registerCapabilities()`), while `SettingsRegistry` is a **static** catalogue with a private constructor and **328 static call sites across 36 files**. Two options:

- **(a) Convert to an instance service.** Architecturally cleanest, matches the precedent exactly, no static mutable state — but it touches all 328 call sites, which is a large mechanical diff with real regression surface.
- **(b) Keep the static facade, add a static registration path** — `SettingsRegistry::registerPluginKeys(string $source, array $descriptors)`, called from `PluginLoader::registerCapabilities()` right after the permission registration. Recommended.

Under (b):

- **Declaration**: a new optional `PluginSett

author: jredrupp
body:
marrow doesn't compile against current Mojo nightlies. I hit this while bumping bison's own pin and had to work through it end to end to get a clean `mojo package --Werror` build, so figured it was worth sending back.

Most of this is mechanical churn from stdlib/max relocations and renames: relative imports where absolute ones created a second nominal identity for the same type, `deinit`'s move-constructor parameter needing to be named `move` specifically, `ImplicitlyDeletable` trait requirements tightening up (ArrayData/AnyBuilder/StructBuilder had a mutually-recursive auto-derivation cycle to break), `String.write` removal, `trait_downcast` removal, and narrowing a bunch of `ref[...]` return-type annotations on the `as_*` downcasts that had gone stale relative to what they actually return.

The two substantive ones are in `views.mojo`:

- `DevicePassable._to_device_type` picked up a `mut encoder: Some[DeviceTypeEncoder]` parameter — `BufferView`/`BitmapView` needed updating to match.
- `elementwise` (now `max.algorithm.functional`, moved from `std.algorithm.reduction`) dropped its `Optional[DeviceContext]` overloads and `IndexList`-taking closures in favor of a mandatory `DeviceContext` argument and `Coord`-taking closures; `reduce_dim` moved from a runtime kwarg to a comptime parameter; `use_blocking_impl` is gone. `DeviceContext()`'s default `api` argument also now fails at compile time on CPU-only machines (`constraint failed: Unknown GPU architecture`), so the CPU call sites construct `DeviceContext(api="cpu")` explicitly instead — this matches MAX's own internal pattern in `backend/cpu/parallelize.mojo`.

Also included: the `_null_ptr()` fix from #2 (literal `unsafe_from_address=0` now rejected at compile time as non-nullable; the runtime-`Int` overload via `unsafe_from_address=Int(0)` has no such restriction and produces the same pointer).

Verified against `1.0.0b3.dev2026080206` specifically, not "latest" — nightlies in this window flip-flopped on the `Deinitable`/`ImplicitlyDeletable` trait name within days of each other, so pinning to an exact build that's confirmed to work seemed safer than chasing a moving target.

One thing this doesn't fix, flagged in the CHANGELOG entry: `mojo package`/`mojo precompile` now rejects any `def main()` reachable under the packaged directory, which affects marrow's own `tests/`, `kernels/tests/`, and `expr/tests/` (all of which have `def main()` by the `TestSuite.run` convention). That makes `mojo package marrow --Werror` fail immediately regardless of the fixes here. I worked around it downstream by packaging a filtered mirror with `tests/` excluded, but didn't touch marrow's own layout to fix it properly since that's a bigger structural change.

marrow's own `pixi run -e dev pytest` suite is still blocked by an unrelated pontoneer build-dependency failure, so this was verified via standalone `mojo run` probes for the API-shape changes plus `mojo package marrow --Werror` (tests excluded) going from 762 errors to 0, not the project's own test runner.

author: blarq-app
body:
## El problema

MJ armó el EP 2 de Paseo del Sena, cargó los avances, salió de la pantalla y al volver estaban en cero.

> *"Es raro que tenga que apretar guardar si en ninguna otra parte tengo que hacerlo, se guarda solo"*

Confirmado en la base: el EP se había creado bien (V3 obra, maestro Jefrey Gomez, 50 partidas) pero con `updatedAt == createdAt` — **la creación se guarda sola, los avances tipeados no**.

`EditorEP.tsx` era la **única** pantalla de la app con guardado manual (estado `dirty` + botón "Guardar cambios"). Solo guardaba solo en 3 momentos: al abrir el modal de sync, al cerrar el EP y al abrir el PDF. Fuera de eso, salir perdía todo. `ObraEditor.tsx` y `MueblesEditor.tsx` guardan al salir de cada campo desde siempre.

## Qué cambia

- **Guarda al salir de cada campo** (blur o Enter), como el resto de la app.
- **Se saca el botón "Guardar cambios"** — con autosave no tiene sentido dejarlo deshabilitado para siempre. En su lugar va la señal `SenalGuardado` que ya usa el banco ("guardando… / ✓ guardado", PR #325).
- **Sin aviso de "tenés cambios sin guardar"**, por decisión expresa de MJ: el objetivo era que el EP dejara de ser la excepción, no darle una excepción nueva.

## Por qué un endpoint por partida y no el PUT completo debounceado

Se agrega `PATCH /api/estados-pago/[id]/items/[itemId]`. Con 50 partidas el PUT reescribía **las 50** en cada edición, y dos guardados encimados se pisaban — el gotcha del PR #202 con las cantidades de herrajes. Por partida, dos filas editadas seguidas son incapaces de pisarse. Además revalida el tope del EP en el servidor, no solo en pantalla.

## GOTCHA que apareció al verificar

El refresco de pantalla **no puede ir dentro de la cola de guardados**. Los guardados se encadenan (uno por vez) para que no se pisen; la primera versión metía el `router.refresh()` adentro de esa cadena, así que cada guardado esperaba el re-render del anterior y cargar 5 partidas seguidas arrastraba la cola varios segundos: al recargar, **el último avance todavía no había salido**. Ahora el refresco va afuera y solo cuando no queda nada por mandar — 5 partidas seguidas hacen UN refresco, no 5. "✓ guardado" significa literalmente "la cola está vacía".

## Verificación

`scripts/verify-ep-autosave-146.ts` contra la base de **desarrollo** (EP #1 de Lefevre, 51 partidas):

- el avance queda al **recargar** la página;
- queda **saliendo de la pantalla sin apretar nada** (el caso de MJ);
- 5 partidas cargadas rápido **persisten las 5**;
- el tope sigue avisando y el campo vuelve solo al valor bueno cuando el servidor rechaza;
- el botón "Guardar cambios" ya no está.

Capturas antes/después en `scripts/_capturas/146-*`.

## Plata

**No toca plata.** `metrics.ts` y `src/lib/ep/calculations.ts` sin tocar; se guardan los mismos dos campos (`quantityExecuted` + `pctAccumulated` derivado igual). Verificado que el "monto de este avance" y el acumulado dan exactamente lo mismo antes y después de recargar. **No se tocó el cierre del EP** (`/close`), donde las cantidades se congelan como snapshot histórico.

## Bug de paso

El PUT del EP hacía el `update` **antes** de chequear si el EP estaba cerrado, así que un EP cerrado se quedaba igual con la fecha y las notas nuevas pese a devolver el 409. Ahora el guard va primero.

author: imaginethegames
body:
> *"we need to add a hangar to the main menu (thats where the shop will be, with the things you can unlock)"* — the developer, 2026-08-07

The fourth door. A screen that renders your ship from the real generators, your level from the one profile, and the level→unlock list of cosmetics — which is **empty**, and says so.

---

## The thing you should know before reading the diff

**The profile did not exist.** `src/progression/` was empty on `main`. a0-13 ratified the progression direction and emitted the chain (`docs/briefs/pr-*.md`), but nobody has claimed `pr-01` (the profile store) or `pr-03` (the level curve). a0-14 is gated on that *spec*, and says in as many words that the implementing PR **must not invent its own storage — one profile, one key, one reader**.

Both of those briefs name **UI Engineer** as an owner and both are `needs: nothing`. So this PR lands them, **to their briefs, verbatim, as their own commits** (`d3df684`, `ae5fa52`) — which is the only reading of "must not invent storage" that also finishes the work. If another lane has these in flight, this is the implementation to reconcile against; the key, the shape and the three load paths are the plan's, not mine.

Two departures from pr-01's literal text, both flagged rather than smuggled:

- **`ProfileStorage`, not `Storage`.** `Storage` is a DOM lib global; a local interface by that name shadows it silently for every reader of the file. Structurally identical — `platform.storage` passes straight in.
- **`equipped?: Record<slot, id>` added to the shape**, for a0-14. Unlocking and equipping are different verbs: unlocked is derived from level (the plan's own ruling — the stored array is a cache, §4), equipped is a stored fact. Optional, validated field by field, and it round-trips.

---

## The wiring test, and the proof it has teeth

a0-14: *"Write it so it fails if you delete the `hangar` case, and prove that in the PR body."*

`mainMenuRoute(option)` and `flowScreenHandler(screen)` are exhaustive switches with `default: return null`. That covers both directions of the failure: **the compiler** rejects a case deleted from the *union*, and **the tests** reject one deleted from the *switch* — which is the half the compiler cannot see.

`src/ui/main-menu.test.ts` then walks both lists. For every `MAIN_MENU_ITEMS` entry: it routes to a declared `NavScreen`, the graph has a `main-menu → that-screen` edge, and that screen reaches the menu again without starting a match. For every `FLOW_SCREENS` entry: the handler name resolves to a real export of `lobby-flow`, so the string cannot be a lie either.

Deleting `case 'hangar'` from **both** switches:

```
→ HANGAR routes nowhere: expected null not to be null
→ no main-menu → null edge for HANGAR: expected undefined to be truthy
→ HANGAR → null is a trap: expected false to be true
→ expected null to be 'hangar'
→ the hangar screen has no handler: expected null not to be null
→ expected null to be 'flowTapHangar'

6 failed, in src/ui/main-menu.test.ts > the wiring contract
```

Restored, green. `menu-nav.ts` gains the node **and** both edges in this same PR — the rule that file's own header states.

---

## Silhouettes are information — the boundary, written before the content

GDD §2.11 assigns hulls by name; style-guide §4 gives the reason: *"a silhouette on the minimap is information"*, and *"recognising a shape at 24 pixels tells you who you are dealing with before you can read a name."*

So the line is in `src/ui/hangar.ts`'s contract rather than in a review comment:

```ts
export const COSMETIC_VARIABLE  = ['colour', 'livery', 'decals', 'trim', 'engine glow'];
export const COSMETIC_INVARIANT = ['outline', 'proportions', 'class-identifying geometry'];
```

`CosmeticSlot` enumerates exactly the first list, `COSMETIC_SLOT_SURFACE` maps every slot into it, and a `Cosmetic` is `{ id, name, slot, level }` — **no geometry field, and no price**. The type system, not a reviewer, is what stops a hat from changing a hull. There are tests asserting no slot can be named `hull` / `shape` / `silhouette` / `outline` / `geometry` / `size` / `scale`, and that nothing a player can read on the screen says `buy` / `price` / `cost` / `credit` / `coin` / `purchase` / `shop` / `store` / `$`.

**To the first person adding content, and to the Director:** if the developer later wants a cosmetic that crosses that line, it is a design decision with a measurable cost — every shape-reading in the game is re-opened by it (minimap identification, the lobby's hull read per a0-06, the 24 px CI raster in `style-guide` §4) — not a content addition. It would need a ruling, not a PR.

---

## The empty state, which is what actually ships first

`COSMETICS` is `[]`. a0-13 designs no content on purpose (*"the list is empty until the developer fills it"*, plan §4), and there is a test pinning that so content cannot arrive without someone reading the contract above.

An empty grid is indistinguishable from a broken one (LESSONS §20), and the first thing the developer will do is open this screen. So:

- the bay draws **the real `shipSprite`** through the same `drawSprite` the match renders with — if a hull changes shape, the hangar shows it without anybody remembering to update a preview;
- the level block **reads**: `levelProgress(profile.xp)`, the same function the end-of-match summary will call over the same profile. `profile.level` is treated as a *cache* of that derivation — there is a test for a profile claiming level 99 on level-3 XP, and the shipped bundle proved the same thing by accident during the evidence run (a first-draft seed of 12 000 XP claiming `level: 7` drew **LEVEL 6**, which is correct);
- where the list would be, `model.empty` carries `"No cosmetics yet — they unlock as you level up."`

## Evidence

`node evidence/a0-14-hangar/run.mjs` — against the **shipped bundle** (`vite build` → `vite preview`), real Pixi, real generators, real reader. The only thing seeded is `localStorage`. Every screen is reached with a **real press** at the physical point the seam reports, never by calling a model function a player cannot.

| frame | what it shows |
|---|---|
| `a0-14-hangar-desktop.png` | LEVEL 7 · 1 480 / 6 750 XP · 27 MATCHES |
| `a0-14-hangar-phone.png` | 390×844 portrait → the landscape lock rotates the root, so it lays out in an **844×390 logical** viewport — the case the brief says must *work*, not merely fit |
| `a0-14-hangar-empty-fresh.png` | **the one that matters**: a clean install, no stored profile at all, so the reader folds to LEVEL 1 · 0 / 300 XP · 0 MATCHES |

A picture cannot prove a panel is *honestly* empty rather than blank, so the sentence is asserted as a **string** through `window.__mainMenu.hangarEmpty` and written to `readback.json` beside the images:

```json
"empty-fresh": { "ship": "VANGUARD · Anvil", "level": "LEVEL 1",
                 "empty": "No cosmetics yet — they unlock as you level up." }
```

The phone spec asks the harder question too: BACK is reported at a physical point inside the frame, and a real tap on it comes home to the menu. A control reported off the bottom of a 390 px phone is a bug this project has already paid for once.

Port **4188**, private and `--strictPort`: a preview already listening on the shared 4173 serves whatever bundle it was started with, which is how a capture ends up green against another lane's stale artifact.

---

## Keyboard reach needed a focus ring

a0-14 test 2 asks for HANGAR by keyboard *and* by tap. The menu answered exactly **one** key before this — Enter, which was PLAY — so a keyboard player could reach the first plate and nothing else.

Arrows (or W/S) now walk the focus ring and Enter activates it. `mainMenuStep` / `mainMenuIndexOf` are pure and index-based, so *"three steps down reaches HANGAR"* is a unit test rather than a click-through. **Focus starts on PLAY, so every keyboard path that existed behaves identically.** A tap and a keypress both go through one `activateMenu`, so

body:
## What changed

Builds VerityGraph's second ingestion mode on top of the green document-provenance vertical slice.

- official MediaWiki Action API provider for Wikipedia full-text search
- current `prop=tocdata` article-outline parsing rather than deprecated `prop=sections`
- selected-section retrieval and readable HTML normalization
- Wikipedia search/outline/import domain contracts
- canonical Wikipedia ingestion into the same `SourceDocument` / `SourceSpan` model as uploads
- public source URL + page ID + revision ID provenance
- `GET /api/v1/wikipedia/search`
- `GET /api/v1/wikipedia/pages/{page_id}/outline`
- `POST /api/v1/wikipedia/import`
- deterministic `FixtureWikipediaProvider` for E2E only
- mocked MediaWiki protocol tests using `httpx.MockTransport`
- SourceSpan offset invariant validation
- React Source Studio with separate Documents and Wikipedia modes
- reusable SourcePreview shared by both ingestion paths
- Wikipedia search results, article section chooser, and selected-section import UI
- browser E2E: search -> outline -> section selection -> import -> canonical provenance preview
- CI and local `--e2e` explicitly use the fixture provider, so external Wikipedia availability cannot make QA flaky
- ADR documenting official MediaWiki + deterministic boundary testing

## Why

The product promise is **different inputs, one evidence contract**. Wikipedia must not become a parallel ad-hoc text path; selected public content is normalized before NLP and retains revision-aware source provenance.

## Free-by-default behavior

Normal runtime defaults to live English Wikipedia via the official MediaWiki API and requires no API key or paid service. The fixture provider activates only when explicitly configured for deterministic QA.

## QA expected

1. Ruff backend/scripts
2. pytest document + Wikipedia + mocked MediaWiki protocol tests
3. frontend TypeScript/Vite build
4. Docker Compose startup
5. document upload browser E2E regression
6. Wikipedia browser E2E using deterministic provider
7. health contract regression

## Stacked PR note

This PR targets `agent/source-domain-and-document-ingestion`. PR #3 is green and ready for review; once earlier stacked PRs are merged, this can be retargeted to `main` without changing its feature diff.

body:
## المشكلة
بعد تغيير الاسم، ضلّ الاسم القديم ظاهر على كروت الطلبات.

السبب: الاسم الظاهر على كرت الطلب هو اسم **الصفحة** (`pageName`) وليس اسم المتجر — وهو **منسوخ نصّاً داخل كل طلب** وقت إنشائه. `editEmpPage` كانت تحدّث مستند `employee_pages` فقط، فتضل كل الطلبات القديمة حاملة الاسم القديم. ونفس الشيء لـ `operator_stores.pageName` و `page_refunds.pageName`.

## التنفيذ
- **`_migrateNameRefs`** — مساعد عام لترحيل أي اسم مخزّن نصّاً: بالمعرّف أولاً (السجلات الحديثة) ثم بالاسم القديم (سجلات قديمة بلا معرّف)، على دفعات من 400 مستند، ويتخطّى المستندات المحدّثة سلفاً.
- **`_renamePageEverywhere`** — يحدّث `employee_pages` ثم يرحّل `pageName` في `employee_orders` و `operator_stores` و `page_refunds`، ويحدّث نسخ الذاكرة (`_empOrdersAllData`, `_opOrdersAllData`, `_opStoresList`, `_empPagesCache`).
- **`editEmpPage`** — صار يرفض الاسم الفارغ والمكرر، يعرض رسالة تأكيد، ويستدعي الترحيل الكامل بدل تحديث المستند وحده، ثم يعيد رسم قائمة الطلبات.
- **`renameOpStore`** — يستخدم المساعد الجديد، وإذا كان المتجر مربوطاً بصفحة يعرض سؤالاً واضحاً: «الاسم اللي بيظهر على كروت الطلبات هو اسم الصفحة مش اسم المتجر — بدك نغيّرها كمان؟».
- رفع الإصدار إلى `v205`.

## الفحص
مجموعتا اختبار آلي على مخزن Firestore وهمي — 38 فحصاً نجحت كلها: ترحيل الطلبات بالمعرّف وبالاسم القديم، عدم المساس بصفحات/متاجر أخرى، رفض الاسم المكرر والفارغ، تحديث الذاكرة، وسلوك القبول والرفض في سؤال الصفحة المربوطة.

author: atyrode
body:
Enables the yabai scripting addition by explicit operator decision (2026-08-08), reversing the Phase 1 default. **Draft until the runbook below is completed on the Mac and the addition is verified loaded.**

## What this buys and what it doesn't

- Now: `window_animation_duration = 0.25` — smooth animation of yabai-initiated frame changes (warp, balance, zoom, window moves).
- Later: keyboard Space create/destroy — real i3 workspace parity.
- **Not**: live neighbour tracking during a mouse drag-resize. That capability does not exist in yabai at any permission level; frames apply when the drag ends and the animation smooths that jump.

## Audited security shape

- Sudoers rule generated by nix-darwin, pinned to the **sha256 of the exact declared binary**: `%admin ALL=(root) NOPASSWD: sha256:<hash> <store-path>/bin/yabai --load-sa`. Nothing else gains root.
- Root launchd daemon `yabai-sa` loads the addition at boot; `KeepAlive.SuccessfulExit = false`.
- The addition injects a payload into Dock.app — this is the part that requires SIP's debugging protections off.
- Screen Recording grant for yabai is TCC-keyed to the Nix store path: **every yabai version bump will re-prompt**. Known recurring toll, accepted.
- SIP change required: `csrutil enable --without fs --without debug --without nvram` plus the `-arm64e_preview_abi` boot-arg on Apple Silicon, which relaxes pointer-auth ABI restrictions for non-Apple arm64e code system-wide.

Until the runbook is done, the load daemon fails (bounded retry) and yabai behaves exactly as before; all non-SA features are unaffected.

## Operator runbook (needs physical presence, two reboots)

1. Shut down. Hold the power button → Options → Recovery. Utilities → Terminal:
   `csrutil enable --without fs --without debug --without nvram`
2. Reboot to macOS, then: `sudo nvram boot-args=-arm64e_preview_abi`
3. Reboot again.
4. `atyrode apply` (this branch, or after merge), then verify:
   - `csrutil status` → shows the three protections disabled
   - `sudo yabai --load-sa` → exits 0, or check `launchctl print system/org.nixos.yabai-sa`
   - `yabai -m config window_animation_duration` → `0.250000`
   - toggle `caps+f` on a window → animated zoom, approve the Screen Recording prompt on first use
   - `yabai -m space --create` then `yabai -m space --destroy` → Space count changes without Mission Control

## Checks

author: alexander-turner
body:
Claims the release-path race, the auto-resolve credential ladder, and the `guard-pairs` count that is currently red on `main`.

## Summary

Three CI failures that all end in "the automation gave up, and said the wrong thing about why".

**1. The stranded release.** Two `auto-version` runs overlapped. The later one's release-docs commit conflicted with the earlier one's `version` line in `plugin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, `push_with_rebase` refused to force-push, and 2.26.1 landed on npm with **no git tag** and a manifest still reading 2.26.0 — the exact drift the stamping step exists to prevent. The manifest's `version` is the one rebase conflict with a deterministic answer, so resolve it narrowly instead of abandoning the release.

**2. The conflict resolver never reached the model.** `claude-conflict-resolve.sh` required `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` **by name**. This repo has rung 1 empty and `_FALLBACK`, `_FALLBACK_3..6` provisioned, so every `Auto-resolve merge conflicts` run died at that line — and because it died before any execution log existed, the downstream gate reported `produced no execution log — the action failed to run before invoking Claude (action config or credential plumbing)`, which names the wrong cause. The ladder library's own header warns about exactly this short-copy failure mode.

**3. `main` is red on the guard-pair count.** `c12f4de` paired `README.md` with the claude-hooks exports guard, so the AST walk now resolves a 28th data file, but `RESOLVED_PATH_COUNT` stayed at 27. Every PR inherits the failure through its merge ref. Verified against a clean `origin/main` worktree, not just this branch.

## Changes

- `.github/scripts/version-bump.sh`: `restamp_manifest_conflict()` — when the plugin manifest is the **sole** conflicted path during the release-docs rebase, take the upstream file (so a concurrent edit to any other field survives), re-run the stamper over just `version`, and continue the rebase. Any other conflicted path still aborts.
- Same file: the re-stamp **verifies** the published version is the maximum via the existing `max_version` helper rather than assuming a concurrent stamp is always older — with the racing runs' push order reversed, upstream holds the newer stamp and re-stamping would walk the manifest backwards. An unreadable or empty upstream version is its own refusal. Corrected the two comments that documented the old unconditional behaviour.
- `.github/scripts/claude-conflict-resolve.sh`: gate on the **ladder** being empty, not on rung 1 being set, and name the settable variables in the refusal. The refusal still lands before the CLI install is paid for.
- `test/guard-pairs.test.mjs`: `RESOLVED_PATH_COUNT` 27 → 28.
- `scripts/version-bump.test.mjs`: added `makeReleaseSandbox()` / `makeRacingClone()` / `runRelease()` / `showOnRemote()` and rewrote the three copy-pasted release sandboxes onto them; each test now carries only its racing commit and assertions.

## Tests / verification

- Full suite on this branch merged with current `main`: **3054/3054**.
- `scripts/version-bump.test.mjs` — 14/14. Two new cases race a second clone against the release run: one stamping an **older** version plus a second field (asserts `version` becomes the published one, the concurrent `description` survives, the tag lands), one stamping a **newer** version (asserts non-zero exit, `Refusing to re-stamp …: it reads 1.2.0`, upstream manifest untouched, no tag pushed).
- `.github/scripts/auto-resolve/lib.test.mjs` — 11/11. Two new cases run the real entrypoint in a sandbox with the install and fan-out stubbed: one asserts a fallback-only ladder reaches the fan-out with that rung, one asserts an empty ladder exits 1 naming the variables and never pays for the install.
- Non-vacuity checked in both directions for every new case: reverting the ordering check fails 1/14; reverting the credential guard fails 2/11; both pass with the fixes restored.
- The count bump is not a rubber stamp: the partition, direction and stale-entry assertions all stayed green throughout, so the 28th path is the deliberate `README.md` pairing and not a resolver regression widening the set.

## Decisions made

- **Resolve narrowly rather than force-push.** The resolver only fires when the manifest is the *only* conflicted path and only moves `version` forward. The alternative — `git checkout --theirs` on the whole manifest — would silently drop a concurrent edit to any other field.
- **`JSON.parse(readFileSync(...))` over `require('./…')` for the upstream version.** `require` of a relative path resolves against the script's directory, not the process CWD, and a swallowed read error would yield an empty version that `max_version` treats as smallest and waves straight through.
- **Carried the `main`-red count fix here rather than opening a sibling PR.** This branch cannot go green without it — the merge ref runs `main`'s tests — so a separate PR would just be a second thing to land first.
- **Left the stranded 2.26.1 unreconciled.** The remaining gap is a missing `v2.26.1` git tag; it belongs on `d36b2f5`, the head of the run that published it. Creating a release tag is not this branch's to do. The CHANGELOG needs no edit — `v2.26.1`'s commits predate the `v2.26.0` docs commit, so its notes are already inside the `[2.26.0]` section.

## Checklist

- [x] Commits follow Conventional Commits; each subject reads as a user-facing release note.
- [x] `pnpm test`, `pnpm lint` pass locally.
- [x] New detectors: n/a — no detector changes.
- [x] No real secrets/tokens in the diff, tests, or description.
- [x] `CHANGELOG.md` and `package.json` version left untouched.

## Lessons Learned

- **What:** make the release-docs push resolve a plugin-manifest `version` conflict forward instead of aborting, and verify the ordering with `max_version` before re-stamping. **Where:** `.github/scripts/version-bump.sh` (`push_with_rebase` / `restamp_manifest_conflict`). **Why:** two concurrent `auto-version` runs is the normal steady state on an active repo; the abort strands a published version on npm with no tag and a stale manifest, and the naive resolution regresses the manifest when the push order reverses.
- **What:** admit on "the OAuth ladder is non-empty", never on `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` being set. **Where:** `.github/scripts/claude-conflict-resolve.sh`, and any other entrypoint reading `lib/claude-oauth-ladder.bash`. **Why:** rung 1 is the first credential an adopter rotates out; a by-name requirement turns a fully-provisioned fallback ladder into a total outage, mis-reported by the execution-log gate as credential plumbing rather than a missing token.
- **What:** when a guard test pins an exact count of scanned files, changing the data it scans must bump the count in the same commit. **Where:** `test/guard-pairs.test.mjs` (`RESOLVED_PATH_COUNT`) and `.hooks/guard-pairs.json`. **Why:** adding a pairing without the bump reds `main` itself, and every open PR then inherits a failure that looks like its own.
- **What:** in a script-based test suite, build the sandbox once in a helper rather than per test. **Where:** `scripts/version-bump.test.mjs`. **Why:** three verbatim copies meant a new precondition of the release script had to be applied three times, and the copy that missed it failed opaquely.

author: ymatsuza
body:
Close #4

## 概要

トップページの「ブラウザだけで処理されているので、データは保存されません。」が事実と異なっていたので修正した。**HTML の文言のみの変更で、ツールの実装には触れていない。**

## 影響範囲

| 対象 | 変更 | 影響 |
|---|---|---|
| `index.html` | ヒーローの説明文 1 行 | 表示文言のみ |
| 各ツールの実装 | **変更なし** | なし |

## 変更内容と根拠

`index.html:78` からリンクされている `tostr.php` はサーバー側で動作する:

- `tostr.php:77` — `$result = @file_get_contents($pageUri);` 利用者が入力した URL をサーバーが取得する
- `tostr.php:61-67` — `function sendMail(...)` → `mb_send_mail($mailaddress, $subject, $body, "From:info@beyonds.co.jp")` 入力アドレス宛に本文をサーバーから送信する

`index.html` からリンクされている 17 ツールのうち、サーバー側処理は `tostr.php` の 1 件だけで、残り 16 件は `.html`（クライアント処理）。カード側には既に `PHP` のピルと「メール送信も可能」の記載があり、ヒーロー文だけが全ツールをブラウザ内処理と言い切っていた。

変更後:

> ほとんどのツールはブラウザ内だけで処理され、入力したデータは送信されません。
> `PHP` の付いたツール（ウェブページをテキストに変換）だけはサーバー側で処理し、指定した URL の取得とメール送信をサーバーが行います。

`README.md` と `AGENTS.md` は元から正確（`AGENTS.md:11`「PHP ページはローカルサーバーで確認します」）で、修正不要。

## テスト

文言のみの変更のため実行なし。

関連: Asana `AI 正本（AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md / README.md）が実装と食い違っている件の是正`

author: canyouseeus
body:
## What went wrong

An apply came back **`RENAMED 0 / REMAINING 418 / FAILED 0`** with no error on screen and **nothing in the platform logs**. Those numbers are the exact signature of the auth-error path — throw on the first file, return immediately — but two things I introduced hid it.

### 1. I deleted the logging

Converting auth failures into `DriveAuthError` removed the per-file `console.error` that used to record them. The earlier run left 418 log lines saying `invalid_client`; this one left none.

Trading a loud failure for a silent one is worse than the bug I was fixing. Both the throw site and the abort now log before returning.

### 2. No sign of life

A run occupies up to its full 50-second budget inside a single request, so the panel sat unchanged for minutes with no way to distinguish a working run from a hung one.

There's now an elapsed counter while a run is in flight. **It counts seconds, not files** — the request is one call, so per-file progress genuinely isn't knowable client-side. An honest clock beats a fake progress bar.

## Also worth stating

The red auth panel shipped in #199. A browser holding a cached bundle renders none of it and sees only the zeros — which is probably what happened here. That isn't fixable in code; it needs a hard refresh.

## Verification

`tsc --noEmit` clean in the changed files, build clean.

The auth path itself still can't be exercised from a container without valid credentials. What this changes is that the *next* failure leaves evidence in two places instead of zero.

author: claude[bot]
body:
## Summary

Closes a live data-loss bug: `orchestrate.Render` emits zero `volumes` for any service, so git repositories and the SQLite database live in the forgejo container's writable layer. `Converge` runs `docker compose up -d --remove-orphans`, which recreates any service whose resolved config changed — so an ordinary `up` today can destroy the forge's state. This is core-only (no CLI/API/UI surface change): `internal/core/deploy` and `internal/core/forge`.

- `deploy.Up` gains a `configureState` step, run before `Converge`, that creates `<RemoteDir>/state/git` and `<RemoteDir>/state/gitea` on the host, owned by the uid:gid the official Forgejo image's `git` user runs as (`1000:1000`, the image's unoverridden default — Docker otherwise creates a missing bind-mount source root-owned, which Forgejo can never write to), and bind-mounts both into the forgejo service at `forge.RepoRoot` and `forge.DataPath` (both now exported from `forge/appini.go` for this).
- `forge.DataPath` is also where `RenderAppINI` already stores LFS objects, attachments, avatars, and CI artifacts by default, so this one mount keeps everything Forgejo itself writes durable — not just the database.
- Directory creation and `chown` are both idempotent (`mkdir -p`, `chown` on an already-owned directory), so a re-run against an already-converged host changes nothing (UP-003).
- No new `orchestrate` API was needed: `orchestrate.WithBindMount` already generically declares a host-path bind mount on a named service (it's what `configureForge` uses for `app.ini`), so `configureState` reuses it directly for both state mounts.

## A design call worth flagging

`docs/tech-spec.md` "Host state layout" also names a third row: `<RemoteDir>/state/blobs → the local blob adapter's path, when the bundle uses one`. Nothing in the tree today configures Forgejo's own storage (`app.ini`) to write anywhere other than `forge.DataPath` — `Drivers.Blob` isn't resolved into an adapter anywhere in production code yet (that's `BKUP-006`/a future storage-wiring requirement) — so there is no container-side path yet for a local blob adapter's content to land at. Rather than guess at one, `configureState` creates `<RemoteDir>/state/blobs` on the host **only** when the bundle's blob driver is `local`, but deliberately leaves it unmounted and unowned by the forgejo container's uid. `docs/tech-spec.md` is updated in this PR to say so explicitly. If that reading is wrong, happy to revisit once the storage-wiring decision exists.

## One-time impact on already-deployed hosts

Adding volumes changes the forgejo service's resolved config, so **the first `up` after this lands will recreate the forgejo container**. On an instance whose state is currently container-internal (i.e., any host deployed before this PR), that recreation is exactly the data loss this PR fixes — it is unavoidable and one-time. Anyone with a live instance should back up before running `up` with this change, until `backup`/`restore` (BKUP-006/RSTR-*) land.

## Test plan

- [x] `go build ./...`
- [x] `go test ./internal/core/deploy/...` — new tests cover: git/gitea mounts + ownership, blobs dir created only for `local` blob driver (and left unmounted/unowned), state directories created before `docker compose up` runs
- [x] `go test ./internal/core/forge/...`
- [x] `go test ./internal/core/orchestrate/...`
- [x] `go test ./internal/api/...`
- [x] `gofmt -l .` clean

Refs: UP-004

## Summary
- `rescaleIngredientLine` and `parseIngredient` both located an ingredient's quantity via a start-anchored regex, so name-first lines like `"Soy sauce, 2 tbsp"` silently failed to scale on the serving-size toggle — and, worse, silently defaulted to a grocery-list quantity of `1` in `pipeline/normalize.ts`.
- Added `findQuantityToken()` (`src/lib/units/numeric-extract.ts`), which falls back to scanning for a `<number> <unit>` pair anywhere in the line when nothing is found at the start. `rescale.ts` and `parser.ts` both now use it, so the fix covers the `RecipeView`/`RecipeEditor` display toggle and the actual grocery-list quantity math from one shared root-cause fix — no changes needed to those call sites.
- `raw_text` is never rewritten; it stays exactly as imported, preserving the "preserve original for manual-edit step" contract in the data model.
- Scope boundary (intentional, tested): a non-leading quantity with no unit immediately next to it (e.g. `"Eggs, 2"`) still doesn't resolve — same ambiguity tradeoff already documented in `rescale.ts` for embedded numbers.
- Moved `UNIT_TOKENS`/`UNIT_RE_SOURCE` into a new `src/lib/units/unit-vocab.ts` to avoid a circular import; `parser.ts` re-exports them unchanged so `instagram.ts`'s existing import keeps working.

## Test plan
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean
- [x] `npm test` — 472/472 passing across 18 suites, no regressions
- [x] Added regression tests: `tests/units.test.ts` (`parseIngredient` non-leading cases), `tests/rescale.test.ts` (`rescaleIngredientLine` non-leading cases), `tests/pipeline.test.ts` (grocery-list quantity no longer defaults to 1)
